Tom never forgot his experience in the magical land and how he was introduced to the wonderful youths. From then on, he proudly called the youths his best friends.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play together in the park. One day, they saw a big tent with many people inside. They heard music and laughter. They wanted to see what was inside.

They sneaked into the tent and saw a man and a woman in pretty clothes. The woman had a veil on her head. It was white and shiny. The man and the woman were holding hands and smiling. They looked happy.

Lily and Ben watched them for a while. They saw them kiss and hug. They heard the people clap and cheer. They learned that the man and the woman were getting married. They were uniting their hearts.

Lily and Ben thought that was nice. They wanted to do the same. They found a veil in a box. It was pink and sparkly. Lily put it on her head. Ben took her hand and smiled. They kissed and hugged. They pretended to be married. They united their hearts.

But then, a fierce dog came into the tent. It barked and growled. It saw Lily and Ben and ran towards them. It wanted to bite them. Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the veil and ran away. They hid behind a tree. They hoped the dog would go away. They held each other tight. They were still best friends.

There were three friends - Sid, Dave, and Mark. One day they were playing with their board in the park. Suddenly, it began to rain, so they decided to take their board and go to Sid's house. 

When they reached Sid's house, they knocked on the door and waited. Sid's mum answered and said they could come in. But she also said they had to be safe in the house.

Dave and Mark agreed and started playing with their board indoors. But Sid refused. He wanted to keep playing outside in the rain. Sid's mum tried to explain why it was not safe, but Sid was too stubborn to listen to reason.

At last, Dave stood up and said, "Sid, it's not wise to disobey your mum. If we do as she says, then we will be safe. We all have to work together to help each other stay safe."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a house with a big hedge. She liked to play outside and run around the hedge. One day, she saw a bird sitting on the hedge and she wanted to catch it. She climbed up the hedge but she was clumsy and fell down. She hurt her leg and cried.

Her mother came outside and asked what happened. The little girl told her that she fell down from the hedge and hurt her leg. Her mother knew that she shouldn't have climbed the hedge because it was dangerous. She took her inside to make her feel better. Unfortunately, the little girl's leg got worse and she had to go to the hospital. The doctor said that she had broken her leg and needed a cast. The little girl was sad and couldn't play outside anymore. She knew she shouldn't have climbed the hedge.

One day, Sally was walking with her dad. She loved exploring the park and playing with all the animals she could find. 

Suddenly she saw something shiny under the ground. She was excited, but when she tried to pick it up, it got stuck.

"Dad, look! What is it?" she asked, pointing to the shiny thing.

"It looks like a mineral, Sally," her dad said.

Sally was determined to get the mineral, so she kept trying to pull it out of the ground. But no matter how hard she pulled, it wouldn't come out.

Suddenly, the ground started to shake and the mineral slipped out of her hands. Sally was so sad that she lost it.

"Don't worry, Sally," her dad said. "You were very brave to try and get that mineral, even though you were feeling weak."

Sally smiled and they went off to explore the rest of the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun. Bun loved to hop around in the fields and play with his friends. One day, Bun saw a wise old owl sitting on a tree branch. 

"Hello, Mr. Owl!" said Bun. "What are you doing up there?"

"I'm just watching the world go by," replied Mr. Owl. "What are you up to, little one?"

"I'm playing with my friends," said Bun. "We're trying to make a mark in the ground with our hopping!"

"That sounds like fun," said Mr. Owl. "But remember, it's not about how high you hop or how big your mark is. It's about having fun with your friends."

Bun thought about what Mr. Owl said and decided to go back to playing with his friends without worrying about their marks. They all hopped around happily, enjoying each other's company. And from that day on, Bun knew that being wise meant having fun with friends, not just making big marks.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she wanted to have a party with her friends. So, she decided to invite them over to her house. She made pretty invitations with colorful paper and stickers.

Suddenly, there was an emergency! The cake she baked fell on the floor and broke into pieces. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. But, she remembered that she was creative. She decided to make cupcakes instead and decorate them with sprinkles and frosting.

When her friends arrived, they were happy to see the pretty cupcakes. They played games and danced to music. Lily was happy that her friends came to her party and that she was able to be creative and make something yummy for them to eat.

Once upon a time, there was a hidden toy box in a little girl's room. The little girl, named Sally, loved to play with all her toys. One day, Sally found a new toy in the box. It was a thermometer.

Sally asked her mom, "What is this?" Her mom replied, "It's a thermometer. It helps us know if it's hot or cold." Sally was very happy to learn about her new toy.

Every day, Sally played with her thermometer. She would ask her mom, "Is it hot or cold today?" Her mom would always reply with a smile. Sally loved her new toy and always kept it safe in her hidden toy box.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, she saw a pin on the ground and picked it up. She thought it was pretty, so she put it in her pocket.

As she was playing, she saw a bird flying high in the sky. It was a wild bird with beautiful feathers. Lily wanted to talk to the bird, but she didn't know how. She remembered the pin in her pocket and thought it might help her talk to the bird.

But as she reached into her pocket, the pin poked her finger! Lily learned that sometimes things that look pretty can hurt you. She also learned that it's important to be careful and not touch things that you don't know are safe. From that day on, Lily made sure to always be careful and not pick up anything that could hurt her.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little bird. The little bird had a small nest on a tree. The nest was made of many twigs. Some twigs were fragile, but the bird was happy.

One day, the little bird wanted to add a new twig to its nest. It looked for the best twig it could find. The bird saw a very nice twig on the ground. It tried to pick up the twig, but it was too heavy. The little bird did not give up.

The bird tried again and again. It wanted to succeed. The bird pushed and pulled the twig. At last, the little bird got the twig to its nest. The bird was very happy. It had succeeded. The nest was now even better. The little bird was proud of its hard work.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. They also like to eat yogurt. Yogurt is yummy and good for them.

One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide. They run to the slide and wait for their turn.

"Can I go first?" Tom asks Jen.

"Okay, you can go first. But be careful. The slide is very fast," Jen says.

Tom nods and climbs up the ladder. He sits on the slide and moves down. He feels the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He laughs and shouts, "Whee!"

Jen watches Tom and smiles. She is happy for him. She is a dependable friend. She waits for him to get off the slide. Then she climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. She moves down too. She feels the same wind and sun. She laughs and shouts, "Whee!"

Tom and Jen meet at the bottom of the slide. They hug and high-five. They are proud of themselves. They are brave and fun.

They run to their moms and tell them about the slide. Their moms are proud of them too. They give them yogurt as a treat. Tom and Jen eat their yogurt and share it with each other. They are happy and full.

They thank their moms and say goodbye to the slide. They hold hands and walk to the swings. They are ready for more adventures. They are the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the store with her mommy. They wanted to buy a soft blanket for her bed. While they were walking around the store, they saw a big leopard toy. 

Lily said to her mommy, "I want to buy the leopard toy, please!" 

Her mommy said, "Okay, we can buy the leopard toy and the soft blanket for your bed." 

Lily was very happy and hugged her new leopard toy. When they got home, she put the soft blanket on her bed and cuddled with her new friend, the leopard. They both slept soundly all night long.

Once upon a time there were two friends playing in the meadow. One was a little rabbit and one was a small squirrel. They were having so much fun playing in the sun, running and hopping in the tall grass.

But then they saw something strange! A giant, red mushroom! The little rabbit and the small squirrel were curious, so they decided to go and explore it.

The rabbit got there first and gave the mushroom a push. It wobbled a bit and made a funny noise. They were so surprised, they both took a step back.

But the squirrel was a bit careless and the mushroom then tumbled down the hill. The two friends chased after it and managed to catch it before it went too far.

They were so glad they were able to save the big and strange mushroom. They knew it was special and they would take care of it forever.

Once upon a time, in a little house, there was a big hall. In this hall, there was a small, sad boy. He felt miserable because he had no friends to play with. He sat on the floor, all alone.

One day, a happy, colorful top came to the hall. It saw the sad boy and wanted to make him happy. So, the top started to spin around and around. It spun so fast that it made pretty colors in the air.

The sad boy saw the spinning top and smiled. He clapped his hands and laughed. The top spun faster and faster, making the boy laugh even more. The boy and the spinning top became good friends, and they played together in the hall every day. The boy was not miserable anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys, but he wanted to build something big. He decided to build a tower out of bricks. Timmy went outside to get some bricks, but he was tired from playing all day. 

Timmy's friend, Billy, saw him and asked, "What are you doing, Timmy?"

"I'm building a tower with bricks," Timmy replied.

Billy said, "That sounds like fun! Can I help?"

Timmy said, "Yes, please help me. I'm too tired to do it alone."

So, Timmy and Billy worked together to build the tower. It took a long time, but they finally finished. Timmy was so happy that he said, "This is the best tower ever! Thank you for helping me, Billy."

Billy said, "You're welcome, Timmy. We make a good team."

Suzy was always very brave, so when she got a special suit in the mail, she was excited to show it off. She loved the bright colors and sparkly buttons and the fabric was so soft and cute! She decided to put on the suit and go outside to show it off to the neighbors.

When Suzy went outside, she noticed that all her friends were already wearing the same suit. Everyone was so excited to see that Suzy had the same suit too, but she started to feel a bit weird. Then, she noticed that the store window was all boarded up and for sale. Suzy realized that the suit must have been part of an old store closing sale!

Suzy started to panic and felt really silly for wearing the same suit as everyone else. She quickly rushed home and changed into her other clothes. Though it was a strange experience, it was a nice reminder to be brave and try new things!

Anna liked to read books. She had many books in her room. She read them every day. She read them on her bed, on her chair, on her floor. She read them with her toys, with her dolls, with her teddy.

One day, Anna wanted to read a new book. She saw it on the shelf. It was big and colorful. It had a picture of a princess on the cover. Anna reached for the book. But it was too high. She could not get it.

She tried to jump. She tried to climb. She tried to use a stool. But nothing worked. She was too small. She felt sad and angry. She wanted the book.

She saw her brother Tom. He was big and tall. He could get the book. She asked him for help.

"Tom, can you please get me that book?" she said.

Tom looked at the book. He looked at Anna. He smiled.

"Sure, I can get you that book," he said. "But what will you give me?"

Anna thought. She did not have much to give. She had her books, her toys, her dolls, her teddy. But she liked them all. She did not want to give them away.

"Nothing," she said. "Just get me the book. It is easy for you."

Tom shook his head.

"No, nothing is not enough," he said. "If you want the book, you have to give me something. How about your mattress? It is soft and comfy. I want it."

Anna gasped.

"My mattress? No, you can't have my mattress!" she said. "That is where I sleep. That is where I read. I need my mattress."

Tom shrugged.

"Then you can't have the book," he said. "It is too bad. It is a nice book. It has a princess and a dragon and a castle. I will read it myself."

He reached for the book. He took it from the shelf. He walked away.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She wanted the book. She wanted to read it. She wanted to see the princess and the dragon and the castle. She did not want to give up her mattress. She did not know what to do.

She ran after Tom. She grabbed his arm. She pulled the book.

"Give it back! Give it back!" she shouted.

Tom pulled back. He held the book.

"No, it is mine! It is mine!" he shouted.

They tugged and pulled. They yelled and cried. They made a lot of noise.

Their mom heard them. She came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting over the book. She saw the book tear. She saw the pages fall. She was not happy.

She took the book from them. She scolded them.

"What are you doing? Why are you fighting? Why are you ruining the book?" she said.

Anna and Tom looked down. They felt sorry. They felt ashamed. They told their mom what happened.

Their mom sighed. She hugged them.

"Anna, Tom, you are both wrong," she said. "Books are not for fighting. Books are for sharing. Books are for learning. Books are for enjoying. You should not be greedy or mean. You should be kind and generous. You should help each other and respect each other. Do you understand?"

Anna and Tom nodded. They understood. They said sorry to each other. They said sorry to their mom. They said sorry to the book.

Their mom smiled. She fixed the book. She gave it to them.

"Here, you can both read the book," she said. "But you have to take turns. And you have to be careful. And you have to say thank you."

Anna and Tom said thank you. They took turns. They were careful. They read the book. They saw the princess and the dragon and the castle. They liked the book. They liked each other. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom was cooking dinner and some smoke came out of the oven. Lily's mom quickly opened the window to remove the smoke from the kitchen. 

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toys when she accidentally knocked over her brother's tower of blocks. Her brother started crying and Lily felt guilty for what she had done. 

To make things better, Lily decided to help her brother rebuild the tower of blocks. They worked together and soon the tower was even bigger and better than before. Lily's brother stopped crying and gave her a big hug, making Lily feel happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing hide and seek when they saw a hot air balloon in the sky. Lily was so excited, she ran to her mom and asked if they could go for a ride.

Her mom said yes, and they went to the park where the hot air balloon was landing. The pilot was very gentle and helped them get in the basket. Lily was so happy, she signed to her mom that she loved it.

They flew up high in the sky and saw all the trees and houses below. Lily felt like a bird soaring through the air. When they landed, Lily thanked the pilot and said it was the best day ever. From that day on, Lily loved hot air balloons and always signed to her mom when she saw one in the sky.

One day, a nice man went to the airport. He wanted to fly in a big plane. He was very happy and excited to go on his trip.

At the airport, the nice man saw many people. They were all going to different places. He saw a big plane and said, "Wow! That's a big plane!" He paused and looked at it with a big smile.

Then, the nice man got on the plane. The plane went up, up, up in the sky. He looked out the window and saw the clouds. He was so happy to be flying. When the plane landed, he said, "That was fun! I want to do it again!"

Once there was an old man who wanted to have some fun. So he went to the park and brought his old kite. He started to pull it and the kite flew very high. Suddenly, a jolly ghost appeared.

The old man was scared but the ghost said, "Don't be afraid. If you give me a hug, I will help you fly your kite."

The old man thought for a moment and then he said, "Yes! I will give you a hug." With the ghost's help, the man's kite flew even higher.

The old man laughed and said, "Thank you, jolly ghost."

The ghost replied, "My pleasure! Anytime you want to fly your kite, just pull me for help!"

And ever since then, every time the old man pulled his kite, the jolly ghost was always there to help him fly it high.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to go outside and play. She stepped outside and saw a big field full of sheep. She was so excited! She started to point at each sheep, counting them one by one.

"One, two, three, four!" she exclaimed. "Look how many sheep there are!"

Suddenly, one of the sheep bleated and ran over to the girl. She was so surprised! The sheep was very soft and cuddly. She wrapped her arms around it, giving it a big hug.

"Oh, hello sheep," she said. "I'm so glad you're here."

The sheep happily bleated and the little girl smiled. She decided to spend the whole afternoon playing with her new friend. They ran around and laughed together in the sunshine until it was time for the little girl to go inside.

As she waved goodbye, she shouted out "Bye bye sheep!" The sheep bleated one final time in response. The little girl couldn't stop smiling, knowing that her day outside had been so much fun.

Alice was walking in the park on a foggy day. She looked up and the sky was like a white blanket, with the fog covering everything around her. She kept walking, and all of a sudden, she realized that in the fog were harmless creatures. Tiny, white, and fluffy creatures, were flying around in the fog.

Alice was excited to see these creatures, so she stayed and watched them for a while. She wasn't scared, because she knew they were harmless. But then, all of a sudden, the fog cleared away and the creatures were gone!

Alice was sad that she couldn't see the creatures anymore, but she realized that the fog was just a magical moment and it had to end eventually. She continued walking in the park, smiling to herself, thinking fondly of the magical creatures in the fog.

Once upon a time, in a big lake, there was a playful alligator named Ally. Ally loved to swim and play with her friends, the fish and the frogs. They would splash in the water and have a lot of fun together every day.

One day, Ally found a big box with a lock on it. She was very curious and wanted to open it. She asked her friends for help. The fish and the frogs tried their best, but they could not open the lock.

Ally felt sad and thought she would never know what was inside the box. Just then, a wise old turtle came by and saw Ally looking sad. The wise old turtle told Ally, "Sometimes, it's better to leave things locked away. Not everything we find is meant for us." Ally listened to the wise old turtle and decided to leave the box alone.

From that day on, Ally and her friends continued to have fun and play together in the lake, without worrying about the locked box. And they all learned that sometimes, it's better to leave things be and enjoy what they already have.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bob. Bob loved the spring. The sun was bright, the grass was green, and the flowers were pretty. Bob liked to hop and play with his friends in the peaceful meadow.

One day, Bob hopped too high and fell into a puddle. All his friends saw him and laughed. Bob felt embarrass. His fur was wet and muddy. Bob wanted to find a way to clean up and feel better.

Bob hopped to the river and jumped in. The water was cool and clean. He washed off the mud and felt happy again. Bob hopped back to his friends, and they played together in the peaceful spring meadow. And they all lived happily ever after.

Dave was in a gloomy mood. He looked around his kitchen and saw the freezer. It was old and dull. He knew that he had to do something to make it look new again. 

Dave went to the store and collected all the things he needed: a cloth to wipe the freezer, some polish and a big smile. He was now ready to get to work.

Dave spread the polish over the freezer and wiped it with the cloth. He rubbed and polished until the freezer was shiny and bright.

Once his hard work was done, Dave stepped back and admired his freezer. He was pleased with his work and grinned from ear to ear. He sighed with contentment. 

The gloomy freezer was now gleaming and looking brand new. Dave had done a fantastic job!

Once upon a time, there was a clever duck named Ducky. Ducky liked to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, Ducky was playing with her friend, Bunny. Bunny said, "I am going to hide behind this tree. You will never find me!" Ducky replied, "I am very clever. I will find you!" 

Ducky looked and looked, but she could not find Bunny. Suddenly, Bunny disappeared! Ducky searched everywhere, but Bunny was nowhere to be found. Ducky was very sad and started to cry. 

Just when Ducky thought Bunny was gone forever, Bunny jumped out from behind the tree and yelled, "Surprise!" Ducky was so happy to see Bunny and they hugged each other. Bunny said, "I knew you would find me, clever Ducky!" From that day on, Ducky and Bunny always played together and had lots of fun.

One day, a small dog named Snap wanted to win a race. Snap was a very fast dog and he thought he could be successful. He was so excited to run and play with his friends.

The race began and all the dogs were running fast. Snap ran as fast as he could. He saw his friends running too. Snap wanted to win so much that he did not stop to rest. He kept running and running.

In the end, Snap was the first to cross the finish line. He was so happy to win the race. All his friends cheered for him. Snap felt successful and proud. Now, he knew that he could do anything if he tried his best.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who wanted more friends. So the fish decided to come and explore the big wide ocean. On the way, the fish found the sea was filled with so many strange new creatures. 

The fish became a bit scared, so to make sure he was safe, the fish swam very fast. He swam amongst whales and sharks, as far as he could see, but wherever he went, the fish couldn't find anyone like himself. 

Suddenly, the fish heard a voice calling out to him. It was a sea turtle! The fish was so happy and went over to say hello. The turtle showed the fish many things, including her favourite swimming spots. 

Over the next few days, the turtle and the fish spent time together. They became the best of friends, despite the difficult times they faced. They explored the depths of the ocean and the mysteries it held. 

Eventually the fish had to return home, but the sea turtle promised that the fish would always be welcome if ever he wanted to come back. And the fish found himself surrounded by many new friends!

Tim likes to jog with his dad. They jog in the park and see many things. They see birds, flowers, dogs and people. Tim likes to say hello to everyone. He is a compassionate boy.

One day, they jog near a big drain. The drain has a metal cover with holes. Tim is curious and looks inside. He sees water and mud. He wants to touch it, but his dad says no. He says the drain is dirty and dangerous.

Tim listens to his dad, but he sees something shiny in the drain. It is a coin. He thinks it is a treasure. He reaches for it, but his dad stops him. He says the coin is not worth it. He says he has a better treasure for him.

He takes out a small box from his pocket and gives it to Tim. Tim opens it and sees a compass. It is a gift from his dad. He says the compass can help him find his way. He says he loves him very much.

Tim hugs his dad and says thank you. He is very happy. He puts the compass in his pocket and holds his dad's hand. They jog away from the drain and continue their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to walk around his town and explore new things. One day, he saw a big factory that he had never seen before. He was so curious that he decided to walk inside.

Timmy walked and walked through the factory, but he got very tired. He wanted to rest, but he couldn't find a place to sit. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and the factory started to shake. Timmy was scared and he tried to run out, but it was too late. The factory exploded and Timmy was hurt.

Timmy's parents were very sad when they heard the news. They wished that Timmy had never walked into the factory. From that day on, they made sure to always keep an eye on their little boy.

Once upon a time there was a hunter. He walked through a peaceful forest, looking for something. He came to a pond and looked around. Suddenly, he heard a voice! It was a frog.

The hunter said, "Hello, little frog. What are you doing out here?"
The frog replied, "I'm looking for something too! I'm looking for my friend."

The hunter asked, "Will you let me help you find your friend?" The frog smiled and said "Yes!"

So the hunter and the frog began to follow a trail around the pond. They looked everywhere, but they couldn't find the frog's friend. Just then, they heard a loud croak! It was the frog's friend!

The hunter and the frog were so happy to find the missing frog. They all hugged each other and then went off together, enjoying the peaceful forest.

Once upon a time, there was a shy mixer. He was very lonely and wanted a friend to play with. But every time he saw someone, he got too shy and hid behind a tree.

One day, the sun started to shine hotter and hotter. He wanted to cool down, so he searched for water. After a while, he found a big pool of water. 

He jumped in and splashed around. It felt good and he suddenly wasn't so shy anymore. Then he noticed something strange in the pool. It was a big mixer, just like him. 

The two mixers were so happy that they could finally meet. They laughed and joked together. But then the sun started melting the ice cubes around them and the pool started to get smaller. 

The two scared mixers quickly got out of the pool and hugged, vowing to always be friends. From that day on they stayed together and were never shy again.

Once upon a time, there was a frightened little animal called Jim. Jim was very small and liked to hide away from people who might hurt him.

One day, Jim was walking around in the forest when he saw a big cane. He thought the cane looked very dangerous and began to get very frightened. He wanted to run away and hide, but the cane was too close.

Suddenly, the cane started to move and Jim realised it was a snake. The snake was moving closer and closer and Jim was petrified. He was so frightened that he couldn't move. 

Just as the snake was about to bite him, he closed his eyes and thought of his family. He realised that if something happened to him, they would all be very worried. Suddenly, he found the courage to turn around, face the snake and scare it away.

Jim learnt an important lesson that day: no matter how small or frightened you are, you can find the courage to stand up for yourself and protect your family.

Henry was a gray mouse who lived in a big house. He was very happy and always smiled. One day, he went outside and saw a big cat. The cat looked very mean and silly. 

Henry said to the cat, "Hi! What are you doing?"
The cat didn't reply. He just stared at Henry.

Henry said, "Do you want to eat something?"
The cat just stared. 

Henry said, "I'm going to eat some cheese now, do you want some?" 
The cat just looked stupid and said nothing.

Henry realized the cat didn't want to talk, so he went back into his house and ate some cheese. Henry had a great time enjoying his cheese!

Bunny and Squirrel were best friends. They liked to play in the forest and find nuts and carrots. One day, they saw a big pile of nuts near a tree. They ran to the pile and started to eat.

"Yum, these nuts are so good!" said Bunny.

"Let's take some to our homes!" said Squirrel.

They filled their cheeks with nuts and ran to their holes. But they did not see that the pile of nuts belonged to Bear. Bear was sleeping under the tree. He woke up and saw his nuts were gone.

"Who took my nuts?" he roared. He followed the trail of nuts to Bunny's hole. He saw Bunny hiding inside.

"Bunny, did you take my nuts?" he asked.

Bunny felt guilty. He knew he did a bad thing. He nodded his head.

"I'm sorry, Bear. I was hungry and I did not know they were yours," he said.

Bear was angry. He wanted his nuts back. He reached into the hole and tried to grab Bunny. But the hole was too small for his paw. He got stuck.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cried.

Squirrel heard Bear's cry. He ran to Bunny's hole. He saw Bear's paw in the hole. He saw Bunny's scared face.

"Bunny, are you okay?" he asked.

"No, Squirrel. Bear is mad at me. He wants his nuts back. But I ate them all," said Bunny.

Squirrel felt sorry for Bunny. He also felt guilty. He knew he did a bad thing too. He had some nuts in his hole. He decided to share them with Bear.

"Squirrel, what are you doing?" asked Bunny.

"I'm going to give some of my nuts to Bear. Maybe he will forgive us and let us go," said Squirrel.

He ran to his hole and brought some nuts. He gave them to Bear.

"Here, Bear. These are some of the nuts we took. We are sorry. Please let us go," he said.

Bear looked at the nuts. He looked at Squirrel. He looked at Bunny. He saw they were sorry. He felt a little better.

"Thank you, Squirrel. That was very nice of you. I forgive you and Bunny. But don't take my nuts again. They are mine," he said.

He pulled his paw out of the hole. He took his nuts and walked away.

Bunny and Squirrel came out of the hole. They hugged each other.

"Thank you, Squirrel. You are a good friend," said Bunny.

"Thank you, Bunny. You are a good friend too," said Squirrel.

They learned their lesson. They never took nuts that were not theirs again. They played in the forest and found nuts and carrots that were free. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He was very heavy and had a long trunk. One day, he was walking in the jungle when he saw a small mouse. The mouse was very scared and asked the elephant for help. 

The mouse told the elephant that he needed to cut some cheese, but his knife was broken. The elephant felt sorry for the mouse and decided to help him. He used his strong trunk to cut the cheese into small pieces. 

The mouse was very happy and thanked the elephant. He said that he would never forget the kind elephant who helped him in his time of need. From that day on, the elephant and the mouse became good friends and they would often play together in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who loved to play in the park.
One day, they both had a big idea: to build a see-saw. They started collecting materials from the park like logs and sticks and collected some stones to weigh it down.

Once they had finished, the two friends climbed up on the ends of the see-saw. They began to laugh as they went up and down. 

An old man then walked by and saw the two playing. He smiled, and said to them, "That is a very humble idea you both have. It's very impressive." 
The two friends thanked the old man and returned to playing on their see-saw. 

The two friends had a wonderful time playing together. It was a memory they would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was frightened of going to school because she didn't want to leave her mommy. One day, her mommy found a tutor who could help her with her schoolwork. Lily was hesitant at first, but the tutor was very kind and made her feel comfortable.

During their first lesson, the tutor asked Lily what her favorite thing to do was. Lily said she enjoyed playing with her dolls. The tutor smiled and said, "That's great! You can learn while having fun." Lily was happy to hear that.

After a few lessons, Lily started to feel more confident and less frightened about going to school. She even started to look forward to her lessons with the tutor. One day, her mommy asked her how school was going and Lily replied, "It's great! I have a tutor who makes learning fun and I enjoy it." Her mommy was proud of her.

The moral of the story is that learning can be fun and it's okay to ask for help when we need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was finding things to do and she touched everything in sight.

Suddenly, she noticed a spider. She was so excited that she touched it. The spider scooted away from her and hid in the corner.

The little girl was embarrassed. Even though she had meant no harm to the spider, she thought it must have not liked her touching. She felt bad and wished she could do something to help.

She got an idea. She said a kind word to the spider and told it that it was safe. The spider slowly came out of hiding and soon the two were friends. She learned that sometimes kindness was the best way to make someone feel better!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Dan and Tilly. They were walking in a forest and they found a bush full of ripe berries. Dan was ready to give Tilly some of the juicy berries.

Tilly said thank you to Dan and ate one of the sweet berry. She said yummy with a big smile. 

Dan went to pick more of the delicious berries. He was careful to pick only the ready berries that looked good. He gave some of the berries to Tilly, who said thank you over and over. 

They both enjoyed the berries and had a wonderful time in the forest. They were glad to have so many ready berries they could share.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Annie. Annie had a special pole that she loved and she always played with it in her backyard. One day, Annie wanted to show her pole to her friends. She ran to their yards and waved the pole in the air. Her friends laughed and clapped their hands. 

Annie was so proud that she kneeled down on the ground and hugged her pole. But when she stood up, the pole had cracked and the tip was broken. Annie felt very ashamed. She ran and hid behind a bush. 

Her friends found her and asked, "What's wrong, Annie?" 

Annie replied, "My pole is broken. I'm so ashamed." 

One of her friends said, "Don't be sad. We'll help you fix it." 

All of her friends knelt down around her and together they put the pole back together.

The next day, Annie was playing with her pole again and she was so happy. She knew she had great friends who always there to help.

Once there was a poor cabin. Inside the cabin was a family. The family had a little boy. His name was Matt.

Matt wanted to study and all day he played and learned. He read books and did puzzles. He even wrote a few words.

Matt's parents were so proud of him. They said he was such a smart boy.

Every day, Matt would wake up early and go to his cabin to study. He worked hard and soon he was the smartest boy in the class.

Finally, Matt had studied enough and was so proud of himself. He was no longer poor and had become a smart boy. He would always remember his time in the cabin studying and be thankful that his hard work paid off.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. They saw a big flame in the sky. Lily asked her mom, "What is that?" Her mom said, "It's a hot air balloon. It's different from an airplane."

Lily was curious and wanted to see the hot air balloon up close. They walked closer and saw a man getting ready to fly it. The man saw Lily and said, "Hello! Would you like to come with me on my hot air balloon ride?" Lily was excited and said, "Yes, please!"

They got on the hot air balloon and flew up in the sky. It was so much fun! After they landed, the man said, "I'm hungry. Let's eat some sandwiches." Lily and her mom ate sandwiches with the man and talked about their adventure. They had a great time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a box of delicate shapes. She loved to play with them. The shapes were all different colors and sizes.

One day, Lily decided to match the shapes. She put the red circle with the red square, and the blue triangle with the blue star. She had so much fun matching them!

In the end, Lily had matched all of her delicate shapes. She was very happy. She put them back in the box and went to tell her mom about her fun game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and liked to ask lots of questions. One day, her mommy gave her a calendar to wear on her wrist like a bracelet. Lily thought it was funny to wear a calendar, but she liked it.

Lily wore the calendar everywhere she went. She even showed it to her friends at school. But one day, she lost the calendar. She looked everywhere for it, but it was gone. Lily was sad and cried a lot. She wished she had never lost the calendar.

From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful with her things. She never wore a calendar again, but she always remembered the one she lost.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big lion in a cage. The lion looked sad and bored.

"Hello, lion," said Lily. "Why are you in the cage?"

The lion roared softly. "I was caught by bad men who wanted to show me to people. They forget to feed me and give me water. They forget to let me run and play. They forget that I am a lion, not a toy."

"That is not fair," said Ben. "You should be free and happy. Can we help you?"

The lion nodded. "You can help me by finding the key to the cage. It is hidden under a rock near the fence. But be careful, the bad men might come back soon."

Lily and Ben looked around and saw a rock that looked different from the others. They ran to it and lifted it up. There was a shiny key under it.

"Quick, let's open the cage," said Lily.

They ran back to the lion and put the key in the lock. The cage door opened and the lion jumped out. He licked Lily and Ben and thanked them.

"Thank you, friends. You are very kind and brave. You did not forget me. You did not forget that I am a lion, not a toy. You helped me to be free and happy."

The lion ran to the fence and jumped over it. He ran to the woods where he could find his family and friends. He roared happily and waved goodbye to Lily and Ben.

Lily and Ben smiled and waved back. They were happy that they helped the lion. They learned that they should not forget to be nice and helpful to others. They learned that they should not forget that animals have feelings and needs too. They learned that they should not forget to respect and love nature.

John looked out of the window. He felt so hot inside. He didn't like spring. He HATED it! The air outside was so uncomfortable. He felt like he was melting!

John's mom looked at him sympathetically. She pointed outside. She was trying to show him something, but he couldn't see anything. He squinted harder and saw a few flowers in the garden.

John became excited and ran outside. He looked closely at the flowers. Suddenly, he felt the harsh wind on his skin. He didn't like it! The wind was too cold and it made him feel like he was freezing. He quickly ran back inside.

John looked out of the window again. He HATED spring. It was too hot, too cold and so uncomfortable. He wished it was summer soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna who had a very special memory. Every day, she would go to a secret garden and count the petals of the flowers, write stories, and listen to the birds sing. 

One day, she went to her garden like usual and she noticed a broken bird perched on a bush. Anna wanted to help the bird, but she didn't know how. 

She heard a gentle voice say, "Hey Anna, why don't you choose one of two things? You can either give the bird some food, or you can give it your memory." 

Anna thought for a moment and chose to share her memory with the broken bird. The bird seemed to sense it, and it flew away with a newfound strength. 

Anna was sad for a moment, but then she realized that her memory was a gift for the bird that needed it most! Her special memory was now a part of the bird's journey.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy was very hungry. He wanted to eat at a restaurant with his mommy. They went to a fancy place with tables and chairs. Timmy was anxious because he had never been to a restaurant before.

The waiter came and asked them what they wanted to eat. Timmy said he wanted a burger and fries. His mommy ordered a salad. When the food came, Timmy regretted his choice. He wished he had ordered what his mommy did because it looked so yummy.

Mommy saw Timmy's sad face and asked him what was wrong. Timmy said he wished he had ordered the salad like mommy. Mommy said it was okay and they could share. Timmy felt happy again and they enjoyed their meal together.

Once upon a time there was a loyal bear named Ben. Ben loved to sing and he sang all of the time. Every day he would help make meals for his family. He would help his mom stir the pot and he always remembered to stir it for a long time so the meal would be extra tasty.

Then one day his mom said he could pick any song he wanted to sing. Ben was so excited! He thought and thought about what song he would pick, but he couldn't decide. So, he just sang all his favorite songs. He sang so loudly that everyone in the house could hear him.

When he was finished singing, his mom said he did a wonderful job. She said she was so proud of how loyal he was to his family. Ben smiled and said that he had lots of love for his family. Then he went off to bed, dreaming of all the songs he wanted to sing.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe. He was very worried because he did not have peace. He was always feeling sad, scared and angry. One day Joe decided he would try to build his own peace. 

He started by collecting all the things that made him feel calm, like cuddly toys, books and art supplies. He spread them out on the floor and arranged them so he could reach them easily. 

Next, Joe tried to look for things that made him happy. He drew pictures of the people he loved, wrote stories, and sang songs. Joe slowly began to feel better and more peaceful.

Finally, Joe built up a pile of happy memories and lovely things. His pile of peace made him feel safe and happy.  Joe smiled and knew that he could now have peace every single day.

One day, Jack and his Mama went to the park. Jack loved playing with the other kids and running around. But, after a long day of playing and running, Jack was very tired. His Mama told him it was time for a nap. However, Jack didn't want to take a nap. He wanted to keep playing with the other kids.

But, Jack's Mama was very fair. She said he could play for five more minutes and then he had to take a nap. Jack was so excited and continued to run around and play.

Five minutes went by quickly and soon it was time for Jack to take a nap. But, Jack didn't want to take a nap; he wanted to keep playing. So, Jack resisted and tried to stay up.

But, Jack's Mama was very persistent. She kept telling Jack it was time for a nap and he had to listen to her. Finally, Jack gave in and took a nap. He felt much better after his nap and was ready to play with the other kids.

The sun was shining bright and the birds were singing. It was a peaceful day.

Mummy was in the kitchen stirring a bowl of batter. Tommy, the three year old, was curious and asked Mummy what she was doing.

"I'm baking a cake," Mummy replied.

"Can I help?" Tommy asked.

"Yes, you can!" said Mummy, reaching for a brush. "Can you use this brush to spread this icing on the cake?"

Tommy nodded his head and grabbed the brush. He carefully spread the icing on the cake. When he was finished, the cake looked beautiful!

"You did a great job, Tommy!" Mummy said proudly.

Tommy smiled, happy with the peaceful moment spent with his Mummy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very lazy and he didn't like to do anything. One day, his mommy made spaghetti for dinner. Timmy loved spaghetti but he didn't want to unpack the plates. 

His mommy said, "Timmy, please unpack the plates so we can eat the spaghetti." Timmy sighed and said, "Okay, mommy." He unpacked the plates and his mommy served the spaghetti. It was so delicious! 

After dinner, Timmy felt happy that he unpacked the plates. He realized that sometimes it's important to help out and not be lazy. From that day on, Timmy tried to be more helpful around the house. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Harry. He thought he was different from all the other children as he had a special power like no one else did. He could make things appear and disappear.

One day his parents took him to the underground station to show him something very special. On the wall of the underground station there was a beautiful display of different animals and objects. It was a very special sight. 

Harry was amazed at what he saw and wanted to show everyone the same display. So he decided to make it appear everywhere. He used his special power to make the display appear in every part of town. 

Soon people started talking about the display and some even said it wasn't normal. But Harry knew it was special, and that it brought delight to everyone who saw it.
 
So Harry's parents told him that it was okay to be different. That the display he created was not only unique but brought a lot of joy to people. They told him that it was a good thing to show his special power to bring something different and special in the world.

The moral of the story is that it is okay to be different, even if something is not considered "normal". Being different can bring something extra special and extraordinary to the world.

Once upon a time, there was a big fat body. It was so big and fat that it couldn't fit through the door! But this body was happy, because it loved to splash in the water.

One sunny day, it decided to go to the beach. It had a big smile on its face as it waddled over to the sea. When it got to the water, it dipped its toes in and felt the coolness of the water.

"Hurray!", the body yelled and splashed in the waves. It jumped up and down and laughed and shouted. After a while, it looked up and saw a little girl about three years old. The little girl was standing right next to the body and had a big, wide grin on her face.

"Are you having fun?", the little girl asked the body. The body smiled and said, "Yes, I am having so much fun! Do you want to splash with me?" 

The little girl nodded happily and started to splash in the water. Both of them splashed and laughed and had a great time. When the sun went down, the little girl and the body said goodbye and went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time there was an oyster who lived in the ocean near a small beach. The oyster was so excited because he could finally be around all the other animals of the sea. Every day he would greet them with a cheerful hello and the other animals were happy that he was so friendly.

One day, two children came to the beach. They both brought buckets and began to explore. The oyster watched curious what they were doing and then he saw one of the children pick up a large found shell on the shore.

The child exclaimed, "Mom, look what I found! It's called an oyster!"

The mom said, "That's wonderful, but you must remember to behave well around the oysters. Oysters are special and need to be treated with kindness and respect."

The child agreed and the mom put the oyster gently back into the ocean. The child waved good-bye and the oyster was happy that he was still available to live in his home. 

He smiled and said, "Thank you for respecting me. I feel very lucky to have a home here." 

The other animals watched in admiration, proud that the oyster had been well taken care of. They all began to sing a song of appreciation for the available oyster. 

And that's the story of the oyster and the children who were so gentle and kind.

Suzie was very persistent. She wanted to fix her mummy's coffee. She gathered all the things she needed, and started to work. She worked and worked, but she could not make the coffee right. She tried again and again, but no matter how hard she tried, the coffee was always bad. Finally, she gave up, and started to cry. Her mummy was very sad, but she hugged Suzie and said, "It's ok. Mummy still loves you." They both knew that this time, Suzie wouldn't be able to fix the coffee.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Daisy. Daisy lived in an old valley. It was dark, and very quiet.

One day, Daisy thought she would take a walk in the valley. She walked and walked until she got to the top of a hill. The view was beautiful and Daisy felt so proud.

But then something happened. Suddenly, Daisy felt embarrassed. She had forgotten all about the monster who lived in the valley. Daisy knew that the monster got angry when people visited the valley, and she was scared.

As Daisy was about to turn around and run back home, the sun came out and shone on the valley. It made the valley bright instead of dark. Daisy smiled and felt brave.

The monster was nowhere to be seen. Daisy had been brave and the darkness had gone away. She smiled and ran back home, happy that she had seen the beautiful view of the valley.

Once there was a lively little girl who loved to play. She liked to go outside and explore in the sunshine.

One day when she stepped outside she saw a beautiful flower. She wanted to get a closer look so she knelt down beside it.

Just then, a big gust of wind came and blew it away! The little girl chased after it, but the flower was too fast.

Suddenly, she felt something soft lightly touch her arm. She looked up and found a puppy with a big smile on its face. The puppy had brought her the flower!

The little girl was so pleased. She gave it a big hug and thanked the puppy with a cuddle. From then on they were the best of friends.

One day, Jack and his mom went to a store. It was full of interesting things, but what caught Jack's eye was a shiny machine. It was so attractive! He asked Mom if they could pay for it. Mom said yes, and she put money into the machine. Suddenly, the machine made a noise and Jack was so excited. He got a toy out of the machine and went to show his mom. She smiled and said, "Well done, Jack. Now let's go home." 

Jack was so pleased. He had paid for the machine and got something fun in return. He hugged Mom and was very happy with his toy. Jack couldn't wait to go back to the store and pay for the machine again.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the park near their homes. One day, they saw a big drain in the grass. It had a metal cover with holes in it.

"Wow, look at that!" Tim said. "I wonder what is inside."

"Maybe there are bugs or rats or treasure," Sam said. "Let's open it and see."

They tried to lift the cover, but it was too heavy. They pulled and pushed, but it did not move.

"Maybe we need something to help us," Tim said. He looked around and saw a stick. He picked it up and put it in one of the holes. He twisted and turned, but the cover did not budge.

"This is hard," he said. "Maybe we should give up."

"No, we can do it," Sam said. "I have an idea. You hold the stick and I will jump on it. Maybe that will make the cover pop off."

Tim thought that was a foolish idea. He was afraid that Sam would get hurt or fall into the drain. But he did not want to lose his friend. He nodded and held the stick.

Sam ran and jumped on the stick. There was a loud clang. The cover flew off and Sam flew with it. He landed on the grass, but the cover landed on the drain. Tim heard a splash.

"Sam, are you okay?" Tim asked.

Sam got up and rubbed his head. He looked at the drain. He saw water and mud and nothing else.

"I'm okay," he said. "But that was not fun. There is nothing in there. Just water and mud."

Tim was glad that Sam was not hurt. He helped him up and they walked away from the drain.

"Maybe we should not play with drains anymore," Tim said.

"Maybe you are right," Sam said. "They are not very interesting. And they are dangerous."

They decided to play with their ball instead. They admired how high they could throw it and catch it. They had more fun with their ball than with the drain. They learned their lesson.

Once there was a girl named Amy. She was very cute and adorable. Every day when she woke up, she went to work. Work was very fun for Amy, because she got to make different things.

One day, she made some strips of paper. She drew and colored on them, and they were very beautiful. Amy was so proud of what she had made!

Then she made something really fun with the strips she had. She put them together to make a pattern. It was really pretty, and Amy felt so happy.

Every day after that, Amy went back to work and made more strips. She made more beautiful patterns and showed them to her family. Everyone said how cute and adorable they were.

Amy was so proud that her work was so admired. From then on, she kept making more and more patterns with the strips she had made.

Once upon a time, there was a generous family. They had a tall tree in their garden and they loved the windy days that blew around it. One day, the wind was especially strong and it made the branches of the tree turn in all kinds of directions. The family watched in delight, feeling as though the wind was giving them a big hug!

The family embraced the windy days and every time the wind blew, their tree would turn and wave at them. They felt so happy, their hearts filled with joy. The generous family thanked the wind for its beautiful gift and the wind seemed to smile back.

The family enjoyed their windy days so much that they moved the tree to the front of the house so they could see it turn even more. What a generous family! They were always grateful for the gifts the wind gave them!

Once there was a naughty girl named Rose. She never stopped giggling and running around the house. Every day the family would go for a stroll in the park, but Rose would always be in a naughty mood.

One day, something special arrived. It was an invitation for Rose's parents to a marriage. Rose was very excited and asked her parents what a marriage was. They told her that it was a special event where two people decided to live together in love.

The day of the marriage arrived, and Rose got ready to join her parents. They all dressed up nicely and everyone at the marriage was so happy. Rose couldn't stop laughing and clapping with joy. 

At the end of the day, Rose hugged her parents and told them this was the best day ever. She was so happy at the marriage, and promised that she would always be a good girl.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy's mom told him to put on his pants because it was hot outside. Timmy didn't like to wear pants because they made him feel hot, but he put them on anyway.

As Timmy was playing outside, he saw a bird flying in the sky. "Look, Mommy! The bird is rising up high!" he said excitedly. "Yes, Timmy, birds can fly high in the sky," his mom replied.

Later that day, Timmy's friend came over to play. "Why are you wearing pants? It's so hot outside!" his friend exclaimed. "I know, but my mom told me to wear them," Timmy replied. "Let's go play in the sprinkler to cool off!" his friend suggested. Timmy agreed, and they ran through the water, laughing and having fun.

John was feeling very lonely. He wanted to make some friends, but he did not know how. One day, he had a plan. He decided to take one small step at a time.

First, he said hello to everyone he saw. He started with his neighbours, then moved on to other people in his street. He said hello in his very nicest voice.

Next, John decided to join a playground. He made sure to stay even close to other children, so they could all have fun together. He offered to share his toys, and even help them with their games.

Finally, John invited some of the other children over to his house for a playdate. He had fun playing together, and the other children stayed for the whole day. He was very happy and no longer felt lonely.

John's plan worked. He had taken small steps and it made him feel much better. He was no longer lonely and had lots of new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. The boat had a big anchor to help it stay in one place. One day, the boat went out to sea with some friends. But when they got far from the shore, the sky turned dark and the waves got big. The boat was moving a lot and the friends were scared.

One friend said, "I wish we had something to help us stay safe." Another friend said, "I can supply a clear plan! We can use the anchor to keep us in one place until the storm stops." The other friends thought this was a good idea. They quickly got the anchor and threw it into the water. The anchor helped the boat stay in one place, and the friends were safe until the storm passed.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go for a walk. He walked very fast and as he walked he began to observe his surroundings.

He saw a dog chasing a bird. The dog barked and the bird flew away. The little boy watched the whole thing with amazement.

Then he saw a pond with fish swimming in it. He stopped at the edge of the pond to watch the fish.

Soon the little boy became thirsty. He asked his mother, "Mom, can I have some juice?" His mother smiled and gave him a cup of juice. He drank it quickly and said, "Yum, that was delicious!"

His mother replied, "Yes, it was yummy! Now let's go take a walk together." So they went off to observe more fascinating things in their neighborhood.

Once there was a little boy called Tommy. He wanted to find something he liked to eat. He looked in the kitchen and he found an onion. He was curious to taste it. So he picked it up and took a bite.

At first he thought it would taste funny, but it was actually very yummy. He liked it so much he wanted to try some more. He put the onion in his mouth and it tasted even better.

Tommy was so happy, he ate the whole onion! He kept saying how yummy it was. His mum came in and saw how he was enjoying the onion. She said it was a good idea and now they make onion meals all the time and it's Tommy's favourite food.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch the birds in her backyard. One day, she saw a little bird with a broken wing. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help him. She waited for a minute to see if the bird would fly away, but he didn't. So, she gently picked up the little bird and brought him inside. 

Lily knew she needed to take care of the little bird until his wing healed. She gave him some water and seeds to eat. Every day, she would watch the little bird and make sure he was okay. After a few weeks, the little bird's wing was all better. Lily was so happy to see the little bird fly away. She knew she had helped him and felt proud of herself for being kind.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a pencil on the floor. The pencil was very special. It was mighty and strong. Tim picked up the pencil and wanted to use it.

Tim had a problem. His shoe was untied. He needed to tie it, but he did not know how. He looked at the mighty pencil and thought it could help him. Tim held the pencil in his hand and tried to tie his shoe.

With the help of the mighty pencil, Tim learned to tie his shoe. He was so happy and proud. From that day on, Tim always kept the mighty pencil with him. It helped him with many things, and they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big and strong lion. He was very powerful and could run very fast. One day, the lion heard a ringing sound coming from a nearby tree. He went to investigate and found a little bird stuck in the branches. The bird had gotten its foot caught in the tree and was in pain.

The lion knew it was against the law to harm other animals, so he decided to help the bird. Using his powerful claws, he gently freed the bird's foot from the tree. The bird was very grateful and sang a beautiful song to thank the lion. From that day on, the lion and the bird became good friends and would often play together in the forest.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Abi. Abi loved exploring the world around her and especially loved to go outside in the garden and gaze at the sky.

One day, Abi decided to explore her bedroom. She noticed a big, soft sheet on her bed. She gently lifted it up and looked underneath. It was full of surprises!

One of the surprises was a giant soft teddy bear. Abi instantly fell in love with it and hugged it tightly. She then looked around the room, looking at the posters and pictures on the walls and gazing out of the window.

The next day, Abi went to bed and snuggled under the soft sheet. It was so comfy and cosy that Abi soon fell asleep. She dreamt of exploring the garden and gazing at the sky.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a bad bear who didn't like honey. He didn't keep it with him and he never wanted to eat it. One day, he found a beehive full of honey and decided to try it. He liked it so much that he kept eating it until it was all gone. He even kept some with him so he could eat it later.

The bad bear liked to go walking in the forest and sometimes he would forget to take his honey with him. That's when the bees would find him and follow him wherever he went. The bad bear was scared of the bees so he always kept some honey with him so he could feed them. The bees didn't like the bad bear but they kept coming back for more honey. 

The bad bear kept eating all the honey he could and the bees kept following him. Finally, the bad bear found a safe place to hide so he could keep eating all the honey he wanted. The bees were sad but they had to keep looking for more honey for themselves. Now the bad bear is happy, eating all the honey he can find and the bees are happy too.

Ben and Lily wanted to play in the garden. They saw some big jars on the table. The jars had labels on them. The labels said: "Do not touch. Dangerous."

"What are these?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe they are for Mom's plants," Lily said.

"Let's open them and see," Ben said. He reached for a jar.

"No, Ben, stop! The label says 'do not touch'. It is dangerous. It might hurt you," Lily said.

"But I want to see. Maybe it is something fun," Ben said. He did not listen to Lily. He opened the jar.

Suddenly, a loud noise came from the jar. Smoke and bubbles came out. Ben and Lily screamed. They ran away from the table.

Mom heard the noise and came to the garden. She saw the mess on the table. She saw Ben and Lily hiding behind a bush.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"Ben opened a jar. It made a big boom. It was scary," Lily said.

"Ben, why did you open the jar? Didn't you see the label? It was dangerous. I was preparing a science experiment for your big brother. You could have hurt yourself or Lily," Mom said.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was curious. I wanted to see what was inside," Ben said.

"Curiosity is good, but you have to be careful. You have to follow the rules. You have to respect the labels. They are there to protect you. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. I understand. I won't do it again," Ben said.

"Good. Now, let's clean up this mess. And then, we can do something fun and safe together. How about we make some cookies?" Mom said.

"Yay! Cookies!" Ben and Lily said.

They hugged Mom and went to the kitchen. They learned their lesson. They never touched the jars again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very eager. He urged his dad to go on a walk together to a nearby park. His dad said yes, he was thoughtful and could see his son's enthusiasm. 

When they arrived at the park, they both played happily on the swing, the seesaw and the slides. But after a while, the boy's stomach started to grumble. He urged his dad to go home for dinner. His dad, being thoughtful, agreed and promised a bigger adventure tomorrow. 

When they arrived at home, delicious smells filled the entire house. The boy sniffed the air and urged his dad, "Let's have dinner!" His dad laughed and promised a big surprise, later. 

They both sat down at the table, and the boy's eyes widened when he saw what his dad had prepared. It was his favorite food! He thanked his dad for being so thoughtful. 

"It's so good, Dad!" he said, with a mouthful of food. His dad smiled and replied, "Let's enjoy it while it's still hot!" 

And so they did. The boy was full and happy, and thanked his dad once again for the thoughtful dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a blue flea. This flea liked to hop from place to place and explore. One day, the flea hopped onto the back of a dog.

The dog didn't like this, so he tried to remove the flea. He scratched and shook, but no matter what, the flea would not move.

The dog tried harder and harder to remove the flea, but the little blue flea would not budge. Finally, the dog gave up and the flea hopped away.

So the little blue flea continued to enjoy its adventure. It hopped high and low, every day it explored something new. The dog was never able to remove the flea again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play. She was a very obedient and good-natured child. 

One night, she was playing in her room when she heard a sound. It was a squeaky sound and it seemed to be coming from near her favourite chair. 

The little girl went to investigate and found a small mouse perched on the seat. She decided to befriends the little creature and asked it what it was doing there. 

The mouse replied, "I am here because I like to rub my fur against the chair, it feels so nice and smooth!" 

The little girl smiled and helped the mouse to rub against the chair so it could get comfy. Later that evening, the little girl and the mouse snuggled up together in the chair and went to sleep. 

The next morning, the little girl awoke to find the mouse still asleep in the chair. This time, she could not help but notice, that the mouse had a very shiny coat! She smiled knowing that the act of rubbing against the chair had been a very clever one.

John and his mom were in the garden. John saw a pot and showed his mom. His mom was happy and said, "This is a nice pot. Let's put a flower in it."

John said, "Yes!" so they put the pot in the ground and put a flower in it. John was very happy and said, "It looks so pretty!"

John and his mom sat down to discuss what other things they could put in the pot to make it look even better. Then they heard a noise. It was John's dad and he was angry. John and his mom stopped talking and looked at John's dad.

John's dad was angry because he did not know that they were planning to put other things in the pot. He thought they should just leave it as it was.

So they discussed it and explained to John's dad why they wanted to make the pot look even better. Finally, John's dad understood and he was no longer angry. He said, "Okay, let's all work together on making the pot look even better." 

John and his mom were very happy and they all started to work on making the pot look even better.

Once Mary and her mum went on a picnic. Mary was so excited. She had packed a tasty lunch. They spread the blanket onto the grass, put the lunch in the middle and found the perfect spot to eat. 

Mary and her mum opened the lunch box. Inside were sandwiches, apples and a box of juice. Mary took a big bite of her sandwich, it was so tasty! She offered her mum some which she happily accepted. 

Soon Mary was really thirsty so she opened the box of juice and poured a glass for both her and her mum. They both drank the juice up in one go and felt refreshed. 

The picnic was coming to an end but not before they both had a game of running around. They laughed and laughed as they ran around in circles. Eventually, their laughter ended and their stomachs said it was time to go home.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They noticed a small, serious dog sitting by a tree. Tim wanted to pet the dog, so he walked up to it with his mom.

"Can I pet the dog, Mom?" Tim asked. His mom said, "Yes, but be gentle." Tim put out his finger and touched the dog's soft fur. The dog wagged its tail and seemed to like Tim.

Tim and the dog played together in the park all day. They ran, jumped, and laughed. When it was time to go home, Tim waved goodbye to the dog. He knew they would see each other again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a purple car. This car had four wheels. It was a very nice car.

One day, the purple car went for a ride. It went up and down hills, and around turns. The wheels went round and round. The car was very fast.

But then, the car hit a sharp rock. One of the wheels went flat. The purple car was sad. A nice man came and put on a new wheel. The purple car was happy again. It drove off into the sunset, with its wheels going round and round.

Once upon a time there were two best friends; Sally and Steve. Every day they would play together and have a lot of fun.

One day, they decided to go on an adventure. They turned around the corner and saw a big hill. They started walking up the hill and soon they came to a big door.

Sally was scared and asked Steve, "What is this place?" Steve told her, "Don't worry, let's just take a peek inside."

The door opened and they heard a sweet noise. It was a singing bird. They stepped in and to their surprise they saw a beautiful garden full of colourful flowers. They spent a few minutes admiring the garden and they heard the bird's song getting louder and louder. Suddenly, something amazing happened; the sky started to turn a gorgeous shade of pink.

The two friends were filled with wonder, and happy that they decided to take this adventure. They watched in awe as the sky slowly turned to a deep blue colour. As the sky turned dark, Sally and Steve stood hand in hand, feeling the sweet joy of friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a humble little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and play with his friends. One day, Benny saw a purple flower in the field and he wanted to pick it. But he couldn't reach it because it was too high.

Benny asked his friend, a wise old owl, "How can I get the purple flower?" The owl replied, "You must wait until the sun rises and the flower will rise with it." Benny didn't understand how the flower could rise with the sun, but he trusted his friend.

So, Benny waited patiently until the next morning when the sun rose. And just as the owl had said, the purple flower rose up towards the sky. Benny was so happy and grateful to his friend for the wise advice. From that day on, Benny knew that sometimes, things will rise up if you just wait patiently.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to ride her scooter. One day, she saw a big hill that looked like fun to ride down. But her mommy said it was too dangerous. Lily said "please mommy, can I ride down the hill?" Her mommy said no. 

Lily was sad, but she knew her mommy loved her and didn't want her to get hurt. So, she rode her scooter on the flat ground instead. She still had fun, and she was safe. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat steak because it was so tasty. One day, Timmy's mom cooked him a big juicy steak for dinner. Timmy was so happy and said, "Mommy, this steak is so yummy! Can we have it every day?"

His mom replied, "No, Timmy. We can't have steak every day. It's not good for our bodies."

Timmy didn't understand why he couldn't have steak every day, so his mom asked him to imagine eating only one thing every day. Timmy thought about it and said, "I don't want to eat the same thing every day. That would be boring!"

His mom smiled and said, "That's right, Timmy. Eating a variety of foods is important to keep our bodies healthy. So let's enjoy this tasty steak today, but remember to eat different foods every day." And Timmy learned that it's important to have a balanced diet.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They had a big bucket of water and some cups. They wanted to soak each other and have fun.

"Ready, set, go!" Lily shouted. She threw a cup of water at Ben. It hit his chest and made him wet.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Ben said. He threw a cup of water back at Lily. It hit her hair and made her drip.

They laughed and threw more water at each other. They were having a good time.

But then, they heard a terrible noise. It was thunder. The sky was dark and angry. It started to rain hard.

"Oh no, we have to go inside!" Lily said. She grabbed the bucket and ran to the house.

"Wait for me!" Ben said. He followed her, but he slipped on the wet grass. He fell down and hurt his knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cried. He was soaked and sad.

Lily heard him and came back. She helped him get up and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?" she asked.

"It's okay, Lily. It's just a scratch. Let's go inside and get dry." he said.

They went inside and their mom gave them towels and cookies. They were happy again. They decided to play with their toys until the rain stopped. They hoped the sun would come back soon.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin. He had a big task to do, but he was feeling very nervous. He had to pass something very important to another penguin.

The nervous penguin walked slowly and carefully. He wanted to make sure he did not trip or drop the item. He was almost at the other penguin when suddenly he heard a loud noise. He was so scared that he dropped the thing and it fell all the way down to the bottom of a deep hole!

The nervous penguin was so sad and he felt like he had failed his task. He sat down and started to cry, but then he had an idea. He waddled over to the edge of the hole and stretched his neck as far as he could. He was able to reach the thing, and he carefully passed it up to the other penguin.

The other penguin was so pleased. He thanked the nervous penguin and they both hugged. Everything was alright in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little town. In this town, there was a big library. Many kids loved to go there and read books.

One day, a girl named Lily went to the library. She picked a book about a cat. Lily sat down and read the book. She liked the cat in the story.

Lily had an idea. She wanted to send a letter to the cat. So, she wrote a letter and put it in a box. She asked her mom to send the box to the cat. Lily was happy, and she knew the cat would be happy too.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very stubborn and wanted to explore everything. One day she decided to march away from home. She was wearing her favourite red dress, and carrying her favourite teddy bear.

Lucy marched for a long time and came across a hut. It was made from old wood and had a big door. She was curious and wanted to see what was inside. She tried to open the door, but it wouldn't budge.

Lucy got more and more stubborn and kept trying to open the door, until finally it opened a little bit. She peeked inside, but it was too dark for her to see.

So Lucy marched away, and went exploring in the woods. From then on she always passed by the old hut, but she never stopped to look inside again.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Sue. Sue liked to play with her toys and ask questions. One day, Sue found a small box in her room. It looked like a cell. She thought it was a new toy.

Sue asked her mom, "Mom, what is this cell?" Her mom said, "It's a special box to send a gift to your friend, Tim." Sue was happy. She wanted to send a gift to Tim. Sue put her toy car in the cell and closed it.

Sue's mom helped her send the cell to Tim. After some days, Tim got the cell. Tim was very happy to see the toy car. He called Sue and said, "Thank you for the gift!" Sue and Tim were very happy to share toys and be friends.

Tuesday was a sad day for Tommy as he dropped his favorite toy on the floor. As Tommy tried to pick it up, it sharped - he had cut himself! Tommy started to cry. His mom tried to comfort him, saying: "It's okay, Tommy! Let's go get a band-aid. That will make it all better." 

But no matter how much his mom tried to help, Tommy was still sad. On the way to the store, they passed by the pet shop and Tommy saw a puppy in the window. He was so excited. He asked his mom if they could get the puppy, but his mom said they had to keep going and get the band-aid first. Tommy was so disappointed. 

When Tommy and his mom arrived back home, Tommy quickly ran to the window to look for the puppy. But it was gone. Tommy was so sad and started to cry. His mom tried to console him and told him that the puppy had gone to find a new home. 

But the sad ending just made Tommy feel worse. He would never see the puppy ever again. He knew he couldn't get it back and he just wanted his favorite toy. He cried and cried until he fell asleep.

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big pile of pebbles near the river. They decided to make a game with them. They each took some pebbles and threw them into the water, trying to make the biggest splash.

"Look, I found a shiny pebble!" Lila said, holding up a smooth, black stone. "It looks like a star!"

"Let me see!" Tom said, reaching for the pebble. "Maybe it has magic!"

Lila did not want to share. She hid the pebble in her pocket and ran away. Tom was angry and chased her. They ran and ran, until they came to a dark forest.

"Stop, Lila!" Tom shouted. "Give me the pebble!"

"No, it's mine!" Lila shouted back. "Go away!"

They did not see the big bear that was sleeping behind a tree. The bear heard their noise and woke up. He was hungry and angry. He saw the two children and roared.

Lila and Tom were scared. They tried to run away, but the bear was faster. He caught them and ate them. The pebble fell out of Lila's pocket and rolled into the river. It was gone.
