The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and selfish. Share with your brother or sister. And do not disturb a sleeping bear.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a bright butterfly fluttering around in her garden. It was so pretty! Lily tried to catch it, but it was too fast for her. 

Later, she went inside and grabbed her crayons. She drew a picture of the butterfly with lots of bright colors. She even made a mark on the paper where the butterfly's wings had touched the flower. 

Lily was very happy with her picture and showed it to her mom. Her mom said it was beautiful and hung it up on the fridge. From that day on, Lily loved to draw pictures of all the pretty things she saw outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dolls all day long. One day, her mom asked her to help with some chores around the house. 

Lily was busy playing with her dolls and didn't want to help. But her mom said, "Lily, can you please help me? I need you to pick up your toys and put them away." 

Lily replied, "But mom, I'm busy playing with my dolls. Can't you do it?" 

Her mom said, "I can't do everything, Lily. I provide you with a home and toys to play with, but you need to help me too." 

Lily understood and picked up her toys. As she was putting them away, she noticed a cord on the floor. She picked it up and asked her mom what it was for. 

Her mom explained, "That's a cord for the vacuum cleaner. It helps us clean the floor." 

Lily was happy to help and even offered to help her mom with the vacuuming. From that day on, Lily learned that helping her mom was important and made her feel good too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved watching TV shows on her favorite network. One day, she turned on the TV, but the screen was dull and gray. She asked her mom why the TV wasn't showing any shows.

Her mom explained that sometimes the TV network goes offline and needs to be fixed. Lily didn't understand what "network" meant, so her mom showed her a picture of a spider web. She said that the spider web is like a network where all the little threads connect to make a bigger picture. 

Lily was amazed and asked if the TV network was like a spider web too. Her mom said yes and promised to fix the TV so they could watch their favorite shows together. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for showing me the network, Mommy!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to crawl. She would crawl around all day, exploring new places. But one day, she found something very special. She found a radish! It was a bright red colour and looked very crunchy. She grabbed the radish and instantly her hands got stuck! It was too tough for her to pull off.

The little girl was sad but then remembered she had a brilliant idea. She called out to her mom and asked if she had a knife. Mom quickly gave her a little knife and the girl carefully cut the radish off. It worked! She then happily ate the radish, crunching as she chewed it.

The little girl continued to crawl around and found more radishes. She would find them, cut them off with her knife and eat them each and every day. 

The end.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play outside in the sun. But today, the sky is dark and grey. They hear a loud boom. It is thunder.

"Let's go inside, Ben!" Mia says. "It will rain soon!"

But Ben likes rain. He wants to stay outside and feel the water on his skin. He shakes his head. "No, Mia. Rain is fun. I want to play in the rain."

Mia is scared of thunder. She runs to the door. She looks back at Ben. "Please, Ben. Come with me. Rain can hurt you. It can be fierce."

Ben does not listen. He stays on the grass. He laughs and jumps. He opens his mouth and catches the raindrops. He thinks rain is like a shower. He likes showers.

But then, the rain gets stronger. It falls faster and harder. It hurts Ben's eyes and ears. It makes him wet and cold. He does not laugh anymore. He cries.

"Mia, help me!" Ben shouts. "The rain is fierce. I want to go inside!"

Mia hears Ben. She runs to him. She hugs him. She takes his hand. She leads him to the door. She says, "It's okay, Ben. I'm here. We can go inside. We can have a warm shower. We can be dry and cozy."

Ben nods. He is sorry. He says, "Thank you, Mia. You are a good sister. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. I don't like fierce rain. I like sun and fun."

Mia smiles. She says, "You're welcome, Ben. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I was scared of thunder. I don't like loud noises. I like quiet and calm."

They go inside. They have a warm shower. They put on dry clothes. They cuddle on the couch. They watch a movie. They are happy. They love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who lived in a beautiful forest. There were rabbits, squirrels, and birds. They all played together and had fun.

One day, a mean wolf came to the forest. He wanted to take over and make all the animals pay him for protection. The animals didn't want to pay him because they knew he was mean and would hurt them.

The animals got together and made a plan to scare the wolf away. They all worked together and used their different skills to make loud noises and scary faces. The wolf got scared and ran away.

The animals were happy and continued to live in their beautiful forest without having to pay the mean wolf. They learned that working together can solve problems and keep them safe.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a white train that could make sounds and move on the tracks. They always shared the train and took turns to drive it.

One day, their mom gave them a banana each for a snack. Lily ate her banana quickly and threw the peel in the trash. Ben ate his banana slowly and enjoyed every bite. He left the peel on the floor and ran to play with the train.

Lily saw the peel and said, "Ben, you should put your peel in the trash. It is not good to leave it on the floor. Someone might slip and get hurt." But Ben did not listen. He said, "I will do it later. I want to play with the train now. It is my turn."

Lily was angry and said, "No, it is not your turn. You did not finish your snack. You have to delay your play until you clean up your mess." But Ben did not listen. He said, "No, I will not delay. I want to play now. You are mean." He grabbed the train and pushed Lily away.

Lily was sad and cried. She went to tell their mom what happened. Mom came and saw the peel on the floor. She said, "Ben, you were very naughty. You did not listen to your sister. You did not put your peel in the trash. You did not share the train. You made Lily cry. You have to say sorry to her and give her the train."

Ben felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "I am sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. I should have put my peel in the trash. I should have shared the train. You are a good sister. Can you forgive me?" Lily smiled and said, "I forgive you, Ben. You are a good brother. Can we play together?" Ben nodded and said, "Yes, we can play together. But first, let me put my peel in the trash."

They hugged and went to play with the train. They took turns and had fun. Mom was happy and said, "That's good. You learned your lesson. You should always be careful, respectful, and kind. That is how you get along with others."

The moral of the story is: You should not be selfish and careless. You should listen to others and clean up your mess. You should share and be nice. That is how you make friends and have fun.

Once there was a little boy called Johnny. Johnny loved aeroplanes, he watched them flying in the sky all the time.

One day Johnny went outside to play in his garden. It was cold, but he didn't mind. He ran around, chasing the butterflies and making mud pies. Suddenly he heard a loud noise. It was an aeroplane flying in the sky. Johnny looked up and waved.

The aeroplane flew away and soon it was dark. Johnny was feeling cold so he went inside his house. He gave a big shiver and he was so glad to be warm again. His dad lit the fireplace and soon it was very cosy.

Johnny lay down on the sofa, feeling warm and cosy. He waved goodbye to the aeroplane until it disappeared into the night. As he went to sleep, he started to feel happy and relaxed. He was happy he had seen an aeroplane that day.

Bella was three years old and excited to go to the park. She had been watching more birds and squirrels outside her window lately and wanted to see them in person. As she put on her shoes, her mom said to her, "Be sure to be calm at the park. Can you manage that?" Bella nodded and smiled.

At the park, Bella was amazed. The trees were tall and the sky a bright blue. She saw several ducks and birds around the pond. But what she was most excited about was all the oranges that were on the trees! She had never seen oranges on trees before. 

Bella plucked one off the tree, put it in her pocket, and ran to find her mom. Smiling, Bella gave her mom the orange. "Mommy, I managed to find an orange!"

Her mom smiled and laughed. She gave Bella a hug and said, "Yes you did! You did a great job - let's all calm down and enjoy these oranges." 

Bella, her mom, and their friends all sat down and ate the oranges, laughing and enjoying the sunny day. Bella spent the rest of the day running around and watching the birds, but she never forgot how she managed to find the orange.

Ben and Tom are friends. They like to play football in the park. One day, they find a big box near the trees. They open the box and see many things inside. There are books, toys, clothes, and a shiny football.

"Wow, look at this football!" Ben says. "It is new and red. Can we play with it?"

Tom nods. He likes the football too. He takes it out of the box and kicks it to Ben. Ben kicks it back to Tom. They have fun with the football.

But then, a man comes to the park. He looks angry. He sees the box and the football.

"Hey, you kids!" he shouts. "That is my box and my football! Give them back to me!"

Ben and Tom are scared. They do not know the man. They do not want to give back the football.

"But we found them here," Ben says. "They are not yours."

"They are mine!" the man says. "I left them here for a while. They are very useful to me. The football is a gift for my son. The books are for my work. The toys and clothes are for charity. Now, give them back or I will call the police!"

Ben and Tom do not want to make the man more angry. They do not want to go to the police. They decide to give back the football and the box. They are sad. They liked the football.

"Sorry, mister," Tom says. "We did not know. Here is your football and your box."

The man takes the football and the box. He does not say thank you. He walks away.

Ben and Tom look at each other. They are still friends. They do not need the football to play. They can play with other things. They go to the swings and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small hole in the wall of a big house. Every day, Timmy would go outside to find a snack to eat.

One day, while Timmy was looking for a snack, he saw a big piece of cheese on a table. Timmy was so hungry that he couldn't resist the cheese. He climbed up onto the table and started to eat the cheese.

Suddenly, the owner of the house came into the room and saw Timmy eating the cheese. The owner picked up a broom and said, "You naughty mouse! You shouldn't steal my snack!" Timmy was so scared that he bowed his head and ran back to his hole.

From that day on, Timmy was too scared to leave his hole and find food. He became weaker and weaker until one day he passed away from hunger. The end.

Once upon a time a little girl lived in a house with a pretty purple rug. She loved the rug and spent lots of time playing on it. Every morning she would wake up and jump on the rug right away.

One day her mom had to go away, so the little girl had to go stay with her grandpa. She was so sad to leave her rug behind and she missed it so much. She asked her grandpa if she could bring it with her, but he said
no.

The little girl was so sad. She tried to play with her grandpa's rug but it wasn't the same. She just wanted her purple rug back. 

Finally her mom came home and the little girl was so excited! She ran right to the rug and hugged it tight. She was never going to miss it ever again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat dessert, especially ice cream. One day, her mother made her a special dessert, but she hid it from Lily.

Lily asked her mother, "Mommy, where is my dessert?"

Her mother replied, "It's hidden, sweetie. You have to find it."

Lily searched all around the house until she found the dessert in the fridge. She was so happy and started to eat it quickly.

But her mother said, "Stop, Lily! You have to eat your dinner first."

Lily stopped and ate her dinner before having her delicious dessert. She enjoyed it so much that she asked her mother to make it again the next day. And they lived happily ever after.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big red car. The car can make noises and lights. It is very noisy and shiny.

One day, Lila and Ben want to polish their car. They find a cloth and some water. They rub the cloth on the car. They make it more shiny. They are happy.

"Look, Ben, our car is so shiny!" Lila says.

"Yes, Lila, it is very shiny. Can we play with it now?" Ben says.

They turn on the car and make it move. It makes noises and lights. They laugh and have fun.

But then, they smell something bad. They look at the cloth. It is dirty and stinky. They wonder why.

They remember that they used the cloth from the kitchen. The cloth was for wiping the dishes. The dishes had food on them. The food made the cloth dirty and stinky.

"Yuck, Lila, the cloth is dirty and stinky!" Ben says.

"Yes, Ben, it is dirty and stinky. We used the wrong cloth. We should have used a clean cloth." Lila says.

They throw away the cloth. They wash their hands. They wash their car. They make it shiny again.

They learn a lesson. They should not use a dirty cloth to polish their car. They should use a clean cloth. They should also not taste the cloth. It might taste bad. They should only taste food. Food tastes good.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Bobby. He was very adventurous. He loved exploring the world around him.

One day, Bobby went outside to play. He saw lots of things that he wanted to zoom around. He was so excited! But soon he got too tired and stopped to rest.

As he was resting, Bobby started to weep. He was sad because he couldn't zoom around as much as he wanted to. He felt so lonely.

But then, a magical fairy appeared! With a wave of her wand, she gave Bobby wings! Now he could zoom around and be as adventurous as he wanted to be.

Bobby was so happy! He flew and zoomed around, enjoying his new wings. He no longer had to weep. He was free and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy bunny named Floppy. Floppy loved to hop around and play with his friends. One day, Floppy's friend, a little bird named Tweet, came to him looking very sad.

"What's wrong, Tweet?" asked Floppy.

"I can't find any berries to eat," Tweet replied. "I'm so hungry."

"Don't be sad," said Floppy. "I can help you. Let's gather some berries together."

So, Floppy and Tweet hopped around the forest looking for berries. They found some delicious ones, but also some that were poison! Floppy warned Tweet not to eat the poison berries.

Finally, they had gathered enough berries for Tweet to eat. She was so happy and thanked Floppy for helping her. They hugged and went on their way, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved presents. One day, she saw a big present under a tree. She was very happy and wanted to open it.

Lily went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I want the present now!" Her mommy said, "Lily, you must wait until your birthday. It is not today." But Lily did not listen. She was not sorry. She went back to the tree and demanded, "Give me the present now!"

The present opened and out came a big, angry cat. The cat was not nice. It hissed and scratched Lily. She cried and ran away. Her mommy came and hugged her. Lily was very sorry and learned to never demand presents again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toy cat and write letters. She was very good at writing letters. One day, Lily decided to mail a letter to her friend, Tim. She wanted to show him a new spell she learned.

Lily wrote the letter and put it in an envelope. She felt a little embarrassed because she was not sure if Tim would like the spell. But she was excited to share it with him. She put the letter in the mailbox and waited for Tim to get it.

But something bad happened. The letter got lost in the mail. Tim never got the letter with the spell. Lily felt very sad and embarrassed. She wished she had told Tim about the spell in person. Now, Tim would never know the fun spell Lily wanted to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She had a tooth that was very bright and beautiful. One day, Sue and her mum went to the store. Sue wanted to buy a lollipop, so her mum said, â€œLetâ€™s pay for it.â€

Sue shook her head and said, â€œI donâ€™t want to pay for it.â€ She wanted the lollipop for free.

Her mum told her, â€œIf you donâ€™t pay for something it is stealing, and thatâ€™s wrong.â€

But Sue was stubborn and she still wanted the lollipop without paying. Just when she was about to take it, a security guard came. He noticed Sue and said, â€œHey, why donâ€™t you pay for the lollipop?â€

Sue tried to run away, but the guard caught her. He took her to the police station, along with her bright tooth.

The moral of the story is that itâ€™s important to always pay for things and avoid stealing. If you donâ€™t, you could get into a lot of trouble.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite one was Anna. Anna had long hair, a pretty dress and shiny shoes. Lily loved to brush Anna's hair and make her look nice.

One day, Lily saw a bottle of lotion on her mom's dresser. She thought it was a special cream for dolls. She took the bottle and ran to her room. She poured some lotion on Anna's hair and rubbed it hard. She wanted to make Anna's hair softer and smoother.

But the lotion was not good for dolls. It made Anna's hair sticky and messy. It also got on Anna's dress and shoes and stained them. Lily tried to wash the lotion off, but it did not come off. She started to cry. She had ruined her favorite doll.

Mom heard Lily crying and came to her room. She saw the lotion bottle and the doll. She was angry and sad. She said to Lily, "What have you done? This lotion is for my skin, not for dolls. You have been very foolish and naughty. You have spoiled your doll and wasted my lotion. You have to say sorry and clean up this mess."

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She said to Mom, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted to make Anna look nice. I did not know the lotion was bad for dolls. Please don't be mad at me. Can you fix Anna?"

Mom sighed and hugged Lily. She said, "I'm not mad at you, but I'm disappointed. You should not take things that are not yours. You should ask me before you use anything. And you should be careful with your toys. I can't fix Anna, but maybe we can find a new doll for you. But first, you have to help me clean up this lotion. And you have to promise me not to do this again."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, Mom. I will help you clean up. And I will be more careful and ask you next time. I love you, Mom. And I love Anna, even if she is sticky and messy."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love Anna, too. She is still your doll, and you can still play with her. But maybe you can use something else to make her look nice. Like a ribbon or a hat or a necklace. Not lotion."

Lily agreed and said, "Yes, Mom. That sounds like a good idea. Thank you, Mom. You are the best."

Mom and Lily cleaned up the lotion and put Anna in a new dress. They also found a ribbon and a hat for her. Lily hugged Anna and said, "You are still my favorite doll, Anna. I'm sorry I was foolish and put lotion on you. But you are still pretty and I still love you."

Anna did not say anything, because she was a doll. But she looked happy and shiny in her new outfit. And Lily was happy, too. She learned a lesson and she still had her mom and her doll. She did not demand anything else.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little animal called Penny. Penny was always very alert and he loved to explore. One day, Penny set out on an adventure to the nearby reef. He knew there was lots to discover.

Penny soon found what he was looking for, colourful fish, bright starfish and all sorts of wondrous things. He wanted to explore it all! But then he noticed something strange - the water around the reef was very still.

Penny knew he was in trouble. He had been too close and a net had been thrown over the reef, trapping all the creatures inside. Penny was scared, he needed to think fast. He decided he had to cut the net to save the reef.

Penny was brave and worked hard. He jumped over the net and began to cut with his sharp teeth. The net soon started to fray and eventually, it broke. All the creatures in the reef were so happy that they celebrated with Penny!

It was quite a reward for being so alert. Penny made sure to stay away from the reef so he would not get stuck again. He was happy to have saved the reef and knew he was even braver than before.

Once there was a small girl who liked to collect. Everywhere she went she collected things. She was never without some item she was collecting.

One day, the girl found a brick. She thought it was so cool and wanted to add it to her collection. She picked it up, put it in her pocket, and kept collecting.

She soon realized that the brick made it hard to hear. She was almost deaf with the brick in her pocket!

The girl decided that the brick wasn't really a fun thing to have in her collection. She put it back down where she had found it, and kept collecting without it. From then on, her collection was much easier to hear!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her yard. One day, she saw a big storm coming. She ran inside to tell her mommy.

"Mommy, there's a big storm coming!" Lily said.

"Oh no, we need to get inside and stay safe," her mommy replied.

Lily watched as the storm got closer and closer. The wind was blowing really hard and the rain was coming down in big drops. Suddenly, she saw something change. The trees were bending and swaying in the wind. 

"Mommy, look! The trees changed!" Lily exclaimed.

"Yes, the storm is making everything move and look different," her mommy explained.

After the storm passed, Lily went outside to see the original beauty of her yard. The sun was shining and everything looked fresh and new. She was happy to see that even though things change, they can still be beautiful in their own way.

Once there was a little boy who was very eager to explore the world. One day, the boy discovered a big and colorful tunnel. He wanted to go inside the tunnel, but his mom didn't allow it.

Instead, his mom said that he could look from the entrance of the tunnel and see the wonderful colors coming from it. As the boy looked, he saw that the tunnel was full of all sorts of colors: blues, reds, yellows and greens.

The little boy stared and stared at the tunnel, until his mom said it was time to go home. He reluctantly left and promised himself that he would come back and explore more of the colorful tunnel someday soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go outside to see the flowers. One day, her mommy gave her a purple dress to wear. Lily felt happy and excited to wear her new dress.

Later that day, Lily's daddy brought home a newspaper. Lily saw the newspaper and asked her daddy what it was. Her daddy said it was a paper with news about what's happening in the world. Lily felt curious and wanted to read it too.

As they read the newspaper together, Lily saw a picture of a purple flower. She felt amazed and showed her daddy the picture. Her daddy smiled and said, "Yes, that's a beautiful purple flower." Lily felt happy to learn something new and went to bed with happy thoughts.

One day, a little boy was very tired. He had been running and playing all day and it was now late. The little boy looked for somewhere to rest. He found an empty box. He pushed and prodded the box until he was comfortable. He closed his eyes and rested. 

When morning came, the little boy opened his eyes and stood up. He expected to feel tired but found he was not. He felt energized! The result of his rest was that he no longer felt tired. The empty box had become his cozy bed and his resting spot. The little boy smiled, picked up the empty box, and ran off to play some more.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to skip. She had an incredible chain that she wore around her neck. It was her favourite thing in the world.

One day, she went to the park to skip with her chain on. She didn't know that it would come off. She skipped and jumped and choreographed leaps through the grass.

Before she knew it, the chain was gone. She looked everywhere, but it was not to be found. She became very sad, realising that her chain was lost.

But then, something incredible happened. As she looked back at the park, a bright light shone from a chain in the grass. The girl rushed over and couldn't believe her eyes. It was her chain! It was still there! 

The girl quickly put it back around her neck and vowed never to lose it again. She was so incredibly happy.

Once upon a time there was a big tree in a forest. The tree was so tall and strong, it could reach up to the sky. All the other trees in the forest were jealous. Every morning, the tree would bow to the sun to thank it for another day of life.

One day, a little girl went on a walk in the forest. She saw the tall tree bowing and said, "Hello tree! Why do you bow to the sun every morning?"

The tree said, "I bow to say thank you for a new day."

The little girl felt curious, so she said, "Will you teach me how to bow too?"

The tree smiled and said, "Yes, of course. Put your hands together and bow your head."

The girl bowed and said thank you for the new day. From then on, the girl and the tree would bow together every morning. The other trees in the forest were still jealous, but they also acknowledged the special bond between the little girl and the tall tree in the forest.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to splash in the puddles and make mud pies. They saw a big hole in the ground with a metal cover. It was a drain.

"Let's open it and see what's inside," Tom said. He pulled on the cover, but it was too heavy.

"Maybe there are monsters or treasure in there," Lily said. She helped Tom push the cover, but it did not move.

They heard a loud noise. It was Mom. She was holding a hose. She was going to water the flowers.

"Hi, kids. Do you want to help me?" Mom asked. She smiled and offered them the hose.

Tom and Lily nodded. They liked to help Mom. They took the hose and sprayed water on the flowers. They also sprayed water on each other and laughed.

But they sprayed too much water. The puddles grew bigger and bigger. The water reached the drain. The cover slid off and fell into the hole.

"Uh-oh," Tom and Lily said. They ran to the drain and looked inside. It was dark and wet. They saw the cover at the bottom. They also saw something shiny.

"Look, it's a coin!" Lily said. "Maybe it's a treasure!"

She reached for the coin, but Tom stopped her.

"No, don't go in there. It's dangerous. Mom will be angry," he said.

He was right. Mom came and saw the open drain. She was angry and scared.

"Kids, what have you done? That's very naughty and unsafe. You could have fallen in and hurt yourself. Come here right now!" she said.

She took the hose and turned it off. She picked up Tom and Lily and carried them inside. She gave them a bath and a scolding. She told them to never play with the drain again.

Tom and Lily were sorry. They said they were sorry to Mom. They also said they were sorry to the coin. They hoped it was not lonely in the wet drain.

Once there was a girl who liked to run. One day she was running in the park and saw a tree. She wanted to run to it, so she ran faster. When she got to the tree, she looked up and saw a bird. The bird was fit and healthy, so the girl stopped and smiled.

The bird stopped too, and the girl noticed it was looking at her with kind eyes. The bird and the girl just looked at each other, until the bird started to fly away. The girl smiled and waved goodbye.

The girl went back to running, but this time she ran slower. She made sure to stop and admire the trees she saw. She felt fit, happy and excited!

Once upon a time, there was a man who worked in a big building. He had a lot of people who helped him do his work, and they were called his staff. The man liked to have modern things in his office, like a computer and a fancy chair.

One day, the man made a mistake and he felt very sad. He wished he hadn't done what he did, and that made him regret it. His staff tried to help him feel better, but he still felt bad.

The man realized that having modern things in his office didn't make him happy. He decided to spend more time with his family and friends instead. He apologized to his staff and they all became friends. From then on, the man was much happier and didn't regret his decision.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who liked to play outside. His favourite game was catch! He had a little net and he liked to step in and out of it when he played his game.

In the backyard of his house, there was a little lake. He always wanted to play catch there but the lake was too big, he thought his net would never fit inside it.

One day, his parents told him that he could play in the lake if he wanted to. He was very excited and grabbed his net. But when he arrived, he couldn't believe his eyes: the net fit perfectly in the lake!

He played as if he never had before. He laughed and smiled, it was easy to catch the fish with his net. He was so happy and he thanked his parents for having found the perfect spot for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to have a picnic at noon. Timmy was so excited that he started to hurry and get ready.

When they arrived at the park, Timmy and his friends played on the swings and slides. They were having so much fun that they didn't even notice the dark clouds in the sky. Suddenly, the wind started to blow strong and the rain started to pour down.

Timmy's mom quickly gathered all the food and they ran to the car. Timmy was sad that their picnic was ruined, but his mom told him that they could have their picnic at home. They ate sandwiches and fruit and Timmy felt happy again. From that day on, Timmy always remembered to check the weather before planning a picnic.

Once upon a time, there was a brave ostrich named Ollie. Ollie was very tall and had big, strong legs. One day, Ollie was walking in the forest when he saw a little bird. 

"Hello little bird," said Ollie. "What are you doing here?"

"I'm lost," said the little bird. "Can you help me find my way home?"

"Of course," said Ollie. "I'll help you."

Suddenly, a snake struck Ollie with its sharp teeth. Ollie fell to the ground and couldn't move. The little bird flew away to find help, but it was too late. Ollie had died.

The little bird was very sad. "Goodbye, brave Ollie," it said. "Thank you for trying to help me."

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She liked to sell things. One day she had a good idea. She decided to sell the heat from the sun!

Jane went outside and sat in the sun. It was quiet. The heat was so pleasant. Jane decided to sell it.

She began running around the neighbourhood yelling "Heat for sale! Get your heat here!" Everyone was very surprised.

One by one, people started buying the heat from Jane. They put some money in her hands, and Jane gave them some of the heat.

Soon all the heat was gone. Jane was very happy with all the money she made. And she was glad to help make everyone else's day a bit warmer and brighter.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the garden. One day, Timmy saw a beetle crawling on a leaf. The beetle was very colorful and Timmy wanted to touch it. He leaned over to touch the beetle.

Suddenly, the beetle flew up and landed on Timmy's finger. Timmy was so excited! But then, the beetle bit him. It was a dangerous beetle and Timmy got very sick. His parents took him to the doctor, but it was too late. Timmy passed away.

The moral of the story is that sometimes things that look pretty and harmless can be very dangerous. It's important to listen to grown-ups and not touch things that we don't know are safe.

Sara loves flowers. She likes to look at them and smell them. She has a small garden with many flowers. She waters them every day and talks to them.

One day, she sees a new flower in her garden. It is bright yellow and has many petals. Sara is happy. She runs to the flower and says, "Hello, flower! You are so pretty! What is your name?"

The flower does not answer. Sara thinks maybe the flower is shy. She says, "Don't be afraid, flower. I am Sara. I care for you. I will give you water and sun. You can be my friend."

The flower still does not answer. Sara is sad. She thinks maybe the flower does not like her. She says, "Please, flower, talk to me. I want to hear your voice. Do you like me?"

The flower still does not answer. Sara is about to cry. She thinks maybe the flower is sick. She says, "Are you okay, flower? Do you need something? I will help you."

Then, she hears a small voice. It is the flower. The flower says, "Hello, Sara. I am sorry I did not talk to you. I was asleep. I am a sunflower. I only wake up when the sun is bright. Thank you for caring for me. You are very kind. I like you."

Sara is happy. She smiles and hugs the flower. She says, "I am glad you are awake, sunflower. You are very beautiful. I am happy to be your friend."

The flower smiles and nods. It says, "I am happy to be your friend, too, Sara. You make me feel warm and loved. Let's talk and play together."

Sara and the sunflower become good friends. They talk and play every day. They care for each other and make each other happy. They are the brightest flowers in the garden.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to play in the garden. She went there every day and had lots of fun.
She liked to explore the garden and see all of the different plants and creatures. She saw regular things like butterflies and bees, but she also saw special things too.

One day the girl was playing in the garden when she heard a noise. She was scared and wanted to leave. She quickly ran to the gate of the garden and shut it behind her. 

That night, the girl decided she would visit the garden again, but she would be more careful. She went back the next day and was happy to find the garden just as she had left it. She explored and saw the same regular things, but it still felt special to her. 

The girl visited the garden regularly and never forgot her first day there when she was scared and had to leave. She still loved to explore the garden's wonders.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink milk every day. One day, her mom gave her a cup of milk that tasted funny. Lily was troubled and didn't know what to do. She wanted to ask her mom about it, but she was afraid. 

Lily decided to ask her dad for help. Her dad listened to her and asked her to show him the milk. He smelled it and realized that it was spoiled. He explained to Lily that it's important to ask questions when we are unsure about something, especially when it comes to our health. 

From that day on, Lily learned to ask questions when she was troubled or unsure about something. She knew that it was better to ask and get an answer than to stay quiet and worry. And she never drank spoiled milk again!

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He liked to play with his friends. One day, they decided to throw a ball. The elephant was very good at throwing. He threw the ball high into the sky. 

The elephant's friends were amazed. They had never seen such a good throw before! They asked the elephant how he learned to throw so well. The elephant said he practiced every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go outside and play in the park. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. They brought a kite with them. The kite was big and colorful.

Suddenly, a strong wind blew and the kite started to pull very hard. Lily's mommy and daddy helped her to hold on to the string. They all laughed and had fun together. After a while, the wind calmed down and they went home. Lily was very proud of herself for flying the kite all by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy. One day, they decided to make spaghetti with red sauce. Mommy asked Lily to help cut the pepper. Lily managed to cut it with her little knife.

Mia noticed there were little splits in the muddy field. She asked her mommy what the splits were and her mommy said they were worm tunnels. Mia got closer and tried to put her finger in one of the splits, but it was too hard. She saw a big, brown earthworm and decided to give it a hug. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, her mommy was making spaghetti and asked Lily to stir the sauce. Lily grabbed the spoon and stirred and stirred until the sauce was just right.

After the spaghetti was cooked, her mommy asked Lily to help drain the water from the pot. Lily carefully held the pot while her mommy poured the water into the sink. She felt so proud to be able to help out.

But then, as they were putting the spaghetti on the plates, they realized they had run out of sauce! Lily felt helpless, but her mommy told her not to worry. Together, they quickly made a new batch of sauce and Lily got to stir it once again. And the spaghetti turned out delicious!

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who lived on a farm. The farm was big and had many animals. The farmer was a kind man who loved his animals very much. Every day, he would feed them and take care of them.

One day, a little girl came to the farm. She saw the animals and said, "Wow, they are so peaceful!" The farmer smiled and said, "Yes, they are happy because I take good care of them."

The little girl asked the farmer, "Can I help you with something?" The farmer said, "Sure, can you tie this rope for me?" The little girl tied the rope and was very proud of herself.

The moral of the story is that when we help others, we feel good about ourselves. And when we take care of things, they become peaceful and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, she went to a store with her mommy. While they were there, Lily saw a toy she really wanted. She requested her mommy to buy it for her, but her mommy said no.

Once upon a time there was a man who went on an adventure. He came to a big bush he had to go through. He tried to push through it but it was too tight and he couldn't pass. Mommy, why do we have to close our eyes? Jane asked her mommy as they lit the candle.

One day, a little girl named Amy found a soft notebook. She loved to touch it because it felt nice. The notebook was her new friend. She took it everywhere she went.

One day, a family decided to go to the park. They had a lot of fun running around and playing, but the little girl was most excited to see the furry model at the park. Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a unique theater. Many people went there to see shows. One day, a boy named Tim went to the theater with his friends. They were very excited.

At the theater, Tim saw a big box. He asked his friend, "What do you think we can use this for?" His friend replied, "I don't know, but we should not touch it." Tim did not listen and opened the box.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop and play in the meadow with his friends. One day, Benny saw some sparkly things on the ground. He went to investigate and found shiny rocks that sparkled in the sun. Benny wanted to gather them all up and show his friends.

Benny hopped around the meadow and gathered up all the shiny rocks he could find. His friends were so happy to see the sparkly rocks and they all played with them together. They had so much fun that they decided to gather more things from the meadow.

Once upon a time there was a naughty little boy. He did not listen to his parents and often made messes. One day his mum went to the field to get some wheat. She asked the naughty boy to help her lift the wheat, but he didn't want to!

Finally, the naughty boy agreed to help, but not without a bit of grumbling. He carefully lifted the big bags of wheat and carried them to the wagon. It was hard work, but he did it!

Mum was very pleased with the naughty little boy for helping her, and rewarded him with an ice cream. He smiled and knew that helping was the right thing to do.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. Every day Mia would pray to the Lord to make her happy. One day while Mia was praying, she had a special idea. She asked the Lord to send her a video. The Lord said yes and the next day a special video arrived in the post.

When Mia opened the package, she was so excited to see the video. She popped it into her video player and watched it. The video was about regular activities like brushing her teeth and gathering eggs from the hen house. Mia was so happy that all her prayings had been answered.

The next day, Mia showed the video to all of her friends. They all loved it! They watched it every day, and started to do all of the activities in the video every day too. Mia was so pleased to know that the Lord had sent her a special video to help her and her friends live regular lives.

Once, there was a little girl who loved to balance. She would practice every day and it was lots of fun. She wanted to be the most fancy person at balancing.

One day, the little girl heard about a balancing tournament. She knew that this was a chance to make her dream come true. She knew it would be difficult, but she was determined to try her best.

The little girl started practicing more. She made sure to balance on steeper hills, and it was very difficult.

On the day of the tournament, the little girl was nervous. She watched as fancy balancers tried to prove themselves. It was very exciting - but when it was her turn, she nearly fell over. She was so discouraged and wanted to give up.

But then the little girl remembered all the fun she had practicing. She forgot about being fancy and just enjoyed the challenge of balancing. She tried her best and was able to finish the course. Everyone cheered for her and she felt proud.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play and have fun. Today is their birthday. Mom and Dad have a big surprise for them. They make a big cake with candles and frosting. They hide the cake in the kitchen.

Mom and Dad call Lily and Ben to the living room. They say, "We have a surprise for you. But you have to be quiet and close your eyes. No peeking!" Lily and Ben are excited. They do what Mom and Dad say. They are quiet and close their eyes.

One day, a girl named Lily went for a walk. She had a regular basket with her. In the basket, there were fruits like apples, bananas, and oranges. Lily wanted to share them with her friends.

One day, a little girl called Lucy found a box in the garden. She was very happy and lay it down on the grass. She opened the box and saw that it was full of shining stars. She wanted to play with the stars, but they were too high, so she ran and fetched her mum. Together, mum and Lucy lay on the grass and looked at the stars twinkling in the night sky. Lucy and her mum said goodbye to the stars and put the box of stars back in the garden. Then, Lucy went back to the house to have breakfast. She was so happy to have seen the stars!

Once there was a yellow bird. It was looking for a place to belong. It flew all around searching for the perfect nest. Finally it spied a cozy yellow nest in the tree. It hopped inside and knew that this was the place for it. It felt like it belonged.

The bird stayed in the nest and kept it clean. Every morning it would look out from the nest and sing a song. All the other birds heard the yellow bird's beautiful song and they knew it had found its home.

Once upon a time there was a little brown bear. The bear went on an adventure to find a special victory.

The bear saw a big mountain and decided to climb it. The mountain was very steep, but the bear kept going until he reached the top. The view was amazing. 

The bear saw a river below. The river was very wide and looked like it would take a long time to cross. So the bear changed his plan and decided to float down the river instead.

He grabbed a big leaf and jumped into the river. The leaf carried the bear down the river until he reached a small island in the middle of the river.

The bear was so excited. On the island he saw a tree with a giant shining gem at the very top. The gem was the special victory he had been searching for.

The bear climbed the tree and grabbed the gem. With the gem in his hand the bear had a big smile on his face. He had changed his plan many times, but he had found his special victory in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the forest. One day, she found a pine tree and sat down next to it. She noticed how tall and strong the pine tree was, and she wished she could be as powerful as it.

Suddenly, she heard a small voice coming from the tree. It was a little bird who had lost its way. Lily decided to help the bird find its home. She asked the pine tree if it knew where the bird's home was.

The pine tree said, "I do not know, but if we unite and search together, we will find the bird's home." So, Lily and the pine tree searched together and found the bird's home. The bird was very happy and thanked them both.

The moral of the story is that when we unite and work together, we can accomplish great things.

Anna likes to play with her furry cat, Luna. Luna is black and white and has green eyes. Luna likes to chase balls and mice and nap in the sun. Anna and Luna are best friends.

Once there was a lonely gem. It was tucked away in a corner all by itself. Then one day it decided to break free. It tumbled out and was no longer lonely.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to dance and twirl around. He would dance whenever he felt happy or excited. One day, Timmy saw an old man walking with a cane. The old man looked nervous and scared.

Once upon a time, there was a tank in the zoo. It was filled with strange unknown fish. Everyone liked to watch and play with them, but nobody could understand why they were in the tank.

Jim was a curious boy. He always wanted to know what others thought. One day, he went to his friend's house. He thought it was nice. He asked his friend what he thought about it. His friend said he thought it was very nice. Jim was happy that his friend shared his opinion.

Sara liked to play with her dolls. She had a big box of dolls and clothes and shoes. She liked to dress them up and make them talk. She had a tea party with her dolls every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to observe the world around her. She would watch the birds in the sky, the fish in the pond, and the ants on the ground. Lily was always curious about everything.

The sun was shining on a bright day. Jack and his dad, John, were walking in the forest. They heard a rustling noise.

Her mom replied, "I heard a loud and strange noise, so I came to the kitchen to check what it was. Someone must have opened the refrigerator."

Then, suddenly, a big and furry cat popped out from behind the refrigerator. Tina said, "Look Mommy! The cat opened the refrigerator!"

The mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tina. The cat must have struck the door with its paw!"

Tina laughed and said, "That cat is so funny!" Then she chased the cat out of the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a careless boy. He loved to play outside in the mud and get wet. One day, Tim's mom told him not to play in the mud because it would make him wet and dirty.

Tim did not listen to his mom. He went outside and played in the mud. He got very wet and dirty. His mom saw him and said, "Tim, I told you not to play in the mud! Now you are wet and dirty."

Tim felt sad because he did not listen to his mom. He said, "I am sorry, Mom. I will not be careless again." Tim's mom helped him clean up and they hugged. From that day on, Tim tried to be more careful and listen to his mom.

Once there were two friends named Tom and Sarah. Tom was very shy and Sarah was very loud. One day, Sarah shouted, "Let's go find some cheese!" Tom couldn't believe it. "Where will we find it?" he asked. Sarah knew exactly what she wanted. She shouted out again, "Let's find some big cheese!"

Tom was excited. They looked around and soon found a big, yellow cheese. Sarah shouted, "It's so big!" She picked up the cheese and laughed. Tom couldn't believe it. They had found the best cheese ever! 

The two friends ran back home with the big cheese. Sarah shouted, "Let's make a big, cheesy pizza!" Tom was so excited. They made the biggest, cheesiest pizza ever. Everyone in their neighbourhood could smell the delicious aroma. 

Tom and Sarah shared the big, cheesy pizza with their friends and family. Everyone cheered and shouted with joy. What a wonderful day!

Once there was a little girl named Lila. She had an aunt who was very busy. Lila loved spending time with her aunt because she was always so fun.

One day her aunt said to Lila, "Let's go for a run!". Lila was so excited and she clapped her hands. She loved going for a run with her aunt because it was always so much fun.

So they put on their running shoes and ran outside. Lila ran faster and faster and her aunt chased her. They ran around the park and laughed.

Soon it was time to go home. Lila and her aunt were both so tired from their run. But they were also very happy and they hugged each other to say goodbye.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mom. Timmy loved going to the park because he could play on the swings and slide. But one day, a big dog came to the park and scared Timmy. He didn't want to play anymore.

His mom saw that Timmy was scared and told him that they could leave if he wanted to. But Timmy didn't want to leave. He wanted to be independent and face his fear. So, he decided to follow his mom's advice and stay at the park.

Timmy's mom showed him the value of being brave and facing his fears. They stayed at the park and played together. Timmy felt happy and proud of himself for being brave. From that day on, Timmy knew that he could be independent and face any challenge that came his way.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went for a walk in the forest with his mommy. They saw a stream and Timmy wanted to play with the water. He put his hand in the stream and splashed it around. His mommy told him to be careful and not to get too close to the water.

Suddenly, Timmy saw a butterfly and he started to chase it. He ran and ran, but he didn't notice that he was getting further away from his mommy. When he turned around, he realized that he was lost. He started to cry and called out for his mommy.

Luckily, a kind man heard Timmy's cries and came to help him. He asked Timmy if he was lost and Timmy nodded his head. The man took Timmy's hand and brought him back to his mommy. Timmy's mommy was very serious and told him to always stay close to her so he wouldn't lose his way again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to wear his cozy sweater, even when it was hot outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean his messy room. Timmy didn't want to clean his room, he wanted to play. 

Timmy's friend, Johnny, came over to play. Johnny saw Timmy's messy room and said, "Wow, your room is a mess!" Timmy laughed and said, "Yeah, it's a joke!" 

As they played, they accidentally knocked over a lamp and it broke. Timmy's mom came in and saw the broken lamp and the messy room. She was very angry and sent Johnny home. Timmy was sad because he lost his friend and had to clean his room. 

From that day on, Timmy learned to clean up his messes and not to joke about things that weren't funny.

Tom and Mia were playing on the beach. They liked to find shells and make piles of them. Tom found a big shell that was shiny and had many colors. He was very happy and showed it to Mia.

"Look, Mia, I found a nice shell!" he said.

Mia looked at the shell and frowned. She recognized it. It was the same shell that she had found yesterday and left on her towel. She thought Tom had taken it from her.

"That is my shell, Tom!" she said. "You took it from me!"

Tom was confused and sad. He did not take the shell from Mia. He found it in the sand. He did not want to make Mia angry.

"No, Mia, I did not take your shell. I found it here. See, there are more shells like it." he said and pointed to the sand.

Mia did not believe him. She thought he was lying. She wanted her shell back. She tried to grab it from Tom's hand.

"Give me my shell, Tom! It is mine!" she said.

Tom did not want to give up his shell. He liked it too much. He held it tight and pulled it away from Mia.

"No, Mia, it is my shell! I found it first!" he said.

They both pulled and tugged on the shell. They were both angry and loud. They did not hear their mom calling them.

"Tom! Mia! Come here, please!" their mom said.

She saw them fighting over the shell. She was not happy. She walked over to them and took the shell from their hands.

"Stop it, both of you! What is going on?" she said.

Tom and Mia both tried to explain. They both said the shell was theirs. They both said the other one was wrong.

Their mom looked at the shell. She recognized it too. She had seen it before. She knew who it belonged to.

"Tom, Mia, this shell is not yours. It is not mine. It is not anyone's. It is a shell that belongs to the sea. It is a gift that the sea gives us to enjoy, but not to keep. Do you understand?" she said.

Tom and Mia looked at the shell. They looked at their mom. They looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting. They nodded.

"Yes, mom, we understand." they said.

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She gave them the shell to hold together.

"Good. Now, why don't you share this nice shell and look for more shells to admire? But remember, when we leave the beach, we have to leave the shells behind. They are not ours to take. They are the sea's to give." she said.

Tom and Mia agreed. They thanked their mom and said sorry to each other. They held the shell and looked at its colors. They felt happy and peaceful. They went back to playing on the beach. They found more shells and made piles of them. They shared them and admired them. They did not fight over them. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named John. John was very enthusiastic and he loved to help people. One day, he saw a hut that was on fire. He quickly ran to the hut and saw a kitten inside. He was determined to save it. With his bare hands, John tore down the burning door. He carefully grabbed the kitten and ran outside to safety. 

John was very relieved that the kitten was safe. He hugged it and it meowed in appreciation. As a reward for saving the kitten, the owner of the hut gave John a toy fire truck and thanked him for his courageous efforts. John was so happy and couldn't believe his luck. He hugged the kitten once more and ran off to show his new toy fire truck to his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a big house with lots of rooms and lots of cheese. One day, Timmy saw a match on the ground and he wanted to play with it. But his mommy told him matches are dangerous and he shouldn't touch them. Timmy thought it was stupid, but he listened to his mommy and walked away.

Later that day, Timmy was playing in the kitchen when he saw a big cat coming towards him. He knew he had to escape, so he ran as fast as he could. He ran through the living room, up the stairs and into his bedroom. The cat followed him, but Timmy was too quick and he escaped through a little hole in the wall. 

Timmy was so happy he escaped from the cat, but he knew he had to be careful and listen to his mommy. He never played with matches again and he stayed safe from the big cat. The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars. One day, they find a big box of blocks in the playroom. They are happy and start to build a network of roads and bridges.

"Look, Mia, I made a long road!" Tom says.

"Wow, Tom, that's good! I made a high bridge!" Mia says.

They play for a while, but then Tom wants to make his road longer. He sees a block that Mia is using for her bridge. He takes it and puts it on his road.

"Hey, Tom, that's my block! Give it back!" Mia says.

"No, Mia, I need it for my road! It's mine now!" Tom says.

Mia is angry. She wants her block back. She tries to pull it from Tom's road, but Tom holds it tight. They start to tug and shout.

"Let go, Mia! It's mine!"

"Let go, Tom! It's mine!"

They tug harder and harder, until the block flies out of their hands. It hits the wall and breaks in two. They both gasp and stop.

"Oh no, the block is broken!" Tom says.

"Oh no, the bridge is ruined!" Mia says.

They look at each other and feel sad. They both like the block and the network. They don't like to fight and break things.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I shouldn't have taken your block," Mia says.

"I'm sorry, Mia. I shouldn't have pulled your block," Tom says.

They hug and say sorry. They decide to share the blocks and fix the network. They are friends again. They are happy.

Once upon a time, a panda was very busy. She kept moving and moving, but she never seemed to get tired. She was looking high and low, but she couldn't find what she was looking for.

Then one day, while she was playing in the forest, the panda heard a voice. It came from the top of a tall tree. The voice said, "Keep running! Keep looking! You will find it if you keep going!"

The panda was so excited. She kept running and exploring every corner of the forest. Finally she found what she had been looking for- her very own home! She was so happy and so busy building and arranging her house that she barely stopped to eat or sleep.

The panda was so busy for such a long time that she started to get tired again. The voice from the top of the tall tree said, "Keep going! Don't stop now! You can do it!"

The panda kept going and eventually she was done with her house. It was cozy and beautiful and she was so proud. After all her hard work, she was ready for a rest. Now she always has a comfy place to go home to after a busy day.

In the farm, the sun was shining bright. The corn was growing high. In the field, the ground was wet. Jennie owned the farm. She liked to walk through the tall, green corn. The corn felt soft and cool. As she walked around, drops of water tickled her toes. Jennie looked around and smiled. She was so proud to own the farm and all of the corn. She was grateful for all the wet, green stalks. With a happy heart, she waved to the birds in the sky and the clouds that were gathering. Jennie loved to own the farm and the corn.

Once upon a time, there was an old turtle named Tom. Tom was very slow because his shell was thick. He wanted to go faster but he didn't know how. 

One day, Tom met a rabbit named Benny. Benny asked Tom why he was so slow. Tom said, "I am old and my shell is thick." Benny said, "Don't worry, Tom. I will encourage you to go faster."

Benny and Tom started to walk together. Benny said, "Come on, Tom. You can do it!" Tom tried his best and started to walk faster. Benny was so happy and said, "Great job, Tom! You are not so slow anymore." Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Benny. You are a good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to travel with his family. One day, they went to the amusement park. Timmy saw a big circle ride and wanted to go on it. 

"Mommy, can we go on that ride?" Timmy asked.

"Yes, we can," Mommy said. "But it might make you feel uncomfortable."

Timmy didn't know what uncomfortable meant, so he asked his mom. "What does uncomfortable mean?"

"It means you might not feel very good," Mommy explained.

But Timmy wanted to go on the ride anyway. So, they got on the ride and it started to spin. Timmy felt a little uncomfortable, but he held on tight and enjoyed the ride. When it was over, Timmy said, "That was so much fun! Can we do it again?"

Once upon a time, there was a skeleton. He was sad because the world around him was so harsh. Everywhere he went, people were mean and there was no love.

So, the skeleton decided to resist. He fought against the meanness, and fought for kindness. He shared love and tried to make the world a better place.

But it was hard. The skeleton was tired and sometimes he felt like giving up. He wanted to give in to the harshness.

But then, something changed. He felt others join him in his mission - more and more people also started to resist against the meanness. Together, they made their world kinder and showed everyone that even something small could make a huge difference.

The skeleton was so happy that he had persisted and was no longer alone. From then on, he was sure that he could conquer the darkness and fill the world with love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very good at drawing and everyone said she was gifted. One day, her mommy told her that if she drew a picture of their house, she would get a prize. Lily was very excited and started drawing right away. She worked very hard and finally finished her picture. Her mommy was very happy with it and gave her a big hug. She also gave her a prize, which was a yummy cookie. 

Later that day, Lily's little brother Jack broke her favorite toy. She was very angry and wanted to punish him. But her mommy told her that it's not nice to punish others and that they should forgive each other. So, Lily forgave Jack and they played together again. The end.

Tom was a boy who liked to polish things. He had a cloth and a bottle of polish that he used to make his toys and shoes shiny. He was very proud of his work and liked to show it to his friends.

One day, he went to the park with his mom and saw a big statue of a king. The king had a crown and a sword and a long coat. Tom thought the statue looked dull and dirty. He wanted to make it shiny like his toys and shoes.

He ran to the statue and climbed on it. He took out his cloth and polish and started to rub the king's face. He did not see the sign that said "Do not touch". He did not hear his mom calling him to come down. He did not notice the people staring at him.

"Hey, what are you doing?" a loud voice said. Tom looked up and saw a man in a uniform. He had a badge and a hat and a whistle. He was a guard. He was angry.

"I'm polishing the king," Tom said. "He looks sad and dirty. I want to make him happy and shiny."

The guard frowned and blew his whistle. He grabbed Tom and lifted him off the statue. He scolded him and told him he was not allowed to touch the statue. He said he could damage it and get in trouble.

Tom felt scared and embarrassed. He did not mean to do anything bad. He just wanted to polish the king. He started to cry and said he was sorry.

The guard softened and gave Tom a tissue. He said he understood that Tom liked to polish things, but he had to be careful and respectful of the statue. He said the statue was very old and important and needed to be protected. He said Tom could polish other things, like his bike or his spoon, but not the statue.

Tom nodded and wiped his tears. He said he was sorry again and promised not to touch the statue anymore. He hugged his mom and said he wanted to go home.

The guard smiled and said it was okay. He said he hoped Tom learned his lesson and would be more careful next time. He said he liked to polish things too, when he was a boy. He said he had a polish for his badge and his hat and his whistle. He said he would show Tom how to use it, if he wanted.

Tom smiled and said yes. He said he liked the guard and his polish. He said he wanted to be a guard when he grew up. He said he would polish his badge and his hat and his whistle every day.

The guard laughed and said he was glad. He said he would be happy to have Tom as a friend and a helper. He said he would teach Tom how to be a good guard and how to respect the king. He said he would let Tom polish his badge and his hat and his whistle, once in a while.

Tom was happy. He said he liked the king and his statue. He said he wanted to make him happy and shiny, but not with his polish. He said he would make him happy and shiny with his smile and his wave and his thank you. He said he would be a good boy and a good guard and a good friend. He said he learned his lesson and would not be embarrassed again.

Once upon a time, there was a big TV in a house. The TV was very large and it had many colors. One day, a boy was playing with a toy and he accidentally hit the TV. The TV fell down and broke. The boy was very sad because he loved watching cartoons on the TV. His mom told him not to worry and that they would get a new TV. The new TV was even bigger and sharper than the old one. The boy was very happy and he watched his favorite cartoons on the new TV every day.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl named Daisy. She liked to pinch things. One day, in the park, she saw an opera. She liked how it sounded, so she pinched it. But when she pinched it, a big spark came out! Daisy was so surprised she started to laugh. Then Daisy pinched the opera again and again, and the sparks kept coming. She was very happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to read books. He would read books all day and all night. His favorite place to read was in the garage.

One day, Tim found a small, weak cat in the garage. The cat was hungry and cold. Tim felt sad for the cat, so he gave it some food and a warm blanket. The cat was very happy.

Tim and the weak cat became best friends. They would play and read books together in the garage. The cat got stronger and happier with Tim's help. They had so much fun, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the hot sun. But today, the weather was not so hot. It was cloudy and rainy. Lily was sad because she could not play outside.

Lily's mom had an idea to make her happy. They went to the store to buy decorations. They bought balloons, streamers, and a big banner that said "Happy Birthday". Lily was confused because it was not her birthday. But her mom said they were going to decorate the house to make it look like a party.

Lily helped her mom decorate the house. She put up the balloons and streamers. She was so happy that she forgot about the rainy weather. When they finished decorating, they had a party inside the house. They danced and sang and had so much fun. Lily was no longer sad because she had a fun party inside her house!

Mummy and Daddy decided to buy a pizza. It was a big one. It had lots of yummy cheese and tomato on it. Mummy and Daddy wanted to share it. They were so excited! 

They sat down on the sofa and waited for the pizza to arrive. They heard a knock at the door and rushed off to answer it. It was the pizza man with a big box.
Mummy and Daddy opened the box and it was their pizza. The slices looked big and delicious. Mummy and Daddy clapped their hands. They were very happy.

Mummy and Daddy each took a slice of pizza. They chewed it slowly, savouring the taste. There was so much cheese and tomato juice that it was dribbling down their chins. Mummy and Daddy smiled at each other.

After they had finished their pizza, they both gave a big burp. It was the best pizza they had ever had. Mummy and Daddy were filled with joy.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the zoo with his mom. They saw many animals like big lions, tall giraffes, and funny monkeys. Tim was very happy to see all the animals. He wanted to tell his friend Sam about the zoo.

At school, Tim said to Sam, "I recommend you go to the zoo! It is so much fun." But Sam was scared of big animals. He said, "I am scared of lions and tigers. I don't want to go to the zoo."

Tim thought for a moment. Then he said, "Don't worry, Sam. The big animals are in cages. They cannot hurt you. You can just look at them from far away." Sam thought about it and decided to go to the zoo with Tim.

At the zoo, Sam was still a little scared, but Tim held his hand. They looked at the animals together. Sam started to like the zoo too. In the end, both Tim and Sam had a great time at the zoo. They were not scared anymore, and they loved all the animals.

Once there was a little boy, named Dan. Dan was three years old and lived with his mom and dad. Every Tuesday morning, Dan would get out of bed early. He liked Tuesdays because they were always fun, and usually something special would happen on Tuesdays.

Today was a Tuesday. Everything outside was gray and quiet. Dan went down to the kitchen. His mom had made him a special breakfast. It was Dan's favorite: cereal with milk and blueberries.

After breakfast, Dan and his mom went to the park. Dan loved playing in the park. He ran around, exploring and finding all kinds of new things. Dan only stopped running when he got tired. Sooner or later, he would take a break and sit in one of the swings.

Dan had a great time at the park, but eventually it was time to go home. As they were walking back, his mom said, "Dan, today was Tuesday and we had a lot of fun. Tomorrow will be Wednesday and there will be more fun! 

Dan smiled, happy that he had been able to get out and enjoy a fun special Tuesday.

Once upon a time, there lived a brave girl named Mallory. She loved adventures, and she was never scared. One day, she had an amazing idea. She wanted to go to the ancient train station.

Mallory asked her mom, "Mom, can I dare to go to the ancient train station?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, but be careful". So Mallory set off to the ancient train station.

When Mallory got to the train station, she saw a big ancient train. She was so excited she ran up to it and started hugging it. She noticed there was a conductor in the train and waved at him. The conductor smiled and then waved her inside.

Mallory sat on the train with a huge smile on her face. She waved goodbye to the conductor as the train slowly started to move. Mallory was so proud that she dared to venture to the ancient train station.

Sam was a generous three year old who loved to cook. He had his own grill and was always inviting his friends over to cook together. His friends loved eating the delicious treats that he prepared for them.

One day, he was so busy cooking that he didn't notice a mean, old sign that had been posted in the park. It said that grills were not allowed in the park. Sam was worried that he might get in trouble if someone saw him with his grill. 

But just when he was about to turn around and leave, one of his friends saw him and screamed out in delight. Soon enough, all the kids in the park were gathered around the grill, rubbing their tummies and excitedly watching Sam prepare the food.

Just then, a park ranger appeared and looked ready to scold Sam for having the grill in the park. But upon spotting the group's joyful faces, the ranger's stern expression softened and he said, "Well I guess you can stay because you are being generous with your delicious food."

Sam and his friends were so relieved and grateful that the ranger was so generous. From then on, they only tried to stay away from places where grills were banned.

Mrs. Jenny was a very busy lady. She had lots of tasks to do each day, from organizing her groceries to helping her kids with their homework. She was always trying to find a way to organize her tasks more efficiently.

One day, Mrs. Jenny had an incredible idea. She decided to make a list of all the tasks that she had to do each day. She wrote them all down on a big piece of paper and to make it easier, she divided the tasks into four categories.

Mrs. Jenny was excited to show her idea to her three year old daughter, Mandy. When Mandy came into the kitchen, Mrs. Jenny said, "Look Mandy, I made this list of tasks help me organize my day. Isn't it incredible?"

Mandy nodded her head in agreement. "Yes, It's so cool," she said. Then Mandy took the paper and started to put stickers on each task. Soon the sheet looked colorful and fun.

Mrs. Jenny smiled. She knew that with her task list, organizing her day would be much easier.

One day a wealthy man had a dream about a magical jungle. He wanted to see it for himself so he got on a plane and flew away.

When he arrived he saw a beautiful and colourful jungle filled with birds and monkeys. He was so happy and curious that he started to explore. 
He soon found a hidden cave filled with treasure. The man took as much as he could and left to go home. 

On the plane he looked at the treasure and laughed, remembering how beautiful the jungle was. But his laughter quickly stopped when the plane crash-landed. The man's wealth was all gone and he never saw the jungle again.
 
The man looked into the sky and said, "I will remember you forever, jungle!"

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Sam. They were both silly and full of energy. One day they saw a piece of cardboard and they decided to use it to make something. 

First, they used it to make a boat. They stepped inside and pretended to sail away to a magical island. Then, they stepped out of the boat and made a castle instead. They stepped up the stairs and pretended to be princes and princesses. 

Next, they made a plane with the cardboard and pretended to fly around the world. They were laughing and having fun as they stepped into it. Finally, they made a train out of the cardboard and stepped into it. They rode the train around the house and were having a silly time. 

When they were done, they stepped out of the train and looked at the piece of cardboard. They had a lot of fun with it, and they decided to write their names on it as a reminder. They smiled and hugged each other, and then they went off to play again.

Lily was a normal child who liked to talk a lot. She talked to her mom, her dad, her toys, and her friends. She talked about what she saw, what she felt, and what she wanted. She talked in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big dog with a red collar. She wanted to talk to the dog, so she ran to it and said, "Hi, dog! What is your name? Do you like to play?"

The dog looked at Lily and barked. He did not talk like Lily. He talked like a dog. Lily was confused. She asked, "Why don't you talk like me? Can you understand me?"

The dog wagged his tail and licked Lily's face. He did not understand Lily, but he liked her. He wanted to play with her. Lily giggled and hugged the dog. She said, "You are a nice dog. I like you too. Let's play!"

Lily and the dog played in the park. They ran, they jumped, and they rolled on the grass. Lily's mom watched them and smiled. She was happy that Lily made a new friend. She said, "Lily, you are a good child. You can talk to anyone and make them happy."

Once upon a time, there was a very adventurous boy. He wanted to have some fun, so he went to the forest. He saw a big piece of wood and he wanted to pull it. He grabbed hold of it and started to pull. He tugged and tugged, but the wood wouldn't move. He tried and tried, but he couldn't get it to budge!

Then a big, furry bear came along and saw what the boy was doing. He said, "Let me help you." He grabbed hold of the wood and pulled with all his might. With the bear's help, the wood moved a little.

The boy and the bear kept pulling, and before long, the wood started to move more and more. The boy was so happy that he clapped his hands and cheered. After a lot of hard work, the wood was finally free! 
The boy thanked the bear for all his help. They said their goodbyes, and the boy went home feeling very accomplished. What an adventurous day it had been!

Once upon a time, there was a driver who had an important job. He drove a bus full of people and always drove carefully. One day, the driver was feeling a bit tired from working so hard the day before. He decided to take a break and stopped his bus at the side of the road. Suddenly, he heard a harsh voice talking. He looked around and saw that the harsh talking was coming from a small and angry three-year-old. 

The driver asked the three-year-old why he was so upset. The little boy said that he was scared of getting back on the bus and being driven away. The driver felt bad and knew he had to make the little boy feel better. So he gave the three-year-old a big hug and talked in a gentle, friendly voice. He told the three-year-old that everything was going to be okay, and he should not worry. 

The driverâ€™s kind words made the three-year-old feel much better. He stopped feeling scared and, instead, felt full of joy. The driver invited the three-year-old back on the bus and he happily accepted. Everyone on the bus was very pleased with the driver and praised him for his kind and gentle words. They all drove off, happy and safe!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old. Every Saturday, her mom would take her to the park. One Saturday, Jane's mom brought a big ice-cream cake. It was very fragile so they had to be careful with it. 

When they got to the park, they found the perfect spot. They put the cake down on the grass and Jane wanted to help. She sat down, crossed her legs and began to fold the wrapping.

Jane's mom smiled as she watched her daughter concentrating and folding the wrapping so carefully. After a few minutes, the wrapping was all folded up. Then Jane's mom opened the fragrant ice-cream cake.

They both dug in and soon their faces were covered in ice-cream! Jane had so much fun that day and soon it was time to leave. She carried the wrapping with her and hoped that the next Saturday would be just as fun.

Mama and Daddy had a very special plan. They wanted to invite someone special to their house to play. But who should they invite?
