Mama and Daddy both had an idea. Mama wanted to invite Grandma, while Daddy wanted to invite the neighbour. Both of them were very stubborn.

"Let's ask the little one," Mama said with a smile. So they asked the three-year-old. The little one said: "Let's invite Grandma and the neighbour!"

Mama and Daddy felt better. So they invited both Grandma and the neighbour to come play outside in the grounds. But little did they know that the two were not very friendly.

When Grandma and the neighbour met on the ground, they were not very warm. They argued for a long time about who should be there to play. Mama and Daddy were very sad.

Suddenly the argument became so loud that Mama and Daddy had to intervene. The two got so mad that they decided that they would never step on the ground together again. 

Mama and Daddy were very disappointed. Their plan to have a special playday had gone wrong. They soon learned that being stubborn can have very bad results.

Johnny was a 3 year old boy who was always stretching his legs. He loved running and jumping around. But lately, he had noticed something very ugly in his backyard. It was an old fence that cost a lot of money. His family could not afford to replace it, so Johnny had a great idea.

He asked his dad if he could stretch the fence to make it bigger. His dad thought it was a good idea, so the two of them worked together. Johnny pulled and pulled on the fence until it was twice as long as it was before.

The ugly fence now looked much nicer. Johnny was very proud of what he had done and his dad was very proud of him too. From that day on, whenever there was a problem that was too expensive to fix, Johnny and his dad would always try to stretch it out and make it bigger.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine and watch the big, fluffy clouds go by. One day, she saw an ancient tree in the park and decided to go see it up close.

When she got there, she saw a man kneeling next to the tree. He was looking up at the branches and smiling. Lily asked him what he was doing and he said he was talking to the tree. Lily thought that was very funny, but the man explained that he believed the tree was very old and wise and had many stories to tell.

Lily thought about that for a while and then looked up at the clouds again. She wondered if they had stories to tell too. Maybe if she knelt down and listened closely, she could hear them whispering their secrets. So she knelt down and closed her eyes, and listened very carefully. But all she could hear was the sound of the wind blowing through the leaves of the ancient tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her plastic dolls. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. They sat down on a bench to rest and watch the other children play.

Lily saw a boy playing with an interesting toy. She wanted to play with it too. So, she went up to the boy and asked, "Can I play with your toy please?"

The boy smiled and said, "Sure, you can play with it with me!" Lily was happy and they played together for a while. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to the boy and thanked him for letting her play with his interesting toy. She went home with her mommy, feeling happy and rested.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big eye that he liked to look out of. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He saw a popular slide that all the kids were playing on. Timmy wanted to try it too, so he climbed up the ladder and went down the slide. He had so much fun that he wanted to do it again and again! 

After a while, Timmy's eye started to hurt. He looked in the mirror and saw that it was red. His mom took him to the doctor, who said he had a scratch on his eye. Timmy had to wear an eye patch for a few days so his eye could heal. He couldn't play with his friends, but they came to visit him and brought him toys to play with. Timmy was happy that he had such nice friends who cared about him.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was never very busy, but he still had dreams. Sometimes his dreams were scary nightmares.

One night in his dream he was walking down a long, dark road. Suddenly, he saw a big dragon. He was very scared and started to cry. But then the dragon smiled at him and gave him a hug. 

The dragon said, "It's okay. I just wanted to give you a hug." Then the dragon blew softly on the little boy and made the tears dry. 

The little boy laughed and thanked the dragon. The dragon told the boy to never be scared of his nightmares. With that, the dragon said goodbye and flew away. 

The little boy felt much better and didn't feel so busy anymore. He smiled and went to sleep, knowing that his nightmares weren't as scary as they seemed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl, named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to play outside. Every day, Lucy would let her imagination take her to wonderful places. 

One day, Lucy went to a park in her neighborhood. She was very careless and stumbled on the grass. Suddenly, she bumped into an old man who was sitting on the bench. He smiled at her and wrapped her in a hug. 

The old man was full of kindness and love. He said he wanted to share his joy with someone. He then asked Lucy to share a smile with him, so he could be happy. 

Lucy was so happy that she let her smile be as big as she could and said, "Yes! I will share my smile with you." The old man smiled and gave her a big hug. Lucy hugged him back. 

From that day forward, the old man and Lucy became good friends. They would spend time together at the park, and every time they were together, they would each put on a big smile. 

The old man's presence made Lucy so happy and provided her life with joy. He taught Lucy the importance of being kind, loving and careless. And whenever Lucy needed a friend, she knew that she could always go to the park and find her old friend waiting with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a soft teddy bear that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy accidentally ripped a hole in his teddy bear's arm. Timmy was sad because he thought his teddy bear was broken forever.

But Timmy's mommy told him not to worry. She said they could replace the ripped arm with a new one. Timmy was happy to hear that! They went to the store and bought a new soft arm for his teddy bear.

After they got home, Timmy and his teddy bear went for a ride in their jeep. They drove through the park and had so much fun! Timmy was happy that his teddy bear was fixed and they could play together again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a rude girl called Helen. One day, Helen was playing with her scissors. She wanted to cut a picture of her best friend, Jack. But as she cut, her scissors got stuck! 

Helen was frustrated and she shouted at Jack. She was very rude to him. Jack didn't like it and he ran away.

Helen chased after him, holding her scissors. But Jack was too fast and he managed to escape. So Helen stopped running and just stood still. 

She couldn't believe she had been so rude. Suddenly, she saw Jack a few metres away, looking at her sadly. Helen slowly smiled and waved at him. Jack smiled back and waved. 

The situation had ended. Jack and Helen both realised that being rude wasn't nice. They hugged and made up, then went off to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal little puppy named Pete. Pete was always so obedient, and he was so in love with his owner, Cindy.

Whenever Cindy asked Pete to do something, Pete always said yes. One day, Cindy asked Pete to take a bath in the river. She said, "Come on Pete, let's go bathe in the river!" 

So Pete and Cindy went down to the river. The water was cool and felt so nice on Pete's fur. But then, as Pete was bathing, something weird happened. He reached down into the water and pulled out an oyster! 

Cindy said, "Oh, Pete! What a loyal puppy you are! I'm so lucky to have you." Pete was so happy to hear that. 

And ever since then, Pete and Cindy have gone to the river to bathe every day!

Once upon a time, there was a neighbor. He was very messy. He never cleaned up after himself, and his house was often cluttered with things.

One day, his friends saw how messy he was and started to laugh. They were teasing him for being so untidy.

But, one of his friends stepped forward and said, "Wait! We don't need to laugh at our neighbor. We should support him instead!"

The other friends agreed and they helped him clean up his house. They even offered to come by to help him clean.

The moral of this story is that it is always better to support your friends instead of making fun of them. We all make mistakes, but it is important to help each other and be kind.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. But sometimes they fight over them. One day, they both want the same truck. They pull and pull, but the truck does not move. It has a knot in the string.

"Let go, it is mine!" Anna says.

"No, it is mine!" Ben says.

They pull harder and harder. The knot gets tighter and tighter. Then, snap! The string breaks and the truck splits in two. Anna and Ben fall back and cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see. She sees the broken truck and the sad twins. She hugs them and says, "I'm sorry, my loves. The truck is not available anymore. But I have an idea. Why don't you share these blocks? You can build anything you want with them. And you can help each other and have fun."

Anna and Ben wipe their tears and nod. They say, "Okay, Mom. We will share the blocks. And we will not fight anymore." They hug Mom and say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you."

Mom smiles and says, "I love you too, my loves. Now, let's go and build something amazing." She helps them pick up the blocks and they go to the living room. They start to build a castle, a bridge, and a car. They use their imagination and their teamwork. They are happy and proud of their creations. They forget about the truck and the knot. They only remember their love and their fun.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big truck with a loud horn. The truck was carrying many fruits and vegetables.

"Look, Ben, apples and bananas!" Mia said. "They are delicious. I want some."

"Me too," Ben said. "But we have to ask mom first. She is over there, on the bench."

They ran to their mom and asked if they could have some fruits. Mom said yes, but they had to be careful and not go too close to the truck.

"OK, mom," Ben and Mia said. They took a basket and followed the truck. They waited for the truck to stop at a red light. Then they quickly picked some apples and bananas from the back of the truck. They put them in the basket and ran back to their mom.

"Look, mom, we have fruits!" Ben and Mia said. They showed their mom the basket.

Mom smiled and hugged them. "You are very clever, Ben and Mia," she said. "But you know, you should not take things that are not yours. The truck driver worked hard to get those fruits. He might be angry if he sees that some are missing."

Ben and Mia felt sorry. They did not know that they did something wrong. They wanted to say sorry to the truck driver.

"Can we give the fruits back, mom?" Ben asked.

"Yes, you can," mom said. "That is very kind of you. Let's go and find the truck driver."

They followed the truck again, until they saw it parked at a store. They saw the truck driver getting out of the truck. He had a big hat and a beard.

"Excuse me, sir," mom said. "We have something to tell you."

The truck driver looked at them. He saw the basket of fruits.

"What is this?" he asked.

Ben and Mia told him what they did. They said they were sorry and they wanted to give the fruits back.

The truck driver was surprised. He did not expect that. He smiled and thanked them.

"That is very honest of you, Ben and Mia," he said. "You know, I have plenty of fruits. You can keep some for yourselves. And here, have some more. These are oranges. They are delicious too."

He gave them some oranges and put them in the basket. He also honked his horn and made them laugh.

"Thank you, sir," Ben and Mia said. They were happy and grateful.

They waved goodbye to the truck driver and went back to their mom. They shared the fruits with her and enjoyed them.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that it is wrong to take things that are not yours, and that it is good to say sorry and be honest. They also learned that fruits are delicious and that truck drivers are nice.

One morning, Bob went on a walk in the park. He was wearing bright yellow boots which matched the bright orange leaves on the ground. As he walked, he looked around and saw a shiny blue leg. He was very curious and he picked it up. It was heavy, like a rock.

Bob asked, "Who does this belong to?"

An old lady sitting nearby said, "That's my leg. I was taking a walk and it was so heavy that I had to leave it here."

Bob was very sad and he said, "Can I help you carry it home?"

The old lady smiled and said, "Thank you so much, Bob. You are a very kind boy." 

So Bob and the old lady walked side by side. Bob carried her leg and they both sang a happy tune. When they reached the old lady's home, Bob said goodbye with a big smile on his face.

The old lady looked at Bob and said, "You are a special boy. Thanks for making my walk home a little lighter." 

Bob waved goodbye and walked away feeling very happy. He had made a new friend and he had helped someone in need. What a wonderful day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big clock in her room that tick-tocked all day long. One day, Lily's mommy was very busy with work and couldn't play with her. So, Lily decided to study her favorite book about animals. She read about lions, tigers, and bears. The clock tick-tocked as she studied, and before she knew it, it was time for dinner. Lily was so happy that she learned so much from her book!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna who wanted to go out and explore the world. She admired the trees, the birds and the flowers. She especially loved the big brown butterflies that flew around her.

One day, as Anna was exploring, she saw a tall building with big brown gates. She asked her mother what it was, and her mother replied, "That is jail my dear. Jail is where people are sent when they do something wrong."

Anna felt sad for the people who were stuck behind the big jail gates. She felt like she should be helping them in some way, so she decided to be kind and generous to everyone she met.

She started to give away her toys whenever a friend needed them and shared her lunch with strangers who looked hungry. Soon, Anna's kindness spread and many people started to admire her.

The moral of the story is that being kind and generous can bring admiration and happiness. Anna teaches us to always stay generous and be kind to everyone, no matter where they come from.

One day there was a large guard. He was tall and had a big smile. He walked around the town and said hello to everyone he met.

One day he met a little girl. She was very small and had bright eyes. She asked the guard, "Will you play with me?" The guard said, "Yes, I would love to play with you!"

The guard then took the little girl to a river. He said, "Let me show you how to wash your hands." He showed her how to splash some water on her hands and how to rub them together. 

The little girl smiled and said, "This is fun!" The guard smiled back and said, "It sure is!"

After they finished washing their hands, the guard gave the little girl a hug. He said, "It was so nice to meet you. I'll see you around!"

The little girl smiled, waved goodbye, and ran back home. She was proud of herself for learning how to wash her hands.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie. The birdie had a shiny triangle on its beak that sparkled in the light. One day, the birdie flew to a big tree and saw a shiny bell. The bell could ring very loud and the birdie wanted to try it. 

But the bell was too big for the birdie to ring. So, the birdie flew up to the top of the tree and saw a small bell. The birdie rang the small bell and it made a beautiful sound. The birdie was happy and rang the bell again and again.

But soon, the birdie realized that it was getting dark and it was time to go home. But the birdie had been ringing the bell for so long that it had attracted a big cat. The cat pounced on the birdie and sadly, the birdie didn't make it. 

The moral of the story is that sometimes, we can have fun playing with things, but we need to be careful because it can attract danger.

Once there was a small bear. He found a seat at the side of the road. He sat down and looked around. Suddenly he heard someone calling: "Hello small bear, who are you?"

He looked up and saw a big bird. The bear was a bit scared but said: "I'm a small bear."

The big bird smiled. "I'm a big bird," he said. "I like to repeat the same things again and again. Would you like to join me?"

The bear thought for a moment and said: "Yes, I'll join you."

The big bird smiled again. "Great!" he said. "Let's start now. I'll say something and you must repeat it."

The bear nodded.

The big bird said: "It's fun to say things together!"

The small bear smiled and repeated: "It's fun to say things together!"

Once upon a time there was a lion. He was big and strong with a loud voice and bright yellow fur. Every day he would wake up early and roar up to the sky with all of his might, which everyone could hear.

Some of the animals living in the nearby forest were scared of the roaring, but one brave little songbird enjoyed it. She found the lion's roar lively and full of energy and eventually she started singing her own song in response.

The lion was happy to hear the little bird. He would roar and the bird would sing. And soon all of the other animals, from elephants to monkeys and even more songbirds, started joining in. The noise was happy and loud with everyone singing and roaring and playing together.

The lion and his animal friends had lots of fun making music together. Their song would go on until the sun went down and a peaceful nighttime win over the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy dog named Spot. Spot had a toy skull that he loved to play with. He would carry it around in his mouth and play fetch with it.

One day, Spot's owner, a little girl named Lily, did not permit Spot to play with his skull. She was afraid that he might break it. Spot was sad and missed his favorite toy.

Later, Lily saw how sad Spot was and decided to permit him to play with his skull again. Spot was so happy and wagged his tail. They played fetch together and had lots of fun. And from that day on, Spot and Lily played with the skull every day, and they were the best of friends.

Nanny took Bob and Sue to a restaurant. Their parents had to go to work and needed someone to look after them. Nanny ordered food for Bob and Sue and put it on the table with a napkin. Nanny explained to the two children that the napkin was for wiping their hands and face if needed.

Bob was very excited to start eating but Sue wanted to understand something. She wanted to eat her dinner fast, so she asked Nanny why she should use the napkin.

Nanny gently explained that it was important to use the napkin and not to rush when eating dinner. If they used the napkin they could enjoy the food and stay clean.

At the end of their dinner, Bob and Sue had both wiped their hands and face with the napkin. Both of them learnt that it was important to take their time and use the napkin when they ate. It was a valuable lesson and they will remember it in the future.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with many roots. The roots are like long arms that come out of the ground.

"Let's visit the tree," Sara says. "Maybe we can find some bugs or worms."

"OK," Tom says. "But be careful. The roots are hard and rough. They can hurt you if you fall."

They run to the tree and start to look for bugs or worms. They see some ants, a spider, and a snail. They are happy and curious.

"Look, Sara, I found a snail!" Tom says. "It has a shell and a slimy body. It moves very slow."

"Wow, Tom, that's cool!" Sara says. "Can I see it?"

Tom gives Sara the snail. Sara holds it in her hand and looks at it. She smiles.

"Hello, snail," she says. "You are cute and funny. Do you like the tree?"

The snail does not answer. It hides in its shell.

Suddenly, Sara trips on a root. She falls and drops the snail. The snail falls on a rock and breaks its shell. Sara and Tom are shocked and sad.

"Oh no, Sara, are you OK?" Tom asks. He helps Sara get up.

"I'm OK, Tom, but look at the snail!" Sara says. She points at the snail. The snail is still and quiet.

"Oh no, Sara, I'm sorry!" Tom says. He picks up the snail. The snail does not move.

"I'm sorry, too, Tom!" Sara says. She starts to cry. "We hurt the snail. We were not careful. We were bad."

They hug each other and cry. They feel sorry for the snail. They wish they could fix the snail.

They decide to bury the snail under the tree. They dig a small hole with their hands. They put the snail in the hole. They cover the snail with dirt and leaves. They say goodbye to the snail.

"Goodbye, snail," Sara says. "We are sorry we hurt you. We hope you are happy in the ground. We will not forget you."

"Goodbye, snail," Tom says. "We are sorry we hurt you. We hope you are safe in the ground. We will remember you."

They leave the tree and go back to their parents. They tell their parents what happened. Their parents hug them and comfort them. They tell them they are sorry for the snail, too. They tell them they are not bad, but they should be more careful. They tell them they are proud of them for being honest and kind.

Sara and Tom feel a little better. They learn a lesson. They promise to be more careful and respectful of the bugs and worms. They thank their parents and their friends. They still miss the snail. They hope the snail is OK.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with their bikes in the park. Lily had a pink bike with a basket and a bell. Sam had a blue bike with a pedal and a horn.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a big bike with a lot of stickers and lights. He rode very fast and made loud noises. He stopped near Lily and Sam and said, "Hi, I'm Max. Do you want to see my bike? It's the best bike in the world!"

Lily and Sam looked at his bike. They thought it was too flashy and noisy. They liked their bikes better. They said, "No, thank you. We're happy with our bikes. They're regular bikes, but they're fun."

Max was angry. He wanted them to admire his bike. He said, "Your bikes are boring and old. You don't know anything about bikes. You're silly and stupid."

Lily and Sam felt hurt by his words. They decided to ignore him. They rode away from him and went to the other side of the park. They played with their bikes and had a good time. They didn't care about Max and his bike. They were still best friends.

Lily was a big girl who liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She could stir the soup, wash the fruit, and set the table. But she was not allowed to touch the hot things, like the oven or the stove. Mom said they could burn her and make her cry.

One day, Lily wanted to surprise her mom with a cool plate. She saw a pretty blue plate in the cupboard and thought it would look nice with the soup. She reached for the plate, but it was too high for her. She got a chair and climbed on it, but she still could not reach the plate. She stretched her arm and stood on her toes, but she lost her balance and fell off the chair.

The plate fell with her and broke into many pieces. Lily was scared and hurt. She had a big bump on her head and a cut on her hand. She started to cry and worry. What if mom was angry with her? What if she had no more plates? What if she could not eat soup anymore?

Mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily on the floor, surrounded by broken glass. She was not angry, she was worried too. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, my sweetie. You are more important than any plate. I'm sorry you got hurt. Let me clean your wound and put a band-aid on it. Then we can have some soup and ice cream. I have more plates, don't worry. And you can pick a cool one for yourself."

Lily felt better and smiled. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are the coolest mom ever." Mom kissed her and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the bravest girl ever. But next time, please ask me for help if you want to reach something high. Okay?" Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry I broke the plate. Can I help you clean it up?" Mom said, "No, sweetie. That's too dangerous. You can help me with something else. How about you choose a cool spoon for the soup?" Lily said, "Yes, mom. I can do that." And they went to have a nice lunch together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to clean up his toys and put them away. Timmy didn't want to clean up because he wanted to keep playing. 

His mom said, "Timmy, if you clean up your toys now, you can gain extra playtime later." Timmy thought about it and decided to clean up his toys. He felt proud of himself for doing the right thing. 

As Timmy was putting away his toys, he noticed that his favorite toy was missing. He looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it. He felt sad and guilty because he didn't take care of his toy. 

Timmy went to his mom and said, "Mommy, I lost my toy. It's a symbol of my favorite thing to play with. I'm sorry for not taking care of it." His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. We can look for it together and maybe we can find it." Timmy felt better knowing that his mom was there to help him.

Lily liked to play with her tap. She had a big tub of water and some cups and spoons. She liked to fill the cups with water and pour them out. She liked to make bubbles and splashes. She liked to hear the tap go drip-drip-drip.

One day, Ben came to play with Lily. He saw her tap and wanted to play with it too. He asked Lily if he could borrow her tap. Lily said no. She did not want to share her tap. She liked her tap too much. Ben was sad and angry. He wanted to play with the tap.

Ben waited until Lily was not looking. He ran to the tub and grabbed the tap. He pulled it hard. He wanted to make the water come out faster. But he pulled too hard. The tap came off the tub. Water sprayed everywhere. The tap was broken. Lily saw what Ben did. She screamed and cried. She was very upset. She loved her tap.

Lily's mom heard the noise. She came to see what was wrong. She saw the water and the broken tap. She saw Lily crying and Ben looking sorry. She was not happy. She told Ben to say sorry to Lily. She told Lily to calm down. She told them both to play nicely. She took the broken tap and the tub away. She gave them some books and toys instead. She hoped they would learn to share and be careful.

Once there was a generous plastic. Everyone liked him because he was nice to everyone. One day he went out for a walk and he saw a big scare. He was so scared, he ran back to his house. He told his family all about it and they decided to help him.

The family took the plastic to the scare and they all said "Hello!" To the scare. The scare was so surprised, it started to smile. The scare realized that the plastic was very generous and that he was no longer scared.

From then on, the plastic and the scare became best friends. They would play together every day and the generous plastic helped keep everyone safe. It was a great reminder for everyone to always be generous.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly who was very excited. She was getting a new crib for her bedroom. She had kept it a secret from her mom, but she could not contain her joy.

That day, her mom took her to a store that had lots of cribs. Molly wanted to pick one out for herself. She gasped when she saw one with a canopy. It was pink, her favorite color. She knew it was the one for her.

Back at home, it was time to put the crib together. Her mom was busy trying to make sure everything fit together properly. Molly was eagerly waiting for the crib to be done. She was really excited!

All of a sudden, they heard a squeaking noise. It was Molly's brand new crib! They both smiled. Finally, Molly's room was ready and she couldn't wait to go to sleep. She grabbed her stuffed bear, climbed in and tucked herself in. Molly hoped that she would sleep well in her new crib.

Minty was a happy three-year-old girl. She loved playing with her toys and knitting with her mom. Today, she got a new ball of yarn to play with. She was very excited and she asked her mom, "What can I do with the yarn?"

Her mom smiled and said, "You can make something with it!" Minty was even more excited now. "Like what?" she asked.

"You can knit a scarf!" her mom answered. "Just rub the yarn with your fingers and you can make it into a string."

Minty rubbed the yarn with her fingers and started making her scarf. Her mom helped her a bit, but she mostly did it on her own. It was very mild and soft. When she was done, Minty had a beautiful scarf that was just perfect! She was very proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a fat pig. She loved to carry things. One day she found a diamond. It was so sparkly and special! She decided to carry it around with her everywhere she went. She showed her friends and everyone wanted to see the diamond too. 

The pig couldn't decide what to do with it, so she decided to put it in a box and keep it safe. She carried the box around with her everywhere she went. 

One day, she met a wise old owl. The owl told her that the diamond was very precious and that she should take good care of it. The pig thanked the owl and carried the box even more carefully. 

She showed everyone the diamond and everyone was very impressed that she had such a sparkly thing. The pig was very happy because she felt very proud of her diamond. 

She carried her diamond everywhere and was very careful with it. She always made sure it was safe and sound. She was the happiest when she was carrying her diamond.

Once upon a time there was an elderly grandma who liked to jog. She had a bright, shiny motorcycle that she liked to ride. She enjoyed taking trips in her motorcycle and going for jogs.

One day, Grandma was jogging around the park. She saw a little three year old girl running around the trees. Grandma stopped jogging and said hello to the girl.

The girl looked up at Grandma and smiled. She asked, â€œWhat is that big shiny thing you were riding?â€

Grandma explained that it was a motorcycle. She said, â€œI go for jogs with it to stay healthy and strong.â€

The little girl smiled and looked at Grandma with admiration. She said, â€œYouâ€™re so strong! I want to be as strong as you when I grow up.â€ Grandma smiled and said, â€œYou will be.â€

With that, the two said goodbye, and Grandma continued her jog while the little girl waved goodbye. Grandma smiled and thought to herself, â€œIâ€™m so lucky to have this motorcycle and to be able to jog.â€

Once upon a time there was a seed. It was small and round, and it lived in the dirt. Every day it grew bigger. The seed was filled with a special power - the power of space. 

Soon, the seed grew into a flower. Its petals were very beautiful, and its strong stem reached high into the air. The flower spread its petals wide, and it started to open. Inside was a deep, secret space. 

The flower stayed in the dirt, and its space slowly filled up with different things. Soon, that tiny secret space held many great things. It became a place to grow memories, happiness, and lots of love. 

The flower's special space was so deep that it filled the whole world. Everyone loved to visit the special flower, and they filled it with laughter and joy. 

And that is how the deep, special space started to grow.

The day was almost over and the sun was close to the horizon. As the sun slowly moved closer to the sky, Charlie was playing in the backyard. He was playing with his yellow toy truck and pushing it around in circles.

As he kept playing, the sky grew darker and the colors around him changed. He watched as the sun slowly disappeared and darkness spread over the sky. But just before the sun was gone, Charlie saw the most beautiful sight- a yellow sunset! 

He was mesmerized. He had never seen something so beautiful before. In that moment, he knew he would always remember the brilliant yellow sunset. 

He smiled from ear to ear and kept playing as the sky grew darker and darker. Even as the night came, he stayed there in the backyard playing with his truck. When it was time to go to bed, he snuggled in his bed and fell asleep with a special memory of the magical yellow sunset.

Once upon a time two friends, kids named Jack and Jill, were playing together. Jack was jumping into a pool, hoping to make a big splash.

Jill watched from the edge: "Jack, don't dive too deep!"

But Jack didn't listen and dived in as deep as he could.

Jill was worried so she followed Jack and dived after him. She caught up with him and they both bobbed up to the top of the pool together.

Jack smiled at Jill and said: "Thanks for finding me. You're very polite."

Jill laughed. "It's alright. We should stay at the top though, ok?"

Jack agreed. They swam around the top of the pool and had lots of fun. The time went too quickly and before they knew it, it was time to go home.

Both Jack and Jill hugged each other goodbye and promised to play together soon.

Once there was a kid. He wanted to swim in the ocean. But he felt guilty. He thought he didn't know how to swim. So he stayed on the beach.

But then he saw another kid in the water. That kid was swimming! He was having a lot of fun.

So the first kid got brave. He jumped into the water too! He tried to swim. And then he found out he could swim! He was so happy.

He swam and swam and then he went back to the beach. He was no longer feeling guilty. He had learned he could swim!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but he never listened to his mom when she told him to come inside before dark.

One day, Timmy was playing outside when he saw a big emergency truck with flashing lights. He wanted to see what was happening, so he ran towards it. But he didn't see the dark hole in the ground and he fell in.

Timmy tried to yell for help, but no one could hear him. He started to get scared and didn't know what to do. He tried to shrug his way out, but he couldn't.

Eventually, Timmy's mom realized he was missing and went outside to look for him. She found him in the hole and called for help, but it was too late. Timmy had learned a hard lesson - to always listen to his mom and be careful when playing outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved her blanket very much. It was warm and cozy, and she took it with her everywhere she went. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She was playing on the swings when she saw a little boy who looked very cold. 

Lily felt sad for the boy, so she went over to him and asked if he wanted to share her blanket. The boy was very grateful and snuggled under the amazing blanket with Lily. They played together for a while, and the boy went home feeling happy and warm. 

Lily's mom was very proud of her for sharing her blanket and helping someone in need. She explained to Lily that it's always nice to help others and to order your things in a way that you can share them with others. From that day on, Lily made sure to always bring an extra blanket with her to the park, just in case someone else needed it too.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with his tool, a ball of yarn. One day, Tom saw a little mouse named Jerry. Jerry took Tom's ball of yarn and ran away.

Tom said, "Give me back my tool!" But Jerry did not listen. Tom chased Jerry all around the house. They ran and ran, but Tom could not catch Jerry. Tom was sad.

In the end, Tom did not get his ball of yarn back. He had to suffer without his favorite tool. Tom was very sad and never saw his ball of yarn again.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max was a good dog who loved to play fetch with his owner. Max was also very reliable and always kept his owner safe. 

One day, Max saw a cat who looked very tasty. Max wanted to bite the cat, but his owner said no. Max knew he had to be a good dog and listen to his owner. 

Later that day, Max's owner accidentally spilled ink on the carpet. Max tried to help clean up the ink with his tongue, but it didn't work. Max's owner had to use a special cleaner to get rid of the ink. 

Max learned that even though he couldn't clean up the ink, he could still be a reliable and good dog by listening to his owner and not biting the cat.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the grass. One day, he found a treasure chest under a tree. He was so happy! He opened the chest and found shiny gold coins inside. Timmy decided to roll the coins on the ground. They made a fun sound as they rolled. Timmy thought the coins looked so fine and pretty. He put them back in the treasure chest and took it home to show his mommy and daddy. They were very proud of him for finding such a special treasure.

Tim and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. But Tim and Lily liked the penguins best. They watched them swim and slide on the ice.

"Can we feed them?" Lily asked Mom.

"No, sweetie, we can't. They have their own food," Mom said.

Tim saw a man with a bucket of fish. He was wearing a blue coat and a hat. He looked like he worked at the zoo.

"Maybe he can give us some fish to feed the penguins," Tim said. He ran to the man and said, "Hello, sir. Can we have some fish, please?"

The man smiled and said, "Sure, kid. You can have one fish each. But be careful, they might bite."

He offered Tim and Lily a fish from the bucket. Tim and Lily thanked him and walked to the penguin pool. They held the fish in their hands and waved them at the penguins.

The penguins saw the fish and came closer. They made loud noises and flapped their wings. Some of them jumped out of the water and tried to grab the fish.

"Wow, they are hungry!" Lily said.

But one penguin was different. He was smaller and quieter than the others. He stayed in the corner of the pool and looked sad.

"What's wrong with him?" Tim asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he is sick or lonely," Lily said.

She felt sorry for the little penguin. She decided to give him her fish. She walked to the edge of the pool and said, "Here, little penguin. This is for you. I hope you like it."

She threw the fish to the penguin. He looked surprised and happy. He caught the fish in his beak and ate it. He waddled to Lily and rubbed his head against her hand. He made a soft noise.

"Aw, he likes you!" Tim said.

Lily smiled and petted the penguin. He felt warm and soft. She said, "You're welcome, little penguin. You're very cute."

The penguin nodded and smiled. He followed Lily wherever she went. He wanted to be her friend.

But the other penguins were not happy. They were jealous and angry. They wanted more fish. They wanted Lily's attention. They started to chase the little penguin and peck at him. They made loud noises and flapped their wings.

"Hey, stop that!" Tim said. He tried to protect the little penguin. He said, "Leave him alone. He's our friend."

But the penguins did not listen. They kept attacking the little penguin. They made him cry.

Lily was scared and sad. She said, "Mom, Dad, help! The penguins are mean to the little penguin. They hurt him."

Mom and Dad heard Lily's cry. They ran to the penguin pool. They saw the penguins fighting. They saw the little penguin bleeding.

They called the man with the bucket. He came and said, "What's going on here?"

He saw the little penguin and said, "Oh, no. He's the new penguin. He just arrived yesterday. He's not used to the others. They don't like him. They bully him."

He picked up the little penguin and said, "Don't worry, little guy. I'll take you to the vet. He'll make you better."

He thanked Tim and Lily for feeding the little penguin. He said, "You're very kind, kids. You made him happy. He likes you. Maybe you can visit him again when he's well."

He took the little penguin away. Tim and Lily waved goodbye. They hoped the little penguin would be okay.

They hugged Mom and Dad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom and Dad. We didn't mean to cause trouble. We just wanted to feed the penguins."

Mom and Dad hugged them back. They said, "It's okay, Tim and Lily. We know you meant well. You did a good thing. You showed the little penguin some love. You're very brave and sweet."

They kissed Tim and Lily. They said, "We're proud of you, kids. We love you."

They left the zoo. They went home. They had a warm and cozy night. They dreamed of the little penguin. They hoped he would be happy. They hoped he would find some friends. They hoped they would see him again.

Once there was a girl who liked to take the subway. Every day she would use the regular subway. Every morning she would hop on the subway and go downtown. She would take the regular subway the whole way there.

One day, something special happened! Instead of taking the regular subway, she took a special one. It was called the express subway. On the express subway, she went much faster than she went on the regular one.

When she got downtown, she was very excited. She was happy that she had gotten there so quickly using the express subway.

From then on, she usually took the express subway. But every now and then, she would use the regular subway, so she could go at her own pace.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy called Jack. He loved to read magazines and shared them with his sister, Elsa. One day, Jack asked Elsa if they could read a magazine together.

Elsa said to Jack, â€œNo, I don't want to share. I want to keep it all to myselfâ€.

Jack was very sad and he didn't understand why his sister was being so selfish. He said, â€œBut we can discuss the magazine together and have fun!â€ 

Elsa thought about it and realized she was being rude and selfish. She said, â€œYou're right, let's read the magazine together and discuss itâ€.

So Jack and Elsa shared the magazine and enjoyed discussing it. They had a lot of fun and it was a good lesson for Elsa to learn that sharing is better than being selfish. The end.

Once upon a time there was a robot. It was very fancy. Every day the robot would pinch things. It would pinch flowers, books, and toys.

One day the robot got a surprise! It was a little 3 year old child! The child was excited to see the robot and the robot was excited too. They started to play together.

The robot showed the child all sorts of things. It showed the child how to pinch things and the child was so excited. The child pinched flowers, books, and toys and laughed.

At the end of the day the robot and the child said goodbye. The child was happy they got to play and the robot was happy too. They promised to meet again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy was playing with his toy car when he accidentally broke it. "Oh no!" cried Timmy. "My car is broken!"

Just then, a wild storm started outside. The wind was blowing and the rain was pouring down. Timmy's mom came into the room and saw that Timmy was upset. "What's wrong, Timmy?" she asked.

"My car is broken," Timmy said sadly. "But don't worry, we can fix it together," his mom said. They worked on the car while the storm raged outside, and soon it was as good as new. Timmy was so happy that he forgot all about the wild storm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look at the sky. One day, she saw a bird flying and she gazed at it for a long time.

Her mom came outside and asked her, "What are you doing, Lily?"

"I'm looking at the bird, Mommy," Lily said with a serious look on her face.

Her mom smiled and said, "What a beautiful year it has been for the birds. They are so happy in the sunshine."

Lily nodded and continued to gaze at the bird until it flew away. She was happy to have seen it and couldn't wait to see more birds in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play by the creek near her house. The water was always moving and restless, making splashing sounds. 

One day, Lily's friend Max came to play with her. Max wanted to play with Lily's favorite toy, but Lily didn't want to share. Max asked if she could lend it to him, but Lily said no. 

After a while, Lily realized that it wasn't very nice to not share with her friend. She decided to lend Max her toy for a little while. Max was very happy and they played together by the creek until it was time to go home. 

From that day on, Lily learned that lending her things to others could make them happy too. She felt proud of herself for being a good friend. And every time she played by the creek, she remembered the fun she had with Max and her restless toy.

Once upon a time, there was a man. He wanted to go for a swim, but when he looked, the pool seemed empty. He was very sad.

He looked around, and saw that the park was empty too. He decided to keep looking and found a pond. He was happy when he saw that the pond was not empty.

He took off his shoes, and put his toes in the water. The water was really cold, but it seemed nice. He started to swim around in the pond.

He swam around and around, and had lots of fun. After a while, he noticed it was getting dark, so he got out of the pond and put his shoes back on.

He was still happy that he had been able to swim in the pond. He waved goodbye and started to walk home. He was glad that he had found the pond. The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was only three years old, but she was very brave. One day, she decided to take a journey. She wanted to see what was beyond her village.

As she was walking and exploring, she came across a big door. It was very tight and it wouldn't open. She felt sad. She wanted to explore what was behind the door.

Then, an old woman appeared. She was dressed all in black. She said to Jane: "I can help you open the door if you give me some oil". Jane didn't know what oil was but she trusted the old woman. 

The old woman gave Jane a bottle of oil. Jane thanked her and put some of the oil on the door. She rubbed it in with all her strength and - magic! - the door opened. 

Jane was so happy. The old woman smiled and gave her a hug. Jane wanted to say thank you, but all she could do was give the old woman a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his drum. He would bang on it all day long. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy showed him his drum and his friend thought it was impressive. 

Suddenly, Timmy felt funny in his nose. He knew what was going to happen next. He sneezed! Achoo! His friend laughed and said, "Bless you!" Timmy wiped his nose and went back to playing his drum. 

They played together for a long time and had lots of fun. When it was time for Timmy's friend to go home, he said, "Thanks for letting me play with your impressive drum, Timmy. And don't forget to cover your mouth when you sneeze!" Timmy nodded and waved goodbye. He couldn't wait to play with his drum again tomorrow.

Tim and Jen like to play in the garden. They have a big tub of water and some toys. They splash and soak each other and laugh. They also soak the flowers and the grass. They think they are helping the garden grow.

But Mom does not like it. She sees the water running out of the tub and making a mess. She sees the flowers and the grass looking sad and droopy. She thinks Tim and Jen are wasting water and hurting the garden. She is angry and tells them to stop.

Tim and Jen are sad and confused. They do not want to make Mom angry. They do not want to hurt the garden. They want to have fun and be useful. They ask Mom what they can do.

Mom thinks for a moment. She sees a bucket and a shovel. She has an idea. She tells Tim and Jen to fill the bucket with water and use the shovel to dig a hole. She says they can make a pond for the frogs and the fish. She says that will help the garden and make it more beautiful.

Tim and Jen like the idea. They work together to fill the bucket and dig the hole. They pour the water into the hole and watch it fill up. They see a frog hop into the pond and a fish swim by. They are happy and proud. They think they are useful and creative. They hug Mom and thank her. Mom smiles and hugs them back. She thinks they are clever and kind. She is happy and proud too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden and look at the pretty flowers. One day, she saw a big yellow butterfly fluttering around. It was so pretty that she followed it around the garden. 

As she followed the butterfly, she saw a little bird sitting on a branch. The bird was singing a peaceful song. Lily stopped to listen to the bird's song and felt very calm. She realized that even though the butterfly was beautiful, the peaceful song of the bird made her feel even happier. 

From that day on, Lily loved to look at the flowers and listen to the birds in her garden. She found that it brought her a lot of peace and happiness. And every time she saw a yellow butterfly, she remembered the peaceful feeling she had when she listened to the little bird's song.

Tommy was grumpy. He did not want to go to bed. He wanted to watch TV with Mom and Dad. But Mom said, "No, Tommy, it is late. You need to sleep. Come on, let's go to the bathroom and brush your teeth."

Tommy followed Mom to the bathroom, but he was not happy. He did not want to brush his teeth. He wanted to play. He saw a towel on the rack. He had an idea. He grabbed the towel and wrapped it around his neck. He said, "Look, Mom, I am a superhero. I can fly and save the world."

Mom smiled. She said, "Wow, Tommy, you are a great superhero. You can perform amazing feats. But you know what else superheroes do? They take care of their teeth. They brush them every night before they go to bed. That makes them strong and healthy. Do you want to be a strong and healthy superhero, Tommy?"

Tommy thought for a moment. He liked being a superhero. He wanted to be strong and healthy. He said, "OK, Mom, I will brush my teeth. But can I keep the towel? I want to wear it in bed. Maybe I will have a dream about flying and saving the world."

Mom said, "Sure, Tommy, you can keep the towel. But only if you promise to sleep well and not stay up too late. Deal?"

Tommy nodded. He said, "Deal, Mom. Thank you. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Tommy. Good night, my superhero."

She kissed him on the forehead and tucked him in. She turned off the light and left the room. Tommy closed his eyes and hugged the towel. He felt less grumpy. He felt happy. He fell asleep and dreamed of flying and saving the world.

Once upon a time there was a colorful plastic duck. Every day, the duck would go for a swim in the puddle. But each time it got out, it would be all slimy and covered in mud.

One day, the duck's mother saw all the mud and knew it was time to give the duck a wash. She filled up the bath and put in some bubbles. Then she put the duck in the bath water and began to scrub it with a sponge.

The duck felt scared but it also felt good to be in the warm, soapy water. Soon it began to feel squeaky clean and its yellow and orange colors shone brightly again.

The duck's mother took it out of the bath and dried it off with a towel. The duck felt so much better and happy to be clean again!

One day, a little girl was playing with her doll. She bounced it up and down in her hands. The doll was a special one, with a smiley face painted on it.

Suddenly, the doll started to bounce up and down by itself! The little girl was so surprised, she dropped the doll in confusion.

The doll stopped bouncing and said, "Hello!" The little girl was even more confused.

"Who are you?" she asked.

The doll replied, "I'm your new friend. Can I come play with you?"

The little girl thought for a moment, but then she smiled and said, "Yes please!"

She hugged the doll and they played together for the rest of the day. They even bounced up and down together!

Once upon a time, there was a modest house. Inside the house was a family of four. Mum, Dad, brother and sister. They were a close family and spent a lot of time together. 

One day, the family were admiring the view from their garden. They were so impressed by how beautiful it was. The little brother said "I want to keep this view forever". 

His sister disagreed, "How do you do that?" she asked. 

The brother thought for a moment and then replied, "I think the best way to keep it is to value it". 

The family all looked at each other, agreeing that this was indeed the best way to admire and care for the view they loved so much. From then on they made sure they showed they valued what they had and kept the view close to their hearts. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Mittens. Mittens was very soft and loved to cuddle with Lily. One day, Lily and Mittens went to the store to buy some candy. Lily had some money to spend, so she bought a big bag of lollipops. Mittens tried to grab one, but Lily told her no. 

As they were walking home, Lily realized she lost one of her mittens. She looked and looked, but couldn't find it. Mittens tried to help, but she didn't know what a mitten was. Lily was sad because her hands were cold without her mitten. But then, Mittens had an idea! She ran back to the store and found Lily's mitten on the ground. She brought it back to Lily and she was so happy! 

Lily hugged Mittens and thanked her for being such a good friend. They went back home and snuggled up with their lollipops. Mittens even got a little lick of one, but just one!

Once upon a time, there was a crane. The crane was very big and had a long neck. It liked to pick up heavy things with its beak and move them around. One day, the crane was feeling very tired and needed to rest. It found a cozy spot near a pond and took a nap.

While the crane was sleeping, a little girl came by with her mommy. She had a toy camera and wanted to record the crane. She pressed a button and heard a click. The crane woke up and looked at the little girl. It wasn't scared, it just blinked its eyes and went back to sleep. The little girl was happy that she could record the crane and showed her mommy the picture.

Once upon a time, there was a little fairy named Lily. She was very pretty and loved to fly around the garden. However, she was also very careless. One day, she accidentally knocked over a flower pot and made a big mess.

The other fairies were upset with Lily and told her to settle down and be more careful. But Lily didn't listen and continued to fly around without a care in the world.

One day, while flying too close to a spider's web, Lily got stuck. She tried to wiggle free, but it was no use. She was scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, her fairy friends came to her rescue and helped set her free.

From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful and never flew too close to spider webs again. She settled down and became a more responsible fairy. The other fairies were proud of her and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was an old man who lived in the forest. One day, he saw a hoop lying on the ground. He asked the hoop, "What are you doing here?"
The hoop replied, "I was dropped by a little girl who was playing."
The old man looked around, but he couldn't see the girl anywhere. He asked the hoop, "Where did she go?"
The hoop replied, "She ran into the woods."
The old man said, "I will help you find her. Follow me!"
The old man and the hoop began running through the woods together. After a while, the old man found the little girl.
The old man asked, "What are you doing out here all alone?"
The little girl replied, "I wanted to find more hoops to play with."
The old man smiled and said, "Well, we found one!" He picked up the hoop and handed it to the little girl. She was so happy that she hugged the old man.

The old man winked and said, "Well, what are you waiting for? Let's play!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was only three years old and he loved going to the beach.

When he got to the beach he started looking for shells. He stopped when he saw one that was a perfect fit for his hand. He tried to pick it up but it was stuck. He shook it and shook it but it wouldn't come lose.

Suddenly a voice answered. The shell was magical and had a special treasure inside! The little boy was so excited! He opened the shell and found a small toy car inside. It was the perfect fit for him!

He raced around with the car, showing it to all of his friends. From that day forward the little boy was sure to always keep his shell close by and remind himself of the magical surprise inside.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big ball that they threw to each other. One day, they saw a beautiful sunset in the sky. It had many colors, like red, orange, yellow, and pink. They wanted to keep the sunset forever.

"Let's catch the sunset with our ball!" Tom said.

"How can we do that?" Lily asked.

"Easy! We just throw the ball very high and fast, and it will touch the sunset. Then the ball will have the colors of the sunset, and we can bring it home!" Tom said.

Lily was not sure, but she followed Tom. They ran to a hill and threw the ball as hard as they could. The ball flew up in the air, but it did not touch the sunset. Instead, it hit a big bird that was flying by. The bird was angry and scared. It grabbed the ball with its claws and flew away.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Tom shouted.

"Give it back, please!" Lily cried.

But the bird did not listen. It flew far away, and they could not see it anymore. Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They had lost their ball and their sunset. They ran back home, hoping that their mom could restore their ball and their sunset.

But their mom could not. She told them that they had been foolish and greedy. She said that they could not catch the sunset with their ball, because the sunset was not a thing. It was a light that came from the sun and the clouds. She said that they had hurt the bird and made it fearful. She said that they had to learn to share and respect nature. She said that they had to say sorry to the bird and hope that it would forgive them.

But Tom and Lily did not say sorry. They did not care about the bird or the sunset. They only cared about their ball. They went to bed, still sad and angry. They did not know that the bird had a nest on a tree near their house. They did not know that the bird had a baby bird that was hungry and cold. They did not know that the bird had used their ball to make a warm and colorful bed for its baby. They did not know that the bird and its baby were happy and grateful. They did not know that the next day, the bird would fly over their house and drop their ball on their lawn, as a way of saying thank you and sorry. They did not know that they had missed a chance to make a new friend and see a new sunset. They did not know that they had made a bad choice that would make them unhappy for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse named Timmy. Timmy was always scared of everything and everyone. He would hide in his little hole all day, every day.

One day, Timmy saw a big cat walking towards him. He was so scared that he didn't know what to do. He thought about running away, but he knew the cat was faster.

Just then, Timmy remembered something his mommy had told him. She said that if he ever felt scared, he should answer with courage. So, Timmy took a deep breath and stood up to the cat. To his surprise, the cat just walked away.

From that day on, Timmy was no longer scared of anything. He learned that sometimes, even the smallest of creatures can have the biggest courage.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient lake. One day, a fish jumped out of the lake and started to splash around. It was having so much fun!

The fish saw a rail by the lake and swam over to it. Then, it decided to climb the rail. The fish tried its best and eventually, it was able to climb to the top. From there, it had a great view of the ancient lake and the beautiful scenery around it.

The fish stayed on the rail for a while, looking at the lake and the surroundings. Then, it decided to jump back in. It made a big splash as it hit the water. The fish was happy and started to swim around again.

The fish decided to stay in the ancient lake forever. It swam around happily and splashed around in the water all day.

Lily was a friendly girl who liked to help others. One day, she saw a boy who was sad in the park. He had lost his note from his mom. The note said when to go home and what to eat for lunch. Lily wanted to cheer him up, so she gave him a hug and a cookie.

They played together for a while, until Lily saw a piece of paper under a slide. She ran to get it, hoping it was the boy's note. But she did not see the puddle of water on the ground. She slipped and fell into the puddle. She got wet and dirty and hurt her knee.

The boy saw what happened and ran to help her. He took the paper from her hand and looked at it. It was his note! He was so happy and grateful. He thanked Lily and helped her get up. He said he was sorry she slipped and got hurt. He gave her his jacket to keep her warm and dry.

Lily smiled and said it was okay. She was glad she found his note and made him happy. She said he was a good friend. They walked together to the boy's home, where his mom was waiting. She gave them both a hug and a sandwich. She said they were very kind and brave.

Lily and the boy learned that helping others can make you happy, even if you slip and get hurt. They also learned that friendship is a precious gift that can make you feel better. They decided to play together again soon and share more cookies and notes.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to climb it.

"Let's go up the hill!" Anna said. "It will be fun!"

"OK!" Ben said. "But we have to be careful. The hill is steep and rocky."

They put on their shoes and hats and ran to the hill. They started to climb. They held hands and helped each other. They saw birds and flowers and bugs. They were happy.

But then, they came to a hard part. The hill was very high and slippery. Anna was scared. She wanted to go back.

"Ben, let's go back!" Anna said. "This is too hard. I don't like it."

"No, Anna, let's keep going!" Ben said. "We are almost there. I want to see the top. It will be beautiful."

Ben was stubborn. He did not listen to Anna. He pulled her hand and tried to make her climb. Anna did not want to. She cried and kicked and screamed.

"Ben, stop it! You are hurting me! You are not nice!" Anna said.

"Anna, stop it! You are silly! You are not brave!" Ben said.

They fought and fought. They did not have fun. They did not see the top. They did not arrive.

A man was walking by. He heard them and saw them. He was kind. He came to help them.

"Hello, children. What is wrong?" he said. "Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben stopped fighting. They told him what happened. They were both sad and sorry.

The man smiled. He hugged them and said, "It's OK. You are both good children. But you have to learn to listen to each other and respect each other. Sometimes, you have to compromise and cooperate. Sometimes, you have to give up and go back. Sometimes, you have to try and go on. But you always have to be kind and gentle and safe. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They understood. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They thanked the man and said goodbye. They went back to their house. They were friends again. They learned a lesson. They were happy.

"Mommy, what are we having for dinner?" asked the three-year-old.
"Your favorite dish - macaroni and cheese," replied mommy.
"Yay!" the child said with a big smile.

Mommy took the child outside to the backyard. The child could smell something delicious, but they couldn't see anything.
"Mommy, where is dinner?" asked the child, puzzled.
"It's a secret! See if you can find it," Mommy said.

The child began exploring the backyard. After a few minutes, the child saw a small, hidden table with the macaroni and cheese.
"I remember this spot - it's where we had dinner last year!" the child said excitedly.
"You found it!" said Mommy. "Let's enjoy our dinner!"

John was a three year old who loved playing games. One day, he was visiting his grandmother. She was an old woman who lived in a big house with lots of rooms and things. In her living room, there was a vase on the table. It was a perfect vase, with bright colors. John was so excited to see the vase and he asked his grandmother if he could have it.

His grandmother said, "Yes, but first you must wipe it clean." So John found a wipe and he carefully wiped the vase until it sparkled. He was very proud of his work.

After he finished wiping the vase, John went off to play with his toys, happy with his perfect vase. From then on, he kept it forever and thought it was the most special thing he had ever seen!

Once upon a time there was a big, scary monster. It had big, sharp teeth and big, scary ears. It lived in a forest far away from a little village. 

The people in the village were scared of the monster and they tried to stay away from the forest. But one day a little girl called Sarah was lost and she ended up in the forest. 

The monster saw Sarah and he wanted to eat her because she looked so yummy. He chased her and Sarah was so scared. But then Sarah remembered she had her big, strong dad at home and she shouted at the monster. 

The monster was so shocked he ran away and Sarah was safe. Sarah ran back home to her dad and she never went back to the forest again. She knew it was a dangerous place to be.

Once upon a time, a zebra was walking in the hot sun. She was very tired and thirsty. Suddenly, she noticed a quiet lake shining in the sun. She decided to go and have a drink. When she got there, the cool, clear water was so refreshing. She drank and drank and felt much better.

The zebra opened her eyes and saw the lake was still shining in the sun. The lake was so beautiful! She decided to take a swim. She slowly stepped into the lake and the cool water felt so good. She swam around for a while then got out and lay in the sun.

The sun felt good and the zebra was so happy. As she lay there quietly, she was thankful for the shining lake that had made her feel so much better. She stayed until the sun went down, then she said goodbye and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his scooter and would ride it every day. One day, Timmy saw a big, wide hill and wanted to zoom down it on his scooter. 

But as he started to zoom down the hill, he realized he couldn't stop! His scooter was going too fast and he was scared. Timmy tried to put his feet down to stop, but they just kept going. 

Suddenly, Timmy saw a big tree in his path. He closed his eyes and braced for impact, but then he heard a loud "whoosh!" and felt himself lifted into the air. When he opened his eyes, he saw that his scooter had hit a rock and launched him into a pile of leaves. 

Timmy was a little scared and had a few scratches, but he was okay. He realized that sometimes, it's better to go slow and be safe than to zoom too fast and get hurt. From then on, he promised to always wear his helmet and be careful on his scooter. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a bear and a frog. They both loved the outdoors. When it was warm, they liked to go for walks in the woods and play in the sunshine.

As time passed, the temperatures got cooler and the days became shorter. The bear and the frog knew that the season was changing. They knew that the leaves on the trees would start to fall and become crunchy.

The bear and the frog started to talk about their favorite season. The bear said winter was his favorite because he could build snowmen and go sledding. The frog thought summer was his favorite because he loved to swim in the pond and explore the garden.

The friends had a funny argument about which season was the best. Finally, they decided that every season had something fun to offer and they both agreed that exploring outside was always a good time!

Once upon a time there was a dog named Max. He was a very happy pup and liked to bark and play all day.
Max was walking in the park one day when he saw an old man making a cake. The man was using a mixer to mix all the ingredients together.

Max started to bark loudly and the man became very angry. He shouted at Max in a very rude way.

Max was too scared to stay any longer and ran away as fast as he could. He rushed and rushed until he was safe at home.

Max's mom asked what had happened, and Max told her the story. She said, "It's never ok to be so rude, but if you see the old man again, just remember to stay away and hurry home!"

One day there was a humble triangle. It was small but had plenty of uses.

"My triangle is the best!" said a 3-year-old.

The triangle kept its calm and kept on being humble. It said nothing, because it knew it could be used in different ways.

The 3-year-old then picked up the triangle and used it to make a paper airplane. She was so delighted and said, "Oh wow! Look at my triangle, it made a great paper airplane!" 

The triangle was still content and humble. It was happy that it could be used to make something so cool. It was the perfect shape for it. 

The 3-year-old thanked the triangle for being so useful. The triangle smiled knowing it had made someone so happy.

Once there was a young boy named Peter who loved to explore every nook and cranny of his house. One day, he found a mysterious knob on the wall. He asked his mum, "What is this knob for?"

Mum smiled and said, "Let's see, Peter." She wrapped a delicious red ribbon around it and then said, "Now try turning it."

Peter loved the way the ribbon felt and gave the knob a slight twist. The wall suddenly slid open, and behind it was a delicious surprise. A huge chocolate cake sat on a table, tempting him to take a bite.

Peter couldn't believe it. He snatched up the slice of cake and said, "Wow, Mum! This is so delicious!"

Mum laughed and said, "Sometimes, you just have to find a way to wrap up surprises."

Once upon a time, there was a monster. It was big and scary, and it made everyone feel uncomfortable. One day, the monster wanted to try something new. It wanted to learn how to fold.

So the monster found a piece of paper and put it flat on the floor. Then it slowly folded one side up. The monster was very happy that it had figured out how to fold!

But then a problem happened. The monster had folded the piece of paper too much and it no longer fit on the floor! The monster felt upset and uncomfortable. How could it get out of this?

At last, the monster had an idea. It carefully unfolded the paper until it was flat again and the monster was back on the floor. Everyone was happy that the monster had learned how to fold!

Peter was floating out in the ocean, further and further away from shore. He couldn't see anybody, only the endless blue of the sea. He was starting to feel scared. Suddenly, he noticed a white anchor bobbing in the current. He felt reassured that he was not alone as he held onto the anchor. He felt the weight of the anchor and enjoyed the steady feeling it gave him. Little by little, he was carried closer and closer to shore. Soon enough, he could see the white sand of the beach. With strength, the anchor pulled Peter to the beach and he was safe. Feeling happy again, Peter waved goodbye to the white anchor and ran to the shore.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived an elderly lady with her sister. They were very close and loved to take walks together. Every day, they would hold hands and walk around their garden, looking at the pretty flowers.

One sunny day, the elderly lady's sister saw a big, red ball in the garden. She wanted to take it home and play with it. But the elderly lady said, "No, we should not take things that are not ours."

The sister did not listen and took the ball home. They played with the ball all day, laughing and having fun. But soon, a little boy came to their house, crying. He said the ball was his and he had lost it.

The elderly lady and her sister felt very sad for taking the ball. The boy was angry and took his ball back. The sisters learned that it is not good to take things that do not belong to us. From that day on, they always remembered to be kind and honest.

Once upon a time, there was a nice woman named Lily. She had a car and loved to drive it around. One day, she saw a little girl named Mia walking on the street. 

"Hello there!" said Lily. "Do you want a ride?"

"Yes, please!" replied Mia.

So, Mia hopped into the car and they drove around together. They saw many things along the way, like trees, birds, and other cars. 

"This is so fun!" exclaimed Mia.

"I'm glad you're enjoying it," said Lily with a smile.

After a while, they arrived at Mia's house. 

"Thank you for the ride, nice lady!" said Mia.

"You're welcome, little one. Anytime!" replied Lily.

And with that, Mia went inside her house, happy from her nice ride with the friendly woman.

One day, Dad and Jane went to the beach. Jane was excited to build sandcastles and jump in the ocean. When they arrived, Dad put Jane's cooler in a safe place. He said, â€œNow that we are here, letâ€™s pay for the sunscreen.â€

But then Jane noticed something. Someone was trying to steal the cooler! â€œNo!â€ Jane shouted. She ran over to the cooler and yelled at the man to stop.

The man apologized and said, â€œI didnâ€™t mean any harm.â€ Dad stepped in and said, â€œThatâ€™s ok, but please donâ€™t take things that donâ€™t belong to you. Pay for the things you need.â€ The man agreed and left.

Dad and Jane went back to the beach. Jane was happy that her cooler was safe. She knew that it was important to pay for the things she needed, instead of taking them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a delicate teacup that she loved to drink her tea from. One day, she accidentally dropped the teacup on the table and it broke into many pieces. Lily was very sad and started to cry.

Her mom asked her, "Why are you crying, Lily?"

"My teacup broke," replied Lily.

"Don't worry, we can fix it," said her mom.

"But how? It's in so many pieces," said Lily.

"We can use glue to put it back together. First, we need to weigh all the pieces to make sure we have everything," explained her mom.

So, they carefully gathered all the broken pieces of the teacup and weighed them. Then, they used glue to put the teacup back together. Lily was so happy to have her teacup back on the table again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to put the dirty dishes in the dishwasher. 

Lily was very patient and carefully placed each dish in the dishwasher. As she was putting the dishes away, she observed a tiny ant crawling on the counter. 

Lily watched the ant for a while and then gently picked it up and put it outside. Her mommy was so proud of her for being kind to the little ant. From that day on, Lily always observed the bugs in her backyard and made sure to be patient and gentle with them.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Leo and Fred. They loved playing together. One day, Leo asked Fred to come to  his house. Fred was excited and he immediately followed Leo.

When they arrived at Leo's house, Leo went to get something from inside. He came back with a large box and said, "Look what I have here!" Fred was curious, and he opened the box. Inside, there was a small, fragile knife.

Leo said, "This knife will unite us forever!" He explained that no matter what happened, they would always be friends. Fred was touched and he immediately hugged Leo. Suddenly, the knife started to glow.

Leo and Fred knew that the knife was magical and it would unite them forever. They held hands and smiled, knowing that nothing would ever be able to keep them apart.

The little boy was very weak. He wanted to pick something up off the bookshelf but he couldn't lift it. He asked his father to help. His father came over and looked at the bookshelf. He was strong and he could pick it up with no problem. The little boy was happy he didn't have to do it himself. 

The father put the bookshelf down and showed the little boy how to hold it and pick it up without being so weak. He put his hands on either side of the bookshelf and, using his legs and back, he picked it up and carried it. 

The little boy was very happy. He was so proud that he was able to pick the bookshelf all by himself. He hugged his dad and thanked him. He knew he could do it but he was still very weak. He was happy he could do it with a little help from his dad.

Once there was a man who was very tired. His name was Tim. He had been running around all day long. Now he was at home and he sat down in his chair.

Tim was very frustrated. He wanted to take a nap. But his tire was flat. He looked at it, and it was all squished in. He couldn't figure out what to do.

Suddenly, he had a great idea! Tim went to his friend Sally's house. She had a tire pump. He asked if he could borrow it. She said, "Yes, of course!"

Tim took the tire pump to his tire and he pumped it up. It was so nice to have the tire all fixed. Now he could take a nap and rest.

He was so happy that he had found a way to fix his tire. He thanked Sally and was grateful for her help. Tim was no longer tired and frustrated. He was happy and content.

Once there were two volcanoes. They were very competitive and wanted to be the biggest. They spewed ash and smoke up into the sky. The ash was so dark that it blocked the sun from the towns below. Everyone was worried.

The bigger volcano made the situation worse. It became very angry and started to burn everything in sight. Trees and houses were becoming engulfed in flames. People ran and tried to get away from the fire.

Finally, the sun came out again. The bigger volcano was quiet now. Everyone was so relieved that the burning had stopped. They all came together to celebrate because they were now safe. 

The smaller volcano was also quiet and happy that the burning had stopped. But it was still competitive. It wanted to be the biggest volcano. So it started to spew more smoke and ash into the air. Everyone looked up at the volcano and cheered!

Once upon a time there was a bird that could fly. The bird flew so high up into the sky and over the sea.

The bird flew over the house of a strange man. The man was sitting on the beach, looking out to the sea in peacefulness. 

The bird liked to watch the man every day. He would sit perfectly still, enjoying the peacefulness of his surroundings.
