One day, the bird flew down closer to the man and they talked. It was the first time they spoke and they became very good friends. 

They laughed, talked and flew together all around the world. The bird and the stranger shared a peaceful friendship that would last a lifetime.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was 3 years old and loved cherries. Every day he would eat cherries and clean up afterwards. Today, Jack had a plan. He wanted to find a cherry tree and pick as many cherries as he could.

He looked around for the tree and soon saw one nearby. It was filled with cherries! Jack was so excited. He scampered over to the tree and started to pick the cherries. He picked the fruit until his basket was full and then he cleaned up all the fallen cherries.

When he was finished picking, Jack was so happy. He had lots of cherries! He said to himself, "I should go and get some more cherries. I will do this every day and repeat the same thing!"

And that's exactly what he did. Every day Jack would go and pick cherries, then go back home, clean up and store away his cherries. He was so proud of himself and loved to eat the sweet and delicious cherries!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a lollipop that was her favorite treat. One day, she left her lollipop in the sun and it became warm. When she tried to eat it, it was too gooey and sticky. She started to cry because she couldn't eat her lollipop. Her mommy came and gave her a new one that was cool and easy to eat. Lily was happy again and stopped crying. From then on, she made sure to keep her lollipops in a cool place so they wouldn't get warm and gooey again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to take walks. One day, she went for a walk to the edge of town. When she got there, she found a tall gray hotel. The hotel was so tall that it touched the sky!

The little girl wanted to explore the hotel, so she walked around the building to try and find a way in. Suddenly, she saw a door! She stood up straight and tried to reach the doorknob, but it was too high.

Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her! It was an old man who was standing in the doorway. He said, "Come in little one, you are welcome here!" The little girl smiled and went inside.

Inside the hotel was so much to explore. Every corner was filled with surprises. After a long day at the hotel, the little girl was ready to go home. But before she left, she promised to come back and explore some more.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Max. Max loved to play with clay. He would make all sorts of things with it like balls and animals. Max's mom would always prepare a clean space for him to play with his clay. 

One day, Max's friend came over to play. His friend also loved to play with clay. Max's mom prepared another clean space for his friend to play. Max and his friend had so much fun playing with the clay. They made a big castle together. 

After they were done playing, Max's mom prepared a clean-up station for them to clean their hands. They washed their hands and said goodbye to each other. Max was happy that he got to play with his friend and his clay in a clean space.

Once there was a baby who was very sleepy. She wanted to go and see the stadium, but she was too sleepy to walk. So she decided to crawl instead. She crawled and crawled until she arrived at the stadium. There were lots of people there and she was so excited! She crawled around and around to explore the stadium and she was very happy. When she was done exploring, she curled up in a corner and fell asleep. She was so happy and content after her adventure at the stadium.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Finn. Finn was an adorable fish who lived in the big sea. He had many friends, but he missed his best friend, Sam the shark. Sam went away to find food for his family.

One day, Finn decided to find Sam. He swam far away from his home. He asked other fish if they saw Sam, but no one knew where he was. Finn felt sad and missed Sam even more.

Then, Finn saw a big shadow. He thought it was Sam and swam fast to see him. But it was not Sam. It was a mean shark who wanted to eat Finn. Finn tried to swim away, but the mean shark was too fast. The mean shark ate Finn. Finn never got to see his best friend Sam again.

Once upon a time there was a little three year old boy named John. John loved to play outside, jump in puddles and laugh. One day, John started to feel very sick. He coughed and coughed until his parents had to take him to the hospital. 

At the hospital, the doctors put John in a big bed and checked him all over. He was suffering a lot and couldn't feel like playing any more. His parents were very worried. 

The doctor said "John is not feeling very good, he needs to stay in the hospital for a few days while we take care of him". John was very scared. 

"Is it going to hurt?" he asked the doctor. The doctor replied, "I'm sorry, it might be a bit uncomfortable, but we'll do our best to make sure you stay strong," he said.

John then looked deep into his parents' eyes and he knew he was going to be okay. He stayed in the hospital and with rest and care, his suffering was cured. He could soon leave the hospital and go back to his happy, jumping and laughing life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She met a boy named Jack who was sad because he lost his toy car. Lily wanted to help Jack find his car, so they looked for it together. After a while, they found the car and Jack was happy again. 

Suddenly, Lily's mom called her to go home. She said goodbye to Jack and gave him a big hug. Jack said, "Thank you for helping me find my car. You are a good friend." Lily smiled and said, "I am happy to help you." 

On her way home, Lily saw a bee and tried to catch it. But the bee stung her hand and it hurt a lot. Lily started to cry and her mom tried to comfort her. She said, "Don't worry, the pain will go away soon." But Lily's hand got more and more bitter, and she had to go to the hospital. 

At the hospital, the doctor tried to help her, but it was too late. Lily's hand got worse and worse, and she had to stay in the hospital for a long time. Jack came to visit her and brought her a new toy car, but Lily was too sick to play with it. Finally, Lily got better, but she never forgot the bitter bee sting.

Once upon a time, in a small country, there lived a kind dog named Spot. Spot was very tired because he helped everyone in the country. He did not mind helping his friends, but he needed to rest.

One day, Spot met a wise old cat named Whiskers. Whiskers told Spot, "You are a good dog, but you must rest too. If you are too tired, you cannot help your friends well." Spot listened to Whiskers and thought he was right.

From that day on, Spot learned to take breaks and rest when he felt tired. He still helped his friends in the country, but he also took care of himself. And everyone was happy. The moral of the story is that it is good to help others, but you must also take care of yourself.

Once upon a time, there was an old painter. He was very busy because he wanted to make the world look beautiful. Every day he painted colourfully on walls and roofs.

One day, the old painter needed to count how many paint buckets he had. He searched high and low but still couldn't find them. He was feeling sad and had a big frown on his face.

Just then, a little 3 year old ran up to him. The old painter was so surprised to see the little one. The little one asked "What are you looking for?".  The old painter replied, "I'm looking for my paint buckets to count".

Seeing the painter's sad face, the 3 year old child said, "Don't worry, I can help you count", and he started counting the paint buckets in twos. With the little one's help, the old painter was able to count all the paint buckets. 

The old painter was so delighted, he thanked the 3 year old with a big hug! From then on, the old painter and the 3 year old were best friends.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play with their dog, Rex. Rex is a big, black lab. He is very friendly and smart.

One day, Sam and Ben find a big box in the garage. It has many wires and buttons and lights. They do not know what it is. They think it is a toy.

"Let's play with it!" Sam says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They open the box and see a big machine. It has a screen and a keyboard and a microphone. They see words on the screen. They do not know what they mean.

"Maybe it can talk to us!" Ben says.

"Let's try!" Sam says.

They press some buttons and speak into the microphone. They say hello and their names and ask questions. They wait for the machine to answer.

But the machine does not answer. It makes a loud noise and sparks. The screen goes black. The machine is broken.

Sam and Ben are scared. They run away from the box. They find Rex in the living room. He is sleeping on the couch. He hears them and opens his eyes. He sees them and wags his tail.

"Rex, Rex, we are sorry!" Sam says.

"We did something bad!" Ben says.

They hug Rex and tell him what they did. Rex listens and yawns. He does not care about the box. He cares about his boys. He licks their faces and makes them laugh.

"Rex, you are the best!" Sam says.

"Rex, you are smarter than us!" Ben says.

They play with Rex and forget about the box. They do not know that the box is their dad's computer. He uses it for his work. He is a scientist. He will be very angry when he sees what they did. He will think they are foolish. But Rex will not. He will love them anyway.

One day, Mommy and Alice went for a walk. Alice wanted to go to the park, but Mommy said it was time to leave. 

Alice started to cry. She wanted to stay at the park, but Mommy said it was time to leave. Alice was very unhappy. 

Mommy gave Alice a big hug. She said, "Come on, Alice. Let's leave. We can come to the park another day."

Alice pulled away and had a silly look on her face. She said, "But I want to stay here! You can't make me leave!" 

Mommy laughed and said, "We all have to leave sometimes. Come on, let's go." 

Alice pouted and took her Mommy's hand. They walked away from the park, with Alice looking back every few steps.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree named Oak. Oak was very strong and tall. He had many branches that reached up to the sky. One day, a little bird named Tweetie was flying around and landed on one of Oak's branches. Tweetie was very scared because she had never been so high up before. 

Oak saw that Tweetie was fearful, so he decided to support her. He held her gently with his branch and told her that she was safe. Tweetie felt much better with Oak's support and thanked him. From that day on, Tweetie visited Oak every day and they became good friends. Oak was happy to have a new friend and support her whenever she needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Tom. Tom had a big imagination. Every day, he would pretend to be something different. Today, he wanted to be a postman.

Tom took out a piece of paper and some crayons. He drew a picture of a letter on the paper and he pretended to put a stamp on it. He smiled and said, "I'm a postman and this letter is for my friend."

Tom ran to his friend's house and gave her the letter. His friend opened the letter and found a healthy snack inside. She smiled and said, "Thank you for the letter, Tom! It was very nice of you to bring me a present!"

Tom was so happy to hear this. He waved goodbye to his friend and went back home, pretending to be a postman again. He was on a mission to deliver his letters to everyone he could find.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was a little girl and the other was a swan. The girl was very flexible and loved to dance, and the swan was just as flexible and loved to fly.

One day, the girl and the swan were playing in their favorite field when the girl shouted, "Let's play a game!"

The swan smiled and asked, "What kind of game?"

The little girl suggested, "How about hide and seek?"

The swan thought this sounded like fun, so they both shut their eyes. The girl counted to five and then opened her eyes to look for the swan.

But the swan was nowhere to be found! The girl searched high and low but there was still no sign of the swan.

Finally, after a while, the girl spotted the swan in a tree. It had been so flexible that it had even managed to fit itself in a little nook in the tree.

The girl shouted out, "I found you!"

And the swan flew down to join her, and together they had a lot of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a shy boy named Joe. He didn't have many friends because he was too shy and his heart was too scared to talk to new people. 

But one day at the park, Joe saw a puppy. The puppy was very shy too, just like Joe. Joe slowly reached out his hand and the puppy immediately came running to him. He was so happy that he wanted to keep the puppy, but he had to mind his parents and know that he couldn't. 

So Joe decided to visit the park every day and play with the puppy. Every day he would get a little bit less shy and eventually his heart opened up so much that he was making friends with other kids at the park. 

Joe and his puppy were the happiest they had ever been. Soon enough, everyone in the park knew their names and they were no longer feeling shy and scared.

One day, a little boy was walking through the woods. It was a gloomy day, and the trees had no leaves. He walked for a while until he saw a chest in front of him. He was curious, so he started to pull on the latch. It opened, and inside the chest he found a bottle of lotion. He had never seen anything like it and he smiled.

The little boy couldn't wait to use the lotion, so he opened the bottle. Suddenly, he heard a voice from behind him. "What do you think you're doing? That's my lotion!"

The little boy turned around to see a mean-looking old man. He was tall and scowling. The little boy was scared and he quickly put the lotion back in the chest. He apologised and ran off as fast as he could. 

The little boy was relieved to get away safely. But he was still sad that he had to leave the lotion behind. He didn't understand why the old man had to be so mean. He knew he would never forget that gloomy day.

Once upon a time, there was a large pot sitting on a kitchen counter. Every day, two small frogs, Amos and Jody, would play inside it.

One day, Amos and Jody started to fight and chase each other around the pot. Jody was very fast and Amos kept trying to catch her. They ran around and around, until one of them bumped the edge of the pot and it tipped over, spilling the frogs onto the floor.

Amos and Jody were so surprised, they stopped fighting and looked up at the large pot that had been tipped in its place. They looked at each other and started giggling.

"We made a big mess," giggled Jody.

"Let's put it back," said Amos.

So, with a little help from the grown ups, Amos and Jody put the large pot back in its place on the kitchen counter. From then on, they never fought again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with blocks and build tall towers. She would stack them up so high, but sometimes they would fall down. 

One day, Lily's dad helped her build the tallest tower she had ever seen. It was so tall that Lily had to stand on her tiptoes to put the last block on top. Her dad said, "Now, be gentle with it, Lily. We need to balance it just right." 

Lily was careful not to knock the tower over as she stepped back to admire it. She was so proud of herself and her dad. They had worked together to make something amazing. As she looked at the tower, she noticed a little bird perched on top. The bird was so small and light that it didn't knock the tower over. Lily smiled and said, "Look, Dad! The bird is balancing on top of our tower!" 

From that day on, Lily always made sure to be gentle and balance her blocks just right. She knew that if she did, she could make something amazing too.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl called Anna. She wanted to go on an amazing journey but she had no idea how to get there.

One day, Anna saw a magical door in the forest. She opened the door and stepped inside to find a long, winding path. Anna bowed her head and started walking. 

The path was long and tricky but Anna was stubborn. She kept going until she reached the end of the path. At the end of the path there was a beautiful castle. 

Anna bowed when she entered the castle. Inside the castle she found her amazing journey. She met new friends, explored new places and made wonderful memories. 

Anna's journey was amazing and she never forgot it. She even told her grandchildren about it and they were so excited! Her journey was magical and something she would always remember.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She liked to wear pretty dresses and shiny shoes. One day, she went to school and her teacher read a poem. Lily liked the poem very much and she clapped her hands.

After school, Lily went to play with her friends. They played tag and hide-and-seek. But then, Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She cried and her friends helped her up. They took her to the teacher who put a bandage on her knee. Lily felt better and thanked her friends for helping her.

That night, Lily's mom read her a bedtime story. Lily fell asleep and dreamt about wearing a beautiful dress and reciting a poem in front of her friends. She felt happy and her knee didn't hurt anymore. The end.

Tom was a cat who liked to play outside. He ran, jumped and chased birds and mice. He did not like to take baths or brush his fur. He thought he looked fine with his dirty, tangled coat.

One day, it was very cold and windy. Tom wanted to find a warm place to sleep. He saw a big house with a nice garden. He sneaked in through a hole in the fence. He saw a dog house with a soft blanket inside. He thought it was perfect for him.

He crawled into the dog house and curled up on the blanket. He felt cozy and happy. He did not know that the dog house belonged to Rex, a big, friendly dog who lived in the house.

Soon, Rex came back from his walk with his owner. He smelled a strange scent in his dog house. He barked and ran to see who was there. He saw Tom, the dirty cat, sleeping on his blanket. He was angry and scared.

"Who are you? Get out of my house!" Rex growled.

Tom woke up and saw Rex. He was terrified. He hissed and scratched Rex's nose. He tried to run away, but Rex blocked his way.

"Leave me alone! I just wanted to be warm!" Tom cried.

Rex and Tom fought and made a lot of noise. Their owner heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw Rex and Tom, both hurt and scared. He picked up Tom and took him inside. He cleaned his wounds and gave him some food and water. He also gave him a bath and brushed his fur. He made him look clean and shiny.

He also checked on Rex and gave him a treat and a hug. He told him he was a good boy for protecting his house. He also told him he was sorry for the cat who was lost and cold.

He put Tom in a cage and called the animal shelter. He hoped they would find a good home for him. He felt sorry for him, but he knew he could not keep him. He already had Rex, who was his best friend.

Tom felt warm and full, but also sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend like Rex. He wished he had taken better care of himself. He realized he had been selfish and rude. He shivered in his cage and licked his paw. He hoped someone would love him and teach him how to be a good cat. He learned a hard lesson that day. He learned that being dirty and mean was not fun or smart. He learned that being clean and kind was better for him and others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Kim. One day, Kim was very bored and wanted to talk to someone. However, everyone was busy and did not have time to talk.

Kim then spotted a knife on the ground. She was curious so she picked it up and asked the knife, "Hi Knife! Do you want to talk to me?"

The knife was silent and didn't answer her. Kim was feeling very sad and lonely. She started to cry and said, "It's so boring talking to myself."

Suddenly, the knife spoke up and said, "Don't cry Kim. I'm here to talk to you!" Kim was very surprised and excited to hear the knife talk.

Kim and the knife were the best of friends and she wasn't bored anymore. From then on, Kim and the knife talked to each other all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved to play with every day. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to sell the car because they needed more money for food. Timmy was sad, but he understood that it was important. 

After they sold the car, Timmy and his mom cleaned the house. They dusted the shelves and the tables. Timmy thought it was fun to watch the dust fly in the air. 

Later that day, Timmy's dad came home with an impressive surprise. He had bought Timmy a new toy car! Timmy was so happy and he hugged his dad tight. He knew that they didn't have much money, but his dad still found a way to make him smile.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big tree with a swing. They run to the swing and take turns.

"Can I go first?" Lily asks.

"Okay, but only for a little bit," Tom says.

Lily gets on the swing and holds the rope. She pushes with her feet and goes high. She feels happy and free. She laughs and says, "Look at me, Tom! I'm flying!"

Tom watches and claps. He waits for his turn. He wants to go high too.

But then, something bad happens. Lily's hand slips and she falls off the swing. She lands on the ground and hurts her knee. She cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!"

Tom runs to her and helps her up. He sees blood on her knee. He says, "Oh no, Lily! You have a boo-boo! Come on, let's go to the bench. There's an old lady there. Maybe she has a band-aid."

They walk to the bench, where an old lady is sitting. She has gray hair and glasses. She sees Lily and Tom and smiles. She says, "Hello, children. What's the matter?"

Lily shows her knee and says, "I had a trip and fell off the swing. It hurts a lot."

The old lady says, "Oh, you poor thing. Don't worry, I have a band-aid for you. Here, let me put it on your knee. There, does that feel better?"

Lily nods and says, "Thank you, lady. You are very nice."

The old lady says, "You're welcome, dear. And you, young man, you are a good friend. You helped your friend when she was hurt. That's very kind of you."

Tom says, "Thank you, lady. We are friends. We like to play together."

The old lady says, "That's wonderful. Friends are important. You know, when I was young, I had a friend too. We used to play in the park and hang from the branches of the trees. We had so much fun."

Lily and Tom listen to the old lady's story. They forget about the pain and the fall. They smile and say, "That sounds fun. Can you tell us more?"

The old lady says, "Of course, I can. Come, sit with me. I'll tell you all about it."

And so, Lily and Tom sit with the old lady and listen to her stories. They learn about the past and the present. They laugh and talk. They make a new friend. They are happy.

Lily was a very independent girl. She liked to do things by herself, without asking for help. She had a big box of toys in her room, and she loved to play with them. She had dolls, cars, blocks, and a shiny gold key.

One day, she decided to lock her door with the gold key. She thought it would be fun to have her own secret place, where no one could bother her. She turned the key in the lock and heard a click. Then she smiled and went to play with her toys.

But after a while, she got bored. She wanted to go outside and see her friends. She wanted to have a snack and a drink. She wanted to hug her mom and dad. She tried to open the door, but it was locked. She tried to turn the key, but it was stuck. She started to cry.

She heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. "Lily, are you okay? Why did you lock the door?" she asked.

"I wanted to be independent," Lily sobbed. "But now I can't get out. I'm sorry, mom. Please help me."

Her mom called her dad, and they got a tool to open the door. They hugged Lily and told her they loved her. They also told her that being independent is good, but sometimes you need to ask for help and share with others. Lily learned her lesson. She never locked her door again. She played with her toys, but also with her friends and family. She was happy and independent, but not alone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called June. June was a very happy girl and loved to play with her friends.

One day June was walking in the garden and saw a seed. The seed was very small. She decided to take it home.

When she got home, June planted the seed in the ground and watered it. Each day Junewould look outside to see if the seed had grown.

After a few days, June saw the seed had grown into a big, beautiful flower. She was so glad. She ran back into the house and showed her mom the flower.

Momsaid, "What a lovely flower you have grown, June. I am so proud of you." June was so happy.

June asked her mother if she could put the flower in the refrigerator. Mom said, "Yes, you can. Why are you putting it in the refrigerator?"

June said, "Because this flower will last longer if I put it in the refrigerator. Then I can keep it for a very long time." Mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea."

June put the flower in the refrigerator and was very glad. She knew it would last for a long time.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sally and Timmy. They were very jolly and often spent their days on the playground.

One day, Sally had an itch on her arm and started scratching. 'That looks really itchy,' said Timmy. 

They decided to discuss the itch and find a solution. 'Maybe you should put some cream on it?' Timmy suggested.

'Yes, good idea,' said Sally, nodding her head. She ran off to get the cream while Timmy waited. After a few minutes, Sally returned with a pot of cream and they applied it to the itch. 

The cream worked wonders and Sally's itch was quickly gone. 'That was a good idea, thank you,' she said, smiling at Timmy. 

They hugged each other, feeling very jolly. Together, they had found a solution to the itch and they were proud of their achievement. 

The story ends here, but Sally and Timmy continued to be friends and always had lots of jolly fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Tim. He was three years old and he had lots of toys. His favourite toy was a big white bear. Every night, Tim and the bear would get ready for bed.

One night, Tim put on his pyjamas and tucked his bear into bed. But as he was about to get cozy and warm, the bear suddenly disappeared!

Tim looked around the room to find his bear, but he was gone! He started to get scared and he shouted out: "Where is my bear?".

Suddenly, he heard a faint noise coming from outside. It sounded like music. Tim crept over to the window and peeped outside. He saw a parade of people dancing to music with exciting jazz!

He got so excited that he forgot all about his missing bear! He ran outside, warmly dressed in his pyjamas, and he joined in the dancing with the others.

Eventually, the parade disappeared away and it was time to go home. It was then that Tim remembered about his bear. He ran back into his bedroom and there he saw his bear, curled up in the bed. He had been there all along!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ann. One day, Ann and her mum went to the hospital for a check up. Ann saw a unique nurse, who was very kind. The nurse asked Ann to stay quiet and lie down on the bed so she could measure her. So, Ann did as she was told and lay down.

The nurse looked at Ann and smiled. She smiled back. The nurse said, â€œYou can sit up now. Ann. That was very good.â€ 
Ann was very pleased. She wanted to show the nurse how happy she was and said, â€œI like you!â€ The nurse hugged Ann and said, â€œI like you, too!â€ Ann was over the moon!

After the check up was finished, Ann and her mum left the hospital. Ann was very proud of herself. She was happy to have met such a unique nurse.

Peter and Mommy were walking down the street. Peter looked up and saw big, dark clouds in the sky. Rain started to come down. Peter shouted, "Mommy, it's raining!" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's raining. Let's run home!"

They started to run. When they got close to home, Mommy said, "Oh no! I left my knife on the table!" Peter was worried. He said, "Mommy, we can't go back. It's raining too much!" Mommy hugged him and said, "That's ok. It's better to be safe than sorry. We don't need the knife."

They ran home and stayed warm and dry in their house. Peter learned an important lesson: it's best to be careful and stay away from danger. That way, he would always be safe and Mommy would not be worried.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car that they could ride in the garden. They took turns to drive the car and pretended to go on adventures.

One day, Lila and Ben were playing with the car when they saw a big black dog in the garden. The dog was barking and growling and looked very angry. Lila and Ben were scared and ran back to the house. They told their mom about the dog and she said they had to stay inside until the dog went away.

Lila and Ben were sad and bored. They wanted to play with the car, but they were afraid of the dog. They looked out of the window and saw the dog still in the garden. The dog was sniffing around the car and trying to bite the wheels.

"Mom, the dog is ruining our car!" Lila cried.

"Can we do something, mom?" Ben asked.

Mom thought for a moment. She had an idea. She went to the kitchen and came back with a pill. She said it was a special pill that could make the dog friendly.

"Really, mom?" Lila and Ben asked.

"Yes, really. But you have to be very brave to give the pill to the dog. Do you think you can do it?" Mom asked.

Lila and Ben looked at each other. They nodded. They wanted to save their car and make the dog happy. They took the pill from mom and went to the door.

"Be careful, kids. And remember, you have to unite to do this. That means you have to work together and help each other. OK?" Mom said.

"OK, mom. We will unite," Lila and Ben said.

They opened the door and walked slowly to the garden. The dog saw them and barked louder. Lila and Ben held hands and walked closer. They talked to the dog in a soft voice.

"Hello, dog. We are Lila and Ben. We are not here to hurt you. We are here to give you a gift. It is a pill that will make you feel good. Do you want it?" Lila said.

The dog stopped barking and tilted his head. He looked at the pill in Ben's hand. He smelled it and licked his lips. He wagged his tail and came closer.

"Good dog. You are very smart. Here, take the pill. It is yummy. You will like it," Ben said.

He threw the pill to the dog and the dog caught it in his mouth. He chewed it and swallowed it. He smiled and licked his lips again. He looked at Lila and Ben with friendly eyes.

"Wow, it worked! The dog is nice now!" Lila said.

"Yes, it did! The dog is our friend now!" Ben said.

They hugged the dog and the dog licked their faces. They laughed and played with the dog and the car. They had a lot of fun.

Mom watched them from the window and smiled. She was proud of her brave and united twins. She knew they could do anything they set their minds to. She was happy they had a new friend. She hoped the pill would last for a long time.

Tammy was 3 years old. One day, when she was playing outside, she saw something sparkly on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it was a mineral. She didn't understand what it was, so she asked her Mom. 

"Mom, what is this?"

"That is a mineral, dear," Mom said.

"What does it do?" Tammy asked.

"Well," Mom said, "it doesn't do much. It's just a silly rock."

Tammy smiled and put the mineral back where she found it. She was glad to have understood what it was.

Lila liked to play dress-up with her dolls. She had many clothes and hats and shoes for them. She liked to make them look pretty and different. She gave each doll a name and a style.

One day, she was playing with her doll Mia. She put a pink dress and a yellow hat on her. She said, "Mia, you look so nice. You have a sunny style. Do you like it?"

Mia did not answer, because she was a doll. But Lila pretended she did. She said, "Yes, Lila, I like it. But can you remove the hat? It is too hot for me."

Lila was surprised. She said, "But Mia, the hat is part of your style. It matches your dress. Why do you want to remove it?"

Mia said, "Because it is not mild today. It is very warm. The hat makes me sweat. I want to feel the breeze on my hair."

Lila thought for a moment. She said, "OK, Mia, I understand. You can remove the hat. But you have to keep the dress. It is very pretty."

Mia said, "Thank you, Lila. You are very kind. I like the dress too. It is soft and light. Can we go outside and play?"

Lila said, "Yes, Mia, we can. Let me get my shoes and my bag. Then we can go and have fun."

Lila and Mia went outside and played in the garden. They enjoyed the sun and the flowers. They had a happy day.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Freddy. Freddy loved to play in the pond with his friends. He would jump and swim all day long. One day, Freddy saw a big bug and he wanted to eat it. But the bug flew away and Freddy was sad.

Freddy wanted to grow bigger so he could catch the bug. He ate lots of flies and bugs, but he didn't grow much. One day, he saw a sign that said "magic beans available." Freddy thought the beans might help him grow bigger, so he bought them with all his money.

He planted the beans and waited for them to grow. But when they did, a giant beanstalk grew all the way up to the sky. Freddy climbed up the beanstalk and found a castle. Inside, he saw the big bug he had been trying to catch. But the bug was too big for Freddy to eat. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and the castle shook. The giant who owned the castle had come home. Freddy was scared and ran down the beanstalk as fast as he could. But the giant saw him and chased him. Freddy was never seen again.

A bunny hopped along the sidewalk until he came to a big billboard. He leaned in to look at it, but was startled when a big, red balloon bounced out of nowhere. The bunny jumped back, feeling scared. He quickly hopped to safety.

Just then, a little girl walked around the corner, clapping her hands. She was very excited when she saw the big, red balloon. She scooped it up with her tiny hands and shouted, "Wheeee! This is so much fun!"

The bunny watched as she bounced the balloon up and down in the air. He laughed and said, "It sure is a lot of fun bouncing a balloon."

The girl smiled and said, "Yes, I love it! I'm so glad we found it."

The bunny nodded, feeling happy to have found something that made the little girl so happy. He said goodbye to the little girl and hopped away, with a big smile on his face.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big ball on the grass. It was red and shiny. They wanted to play with it.

"Let's lift the ball and roll it," Sara said.

"OK," Ben said. They ran to the ball and tried to lift it. But it was too heavy. They could not move it.

"Maybe we need to push it," Ben said. They pushed the ball with their hands. But it did not roll. It was stuck on something.

They looked under the ball. There was a spike. It was sharp and metal. It had pierced the ball and made a hole. Air was coming out of the hole. The ball was getting smaller and softer.

"Oh no!" Sara said. "We broke the ball!"

They heard a voice behind them. It was the owner of the ball. He was a big boy. He looked angry.

"Hey, what are you doing with my ball?" he said. "You ruined it!"

Sara and Ben were scared. They did not mean to break the ball. They were sorry.

"We are sorry," Sara said. "We just wanted to play with it. We did not see the spike."

The big boy did not listen. He grabbed the ball and threw it away. He glared at Sara and Ben.

"Go away, you little brats!" he said. "You are not welcome here!"

Sara and Ben ran away. They felt ashamed. They wished they had not touched the ball. They wished they had been more careful. They wished they had a ball of their own.

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey called Ben. Ben was very hungry. He was looking for something to eat. He saw a bowl of peaches in the kitchen. He smiled and ran to it.

He grabbed a peach, but it was sticky. He tried to wipe it with his hand, but it still felt sticky. Then he saw a cloth nearby. He grabbed it and wiped the peach. It was clean! He put the cloth back and took a big bite of the peach. It was delicious!

He was so happy and he took another bite. Then he heard someone say, â€œWhat are you doing?â€. It was his mom. He told her all about the bowl of peaches and how he had wiped it. 

His mom smiled and said, â€œYou did a good job, Ben! Now you can eat your peach.â€ 

Ben was so excited and happy. He ate his peach and was still hungry for more!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, while swimming, Fin saw a pretty image on a rock. The image was of a big fish with many colors. Fin wanted to be friends with the big fish in the image.

Fin swam around and asked other sea friends, "Do you know where the big fish is?" But Fin's sea friends did not know. They were ignorant about the big fish. They had never seen it before.

Finally, Fin met an old wise turtle. The turtle said, "The big fish is not real. It is just an image on a rock." Fin felt sad but learned that not everything we see is real. Fin continued to swim and make friends with real fish in the big blue sea.

Jack looked from his window and noticed a gun. It was lying in a mud puddle. He was scared but he decided to take it to his mom. His mom was dependable and he knew she would tell him what to do.

He went outside, hurriedly picked up the gun and brought it to his mom.

"Mom, I saw this gun lying in the mud. What should I do with it?"

His mom looked at him before she replied. "Jack, I'm so proud of you for bringing me this gun. You did the right thing. We don't need guns in our house. It is much better to be dependable and take them away from danger, so no one is hurt. That is the best thing to do when you find something like this."

Jack was happy he did the right thing and was proud to be dependable. Learning to take care of himself and his neighborhood was an important responsibility he was taking seriously. He knew he could make the world a better place to live in.

John was a big rabbit who loved to explore the forest. He jumped through the trees and hopped around in the grass, looking for interesting things. One day, he spotted a pattern on the ground and he wanted to get closer and have a look. He started hopping towards it, but then he saw something big and scary in the distance - a bear!

John was scared and wanted to escape, so he quickly hopped away. He hopped faster and faster, running away from the bear. He kept running until he couldn't run anymore, but he was still far away from the pattern he had been looking at. He was safe, but he couldn't get to the pattern.

Sadly, John had to give up and go home. He never got to explore the pattern and he was disappointed. He knew he had been brave to try, but he couldn't escape the bear.

One day, a girl named Lucy went with her mom to mail a letter. Lucy walked slow because she liked to watch her shadow. She saw her shadow get big and small as she moved. "Look, Mommy! My shadow is dancing!" Lucy said.

"Wow, Lucy! Your shadow likes to dance with you," Mommy said. They both laughed and danced with their shadows all the way to the mailbox. When they got there, Lucy helped Mommy put the letter in the mailbox. "Good job, Lucy!" Mommy said.

On their way back home, Lucy saw a boy who was sad. His shadow was not dancing. Lucy went to him and said, "Hi! My name is Lucy. Let's dance with our shadows!" The boy smiled and danced with Lucy and his shadow. They all had fun. The moral of the story is to be kind and share your joy with others.

Sam and Lily were playing in the yard. They liked to build things with wood and nails. Sam had a hammer and Lily had a saw. They were making a house for their dolls.

"Look, Sam, I cut this piece very well. It is normal and straight. Can you nail it to the other piece?" Lily asked.

"Sure, Lily, give it to me. I am good at hammering. Watch this!" Sam said. He took the piece from Lily and put it on the other piece. He lifted his hammer and swung it hard.

But he missed the nail. He hit his thumb instead. It hurt a lot. He dropped the hammer and cried. "Ow, ow, ow! I suffer, I suffer!"

Lily saw what happened. She felt sorry for Sam. She put down her saw and ran to him. She hugged him and said, "Oh, Sam, I am sorry. You are brave. Let me see your thumb. Maybe we can put some ice on it."

She took his hand and looked at his thumb. It was red and swollen. She said, "We need to go to Mom. She can help you. Come on, Sam, let's go."

She helped him stand up and walk to the house. They left the wood and the nails and the hammer and the saw in the yard. They would play with them another day, when Sam's thumb was normal again.

Once upon a time, there was a big and very tidy kitchen. Everyday, a little girl named Lilly would help her mom tidy up the kitchen and they both enjoyed it very much.

One day, Lilly's mom told her that she was going to go to the library to study and that she should stay at home and help keep the kitchen tidy. She said, "Lilly, while I am studying, I want you to help me make the kitchen very tidy, ok?"

Lilly was so excited to help her mom, so she agreed and said, "Yes! I will make the kitchen extra tidy!"

When Lilly's mom came back from the library, she was surprised to see that not only was the kitchen tidy, but it was also extra clean! She hugged her daughter and thanked her for taking care of the kitchen.

From then on, whenever Lilly's mom needed to study, she would always ask her daughter to help her make the kitchen tidy. Lilly was happy to help, and the kitchen always looked extra clean and lovely.

Anna wanted to go to the beach. She was so excited she could barely contain herself. She was hoping to stretch her legs, and maybe even see a jellyfish.

At the beach, there was so much to do: swimming, building sandcastles, and playing. It was wonderful! Little Anna went from one activity to the next, always discovering something original.

She thought she saw a jellyfish in the shallow water and ran to tell her mom. "Mom, a jellyfish! Can we get closer?"

"Yes, but be careful," said her mom. 

They slowly stretched towards the jellyfish. It was so beautiful and graceful, Anna was mesmerized. She watched as it moved through the water, getting closer and closer. 

"Original," her mom said.

Anna just smiled and nodded, agreeing with her mom. Together they enjoyed the original jellyfish, stretching and admiring it until it disappeared beyond the horizon.

Once upon a time, there was a big tank. The tank was very quiet. It didn't make any noise. One day, some friends came to play with the tank. They wanted to race with it. The tank was slow, but it still tried its best. The friends cheered for the tank and it felt happy. Even though it didn't win the race, it was still a winner in their hearts. The end.

Mum was walking down the hall when she saw her son, Max, playing. All of a sudden, his face changed, turning worried.

Mum: "What is wrong, Max?"

Max: "The sun has stopped shining".

Mum smiled and said, "It's ok, Max. The sun still shines, it's just behind the clouds".

Max looked up and sure enough, he could just see a little bit of sunshine beaming through the grey.

Mum: "See, the sun is still shining. You don't have to be worried".

Max smiled and hugged his mum. He was so happy now that he knew the sun was still shining.

Max looked up and smiled. He wasn't worried anymore now that he knew that the sun was still shining.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Joy. She was outside playing with her friends when they noticed a big block of ice.

"Let's keep the ice!" said Joy.

Her friends weren't sure, but Joy said it would be fair. So they all decided to keep it and take it back to their house.

They used their hands and feet to push and pull the ice. It was hard work, but they were excited to have found such a big block of ice.

When they finally got the ice back to their house, they were excited to play with it. They got some buckets and turned the block of ice into a big ice castle.

They ran around it, splashed in it, and had lots of fun. 

When it was time to go home, Joy said, "Let's keep the ice for next time."

So they covered the ice block with a big blanket and put some rocks around it to hold the blanket in place.

The next time Joy and her friends came to play, the ice was still kept. They all cheered and had lots of fun.

Joy was happy that she thought to keep the ice and that it all had worked out fair for everyone. The end.

Ben and his dad went to the stadium to see a big game. Ben was very excited. He liked to watch the players run and kick the ball. He also liked to cheer with the crowd. His dad told him to be obedient and stay close to him.

"Look, Ben, there is our team. They are wearing red shirts. Can you observe them?" his dad said, pointing to the field.

"Yes, dad, I can see them. They are very fast and strong. I hope they win!" Ben said, clapping his hands.

"Me too, son. But remember, it is just a game. We have to be nice to the other team too. They are wearing blue shirts. Can you observe them?" his dad said, showing him the other side.

"Yes, dad, I can see them. They are also fast and strong. But I like our team more!" Ben said, sticking out his tongue.

"Ha ha, that's okay. But don't be rude, okay? Maybe we can make some friends with the blue team fans. They are here to have fun too," his dad said, smiling.

Ben nodded. He wanted to be a good boy. He looked around the stadium. He saw many people wearing different colors. He saw some flags and banners. He saw some snacks and drinks. He saw some cameras and speakers. He saw a lot of things. He was very curious.

"Dad, can I go and see that?" he asked, pointing to a big screen.

"Sure, Ben, but only for a little while. And don't go too far. I will observe you from here. And come back when I call you, okay?" his dad said, letting him go.

"Okay, dad, I will be obedient. Thank you!" Ben said, running to the screen.

He did not know that the screen was showing a replay of a very important moment in the game. He did not know that everyone was watching it with great attention. He did not know that he was about to do something that would make everyone laugh and cheer. He did not know that he was about to become a star.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved strawberries. She would pick them from her garden and eat them every day. One day, she found a big strawberry that looked very delicious but it was on a high shelf. She tried to reach it but accidentally knocked it down and it broke into pieces. 

Lily was sad because her favorite fruit was gone. She sat on the ground and stared at the broken strawberry. Suddenly, she had an idea. She decided to use the broken pieces to make a strawberry smoothie. 

Lily learned that even when things don't go as planned, there is always a way to make the best of the situation. She enjoyed her delicious smoothie and was happy again. The end.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a big purple cat. The cat was very sad. Mia asked the cat, "Why are you sad?" The cat said, "I want some cream, but I don't dare to ask anyone."

Mia wanted to help the cat. She went to her mom and said, "Mom, can I have some cream for my new friend?" Her mom gave her a small bowl of cream.

Mia took the cream to the purple cat. The cat was very happy. It said, "Thank you, Mia!" The cat ate the cream and smiled. Now, Mia and the purple cat are best friends. They play together every day.

There were two friends, Dave and Joanna. Dave had a secret surprise he wanted to share. He wanted to show Joanna something special. 

He pulled out a big box and said that the box had a surprise inside. Joanna was so excited and felt curious about what was inside. Dave laughed and opened the box. Inside, Joanna saw a beautiful new toy! She was so excited.

Joanna wanted to get a toy like that too. Dave said he was happy she liked it and asked if she would like one of her own. Joanna happily said 'yes'.

The next day, Joanna was so surprised to see Dave had brought her the same toy. She was happy and thanked him. She wanted to show all of her friends.

One of Joanna's friends was envious of her new toy. He wanted one too but couldn't get one. Joanna smiled and said that she could share it. They all had fun playing with the new toy.

One day, Willie the Wombat wanted to go on a new adventure. He saw a bright, enormous path, and he wanted to explore. He took some paint and went to go follow the path. 

The path was so long and twisty - it was all very exciting! With his paint in hand, Willie started to paint the path he was travelling. Soon enough, Willie heard some rustling from behind him and then he heard a voice call out. 

"Why are you painting the path, Willie?" asked an old turtle who was walking past.

"I'm painting it because I want to explore and see where this path goes," said Willie happily.

"That's a wonderful idea!" replied the turtle. "I'm sure this painted path will make exploring even more exciting!" 

And so, Willie continued on his adventure. He painted the path, exploring and following it wherever it would lead. The path was enormous, and he had no idea where it would end - and he was very excited to find out.

Charlie was a little bear who lived in a forest. Every winter, Charlie would remain warm and cozy in his den. But one year was different. One winter, the snow was particularly filthy. It wasn't white and fluffy like other winters. There were big brown patches all over the snow. Charlie didn't like the filthy winter at all. He wished for the snow to be white again. 

One day, he decided to do something about the dirty snow. He grabbed a twig and shook it back and forth. He tried to brush the dirt away. 

Gradually, the snow started to look brighter and brighter. Charlie was very proud of himself. Soon enough, his forest was full of clean white snow. He smiled with joy and reminded himself to stay positive during the winter.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved taking naps. He would dream of the things he wanted to do and see. One day, he was walking in the park, and he saw a man blowing bubbles. The bubbles looked so fun and shiny, he wanted to join in the fun.

The man saw the little boy, so he gave him a special bubble wand. It was more expensive than the one he had, so it was even more special. The little boy waved his wand around and watched the bubbles it made. He giggle with delight as he saw more bubbles form around him.

He was so focused with his bubbles, he forgot the time. Soon, the little boy started to feel sleepy, so he laid down on the grass and took a nap. He slept so well under the warm sun that he had the best dream ever. He dreamt of bubble castles and bubble oceans, and even bubble skies.

When he woke up, he thanked the man for his bubble wand and went home. He was so excited to tell his family of the magical bubbles and his nap in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a small child who was playing with his favorite toy truck. He was so happy that he drove it around the room with a big smile on his face.

Suddenly, the doorbell rang. The child quickly put the truck back in its chamber and shut the door tightly. He rushed to the front door to answer the door.

When he opened it, there was a big dog standing in front of the door. The dog was looking up at the child in an excited way. The child was scared and tried to close the door, but the dog stuck his paw in between to stop him.

The child shouted, "Go away!" but the dog would not leave. He barked and wagged his tail, begging for attention. After some coaxing, the child dropped his defenses and started petting the dog. 

Little did the child know, this was the same dog that kidnapped his favorite toy truck earlier that morning. His truck was still in the chamber, hidden away from view! But the child was about to find out the truth very soonâ€¦

Tommy and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. They saw a big tree with many brown balls on it. Tommy said, "Look, Lily, those are acorns. They are food for squirrels."

Lily said, "Can we eat them too?" She picked up an acorn and tried to bite it. But it was very hard and bitter. She spat it out and made a face. "Yuck, this is not good. It hurts my teeth."

Tommy laughed and said, "Silly Lily, acorns are not for us. They are for squirrels. Let's go and find some squirrels. Maybe they will share their acorns with us."

They walked around the tree and saw a small hole in the trunk. They heard a noise inside. It sounded like a sneeze. "Achoo, achoo, achoo!"

Tommy and Lily peeked inside the hole. They saw a furry gray animal with a long bushy tail. It was a squirrel. It had a red nose and watery eyes. It looked sick. It sneezed again. "Achoo, achoo, achoo!"

Tommy and Lily felt sorry for the squirrel. They wanted to help it. They said, "Hello, Mr. Squirrel. Are you okay? Why are you sneezing so much?"

The squirrel looked at them and said, "Hello, little ones. I'm not okay. I have a cold. I ate too many acorns. They made me sick. They are not good for me. They are too dry and dusty."

Tommy and Lily said, "Oh, no, Mr. Squirrel. That's not good. You need to drink some water and eat some fresh fruits. They are good for you. They are juicy and sweet."

The squirrel said, "Thank you, little ones. You are very kind and smart. Do you have any water and fruits for me?"

Tommy and Lily said, "Yes, we do. We have a bottle of water and some apples in our backpack. We will share them with you. Come out of the hole and we will give them to you."

The squirrel came out of the hole and followed Tommy and Lily. They gave him some water and some apples. He drank and ate them. He felt better. He stopped sneezing. He smiled and said, "Thank you, little ones. You are brilliant. You saved me. You are my friends."

Tommy and Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Squirrel. You are our friend too. We are happy that you feel better. Can we play with you?"

The squirrel said, "Yes, of course. Let's play. I have some acorns for you. But not to eat. To throw and catch. They are fun to play with."

Tommy and Lily said, "Yay, that sounds fun. Let's play with the acorns."

They played with the squirrel and the acorns. They had a lot of fun. They laughed and hugged. They were happy. They were friends.

Once there was a happy little girl. Her name was Emma. One day her mommy said to her, "Let's go to the temple!" Emma was so excited that she laughed and laughed. 

At the temple, Emma could not believe her eyes. It was so incredible! She saw statues of gods, gold decorations, and the most beautiful paintings. "Mommy, look at everything!" she said in amazement. 

Emma and her mommy walked around the temple. Everywhere they went, Emma laughed with joy. She was so excited to be there! 

At the end of their visit, as they were walking back home, Emma said to her mommy, "I wish we could stay here forever!" Mommy smiled and said, "Sometimes, you just have to remember this wonderful place in your heart." 

Emma smiled and hugged her mommy tightly. Together they laughed, happy to have shared such a beautiful experience.

Once there was a man who liked to spend time with his family. Every weekend the man and his family would buy an order of their favourite soft food from the local store. The man would make sure that it was nice and soft so that his little three year old boy could enjoy it too.

The man and the boy would then spend their time together eating their delicious meal. As they ate, the man would make silly faces to make the little boy giggle. Then the boy would always remember the special time spent with his father. 

Afterwards, the man would carry the boy home and tuck him in bed - the little boy was exhausted from all the fun. Every weekend the man and his son would spend the same special time together, making the most of their family time.

Lucy was anxious. She was hiding from Mommy.
Lucy had jumped into a pile of soil and stayed very still. A meow came from behind Lucy and she saw her cat, Fluffy.

"What are you doing here, Fluffy?" Lucy asked.

"I'm here to help you hide." Fluffy said, brushing gently against Lucy's leg.

"Thank you, Fluffy." Lucy smiled.

"No problem," Fluffy said.

Lucy and Fluffy stayed there for what seemed like a long time.

Finally, Mommy called out for Lucy, but she couldn't find her.

Lucy and Fluffy had done a good job at hiding. Lucy laughed and hugged Fluffy tightly.

Once upon a time there was a folder filled with nice things. The folder was happy and peaceful.

But one day, a strong wind came and scattered all the things from the folder. It blew everything around the room.

The folder was upset and started to look for the things that had been blown away. It searched high and low.

Suddenly, the folder heard a special sound. It was the sound of laughter! The folder looked up and saw a group of children playing happily with all the things that had been blown away.

The folder was happy again. It smiled and thought of how happy and peaceful it was to watch the children playing.

Once upon a time there was a tiny spider called Jasper. Everyday, he spun a beautiful cobweb in his small corner of the garden. It was so delicate that everyone said it looked like a rare and delicate piece of art!

One day, a strong wind came and blew Jasper's cobweb away! The poor spider was so sad!

Jasper was determined to build his cobweb back up. He scrambled up the long vines and worked away spinning out his web. But try as hard as he could, the cobweb would not look how it did before. Until one day, Jasper had an idea. He spooled the strands backwards and when he had finished, he was surprised to find that the cobweb was better than before! He had reversed the cobweb and made it look even more special.

From that day on, Jasper's cobweb was admired by all in the garden, and it became even more rare and beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight who loved to ride his horse. He had a symbol on his shield that showed he was a knight. One day, he fell off his horse and hurt his arm. It hurt so much that he couldn't move it. 

The knight went to see a wise old woman who knew how to heal people. She gave him some medicine and told him to rest. The knight was sad because he couldn't ride his horse anymore. 

But one day, the knight's arm felt better. He was so happy that he went outside to ride his horse again. He looked at his symbol on his shield and felt proud to be a brave knight. The end.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Mandy. She was three years old.
She had a big dream. She wanted to be a lamp.
One day she told her mom about her dream. Her mom smiled and said it was a great idea.

So that night, Mandy hoped and wished to be a lamp. Soon enough, her dream came true.
Mandy could now shine and twinkle like a bright lamp. She bounced around and twirled among the stars.

Mandy was so happy that she could make people smile while they looked at her bright light. She realized that hope can sometimes come true.

Toby was a 3-year-old boy who loved to explore the world around him. One day, he went out for a walk in the park. As he strolled along, Toby stopped and gazed at an old, dark pen. He was curious; why wouldn't it move or talk? Toby reached out and touched it. Suddenly, an old man popped up from behind the pen! Toby was very scared and stepped back.

The old man said, "Hello, little one. Don't worry, I'm not scary. I'm here to tell you a story." 
Toby blinked, still a bit scared but curious to hear the story. The old man smiled and said, " Long ago, this pen belonged to a brave knight. He used it to jot down his adventures and battles." 

Toby looked at the pen intently and then back at the old man. He asked, "Did the knight win?" The old man smiled and said, "Yes, the knight was very brave and won his battles. Now he's a legend, who will never be forgotten." Toby smiled, feeling reassured and much less scared. He thanked the old man, said goodbye and continued on his way.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anya. She was very polite and loved to skip around her house.

One day, Anya stepped outside of her house and she noticed something on the side of her house. It was a small, friendly bunny! Anya smiled and said hello to the bunny, and the bunny looked up at Anya and said, "Hi Anya!" 

Anya was so excited to meet the bunny that she started skipping around the yard. The bunny hopped around too and the two playmates soon became friends. 

Anya was so polite to the bunny. She always said hello and goodbye when she saw the bunny, and she always shared her vegetable treats with him. They had lots of fun playing together everyday. 

Anya and the bunny always skip around the side of the house together. The bunny felt so lucky to have Anya as a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she was picking daisies in the field when she saw her friend Ben coming towards her.

"Hi Lily!" said Ben. "What are you doing?"

"I'm picking daisies," replied Lily. "Do you want to help me?"

Ben nodded and they picked daisies together. Suddenly, Lily had an idea. "Let's throw the daisies up in the air and see where they land!" she said.

So, they threw the daisies up in the air and watched as they floated down to the ground. Lily felt calm and happy as she watched the daisies dance in the wind.

After they finished playing, Ben said, "That was so much fun! Let's do it again tomorrow!"

Lily smiled and nodded. She couldn't wait to play with her friend again and throw more daisies in the air.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - Lizzie and Tim. They were very organized and liked to keep their house tidy and neat. One day, they started to quarrel over something small.

Tim had a mustache and thought it made him look cool and grown-up, but Lizzie didn't agree. The quarrel got bigger and bigger, until the friends did not know what to do. Finally, they decided to go outside in the sunshine and have a chat.

Lizzie smiled and said, "I really like your mustache. I think it looks nice!" Tim smiled too and the quarrel was forgotten. 

The friends hugged and laughed about the silly quarrel. They knew that arguing was never the answer, and agreed to always be kind to each other no matter what.

The seal was having a tasty snack. He kept eating, enjoying the crunchy food. Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"What are you eating, seal?" It was a little girl.

"Yummy food," said the seal with a smile.

The little girl was curious. "Can I have some?"

The seal kept the food safe. "No, this is mine."

The little girl's stomach growled. "Please, can I have just one?"

The seal thought for a moment. He gave the little girl half of his snack.

The little girl was so happy. The food was tasty!

The seal kept smiling. He was happy to help.

Once upon a time, there was a fox. He was a very special fox because he liked to decorate! Every day he would go out and find wonderful things like bright leaves and shiny stones to decorate his den. His den was the most decorated den of all the foxes!

One day he found a box filled with beautiful decorations. He was so glad! He started to hang streamers and glittery paper around his den. He was so happy with the way it looked!

The other foxes heard about his decorations and came over to admire them. They were amazed and so excited. The foxes all danced and sang about how wonderful the decorations were. Everyone was glad and had a great time.

The fox was so happy he could make all the foxes smile. After that, he kept decorating his den every day. The foxes were so glad to come over and see the decorations. They were always a surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. She liked to make mud pies and pick pretty flowers. 

One day, Lily's garden was very slow. The flowers were not growing and the mud was not soft. Lily was sad because she loved her garden very much. She asked her mommy what was wrong. 

Mommy said that the garden needed more water and sunshine. So, Lily got a big watering can and poured lots of water on her garden. She also asked the sun to come out and shine on her garden. 

After a few days, Lily's garden was no longer slow. The flowers were bigger and prettier than ever before. Lily was happy again and she continued to make mud pies and pick pretty flowers in her beautiful garden. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to draw pictures with his crayons. One day, Timmy drew a picture of a big green dinosaur. It was very impressive! Timmy was so proud of his picture that he wanted to show it to everyone.

So, Timmy went to the park to meet his friends. He showed them his picture and they all said it was very good. But then, a big dog came and started to chase Timmy's friends. They all ran away, but Timmy was too slow. The dog caught Timmy and bit him. Timmy cried and cried.

When Timmy got home, his mom saw the bite and decided to take him to the doctor. The doctor said that Timmy needed a special medicine. Timmy's mom went to the pharmacy to get the medicine, but they didn't have any in stock. Timmy's mom was very sad.

In the end, Timmy got very sick and had to go to the hospital. His mom was very worried. Timmy's friends came to visit him at the hospital, but Timmy was too sick to play with them. Timmy's mom was sad that Timmy couldn't play with his friends anymore.

Mommy took her little girl outside to the park. It was a cold day and the little girl hugged her coat tight. They began to discuss an activity and soon came up with a unique suggestion - having a picnic. The little girl cheered and ran off to find some friends to invite. 

While they waited, Mommy and the little girl danced around in the cold. The little girl giggled loudly and spun around. They discussed what food to bring and decided on sandwiches, chips, and oranges. 

Soon the friends arrived and started setting up the picnic. Each brought something unique - one brought a dip, one brought a special blanket, and one brought a kite to fly. 

The friends had a lot of fun. They shared stories, laughed, talked, and tossed a ball around. When it got colder, the friends said goodbye and the little girl hugged each one. 

Mommy and the little girl happily went home and discussed their fun day. She couldn't wait for another picnic soon!

Billy wanted to go outside and play. It had been raining earlier, so there were puddles everywhere. He got a kick out of jumping and splashing in them. His mum said, "Okay, but be careful. Remember, you have to act bad in these puddles, okay?"

Billy said that he would and went outside. Everywhere he looked, there were big puddles. He jumped and skipped around them. He tried to stay away from the bigger and harder puddles. But no matter how hard he tried, he always ended up in the biggest, hardest puddles! 

Billy was having so much fun that he didn't even realize how wet he was getting. He just kept running and jumping around. His mum came out after a while and laughed as she saw him jumping around in the big, hard puddles. Then, she took his hand and said, "Come on! Time to get out of the puddles and act good now." 

Billy smiled and ran inside to get change of clothes. He had lots of fun, but he was happy to have followed his mum's advice to act bad outside and act good when he came inside.

One day, a little girl named Jane wanted to make something special. She wanted to find a way to make something that was as pretty as a happy song. 
So she decided to get some paint. She found white, pink, and yellow colors and she was very excited.

Jane got some big paper and put it on the table. Then she used a brush to spread the paint on the paper. She worked hard, mixing colors and making shapes.

When she was done, the picture looked beautiful. She showed it to her mom and her mom was so proud of her. She asked Jane to serve the picture to her friends.

So Jane proudly displayed her art to all her friends. Everyone was amazed at how hard Jane worked on the paint and how pretty it was. Jane was very pleased with her work and knew she could make something even better the next time.

One day, a little girl named Sarah wanted to take her puppy to the veterinarian. She promised her puppy that it was going to be fun.

The veterinarian was really nice, and he promised Sarah he would take good care of her puppy. He said it would be quick and cheap. 

The veterinarian checked if her puppy was healthy. He checked all of its eyes, ears and teeth. Everything looked good. 

The puppy was so happy everything was ok. Sarah promised to take better care of her pet and to take it to the veterinarian more often. 

The little girl and her puppy thanked the veterinarian for being so kind and for helping her puppy, and then they both left the clinic very happy.

Lily and Ben wanted to go to the zoo. They liked to see the animals and hear their sounds. But they needed a ticket to enter the zoo. They asked their mom if she could provide them with a ticket.

"Mom, can we go to the zoo today?" Lily asked.

"Please, mom, we want to see the lions and the monkeys and the penguins!" Ben added.

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, we can go to the zoo. But first, we have to do some chores. Lily, you have to tidy up your room. Ben, you have to help me with the dishes. Then, I will provide you with a ticket for the zoo."

Lily and Ben agreed and did their chores. They worked hard and fast. They wanted to go to the zoo as soon as possible. When they finished, they ran to their mom and said, "Mom, we are done! Can we have our ticket now?"

Mom nodded and gave them each a ticket. She said, "Good job, kids. You are very helpful and responsible. Now, let's go to the zoo and have some fun!"

Lily and Ben were very happy. They thanked their mom and hugged her. They put on their hats and sunscreen. They got in the car and drove to the zoo. They saw many animals and learned many things. They had a cool day at the zoo. They loved their mom and their ticket.

Once there was a chubby girl called Zoe. Every day Zoe liked to go to the park. She would run around, jump and have lots of fun. One day it was time for Zoe to take a nap, so her mum packed her a blanket and a pin.

When Zoe was ready, she went into the park and found a nice spot to take her nap. She spread out the blanket and the pin and lay down. Immediately she felt sleepy. She slowly closed her eyes and started to drift off.

After a while, Zoe woke up feeling quite refreshed. She gathered her things, put them back into her bag and said goodbye to the park. She ran all the way home, ready for whatever the day would bring!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Millie. Millie was very thoughtful and kind. She loved spending time near the sea because the sound of the waves made her feel happy and peaceful.

One day, Millie was walking along the beach when she heard a voice. The voice was coming from a dolphin who was swimming in the sea. The dolphin asked Millie if she wanted to be friends. Millie was so excited and very joyful.

But then the dolphin said that he wanted to trick Millie instead of being friends. He said that he wanted Millieâ€™s help to get some of the fish from the sea. Millie was sad and confused about this. She spoke kindly to the dolphin and told him she wanted to be friends, not to trick the fish.

The dolphin thought about what Millie said and he realized that she was kind and thoughtful. He decided that he wanted to be friends with Millie, and so he stopped his plans to trick the fish. 

Millie and the dolphin said goodbye and she went on her way. Millie was so happy that the dolphin was now her friend and even more thankful for her kind and thoughtful words.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to look nicer. He decided he wanted to get a haircut. He went to the barber and the barber welcomed him. The little boy was so excited for his new look. 

The barber got to work. He used scissors and comb to give the little boy his new haircut. After the haircut, the little boy looked in the mirror and he was so pleased with how he looked. 

The barber smiled and welcomed him to come back anytime he wanted. The little boy thanked the barber.

As he left the barbershop, the little boy felt so spoiled because he had a very nice haircut. He was very excited and happy about his new look.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy fan, but one day it broke. She was sad and didn't know what to do. 

Her mom came and asked her what happened. Lily showed her the broken fan and her mom said they could try to fix it. They looked for some glue and tried to put it back together, but it didn't work. 

Lily was still sad, but then her mom had an idea. She said they could add some new stickers to the fan to make it look pretty again. Lily loved this idea and they worked together to decorate the fan with colorful stickers. 

In the end, Lily was happy again and she learned that even when things break, there are ways to make them better. She also learned that she could be independent and try to find solutions to her problems.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys. Anna likes dolls and Ben likes cars. One day, they go to the toy store with their mom. They see many toys. Some are big, some are small, some are colorful, some are noisy.

Anna sees a doll that she likes. It has long hair, a pretty dress, and a crown. She says to her mom, "Mom, can I have this doll? It is my dream doll!"

Ben sees a car that he likes. It has four wheels, a shiny body, and a horn. He says to his mom, "Mom, can I have this car? It is my dream car!"

Mom looks at the price tags. She says, "I'm sorry, Anna and Ben, but these toys are too expensive. We can't buy them today. Maybe you can save your money and buy them later."

Anna and Ben are sad. They want their dream toys. They start to cry. Mom says, "Don't cry, Anna and Ben. There are many other toys that you can play with. Look, here are some puzzles, some books, some blocks. They are not expensive, but they are fun and good for your brain."

Anna and Ben stop crying. They look at the other toys. They see some puzzles, some books, some blocks. They think, maybe they are fun and good for their brain. They pick one puzzle, one book, and one block each. They say to their mom, "Mom, can we have these toys? They are not expensive, but they are fun and good for our brain."

Mom smiles. She says, "Yes, you can have these toys. They are not expensive, but they are fun and good for your brain. I'm proud of you, Anna and Ben. You learned to be happy with what you have, and not to be greedy for what you don't have. That is a good lesson to learn."

Anna and Ben hug their mom. They say, "Thank you, mom. We love you. We love our toys. They are not our dream toys, but they are our happy toys."

The end.

One day, a dark cloud brought a flood. The flood was big and strong. Everybody was scared and ran home. All the animals ran away too! 
The water came higher and higher. It was dark outside and the water was very cold. The trees and houses were all wet. 
But the sun came out and brought the flood back down. Everybody was happy and could go outside again. They all cheered and hugged each other when the water was gone. 
It was a happy day when the dark cloud brought the flood but the sun and everyone brought it back down.

Once upon a time there was a whale. He was swimming in the deep blue sea, enjoying being free. Suddenly he felt something touch his fin. He looked around and noticed a big, empty bowl.

He swam closer and peeked inside the bowl. It was full of yummy things! He couldn't resist and tasted a little bit of everything. It was delicious.

The whale was so happy that he went up to the surface of the ocean and shouted with joy. He stayed up there for a while, until it was time to go back under the sea.

The whale swam away with a smile on his face, still tasting the delicious flavours of the things he had eaten from the empty bowl.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly painter. He had a problem he couldn't solve. He was very sad and he couldn't figure out what to do.

One day, he went for a walk in the park. He saw a little girl playing. She looked so happy! He asked her for help.

She asked him what was wrong. The painter explained his problem. The girl thought for a minute, then she said she knew how to solve it.

The little girl told the painter what he should do. He did it and the problem was solved! He was so happy! He thanked the girl and gave her a big hug. The girl was very pleased and she waved goodbye as the painter went on his way.

The end.

Mummy and Little John were in the living room. Little John was so excited because they were going to play a game. Mummy said, "Let's play 'Stir the Pot'!"

Little John smiled and clapped his hands. He picked up a big spoon and began to stir the pot. He stirred it round and round, faster and faster. Then Mummy took her turn. She was so good at stirring the pot, she made it move so quickly!

Little John was getting restless. He wanted to stir the pot again, so he did. He stirred and stirred until the pot was full of sugary sweets. Then he and Mummy shared them and giggled as they ate.

Little John enjoyed the game so much. He couldn't wait to play again!

Max and his family lived in a lively house. They loved it because it always had energy and life. One day, as Max was playing around in the backyard, he heard a loud noise from the house. He approached cautiously and saw something he had never seen before - a strange, unfamiliar creature. Max was puzzled, but he bravely tried to greet the creature.

To Max's surprise, the creature spoke! He said he was an old friend of the family and had been looking for them for years. He wanted to come and visit often. Max's parents were stunned, but soon they began to recognize him.

Turns out, the mysterious creature was an old family pet that they had been separated from years ago. The family was overjoyed to have him back. The animal made the house even livelier, bringing joy and happiness to the family. Max was delighted - an old friend had arrived, and he cherished every minute of it.

Ria and Rob are twins. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big black bird on a tree. It is a raven.

"Look, Rob, a raven!" Ria says. "It is so black and shiny. I want to touch it."

"Me too," Rob says. "But it is too high. How can we reach it?"

Ria thinks. She sees a yellow ball near the tree. She has an idea.

"Let's try to throw the ball at the raven. Maybe it will come down," she says.

"OK, let's try," Rob says.
