They take turns to throw the ball at the raven. But the raven is smart. It dodges the ball every time. It makes a loud noise. It sounds like it is laughing at them.

"Stop it, raven!" Ria says. "You are not nice. Come down and play with us."

The raven does not listen. It flies away to another tree. Ria and Rob are sad. They want to make friends with the raven.

"Maybe we should try something else," Rob says. "Maybe we should give the raven something it likes. What do ravens like?"

Ria thinks. She remembers a story her mom told her. It is about a raven and a fox. The raven has a cheese in its mouth. The fox wants the cheese. The fox flatters the raven. The raven opens its mouth to sing. The cheese falls down. The fox eats the cheese.

"I know!" Ria says. "Ravens like cheese. Let's find some cheese and give it to the raven. Maybe it will come down and share it with us."

"Good idea," Rob says. "Let's go to the kitchen and get some cheese."

They run to the kitchen. They find a slice of cheese in the fridge. They run back to the tree. They see the raven still on the branch.

"Hey, raven, look what we have!" Ria says. "We have cheese. Do you want some cheese?"

The raven looks at the cheese. It smells good. It feels hungry. It flies down to the ground. It lands near Ria and Rob.

"Thank you, raven, for coming down," Ria says. "Here, you can have some cheese. But can we touch you? You are so soft and pretty."

The raven nods. It takes a bite of the cheese. It lets Ria and Rob touch its feathers. It feels nice. It makes a soft noise. It sounds like it is happy.

Ria and Rob smile. They are happy too. They have made a new friend. They share the cheese with the raven. They play with the ball. They have fun. They are glad they tried to be nice to the raven.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy liked to explore strange places. One day, she found an attic and she was curious about the attic.

The attic was light and not very scary. Lucy went up the stairs to explore it. Inside the attic she saw a bunch of interesting things.

The most interesting thing was a box of cookies. Lucy wanted to eat one of the cookies, so she opened the box and started to eat a cookie. It was delicious!

Lucy stayed in the attic for a while and ate all the cookies. Then she walked back down the stairs and went to find a new place to explore.

Once upon a time there was a man and his wife. He was strong and she was kind. Every day they worked very hard in the fields.

One day the wife said to her husband, â€œWe should be humble.â€

The husband nodded and said, â€œYes, we should always remember to be kind to others and to be thankful for what we have.â€

The couple worked hard every day and were happy in their life.

At the end of the day they came home and hugged each other. They thanked each other for being a good wife and husband.

The pair were truly happy and always remembered to be humble.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a boy playing with a long rod.

"Mommy, what is that boy doing?" asked Lily.

"He's measuring how far he can throw the stick," replied her mom.

Lily was curious, so she went over to the boy and asked if she could try too. The boy said yes, and Lily picked up the rod. It was very cold in her hands, but she was determined to throw it as far as she could.

She took a deep breath and threw the rod as hard as she could. It didn't go very far, but Lily was proud of herself for trying. The boy smiled and said, "You did a great job, Lily!" and Lily smiled back. From that day on, Lily loved to measure how far she could throw things, just like the boy with the rod.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and generous bear named Benny. Benny loved to share his honey with all his friends in the forest. One day, Benny saw the sky turn dark and cloudy. He knew that a big flood was coming. Benny warned all his friends to be careful and to stay safe.

As the rain poured down, the water rose higher and higher. Benny saw his friends struggling to stay afloat. He knew he had to do something to help. So, he used a big branch to make a raft and started to rescue his friends one by one. 

Finally, after a long and tiring day, Benny and his friends made it to safety. They all hugged and thanked Benny for his kind and generous heart. Benny smiled and nodded his head, knowing that helping others was the right thing to do. From that day on, Benny's friends knew they could always count on him to be there in times of need.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty lion named Leo. Leo lived in the jungle with his friends, the monkeys and the birds. One day, Leo and his friends decided to go on a trip to the hotel.

When they arrived at the hotel, the receptionist told them that they needed to pay to stay there. But Leo insisted that they should be allowed to stay for free because they were animals and didn't have any money. The receptionist explained that everyone needed to pay to stay at the hotel, even animals.

Leo was upset and started to roar loudly. His friends tried to calm him down and told him that it was important to follow the rules and pay for things that they needed. Leo realized that his friends were right and apologized to the receptionist for his behavior.

From that day on, Leo learned that it was important to follow the rules and pay for things that he needed. The moral of the story is that it's important to be responsible and follow the rules, even if we don't always like them.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful reef in the ocean. The reef was filled with colorful fish and bright corals. The coral was so beautiful that everyone wanted to receive it! 

But the reef was far away, and not everyone was able to get there. This made it difficult for those who wanted to receive the coral.

Then one day, something amazing happened. A ship arrived carrying a very special cargo - the reef! It was now available to everyone who wanted it. 

The people were so excited! They quickly packed up the reef and brought it back to their homes. They enjoyed the colors and the beauty of the reef. 

From that day onwards, the reef was freely available to those who wanted to receive it. All because of the special cargo ship! 


The End.

One day, Mum and Dad took Lily to the park. She was very excited! She loved being in the fresh air and watching the trees and the birds.

Lily saw a funny looking man wearing a big red cap. It was very interesting! She wanted to have a look at it. The man smiled at her and said "Hello Lily!"

Lily asked the man if she could try on his cap. He said yes, so she put it on her head. She felt so happy!

As the sun went down, Mum said it was time for Lily to take a nap. Lily said goodbye to the man, and as she walked away she was wearing her special cap.

Once upon a time there was a wild cat. He was wandering through the woods looking for a place he could call home. As he was looking, he passed by a clearing. There, on the floor was a strange box. The wild cat decided to take a closer look. The cat hopped in and found it was the perfect place for him to belong.

The wild cat curled up inside and fell asleep. After a while, a little girl spotted the cat in the box. She waved her hands and danced around, she was so excited. She wanted to take the cat, she knew he belonged with her. The cat meowed and said yes, so she carefully took him home.

Once home, the little girl chose for the cat a special place. It was a soft, fluffy rug on the floor. She knew it would be the perfect place for the cat to nap and play. The cat moved in right away and was so happy, he even jumped and purred to show he was happy he belonged. 

From that day on, the wild cat felt like he belonged with the little girl and her family. He found his true home and he was very happy.

Once upon a time there lived a bee. The bee loved to fly around outside in the fresh air. One day as the bee was flying, it saw a nice sunny spot. The bee liked the warm sun, so it flew down and relaxed. Suddenly, the bee heard a loud noise and felt a sharp pain. The bee was dead!

The bee had been stung by a big bee. The bee was very sad it had died but it was happy it had been able to relax in the sun for a bit before it passed away.

The other bees were sorry to hear that their friend was dead. They made sure to keep an eye out for any more bees flying around, so that they could stay safe.

The lesson from this story is to relax and enjoy life, but also be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play the flute and would practice every day. One day, her friend Emily came over to play. Emily saw Lily playing the flute and felt envious because she didn't know how to play. 

Emily asked Lily if she could try playing the flute, but Lily said no. Emily felt sad and didn't understand why Lily wouldn't share. She started to hate the flute and wished she could play it too. 

Lily noticed that Emily was upset and realized that she should have shared her flute. She apologized and let Emily try playing. Emily was so happy and even though she wasn't very good, Lily was proud of her for trying. From that day on, they played the flute together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful fragile cross.

The cross lived in a magical forest, right by a river. Every morning birds filled the sky with joyous singing and the wind filled the trees with a peaceful melody. 

One day, the cross decided to go on an adventure. She picked herself up and walked over to the river. There she filled her tiny hands with water and cast it into the sky.

Just then, a small creature in a boat appeared. It asked, â€œWhy did you fill the sky?â€

The cross smiled and replied, â€œTo make it look pretty!â€

The little creature laughed and said, â€œThatâ€™s a wonderful idea. Let me take you with me.â€

And so, with a single tug, the little boat filled with the fragile cross, and they spent the rest of the day exploring the river together.

One day there was a patient tortoise and a graceful butterfly. The butterfly was so amazed by how slow the tortoise moved that it wanted to compete against him. The butterfly flapped its wings and said "Let's have a race!" The tortoise was hesitant at first, but then agreed to the race.

The two animals started off, but the butterfly was too fast for the tortoise. It zipped past him with ease and was soon far ahead. The tortoise plodded along, but he was determined not to give up. 

The butterfly flew around and around the tortoise, waiting for him to part. But eventually, the tortoise caught up to the butterfly and they finished the race together! Both the tortoise and butterfly were tired, but they smiled at each other, proud of what they had achieved.

The patient tortoise had won the race with his graceful movements. The butterfly was so amazed, and they both went home happy.

Bob was out walking on the beach. It was a hot day, and he was looking at the waves. Suddenly, it started to rain. Bob was surprised. Rain was rare in this part of the world, so he was happy it was raining. He wanted to go for a swim, so he started running towards the sea.

When he got closer, he saw a big wave. Bob stopped and looked at it. It was so big! He couldn't believe his eyes. He looked around and saw that everyone else was running away from it.

Bob called out: "Why are you running away from the wave?"

One of the people replied: "It's too big! It will sweep us away!"

Bob was brave. He ran towards the big wave and jumped into it. He was happily swimming in the water. Bob had a rare and exciting experience!

Mama and Daddy took a photo of Jim. He was swimming in the pool. He felt happy and smiled. But then Jim made a stupid mistake. He swam too far and couldn't get back. Mama and Daddy were worried, but they found Jim and they all laughed. Mama took another photo with Jim in the pool. He was swimming again and happy.

Lily liked to sing. She sang all the time. She sang in the morning, she sang at lunch, she sang at night. She sang to her toys, she sang to her mom, she sang to her dog. She sang loud and she sang soft. She sang happy and she sang sad. She sang old songs and she sang new songs. She loved to sing.

One day, Lily saw a microphone in her dad's office. She wanted to sing with the microphone. She thought it would make her voice sound big and fun. She asked her dad if she could use the microphone. Her dad said yes, but only for a little while. He said he needed the microphone for his work. He said he had to make a speech with the microphone. He said he wanted to succeed with his speech. He said he worked hard to prepare his speech. He said he was nervous about his speech.

Lily took the microphone and went to her room. She sang with the microphone. She sang louder and louder. She sang faster and faster. She sang all her favorite songs. She had so much fun with the microphone. She forgot about her dad and his speech. She forgot about the time. She forgot to be quiet.

Her dad heard Lily singing with the microphone. He was not happy. He needed the microphone for his speech. He went to Lily's room. He knocked on the door. He asked Lily to stop singing. He asked Lily to give him the microphone. He said he had to go to his speech. He said he was late for his speech. He said he was angry with Lily.

Lily heard her dad knocking on the door. She was scared. She knew she did something bad. She knew she made her dad angry. She knew she had to give him the microphone. She felt sorry for her dad. She wanted him to succeed with his speech. She wanted him to be happy. She opened the door. She gave him the microphone. She said she was sorry. She said she loved him. She said she hoped he would do well with his speech.

Her dad took the microphone. He looked at Lily. He saw her sad face. He saw her sorry eyes. He saw her love. He felt sorry for Lily. He knew she liked to sing. He knew she was just having fun. He knew she was not nosy. He hugged Lily. He said he was sorry. He said he loved her. He said he was proud of her. He said he would come back soon. He said he would listen to her sing later. He left with the microphone.

Lily watched her dad leave with the microphone. She felt better. She knew her dad forgave her. She knew her dad loved her. She knew her dad would succeed with his speech. She smiled. She went back to her room. She sang without the microphone. She sang softly and sweetly. She sang a song for her dad. She sang a song of love.

Once there was a little girl named Sally. She was very eager to go see the big city. One day Sally's mom and dad took her to the city. It was really cool! 

The first thing Sally saw was a big hill with a park on top. She wanted to roll downhill on the grass. So Sally ran up the hill and rolled down it over and over until she was tired. It was so much fun! 

Next, they went to the city center. Sally could see all the tall buildings and the busy streets. She liked to see all the different people. Sally's parents bought her an ice cream and she ate it while strolling through the city. 

Sally was so happy to be in the city. She waved at all the passersby and smiled. The day was so nice and the city was so exciting. 

When it was time to go home, Sally said goodbye to the city with a big smile on her face. She was already eager to come back and roll down the big hill again!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Alice. She was standing in her garden looking up at the big blue sky. Suddenly she heard a loud, harsh noise. It was thunder! It made Alice jump and she was scared. She started to cry. 

Just then, her mum came out of the house and saw what had happened. She smiled at Alice and waved her hand. It was a special wave that said, "Don't be scared, I'm here with you". 

Alice felt better and she dried away her tears. As she looked up at the sky, she noticed that the thunderclouds were moving away. Then there was only sunshine and blue sky again. Alice smiled and waved back to her mum. 

The bright sunshine made Alice feel happy and she knew that there was no need to be scared of the thunder!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big pocket on his shirt. He loved to put things in his pocket like rocks, sticks, and even bugs! 

One day, Timmy went to the park to play. He saw a different boy there who he had never seen before. The different boy had a red ball, and Timmy wanted to play with it. 

But then, Timmy remembered he had a blue ball in his pocket! He took out his blue ball and showed it to the different boy. The different boy was happy to play with Timmy and his blue ball. 

From that day on, Timmy and the different boy became friends and played together often. Timmy always remembered to bring his blue ball in his pocket when he went to the park.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl who loved books. Her favourite place was the library; she went there every day. When she was there the brave girl liked to record different stories that she heard. She wrote them down in her notebook and made An illustrated book.

The brave girl would go to different places in the library and ask the librarian questions, and record the answers. She made all sorts of stories, from fairy tales to scary stories. She was very proud of her work!

One day, the brave girl was feeling extra brave. She went to the highest shelf in the library and took books that were much too big for her. Then, she went to a special room and recorded her own stories. She was so happy with what she heard!

The brave girl wrote and recorded stories every day. She loved spending time in the library learning new words, and recording different stories. Soon, she was the bravest girl in the library!

Once upon a time, there was a poor girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress, but it was old and worn. Lily loved her dress and wore it every day. She wished it could shine like the sun.

One day, Lily met a kind lady who had a magic wand. The lady saw Lily's dress and wanted to help. She said, "Lily, I can make your dress shine if you want."

Lily was so happy and said, "Yes, please!" The kind lady waved her magic wand, and Lily's dress began to shine like the sun. The poor girl was now wearing a beautiful, shiny dress.

Lily went home, and her mom saw her shiny dress. Her mom said, "Lily, your dress is so pretty now!" Lily smiled and said, "A kind lady helped me make it shine."

From that day on, Lily's dress always shined, and she was the happiest girl in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved playing on his computer all day long. His computer was very loud, but Timmy didn't care because he was having so much fun.

One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. His friend saw Timmy's computer and thought it was very cool. But instead of asking to play with it, Timmy's friend decided to steal it when Timmy wasn't looking.

Timmy was very sad when he realized his computer was gone. He didn't understand why his friend would steal from him. But his mom explained that stealing is wrong and hurts other people's feelings. From then on, Timmy learned to be careful with his things and to always be honest with his friends.

Once upon a time there were two nations that were very far apart. One nation was very small and the other nation was very big. The two nations did not get along. 

One day, a thick fog rolled in and the two nations could no longer see each other. They had no idea the other nation was still there. 

The small nation had an idea. They asked their good friend, a big elephant, if they could borrow his trunk. The elephant agreed and gave them a very long trunk. 

The small nation tied their end of the trunk to their village tree and they called out to the other nation. They asked them to accept the trunk and connect it to their village. 

The other nation was scared at first, but they accepted the trunk. As soon as they tied their end to the tree, the fog lifted and the two nations were very happy to see each other again. They became friends and traveled often between the two villages.

One morning, Jenny got up and went outside to the garden. She found a pretty rock and picked it up. She said to herself, "I'm not going to forget this pretty rock."

She brought it with her back inside and put it on a shelf. Later in the day, Jenny was busy playing with her toys. Then suddenly she remembered the rock. She asked her mom, "Mommy, did I forget something today?"

Mommy looked at her carefully and said, "No, I don't think so. What did you think you forgot?"

Jenny said, "I found a pretty rock this morning but I don't remember where I put it!"

Mommy smiled and said, "Oh, the rock. I put it on the shelf for you. You can go get it anytime you want."

Jenny smiled and ran off to get the rock. She looked at it and said, "Thanks, Mommy! I won't forget this pretty rock again!"

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit called Sam. Sam was a chubby little rabbit, who loved to find minerals in the woods. Everyday, he would search for rocks and crystals, and keep them in his pocket.

One day, Sam decided to explore a little deeper in the woods. He hopped for a long time, and discovered something special. It was a cave, made entirely of minerals and shimmering stones. Sam was filled with joy, and he gathered as many rocks as he could carry. He filled his pockets and he kept going deeper and deeper into the cave. 

Eventually, Sam got quite tired and he took a rest by a large rock. Suddenly, he heard a loud rumbling that kept getting louder and louder. He jumped up in shock and all of his rocks spilled out of his pocket. He quickly realized that the rock he had been resting on was a grumpy bear! The bear stood up and chased Sam out of the cave.

Sam hopped back home, safe and sound. He had learnt his lesson and he promised himself that he would never keep so many minerals again. He vowed to never forget about the grumpy bear in the cave, who had taught him a valuable lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, she saw her friend Timmy wearing a very cool shirt. 

"Wow, Timmy! That shirt is so cool! Did you design it yourself?" Lily asked.

"Yes, I did! My mom gave me some markers and I drew on the shirt," Timmy replied.

Lily thought that was a great idea. She wanted to design her own shirt too. So, she went home and asked her mom if she could have a plain white shirt. Her mom gave her one and Lily drew all over it with her markers.

The next day, Lily wore her new shirt to play with her friends. They all thought it was very cool and normal. They played in the sun all day and had lots of fun. The end.

Once there was a boy and a girl. They were best friends and talked all the time. One day, the boy and girl decided to take a trip together. They decided to go to the woods.

As they went, the girl got scared, so the boy put his shoulder close to her. It made her feel safe.

When they got to the woods, they talked about the nature surrounding them. The birds in the trees, the wind in the grass, and the sun warming their faces. It was so peaceful.

The boy and girl stayed in the woods all day, talking and exploring. By the time they left, they felt so happy and safe together.

John and his mommy were going on a big walk. John felt excited, but he was a little confused, because he had never gone on a big walk before.

John asked his mommy, "Where are we going?"

Mommy smiled and said, "We're going to the park, darling. Here, carry this basket."

John looked at the basket. It was light and filled with food for his lunch. He could smell the food, and it made his tummy rumble.

John and his mommy kept walking. The sun was getting very hot, but John wanted to keep walking, until he got tired. Finally, he said to mommy that he was tired, so they stopped and sat in the grass.

Mommy said, "Let's have some food, and then you can have a nap in the basket, if you want."

John was so happy. He loved having naps in his basket. He ate his food quickly and lay down in his basket. He felt so cozy and happy. He closed his eyes and fell quickly asleep.

Mommy watched over John as he slept, feeling very content. She stayed there until John had woken up and then they went home.

Tom and Lily were friends. They liked to play with ropes. They made knots with the ropes. They made big knots and small knots. They made knots that looked like animals and knots that looked like stars.

One day, they found a new rope. It was long and red. They wanted to play with it. They took turns to make knots with it. Tom made a knot that looked like a snake. Lily made a knot that looked like a flower. They were happy.

But then, the rope got stuck. They could not undo the knots. They pulled and twisted, but the rope did not move. They were sad.

They saw a man walking by. He had a hat and a tool. He was a gardener. He saw the children and the rope. He asked them, "Do you need help?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, please. We can't undo the knots. We are sorry."

The gardener smiled. He said, "Don't worry. I can help you. I have a tool that can cut the rope. But you have to be careful. Don't touch the tool. It is sharp."

He took out his tool. It was a pair of scissors. He cut the rope. He freed the knots. He gave the rope back to the children. He said, "Here you go. You can play with the rope again. But be careful not to make too many knots. They can be hard to undo."

Tom and Lily thanked the gardener. They said, "Thank you, thank you. You are very kind. We are grateful."

They hugged the gardener. They hugged each other. They played with the rope again. But they did not make too many knots. They learned their lesson. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a strong elephant. He was walking, looking for something to eat. He saw a big, tasty sandwich on the ground. He was so hungry and couldn't wait to eat it. But when he went to cover it with his trunk, he couldn't reach it. He was so sad. 

Suddenly, he saw a tiny mouse. He asked the mouse to help him. The mouse said yes. Together, they managed to cover the sandwich. 

The elephant thanked the mouse. He said, "You are so strong. Now we can both enjoy this tasty sandwich." They both ate the sandwich and the elephant was so full and happy.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a very peaceful spot in the woods. All the animals liked to come there because it was so peaceful and calm. 

One day a rabbit spotted something strange in the spot. He was very curious and wanted to know what it was so he rushed over. 

When he got there he saw a little cub playing in the spot, making it even more peaceful. The rabbit was so happy he found a friend to play with and they became best buddies. They both loved playing in the spot. 

Every day, the rabbit and the cub would rush to their spot to play games and have fun. They stayed there for hours, until the sun went down in the sky. 

The two friends were always so happy in their peaceful spot.

Once upon a time there was a curious little girl. She liked to explore and find interesting things. One day while she was playing by the river, she spotted a twinkling diamond on the ground. She said to herself, "Ooh, a diamond!" She picked it up and brought it home to show her mum.

Mum smiled and said, "That's a pretty diamond, my love. We should look after it and keep it as our special gem."

The little girl nodded and carefully placed the diamond in her pocket. But later that evening, when the diamond was nowhere to be found, everyone was very sad.

The little girl's mum looked at her and asked, "Do you know where the diamond is, my love? We really want it back."

The little girl felt so guilty and ashamed. She knew she had lost it in the river. She looked up at her mum and said, "I'm so sorry, Mum. I lost the diamond in the river."

Mum smiled and said. "It's ok, my love. I forgive you. Let's go and search for the diamond tomorrow."

The next day they went to the river and searched and searched until they finally found the diamond. Everyone was so happy!

Mum said to the little girl, "I'm so glad we found the diamond. That was so kind of you to come here and help look for it

Once upon a time, there was a little baby girl named Ashley. She was three years old, and wanted to learn all about the world.

One day, Ashley's mom took her to the park. Ashley saw lots of pretty flowers and birds. But, the most beautiful thing of all was a big, shiny diamond! Ashley was so excited, she wanted to pick it up, but her mom said, "No Ashley, that is not yours. We need to be compassionate when we look at things like this."

Ashley's mom knelt down and explained to her why it was wrong to take the diamond. "It belongs to somebody else, and it is not nice to take something that does not belong to us," she said.

Ashley listened carefully and learned the important lesson. She smiled and hugged her mom, and the two of them enjoyed the rest of their day at the park. Ashley never forgot what she had learned about being compassionate with what does not belong to her.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play sport. They have a ball and a bat. They go to the park with their mums.

"Can I hit the ball first?" Tim asks.

"OK, but I will catch it," Sam says.

Tim holds the bat and Sam throws the ball. Tim swings the bat and hits the ball hard. The ball flies in the air.

"Wow, good hit!" Sam says. He runs after the ball.

But the ball is too fast. It goes over the fence and into the road.

"Oh no, the ball is gone!" Tim says.

They look at the road. There are many cars and bikes. They are loud and fast. They cannot get the ball.

They are sad. They like their ball.

A man sees them. He is clever. He has a big stick. He walks to the road. He waits for the cars and bikes to stop. He uses the stick to get the ball. He brings the ball back to Tim and Sam.

"Here you go, boys. Be careful next time," he says.

"Thank you, sir. You are very kind," Tim and Sam say.

They are happy. They have their ball again.

They hug the man. They hug their mums. They spend the rest of the day playing sport in the park. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was walking down the street when he saw a poor little bird with a broken wing. Timmy felt very sad for the bird and wanted to help.

He asked the bird, "Are you okay? Do you need help?" The bird replied, "Yes, please. I can't fly with my broken wing."

Timmy gently picked up the bird and held it close to his shoulder. "Don't worry," he said. "I will take care of you." Timmy took the bird home and gave it some food and water. The bird was very happy and grateful for Timmy's help.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Alex. He had a friend called Beth. One day, they decided to go to the church. When they got there, they saw it was very clean and bright. Alex looked around and saw a beautiful statue. He wanted to touch it, but Beth said to him: "We must not touch things in the church. We must be respectful."

Alex nodded and said: "I promise I won't." Then Beth smiled and said: "That's good. We must always know how to keep our promises."

After that, they decided to explore the church. They saw the altar, the pulpit and the pews. Alex kept his promise and kept his hands to himself. He understood that it was important to keep his word and to show respect. 

When they were done exploring, Alex and Beth went back home. Alex was glad that he had kept his promise. He felt good in knowing that he had done the right thing. He knew he could always trust himself to keep his promises. 

The moral of this story is that it's important to keep the promises we make. We should always do the right thing, even when it's difficult and even when no one is watching.

Once upon a time there were twin brothers. They were very happy and loved to play. Every morning they would hug each other and go off on their adventures.

One day, the twins saw a high hill. They decided to climb to the top together. At the very top of the hill, they hugged each other tightly and stayed like that until the sun went down.

When the twins reached home later that day, they hugged their parents tight and told them about their adventure.

From then on, the twins hugged each other every time they reached the top of a high hill. They would hand-squeeze and never get tired of it.

The twins were best friends forever, and hugging each other helped them make special memories they would always keep close in their hearts.

Molly couldn't help but stare at the tower. It was so attractive! Every day she walked past the tower and was always amazed. She wished she could act like the tower and stand so strong.

One day, Molly decided she would try to act like the tower. She ran around the garden pretending she was the tower and that she was proud and strong. It was so much fun!

After a few hours of pretending, Molly was very tired. But she was happy. She had acted just like the tower, and now she felt brave.

Every day after that, Molly ran around her garden and acted like the tower. She felt proud and happy as she ran around, pretending to be strong and attractive.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Jane. Jane had a naughty streak and she was spoiled by her parents. She was always asking for new things and often got them. 

One day her parents took her to the market. Jane saw a toy vendor and asked her parents to buy her one right away. But her parents said, "No, Jane. You need to earn it first so that you can learn the value of things."

Jane was disappointed but her parents continued walking around the market. Suddenly, she spotted a balloon vendor and saw a big, red balloon that she really wanted. She begged her parents to buy it for her but they again said, "No Jane, you'll have to perform a task first to earn the balloon."

Jane thought hard and finally suggested that she would clean her room if they bought her the balloon. Her parents agreed and Jane was so surprised she jumped with joy! Jane rushed home, cleaned her room and the next day, her parents took her back to the market and bought her the big, red balloon.

The story teaches us that when things are earned, they are more appreciated and treasured than if we just get them for free. Jane learned this lesson and was so happy to have her red balloon!

Once upon a time, there was a happy family living in the city. The family had a nice house and lived there together.

One day, the family found out that their house was too small for them, so they decided to look for a new shelter. They looked and looked, but all the shelters were too expensive. The family was getting worried that they wouldn't find a new place to live.

One day, they were walking in the park and they saw a surprising sign. It said "Cheap Shelter!" The family was so excited that they rushed over to take a look. The shelter looked perfect, it was just the right size and very affordable.

The family were so pleased that they decided to lie and tell the man they had been looking for a shelter for a long time. The man was so happy that he gave them the shelter for even less than the price on the sign. 

The family was so relieved to have found a cheap shelter. They moved in and enjoyed their new home. And they lived happily ever after!

One day, a little cat was very thirsty. She wanted to drink some water. She went to a big bowl to drink. But when she got there, she saw a lot of bubbles in the water. The cat was scared of the bubbles.

A dog came to the bowl. He wanted to drink too. The cat and the dog did not like each other. They both wanted the water, but they did not want to share. The cat was sad and the dog was mad.

Then, a big bird came and saw the cat and the dog. The bird was very wise. It told the cat and the dog to be friends and share the water. The cat and the dog listened to the bird. They drank the water together and the bubbles went away. The cat and the dog were glad and they became friends.

One day there was a little boy who found an oxygen canister. He was so grateful that he had something to fill his lungs with so he ran home and grabbed a balloon. He wanted to stay happy forever and promised to keep the oxygen canister with him always. But suddenly, the oxygen ran out and the little boy started to get sleepy. He wanted to stay awake, but the oxygen was all gone. He lay down, feeling very tired and soon the little boy feel fast asleep and couldn't wake up again. He was gone forever. Everyone was very sad and they were grateful for the time he stayed with them.

One day, a girl named Sarah decided to go for a jog in the park. Her mom and dad said she had to stay on the path. Sarah was excited to go for a jog, so she started running. With each step, she could feel her lungs working hard. She hadn't gone very far when she saw something strange. It looked like a person, but it was fake! It was made of plastic. Sarah was scared and turned around to go back. When she got back to the path, she started to slow down until she was back to her original jogging speed. Sarah thought it was funny that she had seen something so fake during her jog. She was glad that she hadn't gone too far off the path. From then on, she always stayed on the path when she went jogging.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat cereal for breakfast every morning. One day, when he poured his cereal into his bowl, he noticed that his spoon looked bigger than usual. He was confused and asked his mom, "Mommy, why does my spoon look so big?"

His mom replied, "Oh no, Timmy! It's not your spoon that's big, you've shrunk!"

Timmy was shocked and looked down at his hands. They did look smaller than before. "How did I shrink?" he asked.

"I don't know, Timmy. But don't worry, we'll figure it out," his mom reassured him.

Timmy finished his cereal, even though the spoon was now a bit too big for him to handle. He knew that he had to find a way to grow back to his normal size.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. One day it wanted to go to the park. It flapped its wings and flew away. As soon as it reached the park, it saw many other birds. It was excited and wanted to join them. 

It was in a hurry to get there, so it flew as fast as its wings could carry it. But then it started to rain. The rain was very mild, but it was enough to make the little bird scared. It started to tremble and flew back home.

As soon as it reached home it was relieved. It was safe and dry. The little bird taught itself a lesson to not hurry too much and stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fierce lion. He loved to play sport with his friends in the jungle. One day, his friends asked him to supply the ball for their game. The lion was happy to help and ran back to his den to get the ball. 

When he returned, his friends were very happy and thanked him for supplying the ball. They played the game for hours and had lots of fun. The lion was very proud that he could help his friends and make them happy. 

From that day on, the lion always made sure to supply the ball for their sport games. He loved playing with his friends and being a helpful part of their team.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside. One day, he saw an insect. It was green and small. Tim wanted to touch it.

"Hello, insect!" Tim said. "Are you real or fake?" The insect did not talk. Tim realized that insects do not talk. He touched the insect. It moved! It was not fake.

Tim was happy. He had a new friend. He played with the insect all day. They had fun. Tim learned that insects can be friends too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. She was the happiest three year old around. One day, Mary went to the park with her mom. She saw a net lying on the ground and wondered what it was for. She asked her mom and she said it was for catching butterflies. 

Mary was so excited! With her mom's help, she started weaving the net like a spiderweb. When she was done, they went out to the garden and waited for the butterflies to come.
 
Sure enough, a few beautiful, charming butterflies flew by and Mary finished her net. She gracefully placed it over the butterflies and, sure enough, she had caught them. She was so happy and excited that she ran around the garden in excitement. 

At the end of the day, Mary had caught some of the most beautiful and charming butterflies in the world. What a wonderful day she had!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One sunny day, Lily and her friends decided to have a picnic in the park. They brought sandwiches, fruit, and cookies.

As they were eating, Lily's friend Alex noticed that his water bottle was empty. "I need more water," he said. "Can we go to the water line?" 

Lily knew where the water line was. She had seen it before. "Sure," she said. "Let's go." 

When they got to the water line, they saw a big scale. "What's that?" Lily asked. 

"It's a scale," Alex said. "You can weigh things on it." 

Lily thought that was cool. She wanted to weigh something too. "Can we weigh my cookie?" she asked. 

They put the cookie on the scale and saw that it weighed one ounce. "Wow!" Lily said. "That's not very heavy." 

As they walked back to their picnic spot, they noticed that the sun was getting hot. "It's a hot day," Lily said. "But at least we have water and cookies!"

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, Fin met a friendly octopus named Otto. Otto had eight arms and was very useful. Fin and Otto became good friends and swam together every day.

One day, Fin saw a shiny object in the water. He thought it was a treasure and wanted to take it home. But Otto told him it was dangerous and could hurt him. Fin didn't listen and tried to grab it anyway. Suddenly, a big wave came and swept Fin away.

When Fin finally made it back to Otto, he was very scared. Otto scolded him and told him that he could have been punished for not listening. Fin felt very bad and promised to always listen to Otto from now on. They continued to swim together every day and Fin never forgot the lesson he learned about listening to his wise friend.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to part the flowers and smell them. They saw a big red roof over the fence. They wondered what was inside.

They climbed on a chair and looked over the fence. They saw a man and a woman eating a cake. The cake looked delicious. It had white cream and red berries on top. Ben and Lily wanted some cake too.

They jumped over the fence and ran to the table. The man and the woman were surprised. They asked who they were and what they wanted. Ben and Lily said they wanted some cake. They said it looked delicious.

The man and the woman smiled. They said they were their neighbors and they were having a picnic. They said they had enough cake for everyone. They cut two slices and gave them to Ben and Lily. Ben and Lily said thank you and ate the cake. It was delicious.

They became friends with the man and the woman. They told them their names and where they lived. They said they liked their big red roof. The man and the woman said they liked their garden and their flowers. They invited them to come again. Ben and Lily said yes and went back to their garden. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a gray cat named Mittens. One day, Lily and Mittens went to a party. It was a contest to see who could decorate the best cake.

Lily said to Mittens, "I hope we win the contest. I want to decorate a cake with lots of frosting and sprinkles." Mittens meowed in agreement.

Lily and Mittens worked hard to decorate their cake. They put frosting all over it and sprinkled it with colorful candy. When the judges tasted their cake, they said, "You win the contest! Your cake is the best!"

Lily and Mittens were so happy that they won. They celebrated by eating lots of cake and sharing it with their friends. From that day on, Lily and Mittens always loved to decorate cakes together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Ted who loved to explore. One day he was looking through his telescope and he saw something pink up in the sky. He was so excited to see it!

It turned out to be a beautiful little planet. It was a special kind of planet because it was made out of pink bubblegum. The pink bubblegum was so sparkly and delicious, it made Ted's mouth water.

Ted wanted to go explore the planet. He put on his space suit and launched off in his rocket ship. As he got closer to the planet, he was so excited. He was amazed at how soft and bouncy the pink bubblegum planet was. He jumped up and down and it felt like being on a trampoline. He had the best time exploring on the planet.

When it was finally time for Ted to go home he was a little sad to leave the planet. But he knew that he could always come back to explore and have fun. As he flew off into the night, Ted couldn't help but smile.

Grandma was getting ready to bake. She dressed in her ancient apron and smiled as she pulled it over her head.

She noticed little timid Bobby, who had been standing in the corner watching.

"Hi Bobby!" Grandma said. "Why don't you come and help me?"

Bobby's eyes filled with excitement as he ran over to the kitchen counter. He grabbed the bowl and spoon and asked, "What can I do?"

Grandma smiled and said, "You can help me fill this bowl with flour!"

Bobby beamed with pride as he filled the bowl to the brim. Grandma gave Bobby a big hug and said, "Thank you Bobby, this looks perfect!"

Bobby filled with joy, knowing that he had helped Grandma out.

Once, there was a pink wheel that belonged to a little girl. She was so excited to get the wheel, so she quickly put it on and started to ride down the street. As she was riding and having lots of fun, she got very tired. She yawned and her eyes got heavy and all she wanted to do was sleep.

So, the little girl stopped riding and got off the pink wheel. She decided to take a nap right next to the wheel, so she could take it with her when she woke up. She was snoring happily when suddenly the wind started blowing harder. The pink wheel started to move away and the little girl woke up in a shock.

She quickly got up and started running to get her wheel. But before she could reach it, the pink wheel stopped near a small pond. She was so lucky to find her wheel, so she picked it up and put it on again. She was so happy to have her wheel that she yawned with a big smile on her face.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. Today, they both want to play with the same toy. It is a red car with four wheels.

"Give me the car!" Anna says.

"No, it is mine!" Ben says.

They pull the car from each other. They quarrel. They are not nice to each other.

"Stop it!" a voice says. It is Mom. She comes to the park. She sees Anna and Ben. She is sad.

"Why are you quarreling?" Mom asks. "You are friends. You should share and be kind."

Anna and Ben look at Mom. They feel sorry. They let go of the car.

"I am sorry, Ben," Anna says.

"I am sorry, Anna," Ben says.

They hug each other. They are friends again.

Mom smiles. She is happy. She gives Anna and Ben a scarf. It is a warm and soft scarf. It is blue and yellow.

"Here, this is for you," Mom says. "You can wear it when it is cold. You can also share it when you play."

Anna and Ben like the scarf. They thank Mom. They put the scarf around their necks. They play with the car together. They are happy.

Once there was a clever girl named Susie. She loved to make soup. Every day she would go to the store and buy the ingredients for her soup. She would come back home and put all the ingredients into a pot and boil it until it was nice and hot. 

Everyone in Susie's neighbourhood loved her soup. Susie was always very happy when people liked her soup and thanked her for making it. 

One day Susie invited her friends to her house for lunch. She made a big pot of her soup, and her friends ate it all up. They praised her soup and said it was the best soup they had ever tasted.

Susie was so proud of her soup and her cleverness. She smiled gleefully, knowing that she had made something that people enjoyed. From that day onwards, everyone in the neighbourhood knew her name - Susie the Soup-Maker!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big bird with many feathers. The bird was blue and yellow and green. It was very pretty.

"Look, Tom, a parrot!" Lily said. "I want to touch it."

"Be careful, Lily," Tom said. "The parrot might bite you."

Lily did not listen to Tom. She ran to the parrot and tried to grab a feather. The parrot did not like that. It squawked and pecked at Lily's hand. Lily cried out and let go of the feather.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily said. "The parrot hurt me!"

Tom ran to Lily and hugged her. He saw the feather on the ground. It was bright and soft.

"Wow, Lily, you got a feather!" Tom said. "It is very expensive. People pay a lot of money for feathers like this."

"Really?" Lily said. She forgot about her pain. She looked at the feather and smiled. "It is very beautiful. Can I keep it?"

"Sure, Lily," Tom said. "It is yours. But next time, listen to me, okay? The parrot is not a toy. It is a wild animal."

"Okay, Tom," Lily said. "I am sorry. Thank you for being my friend."

They held hands and walked back to their mom. They showed her the feather and told her the story. Mom was glad they were safe. She gave them a kiss and a cookie. They shared the cookie and the feather. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play in the garden with her toys. One day, she saw a snake in the garden. The snake was very long and green. Lily was scared of the snake because she thought it might bite her.

Lily's mom saw the snake too and told her not to touch it because it was fragile and could get hurt easily. Lily listened to her mom and stayed away from the snake. She learned that it's important to be careful with fragile things.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toys again. She saw her friend Emily playing with a new toy. Lily wanted the same toy too. She asked Emily if she could play with it, but Emily said no. Lily felt sad because she couldn't gain the toy.

But then Lily remembered what her mom said about fragile things. She realized that it's important to be happy with what you have and not always want more. Lily learned that it's better to be grateful for what you have than to always want more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in nature. She would run around and pick flowers. One day, Lily saw a big storm coming. She ran to her house and told her mommy. Her mommy said, "We need to cover our windows so the rain doesn't come inside."

Lily helped her mommy cover the windows with big blankets. They were lucky because the rain didn't come inside. But then, they heard a loud noise. They looked outside and saw that a big tree had fallen on their car. They were very sad because they couldn't drive their car anymore. They had to walk everywhere they went. 

One day, when they were walking to the store, it started to rain really hard. They didn't have an umbrella, so they got very wet. When they got home, they were cold and shivering. They realized that they were not lucky anymore. They were sad because they had to walk in the rain and couldn't drive their car. But they were happy that they were safe inside their home.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bob and Sam. They both liked to explore the world around them. One day, they went on an adventure and stumbled across something very exciting - a fire! They had never seen anything like it before and it was very beautiful.

Bob was very scared. He had never seen a fire before and wasn't sure what to do. But Sam was brave and walked towards it. He bent down and put his hand out to see how hot it was. It was warm, but not too hot.

Then he saw something - it was a box that belonged to someone! Sam opened the box carefully and saw that it was full of different coloured things. Some of them were shiny and some of them were sparkly - he had never seen anything like it before.

He called to Bob and Bob slowly came closer. When he saw the box, he was no longer scared. He saw how beautiful the things were and wanted to own some of them! So they both grabbed what they could and put it in the box.

They were so happy that they ran back home. They told everyone about their adventure and showed them what they had found in the fire. It was the best thing that ever happened to them!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found a new truck that he really liked. It was big and blue and had a telephone on the back.

Timmy's friend, Johnny, came over to play. Johnny brought his own truck to play with. It was also big and blue, but it didn't have a telephone on the back. Timmy said, "My truck is better because it has a telephone on the back. It's original."

Johnny didn't agree. He said, "My truck is better because it matches the color of the sky." Timmy didn't like that. He wanted his truck to be the best. They argued for a while, but then Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's race our trucks and see which one is faster!" Johnny agreed.

They lined up their trucks and raced them down the hallway. Timmy's truck was faster, but Johnny's truck matched the color of the sky better. In the end, they both agreed that their trucks were special in their own way. They decided to play with both trucks together and have fun.

Anna and Ben love to play soccer. They have a small ball and two goals in their backyard. They pretend they are in a big stadium with many people watching them. They cheer and clap when they score a goal.

One day, their mom tells them they can go to a real stadium. She has tickets for a soccer game. Anna and Ben are very happy. They put on their soccer shirts and hats. They get in the car with their mom and dad.

At the stadium, they see many people wearing different colors. They hear loud noises and music. They find their seats and watch the players on the field. They see their favorite team in blue and white. They shout and wave their flags.

The game is very exciting. Both teams try to score goals. Sometimes, the ball hits the post or goes over the bar. Sometimes, the goalkeeper makes a great save. Anna and Ben cheer and boo with the crowd.

Near the end of the game, the score is tied. The blue and white team has a chance to win. One of their players runs with the ball and shoots. The ball flies towards the goal. But the goalkeeper from the other team jumps and reaches the ball. He saves it with his hand. The crowd gasps.

"Wow, what a save!" Ben says.

"That was so close!" Anna says.

The game ends in a draw. The players shake hands and thank the fans. Anna and Ben clap and smile. They had a lot of fun. They think the stadium is beautiful. They want to come back again. They hug their mom and dad and say thank you. They go home and dream of playing soccer in the stadium.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Tim. Tim was a very tough bug. He lived in a big green garden with many other bugs. Every day, Tim would play with his bug friends. They would run, jump, and fly all around the garden.

One day, Tim saw a big rock in the garden. He thought it would be fun to climb to the top. Tim told his friends, "I am going to climb that big rock." His friends were scared, but they knew Tim was a tough bug. They said, "Be careful, Tim!"

Tim started to climb the big rock. It was very high, but Tim did not stop. He kept going up and up. His friends watched from the ground, cheering him on. They knew that Tim was a tough bug and he could do it.

Finally, Tim reached the top of the rock. He looked down at his friends and shouted, "I did it!" His friends clapped and cheered. They knew that Tim was a tough bug and he would never stop. From that day on, Tim and his friends played on the big rock every day, and they had lots of fun.

Jan and Jack were best friends. One day they were playing outside and decided to go down the slide. They giggled as they took turns slipping down. 

"Faster, faster!" Jan shouted. 

Jack then had an idea. "Let's use some fuel to make the slide even faster!" Jack said.

Jan thought it was a great plan, so they grabbed a bucket of fuel. They cautiously poured some onto the slide. 

The slide was becoming quite dirty. But finally, they were ready to go. 

"Let's slide!" Jan said. 

So they took turns sliding down the faster, dirtier slide. It was a lot of fun and they both shouted, "Yay!" at the end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Elsie. She loved to run around in the big grassy fields and feel the sun on her face. One day, Elsieâ€™s mom told her to take a deep breath and be still and quiet. Elsie tried, but it was hard to stay still and quiet in the fields. 

Eventually Elsie did find a moment of peace. Everything around her felt so tight and calm. She felt like she could heal and find strength in that peace. 

As Elsie started to relax, a big loud noise came out of nowhere. It was a monster! The monster shouted at Elsie and told her that the peace in the fields was his and he didnâ€™t want her there. Elsie was so scared she ran away and never returned to the fields again.

The monster stayed in the fields and never let anyone enjoy the quiet peace any longer.

Once upon a time, there was a large elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved to play in the mud and roll around in it. One day, Ellie's mom said, "Ellie, it's time to wash up!" 

Ellie didn't want to wash because she loved feeling muddy. But her mom said, "You need to wash, or else you'll get sick." 

Ellie stomped her feet and said, "No, I don't want to wash! I want to stay muddy!" 

Her mom replied, "But Ellie, your friends won't want to play with you if you're all muddy. They might think you're a monster!" 

Ellie thought about it and realized her mom was right. She didn't want her friends to be scared of her. So, she reluctantly agreed to wash up. As she washed, she noticed the soap made a zigzag pattern on her skin. She giggled and said, "Look, Mom! Zigzag!" 

After she was all clean, Ellie felt much better. She hugged her mom and said, "Thanks for making me wash, Mom. I feel much better now!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. He was only three years old and he always loved to play. One day, he was poking around in the yard, looking for something interesting, when he found a present! It was wrapped up in a big, fit bow and Sam was very excited.

Sam ran into the house and showed his mom the present. She smiled and said, "Well, what do you think it is, Sam?"

Sam shook his head. He had no idea what was inside, so they decided to open it up together. Sam poked at the bow until it came apart and together, he and his mom opened the present.

As soon as they opened it, Sam squealed with joy - it was a bright red tricycle! It was perfect and fit Sam's size perfectly. 

Sam jumped up and down with delight and said, "Thank you Mom!"

His mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Sam. I think you'll have lots of fun with it."

And he did â€“ until this day, Sam still loves to go outside and poke around the yard with his new tricycle.

Chris was a chubby three-year-old boy. He liked to think about his familyâ€™s old van. He thought it was so cool and wanted to ride in it all the time.

One day, his family decided to take it for a ride. Chris was so excited that he could hardly wait. He kept on thinking of all the fun stuff they would do.

When they got to the park, Chris was so happy. He thought it would be so fun to ride around in the van. He couldn't believe how much fun he was having.

When it was time to go home, they all hopped in the van and drove away. Chris kept looking at the van from his seat in the car. He knew he would never forget his fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, while playing, Timmy saw a big elephant walking towards them.

"Wow! Look at the big elephant!" Timmy shouted.

His friend Sarah said, "I'm scared of elephants."

"Don't be scared," Timmy said. "The elephant is friendly. Let's go gather some peanuts to feed him."

So, Timmy and his friends gathered some peanuts and fed the elephant. The elephant was grateful and gave them a big hug with his trunk.

From that day on, Timmy and his friends visited the elephant every week and they all became great friends.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Carl and Grandma. Grandma was very curious and every day she would come up with an exciting new adventure.

Today Carl and Grandma were going to the mall. Carl was so excited! 

"Let's go solve something exciting today! What do you think it could be?" Grandma asked Carl.

Carl thought for a moment and then said, "Let's go solve why the mall is so big!"

So off they went to the mall. Grandma was very curious and asked questions about why there were so many stores. Everywhere they went, Carl and Grandma were trying to solve the mystery. 

Eventually, they discovered why the mall was so big - it had many different stores which people visited to buy things!

Carl and Grandma were very proud of themselves for solving the mystery of why the mall was so big. They had a lot of fun and made many more discoveries on their adventure!

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play basketball in the park. They have a big, orange basketball that bounces high. They take turns to throw the basketball into the hoop.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees Sam and Ben playing basketball. He wants to play too, but he is not nice. He grabs the basketball from Sam and runs away.

"Hey, give it back!" Sam shouts. He runs after the big boy.

Ben follows Sam. He is scared of the big boy. He is much taller and thicker than them. He has a mean face and a loud voice.

"Stop, or I will hit you!" the big boy says. He holds the basketball tight.

Sam and Ben stop. They do not want to get hurt. They look at each other. They are sad and angry.

"Please, give us our basketball back. It is ours. We were playing with it first," Ben says. He tries to be brave.

The big boy laughs. He does not care. He says, "No, it is mine now. You are too small and weak to play with it. Go away, or I will hit you harder."

Sam and Ben do not know what to do. They want their basketball back, but they are afraid of the big boy. They wish someone would help them.

Then, they hear a voice. It is Lisa, their friend. She is riding her bike in the park. She sees what is happening. She is not scared of the big boy. She is smart and strong.

"Hey, you, leave them alone!" she says. She rides her bike towards the big boy.

The big boy looks at Lisa. He thinks she is just a girl. He does not think she can do anything. He says, "What do you want, you little brat? Go away, or I will hit you too."

Lisa does not reply. She does not waste her words. She has a plan. She rides her bike faster and faster. She gets closer and closer to the big boy. She lifts her foot and kicks the basketball out of his hands.

The basketball flies in the air. Sam and Ben see it. They run to catch it. They grab it and hug it. They are happy and relieved.

Lisa stops her bike. She smiles at Sam and Ben. She says, "Are you okay, guys? That was a mean thing he did. He should not take your things or threaten you. He should learn to share and be nice."

Sam and Ben nod. They thank Lisa for her help. They say, "You are awesome, Lisa. You are our hero. Do you want to play basketball with us?"

Lisa says, "Sure, I would love to. Basketball is fun. Let's go to the hoop and see who can score more points."

They go to the hoop and play basketball. They have a lot of fun. They forget about the big boy. He runs away. He is ashamed and angry. He does not bother them again.

Once upon a time, there was a carpet. It was very empty. One day, a little girl wanted to mix it up. She took some colours and a big paintbrush. She started mixing the colours. She made yellow, green, blue and orange. She painted the carpet with the colours. The carpet was so colourful! Everyone was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny who loved to work. Every day the bunny worked very hard. But one day, the bunny had a problem. While he was working, the bunny fell off his tree. He was so scared that he started to cry.

Then a friendly bear came by and saw the bunny. The bear was very thoughtful and asked him what had happened. The bunny told the bear that he had fallen over while working.

The bear said to the bunny, â€œDonâ€™t worry, I can help!â€ The bear put his arms around the bunny and they carefully climbed back up the tree.

Once at the top, the bunny thanked the bear. From then on, the bunny was very careful when he was working. The bunny and the bear became great friends and worked together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his tools, especially his hammer. One day, Timmy's dad gave him a new tool. Timmy was so happy he jumped up and down!

"Daddy, thank you for my new tool!" Timmy said.

"You're welcome, Timmy. I'm glad you're happy," replied his dad.

Timmy couldn't wait to use his new tool. He ran outside to his tree fort and began to hammer away. Timmy loved to build things and his new tool helped him do it even better. He felt so proud when he received compliments from his friends about his tree fort.

Once upon a time, there was a baby called Jack. Jack was very special; he loved to dance and play. One day his parents took him to the shops. Jack was so excited.

He saw lots of shoes in the shop and wanted a new pair. His parents let him pick out the best shoes for him. Jack saw a very popular shoe and said, "I want that one!" His parents said, "OK!" and they ordered the shoes for him.

When the shoes arrived, Jack was so happy. He put them on and couldn't stop dancing around! His parents were so proud of their little dancer. The popular shoe made Jack look extra special.

The end!

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys. Sara likes to play with dolls and Tom likes to play with cars. One day, they decide to play restaurant. Sara is the cook and Tom is the waiter.

Sara makes some pretend food with her pots and pans. She puts them on a tray and gives it to Tom. Tom takes the tray and walks to the table. He sees a big teddy bear sitting on a chair. He thinks the teddy bear is a customer. He puts the tray in front of the teddy bear and says, "Here is your food. Enjoy!"

Sara sees Tom talking to the teddy bear. She gets angry. She runs to the table and grabs the tray. She says, "That is not your customer. That is my teddy bear. He is mine. Give me back my food!"

Tom gets angry too. He pulls the tray from Sara. He says, "No, he is my customer. I am the waiter. I serve the food. You are just the cook. You stay in the kitchen!"

Sara and Tom start to fight over the tray. They tug and push and shout. The tray falls to the floor. The pretend food spills everywhere. The teddy bear falls off the chair. Sara and Tom stop fighting. They look at the mess. They feel sad.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees Sara and Tom and the mess. She says, "What happened here? Why are you fighting? Why did you make such a mess?"

Sara and Tom look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing restaurant. But we got angry. We wanted the teddy bear and the food. We did not share. We did not listen. We did not have fun."

Mom says, "I see. Playing restaurant can be fun. But you have to share and listen and have fun. You have to work together. You have to respect each other. You have to be kind. That is how you play well. That is how you make friends. That is how you make Mom happy."

Sara and Tom nod. They say, "We understand, Mom. We will share and listen and have fun. We will work together. We will respect each other. We will be kind. We will play well. We will make friends. We will make Mom happy."

Mom smiles. She says, "That is good. I am proud of you. Now, let's clean up this mess. Then, we can have some real food. I will serve you some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Sara and Tom smile too. They say, "That sounds great, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."

They hug Mom. They help Mom clean up. They have some cookies and milk. They play with the teddy bear. They play restaurant again. But this time, they share and listen and have fun. They work together. They respect each other. They are kind. They play well. They make friends. They make Mom happy. They are happy too. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little puppy. He was always so happy, playing with his friends and wagging his tail. One day, the puppy's best friend got very sick. The puppy felt so sad and didn't know what to do. He started to weep. He wept and wept until his mommy saw him. His mommy told him it was going to be ok and hugged him tight. She took him to see his friend the next day, and the puppy's friend was all better. The puppy was so happy he started to run and jump around, barking and playing with his friend again. They were best friends forever and always had nice days together. The end.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play hide and seek. One day, they play in the park with Mom and Dad. Lily and Ben run and hide behind trees and bushes. Mom and Dad look for them and call their names.

Lily sees a big hill. She thinks it is a good place to hide. She runs up the hill and lies down on the grass. She feels the sun on her skin. She hears the birds sing. She smiles and waits for Mom and Dad to find her.

Ben sees a big slide. He thinks it is a good place to surprise Mom and Dad. He climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. He sees Mom and Dad walk by. He waits for the right moment. He slides down fast and shouts "Surprise!" He laughs and hopes to scare them.

Mom and Dad hear Ben's voice. They turn around and see him on the slide. They are surprised and happy. They clap and cheer for him. They say "Wow, Ben, you are so high on the slide! You are brave and clever!"

Lily hears Mom and Dad's voices. She wonders what is going on. She gets up and looks down the hill. She sees Ben on the slide and Mom and Dad near him. She feels left out and sad. She says "Hey, what about me? I am hiding too!"

Mom and Dad hear Lily's voice. They look up the hill and see her on the grass. They are surprised and happy. They wave and smile at her. They say "Wow, Lily, you are so high on the hill! You are smart and sneaky!"

Lily and Ben see each other. They wave and smile too. They are proud and happy. They run to Mom and Dad and hug them. They say "We love you, Mom and Dad! We love to play hide and seek! We love to surprise you!" Mom and Dad say "We love you, Lily and Ben! You are both amazing! You both surprise us!" They all laugh and hug. They have fun in the park.

A girl was feeling very shy. Every day she would watch other kids playing and wished she could join them. She knew she was too scared to do it.

One day the girl had a plan. She was going to be brave and try to make some new friends.

She took a deep breath, gave a little wave, and said "hello" to the other kids. They all said "hello" back and smiled.

The girl was so happy to have new friends. She played with them until it was time to go home.

The girl told her parents all about her plan and how it worked out. Her parents were so proud of her. From that day forward she was never shy again.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many rocks and trees. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lila!" Tom said. "We can do it!"

"OK, Tom!" Lila said. "But be careful. There might be animals or bugs."

They started to climb the hill. They held hands and helped each other. They were brave and strong. They saw many flowers and birds and butterflies. They were happy and curious.

But they did not see the snake. The snake was hiding under a rock. The snake was hungry and angry. The snake was patient. It waited for the right moment to attack.

When Lila and Tom reached the top of the hill, they saw a beautiful lake. They were excited and proud. They had succeeded in climbing the hill.

"Wow, look, Lila!" Tom said. "The water is so blue and shiny. Can we go and swim?"

"Maybe, Tom." Lila said. "But first, let's rest and have a snack. I'm tired and hungry."

They sat down on the grass and opened their backpacks. They had sandwiches and cookies and juice. They smiled and shared their food.

But they did not see the snake. The snake had followed them up the hill. The snake was fast and quiet. The snake was ready to strike.

The snake bit Lila on the leg. Lila screamed and dropped her cookie. Tom saw the snake and shouted.

"Help, help! A snake! A snake!"

But it was too late. The snake had poisoned Lila. Lila felt dizzy and sick. She fell to the ground and closed her eyes.

Tom cried and hugged Lila. He did not know what to do. He was scared and sad. He had lost his friend.

The snake slithered away. The snake was full and satisfied. The snake had succeeded in catching its prey.

One day, a little girl named Lucy was playing in the park. She saw a monkey swinging from a tree. Lucy was so excited to see a monkey!

"Good monkey," Lucy said.

The monkey turned and smiled at Lucy.

"I like you," said the monkey.

Lucy was very happy, so she hugged the monkey. They decided to go for a walk together, and they had lots of fun.

Suddenly, something amazing happened. Lucy could fly, just like the monkey! They flew around the park together, laughing and having a great time in the air.

At the end of the day, Lucy and the monkey hugged goodbye. They promised each other they would both fly together again soon. Lucy waved goodbye as the monkey flew away.

What a good day, Lucy thought. A day she would always remember.

Once there was a hungry girl called Amy. She saw a path, so she followed it. It was a winding path that was full of exciting things to explore. Amy came across a big tree and she touched it with her hand. The bark was smooth and sharp.

Amy got hungrier and hungrier. Suddenly she saw a big, juicy strawberry growing on the tree. She climbed up the tree and picked it. It was so sweet! She enjoyed it very much and then carried on down the path.

At the end of the path, there was a big lake. Amy saw some fishes swimming in the water, so she decided to try to catch them. She went to the shore and threw in a pebble. The fishes got sharp and started to swim away. Amy was so happy to see them.

She sat by the lake with her strawberry and watched the fishes. It was a beautiful day. And best of all, she was no longer hungry.

Once there was a big green frog who wanted to go outside and have some fun. But first he had to step over a wet cable. He hopped carefully around it and looked at the trees in the sunshine. It was a beautiful day! He could see a pond nearby and he hopped towards it. When he got close, he jumped straight in! The cool water felt so nice on his skin and he splashed around happily. But then he heard a noise! Suddenly he jumped out and saw an animal running away. His heart raced and he looked all around. He was safe, but it was time to go back home. The frog stepped carefully over the wet cable and hopped away. He was so happy to have had such an exciting adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a kind bunny named Benny. Benny liked to hop and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny saw a hunter with a big gun. The hunter was looking for animals to hunt.

Benny was scared and wanted to run away, but he saw his friend, a little mouse, was stuck in a trap. Benny knew he had to help his friend. He hopped over to the trap and tried to open it, but it was too strong. Then, he had an idea. He squeezed through the bars of the trap and helped his friend escape.

The hunter saw what Benny did and was surprised. He realized that not all animals were bad and decided to stop hunting. Benny and his friends were happy that they could play in the forest without being scared anymore.

Once upon a time, in a big city, there was a clever cat named Tom. Tom loved to play in the park near his house. One day, while playing in the park, he saw a big office building. He thought it would be fun to go inside and explore.

Tom went into the office and saw many people working. He also saw another cat named Sally. Sally was very pretty and clever too. Tom said, "Hi Sally! Do you want to play in the park with me?" Sally said, "Yes, Tom! But first, let's find a toy to play with."

Tom and Sally looked around the office, and they found a big box of toys. They knew they would have lots of fun with the toys in the park. They took the box and went to the park.

In the park, Tom and Sally played with the toys all day long. They had so much fun! As they played, they became very good friends. They knew they would come back to the park and the office many times to play and have fun together.

Once upon a time, two friends named Jack and Jill were walking through the woods. As they walked, Jack saw a bright light coming from behind a tree. It was a big, round bulb that was shining light all around it.

The friends were very excited! They quickly grabbed the bulb and held it up so they could get a closer look. Inside the bulb was a very rich, sparkling gold!

Jill was so amazed, she couldn't believe what she was seeing. She shouted, "Let's take it home!"

Jack agreed, so the two friends quickly made their way home. They put the bulb into the ground and waited.

As the sun began to rise in the morning, the bulb lit up the sky. Jack and Jill looked up in awe as the light from the bulb rose high into the sky. Soon, the sky was filled with a golden brightness.

Jack and Jill were so proud of their new bulb. The rich golden light would remind them of their amazing adventure in the woods forever.

Once upon a time, a little girl was playing in her garden. The sun was bright, and the sky was blue. She saw something pink in the grass. She picked it up and saw it was a yogurt. She was so excited because she loved yogurt.

The little girl wanted to share her yogurt with her friends so she invited them to come to her garden. She said, "Come to my garden! I have a pink yogurt!!". Soon, all of her friends came. They were very happy and they loved the pink yogurt. 

The little girl was so happy that she invited her friends to come to her garden all the time. They ate yogurt, ran around, and played all day. The little girl and her friends had so much fun. 

The end.

A mom and dad were getting ready for a trip. The mom packed their luggage and the dad loaded it in the car. Then they hugged each other, kissed their three year old daughter and said goodbye. The daughter was sad, but she knew they would come back soon.

The mom and dad traveled to a big city. They were very serious because they had important business to do. They carried their luggage as they went from meeting to meeting. After many days of hard work, they were done, and they were ready to go home.

At home, their daughter ran to hug them. She was so happy that they were back. As she held them close, she could tell how much they cared for her. She knew that no matter what, her mom and dad would always be there for her.
