Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy asked her if she wanted to help clean the house. 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I think I can help make the house strong." 

Her mommy smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Lily. Let's start by picking up all the toys." 

Lily picked up her dolls and blocks and put them away. As she was cleaning, she noticed her daddy fixing a broken chair. 

"Daddy, are you making the chair strong again?" she asked. 

"Yes, Lily. I'm using glue to make it strong," her daddy replied. 

Lily was happy she could help make the house strong and clean. She knew it was important to take care of her home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had his own toy sword. He liked to play with his sword every day. He would pretend to be a brave knight, fighting dragons and saving the day.

One day, Tim saw a big, angry dog in his yard. The dog was barking very loud. Tim was scared, but he knew he had to protect his family. So, he grabbed his toy sword and went outside.

Tim waved his sword at the angry dog. The dog stopped barking and looked at Tim. Tim said, "Go away, dog!" The dog listened to Tim and went away. Tim felt very brave and happy. He knew his toy sword helped him be a hero that day.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dolphin named Flip. Flip loved to swim in the big blue ocean and jump out of the water. One day, Flip met a silly seagull named Squawk. Squawk was always doing stupid things like flying into rocks. 

Flip and Squawk became friends and played together every day. They would jump and splash in the waves, making big splashes. One day, Squawk tried to jump like Flip, but he was too silly and fell into the water. Flip laughed and helped Squawk back onto the shore. 

From then on, Squawk never tried to jump like Flip again, but they still had fun playing together. They would watch the sunset and listen to the waves. Flip was happy to have a friend like Squawk, even if he was a little bit stupid sometimes.

Once upon a time there was a town that glowed at night. All the houses and shops had special lights that shone so brightly. Everyone in the town was so spoiled; they had all they needed. Everyone shared lots of things and there was kindness all around.

One night something extra special happened. The town was glowing even brighter than usual. Little Peter looked out his window and rubbed his eyes, for the town had become more magical than ever before.

Sparkles were shooting out from the town and everyone cheered. But then, something funny happened. A rainbow dragon came flying down from the sky. It was carrying a big bag of treats for everyone in the town. Soon the town was filled with laughter and joy from all the lucky people who got their treats.

All the people of the town had never been so spoiled! And from that day on, the town kept glowing brighter and brighter every night. That's why no matter how dark it gets the town of lights will always shine.

Once upon a time there was a little bear who had a very special job. His job was to organize the garden. Every morning he got up early and went to work. He put things in order and did his best to create a beautiful structure.

One day there was a big surprise waiting for him in the garden. A rich grandmother lived nearby and had dropped off a basket of treats for the bear. Inside the basket there were cookies and cake, apples and candy. The bear was so excited and couldn't believe his luck. He thanked the grandmother with a big smile.

The bear sat in the garden eating his treats and was so happy. He knew he had to organize the granny's gift. He tried to figure out what the best way to set everything up was. He finally decided to make the biggest apples into a pile and the cookies into a square. 

The bear was so proud of his work. When the grandmother came back to check on the bear, she said "Oh my! What a beautiful and rich structure you've organized. Great job!"

The little bear was so happy to hear his work had been appreciated. He promised to organize the garden even better the next day.  And that's how the little bear spent each day making the garden look even better and more organized.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who wanted to go outside and have some fun. He asked his mum if he could go out but she said no, because it was raining. He was so sorry that he couldn't go out and play, so he stayed inside and played instead.

Afterwards, he heard the rain slowing down, so he got very excited and asked his mum if he could go out and play now. His mum said yes, so he quickly put on his coat and boots and ran outside.

The bunny was so happy that he could go out and play, he laughed and jumped around in the rain. He ran around until he got so wet that he was almost swimming, then he ran back inside. His mum smiled as he came in, and said "Time for a nice warm bath!"

Once upon a time, there was a three year old called Jack. He loved to zoom around on his scooter and was very proud he didn't need help anymore. 

One day, Jack saw a quiz on the ground. He thought it was weird and tried to pick it up. Suddenly, the quiz came to life and spoke to him.

"Let's go on a zoom!" the quiz said.

Jack had never heard something so weird before but was also excited about a new adventure.

"OK!" he agreed, and started scooting away. But the quiz had tricked him! 

The further jack zoomed, the more lost he became. Nothing looked familiar anymore and he realised he couldn't find his way home anymore.

Jack sat down and started to cry. He was lost and alone in a strange place.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat pasta for dinner every night. Her mom always made a generous amount of it, so she never went hungry.

One day, Lily's mom promised to take her to the park after dinner. Lily was so excited! She ate all her pasta as fast as she could so they could go to the park.

At the park, Lily saw a big slide that she wanted to go on. But there was a long line of kids waiting to go down. Lily's mom told her to be patient and wait her turn.

Finally, it was Lily's turn to go down the slide. She climbed up the ladder and slid down, feeling so happy. She realized that sometimes it's worth waiting patiently for something good.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They played on the swings and went down the slide. Lily saw a big ice cream truck and asked her mom if she could have some ice cream. Her mom said they only had a few minutes left before they had to go home.

Lily had to decide if she wanted to spend her last minute at the park getting ice cream or playing on the monkey bars. She thought for a wise moment and decided to get ice cream. She ran over to the ice cream truck and got a big cone with sprinkles on top. It was the best minute of her day!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved summer because he could play outside all day long. One day, Timmy went to the park and saw a little girl sitting alone on a bench. Timmy went to talk to her and asked if she wanted to play with him. The little girl was shy at first, but Timmy was patient and waited for her to feel comfortable. They played together all day and had so much fun. From that day on, they became best friends and played together every summer.

Lily and Ben are playing in the living room. They have a big carpet that is smooth and soft. They like to roll on the carpet and pretend they are animals.

"Look, I'm a snake!" Lily says, as she slides on the carpet. She makes a hissing sound and wiggles her body.

"I'm a lion!" Ben says, as he jumps on the carpet. He makes a roaring sound and shakes his mane.

They have fun rolling and making noises. They laugh and giggle.

But then, Mom comes in. She is not happy. She sees the carpet is messy and dirty.

"Who made this mess?" Mom asks, with a frown. "You have to clean up the carpet. It is not a toy."

Lily and Ben stop playing. They feel sorry. They did not mean to make Mom angry.

"We're sorry, Mom," they say together. "We were just playing."

Mom sighs. She knows they are good kids. She smiles and hugs them.

"It's okay, my loves," she says. "But next time, please be careful with the carpet. It is not cheap. And it is not smooth when it is dirty."

Lily and Ben nod. They help Mom clean up the carpet. They use a brush and a cloth. They make the carpet smooth and clean again.

They learn their lesson. They still play on the carpet, but they are more gentle. They do not roll too hard or make too much dirt. They want to keep the carpet nice and smooth. And they want to make Mom happy.

John was carrying a big box. He was very excited about it. He asked his mother, "What is in the box?" She said, "It is jazz music."

John smiled and said, "Can I carry it?" His mother smiled and said, "Yes, you can carry it."

John wanted to show everyone his new jazz music. He went to his neighbor's house and knocked on the door. When they opened it, he said, "I have jazz music!" 

His neighbor smiled and said, "Oh, that is nice. Let me hear it!"

John was so excited. He opened the box and played the jazz music. Everyone clapped and started dancing. John was so proud of himself.

Suddenly, one of his friends made a mistake while dancing. John felt so ashamed that he put the music back in the box and quickly ran away.

When he reached home, his mother saw him. She said, "Why did you carry the music away? You were having so much fun!"

John said, "I was too ashamed." His mother hugged him and said, "Everyone makes mistakes, it's okay."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dolls. They liked to pretend that their dolls were having a tea party. They had a small table, some cups and plates, and a cake that Lily's mom had made for them.

A man with a big mustache walked by. He smiled at them and said hello. He looked friendly and kind. Lily and Ben gazed at his mustache. They had never seen such a big mustache before. It was black and curly and covered his mouth.

"Wow, what a big mustache!" Lily said. "Can I touch it?"

The man laughed and nodded. He bent down and let Lily touch his mustache. It felt soft and tickly. Lily giggled.

"Can I touch it too?" Ben asked.

The man nodded again and let Ben touch his mustache. Ben smiled.

"It's like a fuzzy caterpillar!" Ben said.

The man smiled and said, "Thank you. I like my mustache. It keeps me warm and makes me happy."

Lily and Ben liked the man with the big mustache. They asked him if he wanted to join their tea party. The man said yes and sat down with them. They gave him a cup of tea and a slice of cake. They talked and laughed and had fun. The man with the big mustache was their new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tommy. Tommy was three years old and he liked to explore. One day he wanted to listen to what the grown-ups were talking about. So he hid behind the couch.

The grown-ups were talking about toilets. They said the red toilet kept making funny sounds. Tommy thought this sounded really cool. But his mom caught him and dragged him away from the couch.

The next day, when Tommy was playing in his room, he heard a funny noise coming from the hallway. It was an even funnier sound than the red toilet! He went to the hallway and saw the red toilet making all kinds of funny noises. It was so much fun that Tommy couldn't help but laugh.

He knew he shouldn't have been playing with the red toilet, but he just couldn't help it. He played with the red toilet until his mom came and told him it was time to go outside. He promised he would listen next time and not get into trouble.

Once there was a little girl named Amy who was very bored. She wanted something interesting to do. So she decided to go for a walk and explore. As she walked, she heard a loud rumbling sound. She looked up to see a tornado coming her way. She quickly hid behind a bush.

While she was hiding, Amy noticed a bright rainbow in the sky. She watched in awe as the tornado passed. When it was gone, Amy ran back home to tell her family what she had seen.

Amy was so excited to share her story of the tornado. But then she realized that it wasn't as interesting as she thought it would be. It was boring. Amy wasn't scared anymore. In fact, she was looking forward to seeing more tornadoes!

It was a warm summer day, and the sun was shining bright. Then all of a sudden, clouds filled the sky and the wind started to blow. Then it started to rain!

The rain was so heavy that it was like a wall of water pouring down from the sky. The horse in the field felt the rain on its hairy back and it liked it. It shook its head, enjoying the feel of the rain.

The rain kept falling and the horse continued to walk around in the field, feeling the rain all over its furry body. Soon, it was drenched with rainwater.

The horse happily trotted around and around in the field. After the rain stopped, the horse shook its body off, sending the remaining bits of rain flying away.

The sun came out once again and the horse continued feeling the warmth of the sunshine on its back. Soon, the horse's fur was completely dry.

Binny wanted to stay warm, so she put on her coat and hat. She went outside and felt the cold air on her cheeks. She was excited to slide on the snow. 

She stepped into the snow and the texture was rough and squishy. Grinning, she started walking. She was peaceful and happy. 

Suddenly, she slipped and nearly fell, but then she remembered her momâ€™s words. She could be safe if she â€œyieldedâ€ -she should just move slowly and carefully, like a snail. So Binny took a deep breath, bent her knees and closed her eyes. 

After a few seconds, she opened her eyes and realized that she was still standing. She had yielded to the cold ground and stayed safe. With a satisfied nod, she continued her adventure.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy who wanted to be a princess. She loved pink and wanted to be surrounded by it all of the time. One day her mom came in with a big box from the store. Daisy ran up to it and carefully opened it. Inside was a pink crown with feathers and glitter. Daisy's eyes opened wide with surprise! She was so delighted that she put it on straight away. 

However, soon Daisy started to realize that the crown was a bit fake. She asked her mom, "Is this crown real?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "No, Daisy, it's not real. But even if it isn't real, you can still trust in the feeling it gives you. You don't need a real crown to feel like a princess."

Daisy smiled. She knew that was true. Even though the crown was fake, it still made her feel special. She decided to trust in that feeling. 

And so Daisy proudly wore her fake pink crown and became the princess she always wanted to be!

Once upon a time there was a ugly fan. The fan was very old and it stood in the corner of the room. One day, the fan stopped working. so the family had to leave it behind. The family was sad that the old fan was gone, but they knew it was time to get a new one. So they went out and found a shiny new fan. The new fan was big and worked perfectly. The family was so happy! They left the ugly old fan behind and started to enjoy the nice cool breeze from the new fan.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was three years old and very curious. 
Every day, she would ask her mom questions. Today, Jane asked her mom, "What is the most important thing to remember?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Always spread value and be ready for anything." 

Jane didn't quite understand so she asked, "What does 'spread value' mean?"

Her mom explained, "If you spread value, it means that you can share something special and make people smile. If you see someone who needs help, you should try to help them and be kind."

Jane nodded her head. She was ready to spread value and make someone smile!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy, especially the delicious gummy bears her mom gave her. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and brought her favorite backpack. Her mom helped her put on the backpack and zippered it closed. 

As they played, Lily noticed a boy playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, but she didn't want to leave her backpack alone. So, she decided to keep it close to her. 

After a while, Lily got thirsty and asked her mom for some water. Her mom reached into the backpack to get the water bottle, but it was gone! They looked around and saw the boy from earlier running away with the backpack in his hand. 

Lily felt sad and scared, but her mom told her they would find the boy and get the backpack back. They searched the park and finally found the boy. He had opened the backpack and was about to eat the gummy bears. Lily's mom asked him to give back the backpack and he did. Lily was happy to have her backpack back and she learned to always keep an eye on her things.

Sam was a young boy who was very curious. Every day he wanted to explore new things, like the cable that hung from the wall. One day, he asked his mom if he could touch it.

"No Sam," his mom said. She was very careful. "That cable is special, we have to be careful with it. We can't allow you to touch it."

Sam was sad. He wanted to touch the cable, so he asked his mom if maybe he could touch it just a little bit.

His mom thought for a moment and then said, "OK, but you have to be extra careful. You can only touch it very gently."
Sam was so excited that he was allowed to touch the cable. He was gentle and careful as he touched it. He was so happy that he was able to explore something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird loved to fly high in the sky. One day, the bird flew over a big field. The field was very clear, with no trees or bushes. The bird saw some bugs on the ground and swooped down to eat them. After the bird ate, it flew back up into the clear sky. The bird felt happy and free while it flew. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little train named Toot. Toot was very miserable. He did not like to work. Every day, Toot would watch the other trains go by, with steam coming out of their tops.

One day, Toot met a big train named Puff. Puff was very happy. Toot asked, "Why are you so happy?" Puff said, "I love to work and help people. It makes me feel good."

Toot thought about what Puff said. The next day, Toot tried to work and help people too. As Toot worked, steam came out of his top. Toot was not miserable anymore. He was happy, just like Puff. And they both worked together, helping people every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her fingers and make pretty pictures. One day, she went for a walk and found a lonely stone on the ground. 

Lily felt sad for the stone because it was all alone. So, she decided to paint it with pretty colors to make it happy. She used her red, blue, and yellow paint to make a rainbow on the stone. 

Now, the stone was no longer lonely. It had a friend in Lily and a pretty rainbow to look at. Lily was happy too because she made a new friend and painted something beautiful. From that day on, Lily always painted stones when she went for walks, and she never felt lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old fox who lived in a big forest. Every day, the fox liked to sit in a clearing and think about life. One day, a little bunny hopped over and saw the fox. The bunny asked, "What are you thinking about, fox?" 

The fox said, "I'm thinking about understanding." 

The bunny asked, "What does that mean?" 

The fox replied, "It means to use your head. You understand things when you use your head to think about them." 

The bunny thought for a moment and then asked, "Can I use my head to understand the color of my hair?" 

The fox smiled and said, "Yes, you can." The fox explained if the bunny looked at his hair and thought about it, he could understand why it was the color it was. 

The bunny thanked the fox and hopped away. The fox smiled and knew that the bunny now understood that using your head to think and understand was a very wise thing to do. 

The moral of the story is this: understanding things is important, and it comes from thinking, not from just knowing facts. That's why it's important to be wise and think before you act.

Nina and her mom were in the kitchen making cookies.
"Mom, can I use the scissors?" asked Nina.
Her mom said, "Yes, you can use the scissors to cut the blanket so it can be a cape." 
Nina took the scissors and cut the blanket into a nice shaped cape, and she put it on.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was so hungry, he couldn't think. He wanted to find a place to get something to eat.

He looked around and found a big house. He knocked on the door to ask if they could fix him something to eat.

The family inside the house were so kind. They opened the door and said, "Come in little boy. We will fix you something to eat."

The little boy was so happy and went inside. The family gave him a big plate of food. He ate it all up, it was yummy.

When he was finished, the family took him to a special place. It was cozy and comfortable inside. The little boy had his own bed to sleep in.

The family said, "See, you can stay here. We fixed you a place to sleep."

The little boy was so thankful. He thanked the family and went to sleep in his cozy bed. He was no longer hungry and he was so happy. The end.

Once there was a girl who really wanted to go on an adventure. She wanted to explore a stream she had never seen. So, she went with her mom to find it. It was a very quiet stream, with no people around. The girl and her mom sat down by the water and the girl started throwing stones in. She wanted to make little patterns in the water. Suddenly she saw a fish swim up to the surface. The fish wanted to play, too. So the girl and the fish had lots of fun together. Then, after playing for a while, she and her mom went home. She was very happy that she had found a new friend in the quiet stream.

Once there was a family who liked to go for walks. Whenever they went for a walk, the staff would help them by carrying their bags. 

One day, the family went for a walk, but something was wrong. The staff seemed very sad. The family asked what was wrong, but the staff could not say. 

The family asked the staff to stop and take a break. The staff was very happy and thanked the family for being so kind. 

The family gave the staff some cookies and a drink. After a few minutes, the staff was feeling better. The family was so happy to see the staff smile again. 

The family offered to help the staff more often when they went on their walks. The staff was so thankful and said they would be happy to have the familyâ€™s help. 

From then on, whenever the family went for a walk, they were sure to help the staff so they could both enjoy their time together.

Sally and her mom were walking along the street one day. Sally really wanted a new toy but it was too expensive for her mom. Suddenly, Sally saw a toy in the window of a shop.

"Mommy, can I get it?" Sally asked.

Mommy shook her head. "I'm sorry, that toy is too expensive."

But then Sally spotted something even better. It was a toy that was only one year old and it was very cheap.

"Mommy, can I please get that one?" Sally begged.

Mommy nodded. "Yes, you can get it. That one is much cheaper."

So Sally and her mom went into the shop. Sally reached out and picked up the toy. She couldn't believe it! With a big smile, she turned around and showed it to Mommy. They both smiled as they paid for the toy and left the shop.

Sally hugged the toy all the way home. She was so excited to have her new toy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was playing in the garden when she decided to pull at a big, tough tree. She grabbed onto one of the branches and yanked as hard as she could, but the branch didn't move. Anna was very curious, so she put her hands on the bark to feel its texture. To her surprise, it felt very tough.

"I can't move it no matter how hard I try," Anna said to the tree. 

The tree replied in a deep, rustling voice, "I'm very tough, little girl. You won't be able to pull me down."

Anna was astonished! She ran to her mom and told her what had happened. Her mom smiled at her sweetly and said, "Yes, trees are very tough. That's why it feels so solid to touch. But don't worry, you can still climb the branches and explore its texture!"

Anna was so happy that she had found out how tough the tree was. She hugged it tightly and vowed to never try to pull it down again!

Once there was a grumpy pig. He always felt mad and unhappy. 

The pig had a very big nose. He liked to show it off when he walked around the barn. He was proud he owned such a big funny nose. 

One day, the pig heard a noise outside the barn. It was a sheep making a lot of noise. The pig stepped outside to see what was happening. 

He saw the sheep was looking for something. She kept calling "Baaaaa"! The pig asked what she was looking for. She said she had lost her brush. 

The pig snorted loudly and said he owned a brush. He showed the sheep his grumpy face. The sheep thanked the pig and followed him back inside the barn, where the pig gave her the brush. 

The pig was proud he could help the sheep. Even though he was grumpy, he was happy to own something the sheep needed!

Lily was a young girl who loved to read books. She had many books in her room, but her favorite one was a book about stars. She liked to look at the pictures of the bright stars and learn their names.

Every night, before she went to sleep, she would read her star book with her mom. They would point at the stars and say their names together. Lily wanted to see the stars for real, but they were too far away.

One night, Lily had a special idea. She took her star book and a flashlight and went to the backyard. She turned on the flashlight and shone it on the book. She saw the stars on the book shine back at her. She felt like she was in space.

She looked up at the sky and saw the real stars shining too. She smiled and waved at them. She felt like they were her friends. She said their names out loud and thanked them for shining.

She went back to her room and hugged her star book. She was happy and sleepy. She dreamed of stars and books and shining.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra named Stripey. Stripey had black and white stripes all over his body. One day, Stripey met his friend, a monkey named Bongo. Bongo asked Stripey, "What are you doing today?" Stripey replied, "I want to make a snowman because it's icy outside."

Stripey and Bongo went to the park to make a snowman. They rolled the snow into a big ball and put it on top of another ball. They made the snowman's head out of a small ball. The snowman looked great! But suddenly, a big gust of wind came and knocked the snowman over. Stripey and Bongo were sad because they worked so hard to make the snowman. 

Stripey said, "I wish we didn't make the snowman. It was too hard." Bongo replied, "I know, but we can try again tomorrow." Stripey and Bongo walked home, feeling sad that their snowman was gone. They learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but it's important to keep trying.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety wanted to go on a journey to see the world. So, Tweety asked his mommy if he could go on a journey. His mommy said yes and she was proud of Tweety for being brave.

Tweety packed his bags and started his journey. He flew over mountains, rivers, and forests. He saw many different animals along the way. He even saw a big, yellow, friendly dog who wanted to play.

When Tweety arrived at his destination, he wanted to send a message to his mommy to tell her about his journey. He found a post office and sent a postcard to his mommy. His mommy was so proud of him for going on a big adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim and a girl called Bella. They were best friends. On a hot summer day, they decided to go and play outside.

Tim took a cooler with him. He put some cold drinks in it to keep them cool. When the two friends reached the park, they got so excited. Tim and Bella started to balance the cooler on their heads. They laughed and laughed when their balance swayed from side to side.

Eventually, they felt too hot and decided to take a break. Tim opened the cooler and they both grabbed a cold drink. They felt so much better. With smiles on their faces, they resumed their fun and games.

What fun it was to balance the cooler! Both Tim and Bella were sure they would never forget this day.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old man. Every day, he would stretch his legs in the morning and always have lots of energy to do his chores. He had an old mop that he used to clean up, but he was getting tired of it.

One day, the old man was so fed up that he went out and bought a new mop. The mop was bigger, better, and more efficient than his old one. So he decided to throw away his old one.

That night, a little boy knocked on his door. He said he had been looking for his old mop, but he couldn't find it anywhere. When the old man told him he had thrown it out, the little boy started to cry. 

The old man could feel guilty so he asked the little boy why the mop was important to him. The little boy explained to him that it belonged to his grandmother and that it was very special to him. The old man suddenly felt regret for his actions.

But it was too late and the bad deed was already done. The old man was not so wise after all.

Once upon a time there was a strong copper pot. It was shiny and beautiful. One day, something came to poke at the pot. The pot didn't know what it was, so it was a little scared. But the something kept poking, so the pot got brave. It poked back! The pot found out that it was a funny little chicken. The chicken and the pot were now friends.

The pot and the chicken played together for a long time and laughed a lot. But then it was time for the chicken to go home. The pot was very sad to see the chicken go. The pot waved goodbye as the chicken flew away. 

The pot kept being strong and kept its shiny copper color. And even though it didn't have its chicken friend anymore, the pot still had lots of fun. Whenever the pot went outside, it would poke at other things and make even more friends. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers who were best friends. One day, they were very hungry. The first brother said, "Let's go eat some lunch."

The second brother thought for a minute and said, "I want steak. That's what I want."

The first brother was surprised. "Steak? That's a big, fat, grown-up food."

The second brother wouldn't change his mind. He insisted, "I want steak!"

So, the first brother said, "Ok, let's go get some steak."

The brothers went to the store and bought a big, fat steak. When they got home, the second brother cooked the steak and shared it with his brother. They both enjoyed the steak a lot and felt very happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny red bike with pedals that went round and round. Lily loved to ride her bike outside in the sunshine. She would go up and down the street, feeling the wind in her hair and the sun on her face.

One day, Lily's friend came to visit her while she was riding her bike. Her friend wanted to try riding the bike too. Lily was happy to share, but her friend couldn't pedal very well. She kept falling off the bike and getting embarrassed. Lily told her friend not to be embarrassed, that everyone falls sometimes. They practiced together until her friend got the hang of it.

From then on, Lily and her friend rode their bikes together all the time. They would pedal up and down the street, laughing and having fun. Lily was happy to share her bike and her love of riding with her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy and his mommy went to the park. They played on the swings and slide. Timmy saw a mysterious object under the bench. He asked his mommy what it was but she didn't recognize it either. 

Timmy was curious and wanted to know what it was. He walked closer to the bench and picked up the mysterious object. It was a shiny rock with sparkles on it. Timmy thought it was very pretty and showed it to his mommy. She thought it was very beautiful too. 

From that day on, Timmy and his mommy went to the park every day to play and look for more mysterious objects. They found many beautiful rocks and leaves. Timmy was very happy and loved going to the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to sing into his toy microphone, but one day he accidentally dropped it and it broke. Timmy was very sad and didn't know what to do.

His mommy told him not to worry and took him to the toy store to buy a new microphone. But Timmy saw a little girl crying because she had a boo-boo on her knee. Timmy knew what to do. He went to the little girl and said, "Don't cry, I will heal your boo-boo." 

Timmy gave the little girl a hug and a kiss on her boo-boo, and it started to feel better. The little girl smiled and thanked Timmy. Timmy felt happy that he could help someone else. He realized that helping others can make you feel good inside, even if you don't get a new toy. 

From that day on, Timmy sang into his new microphone, but he also looked for ways to help others. And whenever he did, he felt like he was singing his favorite song, because he knew he was doing something good.

Jack wanted to succeed. He wanted to do something special. He wanted to draw a picture. 

He got some paper and some pencils. He also got some paints and a brush. He started to draw. 

Jack drew a tree with apples. He painted it brown and green. He was so happy with his work. 

When he was done, he showed his mom. She said it was delicious! She put it on the wall. Now everyone in the family can see it. 

Jack was very proud of his picture. He had succeeded!

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big plastic toy in his room. It was very pretty. He wanted to show it to his friend, Sue.

Tim went to Sue's house and said, "Look at my toy! It is big and pretty!" Sue looked at the toy and said, "Oh, it is so pretty! I like it!" They played with the toy all day long.

Later, Tim's mom called him home. When he got home, his mom asked, "Where did you get that toy?" Tim felt funny and said, "I found it in my room." His mom said, "That toy is not yours. It belongs to your sister. You should not take things that are not yours." Tim felt bad and was embarrass. He said sorry to his mom and sister. He went back to Sue's house and told her the truth. They promised to always share and play with their own toys.

Once upon a time there was a farmer. He was a kind, old man with a big, white beard. One day he was out in the fields, working away. Suddenly he felt very tired and let out a big yawn. He was so glad when he heard the happy sound of a cow mooing.

The farmer smiled and stretched. He felt very tired from all the work he had been doing in the hot sun. He decided to take a break, so he walked over to the fence and sat down. He closed his eyes and took a few deep breaths. As he did he could feel himself getting more and more relaxed.

The farmer couldn't help but yawn again. This time a very big and hearty one, which made the cow look at him with a big grin. They both grinned in the warm sunlight. The farmer was glad that he had taken a break and was enjoying the sunshine and fresh air. He knew that he could finish his work later, and so he stayed there a little while longer, smiling in the warm sun.

One day, a young boy named Tim found a dull, round rock. He picked it up and looked at it. He thought it was not very fun, but he took it with him to the park.

At the park, Tim saw a girl named Sue. She had a big, red ball. "Want to play?" Sue asked. Tim said, "Yes, but all I have is this dull rock." Sue said, "Let's try to roll it."

They tried to roll the rock, but it was not easy. They pushed it and pushed it, but it would not go far. They were sad, but they did not give up.

Then, they had an idea. They put the rock on a hill and let it go. The rock rolled down the hill very fast. Tim and Sue laughed and clapped their hands. They found out that even a dull rock can be fun when you roll it down a hill.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. Anna was only three years old.

Anna was playing in her bedroom when she had to go to the bathroom. She didn't want to get up, so she kept playing.

Soon Anna's mom called from the other room. "Anna, did you mind me when I said to go to the bathroom?"

Anna was ashamed. She knew she hadn't listened. She walked down the hallway to the bathroom.

When she opened the door, Anna's mom was standing there. She gave Anna a hug and said, "I know you tried to mind me, but it's important to listen. Now let's go wash our hands."

Anna smiled and washed her hands with her mom. From then on, Anna always minded her mom when she asked her to go to the bathroom.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He was very grumpy because he didn't want to go to school. His mom tried to make him happy by giving him his favorite breakfast, but Timmy still didn't want to go.

As they walked to school, Timmy saw his friend Billy playing with a ball. Timmy asked Billy if he could play too, but Billy said no. Timmy got even grumpier and kicked a rock on the ground.

Billy saw the mark that Timmy's kick made on the rock and said, "Wow, that was a strong kick! Do you want to play now?" Timmy smiled and they played together all morning. When it was time for school, Timmy wasn't grumpy anymore and he was excited to learn new things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch cartoons on TV. One day, she was watching her favorite cartoon when her mom told her it was time to eat lunch. 

Lily didn't want to stop watching the cartoon, so she asked her mom if she could eat in front of the TV. Her mom said no, but Lily kept asking and asking. Finally, her mom said yes, but only if she promised to eat all her food. 

Lily was so happy to eat in front of the TV, but she got so into the cartoon that she forgot to eat. When she was done watching, she looked down and saw that her food was all spoiled. She felt sad and told her mom that she lost her appetite. 

Her mom explained that if she doesn't eat her food, it will spoil and she won't feel good. Lily promised to always eat her food first before watching cartoons.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Megan. She was only three years old and had a big, strong heart.

One day, her parents gave her a special task. They handed her a bowl of sweet apples and told her to go outside and taste them.

Megan was so excited. She ran outside onto the grass, clutching the bowl of apples. She started tasting the apples, one by one. "Mmmm, these apples are so delicious!" she said as she finished her task.

Just then, her dad came out. He smiled and said, "What do you think of the apples? Do you like the taste?" Megan was so happy she almost burst.

"The apples are amazing!" she shouted with joy. After that day, Megan thought of those apples whenever she felt strong.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends called Daisy and Ben. They were always together. One day, Daisy and Ben were walking and they saw an engine. It was big, shiny and very noisy!

Daisy wanted to use the engine to have a ride, but Ben was kind and said "No, that's not a good idea." 

So, Daisy thought of a new plan. She asked Ben to help her find a peaceful place to use the engine. After some time, Daisy and Ben found a quiet, green place. They laughed and used the engine to have fun.

When Daisy and Ben were done, they sat and shared some fruit. They had so much fun together and felt so peaceful. 

The end.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toy soldiers and cars. They make a big war with their toys. They put some toys on one side and some toys on the other side. They say, "This is my team and that is your team. We will fight and see who wins."

They take turns to move their toys and make noises. "Bang, bang, bang!" Tom says. He moves his car and hits Sam's soldier. "Ha, ha, I got you!" He says. "No, you didn't!" Sam says. He moves his soldier and hits Tom's car. "Boom, boom, boom!" He says. "Now I got you!"

They keep playing and having fun. They do not care who wins or loses. They just want to play. But then, the sun goes down and it gets dark. They cannot see their toys very well. They cannot tell who is who. They get confused and scared. They do not like the dark.

"Tom, where are you?" Sam says. He looks for his friend. "Sam, I'm here!" Tom says. He looks for his friend. They find each other and hug. They are happy to see each other. They do not want to play war anymore. They want to go home.

They pick up their toys and run to their houses. They say goodbye and see you tomorrow. They go inside and turn on the light. They feel safe and warm. They show their toys to their moms and dads. They tell them about their war. They say, "We had fun, but we did not gain anything. We like to play, but we do not like war. We like light, but we do not like dark." Their moms and dads smile and hug them. They say, "We are proud of you. You are smart and kind. You are our heroes."

Once there was a family of five children. They all had names and each day, each of them was given a task to do. One day, the youngest one, who was very playful and liked to have fun, didn't want to do her task. She wanted to have more time to play. 

Her siblings were very angry at her, because if she didn't do her task, the other would have extra work to do. After she refused to do the task, they all went to her parents and asked them what to do. 

The parents were very wise and they decided that the youngest child should do the task she was assigned, but, they also allowed her to have some time to play. Everyone was very happy with the decision, and they all respected and followed it.

The moral of the story is that it is important to take responsibilities, but it's also important to find balance between work and play.

Once there was a humble player. Everywhere they went they filled people with happiness and joy. One day they went to a park with a few friends. Suddenly, they heard a loud sound coming from the playground. It was a young 3 year old child who had Trip the ball into the sand pit.

The humble player decided to help the little one. They picked up the ball, gave it a gentle pat and tossed it back up to the child. The youngster was so delighted with the help they had received and ran over cheerfully to give the player a warm hug. 

Their humble actions filled not only the child, but also the bystanders with a sense of pleasure. Everyone cheered with joy and clapped for the small gesture of kindness. From that day onwards, the player was known for being humble and for always filling others with warmth and cheer.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw a big yellow ball on the ground. Lucy picked up the ball and started to play with it. She was very happy.

Lucy saw a boy named Tom sitting on a bench. He looked sad. Lucy thought Tom might want to play too. She walked over to Tom and said, "Hi! Do you want to play with my yellow ball?" Tom looked at Lucy and said, "Yes, please!" They played together, and Tom was not sad anymore.

After playing for a long time, Lucy had to go home. She gave the yellow ball to Tom and said, "You can keep the ball. I have more at home." Tom was very happy and waved goodbye to Lucy as she left. Lucy was generous for giving her ball to Tom, and they both had a great day at the park.

One day, two brothers were playing together in their backyard. The older brother said, "It's time to count!"

The younger brother said, "I don't want to count!"

The older brother said, "It's fun - I promise!"

So the brothers started counting. The older brother was very good at counting and he counted up to 10 very quickly. But the younger brother kept losing count.

The older brother said, "Come on - let's try again."

The younger brother said, "No! I don't want to count - it's too hard!"

The older brother said, "Let me show you. It can be fun! Here, I'll count with you and make it funny!"

So they counted together, and the younger brother laughed when the older brother made funny voices and faces. Soon, he was as good at counting as his brother. 

The brothers had lots of fun counting together.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bear and Rabbit. Bear was big and tall and Rabbit was tiny and small. One day, Rabbit wanted to find the dragon. Bear told Rabbit it was too dangerous to go. But Rabbit wanted to explore and examine the dragon for himself.

Bear and Rabbit went on an adventure to find the dragon. Finally, they arrived at a clearing in the forest and there was a tall dragon! Rabbit was so excited but Bear felt scared. They stood looking at the dragon for a long time.

Rabbit wanted to take a closer look and started to step closer but Bear stopped him. Bear said it was too dangerous and they needed to leave. Rabbit didn't want to listen and stepped closer to the dragon. Suddenly, the ground started to shake and the dragon opened its mouth and roared!

Bear and Rabbit quickly ran back to safety and Bear was glad they had listened to him. They both knew it was too dangerous to examine the dragon, but they were happy they had gone on an adventure. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a magical bird named Ash. Ash was very famous and was known all around the world!

Every day, people would come to Ash's house and bring special food for him. They always put the food in a bowl and would watch as Ash greedily gobbled it up. Some people even gave him treats!

One day, a small child and their parents came to visit. They had brought some apples and carrots for Ash to eat. The child approached the bird and asked, "Can I feed you?"
Ash replied, "Yes! I would love that!"

So the child fed Ash the apples and carrots. The bird seemed to really enjoy the food as he chirped with happiness. After finishing the food, Ash flew up onto the child's shoulder and rubbed their face with its beak.

The child hugged the bird tightly and said goodbye. From that day on, the child, their parents, and Ash became the best of friends. They would visit often and feed Ash all kinds of tasty treats.

Once upon a time there lived a large dragon. His name was Wisdom. Every day he would go on adventures, often helping others in need.

One day, he encountered a broken machine. Wisdom knew this machine was very important to the people, so he decided to help them. He said, "I will repair it for you."

The people were amazed. "How can you do this?" they asked. 

"Don't worry," Wisdom replied. "I have much wisdom and strength that I can use to fix this machine."

The people were so grateful! With Wisdom's help, the machine was quickly repaired and everybody was happy.

The people thanked Wisdom for saving them and everyone celebrated his wise courage. They learned that with wisdom and strength, anything can be repaired.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, she went to the park with her mom. There, she saw a boy playing with a ball. She wanted to play with him, but she was too shy to ask.

Later, her mom took her to the ice cream truck. Lily saw the boy in line in front of her. She decided to request the same flavor as him. "I want the same as the boy in the blue shirt," she said to the ice cream man. The boy turned around and smiled at her.

As they sat and ate their ice cream, Lily asked the boy if he wanted to play with her. He said yes and they had so much fun together. They played tag and hide-and-seek. Before they left, the boy gave Lily his phone number and said they could play again soon.

Lily went home with a gentle smile on her face, happy to have made a new friend. She couldn't wait to call him and play again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the water. He would jump and splash in the big puddles after it rained. One day, Timmy went to the beach with his mommy and daddy. They brought a big flag to put in the sand. Timmy loved the flag because it was red and had white stripes. He thought it was so pretty. But then, a big wave came and splashed Timmy and the flag. The water was bad and salty, and Timmy didn't like it. But he still loved playing in the sand and watching the flag wave in the wind. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go to the park with her mommy and daddy, but they didn't have enough seats in the car. Lily insisted that she could sit on the floor, but her parents said it wasn't safe. 

Finally, her daddy had an idea. He said, "Lily, why don't you sit in my lap? That way we can all go to the park together!" Lily thought this was a great idea and climbed into her daddy's lap. 

When they got to the park, Lily wanted to play on the swings. But she was a little scared because they looked hard. Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. The swings are easy to use. I'll show you how!" And sure enough, after a few tries, Lily was swinging higher than anyone else in the park. 

Lily had so much fun at the park that day, and she was so happy that her parents found an easy way to bring her along. She insisted that they come back again soon, and they all agreed it was a great idea. The end.

Once upon a time there was a very reliable bear named James. He lived in the woods with his friends.

One day, James was very tired. It had been a long day of playing and adventuring in the woods. He decided to take a rest and find a nice spot to lie down.

He walked around until he came to a clearing. In the middle of the clearing was a big spade. James sat down and rested against the spade. He took a deep breath and closed his eyes.
Charles, James's best friend, was nearby and saw him resting. He walked over to James and said, "Are you okay buddy?"

James smiled and said, "Yes, I'm okay. I just needed a reliable place to rest."

Charles laughed and said, "Well, the spade is a great spot! You should get some sleep now."

James thanked his friend and soon fell into a deep sleep. When he woke up he felt refreshed and ready to continue his adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect pretty stones and shells at the beach. One day, she saw a wide seashell that she really wanted to add to her collection. But it was in the water and she couldn't reach it.

Her friend, a boy named Max, came by and saw her trying to get the seashell. "I can help you pass it to you," he said kindly. And so, he helped her get the seashell.

Lily was very happy and thanked Max for his help. She learned that it's always nice to help others and that friends are there to help each other collect the things they love.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pair of scissors that she used to cut paper and make pretty crafts. One day, Lily went to the store with her mom and saw a toy that she really wanted. But it was too expensive and her mom said no. 

Lily felt sad and started to cry. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can make our own toy at home with your scissors and some paper!" Lily's face lit up and she started to clap with joy. 

They went home and made a beautiful paper butterfly together. Lily was so happy and proud of her creation, and she realized that sometimes the best things in life don't have to be expensive. She hugged her mom and they both clapped in celebration of their fun afternoon together.

Mia was an adventurous little girl. Everywhere she went, she would explore and find new things. One day, Mia stumbled upon a magical door. She knocked twice, and a voice from inside asked, "Who is there?" Mia timidly replied, "It's me - Mia." The voice from inside said, "We warmly accept you, Mia. Welcome to my kingdom."

Mia was so happy that she was accepted. She opened the door and was in awe of the sights before her. Everywhere she looked there were amazing things to explore. She met all kinds of creatures, some happy and some grumpy. Mia enjoyed her visit, and before she left the voice said, "Come back any time, Mia. You will always be welcome here." 

Mia thanked the voice and promised to come back soon. She waved goodbye and went on her way, feeling more adventurous than ever.

Once upon a time, there was a very wealthy man who loved to sit in his chair. He always looked down on the people who had less than he did. Every day, he would remind himself how wealthy he was, and how better he was than anyone else.

One day, an old woman walked up to the wealthy man and said she wanted to change places. The man laughed and said no. But the old woman asked again, and again the wealthy man said no.

Finally, the old woman asked the wealthy man, "if I can make this chair move backwards, will you agree to change places with me?". The wealthy man thought it was impossible, but he agreed. The old woman then began to move the chair slowly backwards. 

The wealthy man then realised how fortunate he was, and how truly blessed he was to have all the wealth he had. He learned a lesson that day and made sure to never again look down on other people who didn't have as much as him.

The rain went on for a long time. But eventually, it stopped. The little girl was cold, but she was happy. She had danced and enjoyed the rain.

One day, Tom and his mom went to the store. Tom wanted to buy some spaghetti. Mom said that was a good idea. 

When they got to the spaghetti aisle, Tom saw a big box of spaghetti. He smiled and started to pick it up. But his mom said, "No Tom, we can't wear this spaghetti. We have to buy it."

Tom looked very sad. His mom felt sorry and gave him a hug. She said, "It's ok. Let's go to the checkout and get some spaghetti for dinner."

Tom cheered up. He and his mom put the spaghetti in their cart and went to the checkout. Then they went home and had a delicious dinner of spaghetti.

Tom and Anna were bored. They wanted to play catch, but it was raining outside. They looked around the house for something to do.

"Let's play catch in the kitchen!" Tom said. He saw a big ball on the floor.

"OK!" Anna said. She liked to play catch. She followed Tom to the kitchen.

They threw the ball to each other. They were careful not to hit anything. They had fun.

But then, Tom threw the ball too hard. It flew past Anna and hit the refrigerator. The refrigerator door opened. A lot of food and drinks fell out. Some of them broke and spilled on the floor.

"Oh no!" Tom and Anna said. They were scared. They heard their mom coming.

"What is this mess?" their mom said. She was angry. She saw the ball, the food, and the drinks. She saw Tom and Anna.

"Tom and Anna, you are in big trouble!" she said. "You should not play catch in the kitchen. You should be quiet and careful. You wasted a lot of food and drinks. You have to clean this up and go to your rooms. No more playing for today!"

Tom and Anna felt bad. They said sorry to their mom. They helped her clean the kitchen. Then they went to their rooms. They were sad. They wished they had played catch outside.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a very messy room. His mom asked him to clean it, but Tim didn't want to. He wanted to design a new room instead.

Tim said, "Mom, I want to design a new room. Can I do that?" His mom said, "Yes, Tim. But you have to clean your messy room first."

Tim tried to clean his room, but it was too messy. He didn't know where to start. He felt sad and cried. His mom came in and said, "Tim, I will help you clean your room. Then you can design a new one."

But Tim didn't listen to his mom. He wanted to design his new room now. He started to draw on the walls with his crayons. He made a big mess. His mom saw the mess and was very upset.

In the end, Tim didn't get to design his new room. His mom was sad, and Tim was sad too. They both wished that Tim had listened to his mom and cleaned his room first.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to eat jelly, especially strawberry jelly. One day, Benny went to the store to buy some jelly. He met a little girl named Lily who also loved jelly.

"Hi, Benny! What are you doing here?" asked Lily.

"I'm buying jelly. Do you want to come with me?" replied Benny.

Lily happily followed Benny to the jelly section. They picked out their favorite flavors and went to pay. Suddenly, a big mean dog came running into the store and scared Benny and Lily. They both started to weep and cry.

The dog ran straight to Benny and ate all of his jelly. Benny was very sad and Lily was scared. They ran out of the store as fast as they could. Benny never wanted to go back to that store again.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient kitchen. Everything in the kitchen was old and still worked. One day, when the cook was making lunch, he sneezed. His sneeze started a chain reaction. The ancient oven began to shake and something started to move. The cook was very surprised! The cupboard opened up and something hidden for a long time was revealed. It was a treasure chest full of coins! The cook was so happy that he shouted out loud. He was going to be rich!

The cook was in such a good mood that he started to dance in the kitchen. He sneezed again and the ancient oven shook even harder. Suddenly, out of nowhere, a genie appeared in the kitchen! He said that the cook was granted three wishes!

The cook thought of what he wanted and wished for two more kitchens, one modern and one ancient. He also wished for an endless supply of coins. The genie granted his wish and disappeared in a puff of smoke. 

The cook was very happy. He looked around and saw a beautiful modern kitchen and an ancient kitchen. He also saw a treasure chest full of coins! He was so thankful for his three wishes!

John looked out the window and saw a big van. "Mommy, that is a big van!" he said. His Mommy smiled. "Yes it is," she said.

John watched as the van drove closer and stopped. Two men got out and they didn't look happy. One said something to John's Mommy. He was rude and John wanted to yell at him, but his mommy put her hand on his shoulder.

John's mommy said something back, but he couldn't tell what it was. The men paused. Then the men got back in the van and drove away.

John looked at his mommy. She was sad. "What did they want, Mommy?" he asked. His Mommy hugged him. "They wanted to take our house away," she said.

John was so sad. That was so rude of the men. He looked out the window and watched as the van drove away. He never wanted to see the van again.

Once there was a girl, who had a brilliant guitar. Her name was Mary and she was three years old. She loved to write songs for her guitar. She got the guitar for her birthday and she was so happy. She wanted to learn all the chords and write a lot of songs.

One day, as she was writing a song, a hummingbird flew in through her window. Mary clapped her hands in excitement and smiled. The hummingbird sang a beautiful tune. Mary thought it was so wonderful.

Mary asked the hummingbird, "Can you help me to write a song?" The hummingbird smiled and nodded. They wrote a brilliant song together! Mary was so excited. 

As the sun set, the hummingbird flew away. Mary waved goodbye and said, "Thank you for helping me write a song!"

Once upon a time, there was a mighty ant. The ant lived near a big hill. The ant was very strong and everybody liked him. One day, the ant found some salt. He thought it was good to eat. So, he took it to his friends.

When the ant's friends saw the salt, they began to panic. They knew that the salt was not good for them. But the mighty ant did not listen. He told his friends to eat the salt with him. They did not want to, but they did it because they liked the mighty ant.

After they ate the salt, they all felt sick. The mighty ant was sad because he made his friends sick. They all went back to their homes and laid down. The mighty ant was not so mighty anymore. And they never ate salt again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sandy. She lived on a farm and every morning she would step outside to play. One morning, she noticed something different. There was a big, round tire sitting in her yard. She was mystified! She cautiously stepped towards it to take a closer look. Suddenly, a voice came from the tire. A tiny rabbit with a modest bow in its hair stepped out. He introduced himself as Frankie. He asked Sandy if she would like to take a ride with him. Sandy giggled with excitement and she quickly stepped inside. Frankie took off! He spun the tire around and around. Sandy laughed as the tire spun and spun. Eventually, they came to a stop and Sandy stepped out, saying it was the best ride ever. She thanked Frankie and waved goodbye as he hopped away. Sandy ran excitedly inside to tell her family about the magical tire ride she had taken with the modest rabbit.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Anna. Anna loved to play in the garden. She ran around and around the big, green tree.

One day, Anna had an idea. She wanted to make a plan. She called her mommy over and said "Mommy, I want to make a plan for the tree".

Mommy smiled and said: "That's a great plan, Anna. What do you want to do?"

Anna thought for a minute and said: "I want to decorate the tree with some pretty things. Can we please do it?"

"Of course," said Mommy.

They started to hang decorations around the tree. They hung up ribbons and sparkly stars. They also put a few little birds' nests in the branches.

Soon, the tree was looking very colourful and full of life. Everyone who looked at it said it was beautiful.

But then, one day, a bitter wind blew through the garden. It blew all of the decorations away. Anna was very sad.

Mommy hugged her tightly and said: "Don't worry, Anna. We can make a new plan for the tree and make it even more beautiful than before". 

Anna smiled and said: "Yes, let's do it!" 

And so, Anna and her Mommy began planning to make the tree look even lovelier than before.

Mama and Papa took Sarah to the fireplace, and Sarah was excited. She had never been to the fireplace before. Mama and Papa picked up some wood and put it in the fireplace. Sarah said, "Wow!" 

Then Mama lit a match and she lit the wood in the fireplace, and a fire began to burn. Sarah was so amazed! She said, "Look! Fire!" Papa said, "Remember, Sarah, to never touch the fire." 

Next, Sarah and Mama and Papa sat together in front of the fireplace, and they toasted marshmallows. They put them on a stick and held them near the fire, and when they were golden brown, Mama and Papa put the marshmallows in a bowl with some spicy sauce. Sarah smiled, and it made Mama and Papa laugh. 

Suddenly, Mama reached for Sarah's hand and gave it a squeeze to remind her of how hot the fire was. Sarah smiled and said, "I remember!"

Jimmy was excited. He was going to see a famous pilot. The pilot was a very special man. He was going to show Jimmy his airplane. 

When they got to the airport, the pilot showed Jimmy around the plane. It was big and shiny and Jimmy was amazed. 

The pilot opened the door and told Jimmy to climb up. Then he held Jimmy's hand and showed him the controls. He taught Jimmy how to move the levers and press the buttons. 

Jimmy was so happy. His wings felt like they were about to take off! Then he heard a loud noise and knew that it was time to go. 

The pilot held Jimmy's hand as they walked back outside. Jimmy waved goodbye and thanked the pilot for the wonderful experience.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, he went to the park and saw a big group of kids playing soccer. Timmy watched them from a distant and thought it looked like fun. 

Suddenly, one of the players kicked the ball towards Timmy. Timmy was scared at first, but then he kicked the ball back and everyone cheered! They all celebrated together and Timmy felt so happy. 

From that day on, Timmy practiced every day and became a great soccer player. He made lots of new friends and they celebrated together after every game. Timmy was so grateful for the day he first watched those players and decided to join in on the fun.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a fancy bird. This bird loved to show off and display its pretty feathers to everyone. All the other animals would stop and look at the bird in wonder. They liked the bird's bright colors.

One day, the fancy bird met a little girl. The little girl was very happy to see the bird. She clapped her hands and laughed as the bird displayed its feathers. The bird felt very special and happy.

The fancy bird and the little girl became good friends. They played together in the park every day. All the animals in the park would watch them and smile. The fancy bird and the little girl brought joy and wonder to everyone they met.

Timmy was feeling bored, so he asked his Mommy for something fun. His Mommy thought for a minute, and then had an easy idea. She asked Timmy if he wanted to help her load the groceries from the car.

Timmy was so excited. He ran outside with Mommy, and when they got to the car, Timmy immediately started helping. He grabbed the bags and brought them inside. It was so easy that Timmy finished loading all of the groceries in one minute!

Mommy was so proud of Timmy and hugged him tight. She promised that anytime Timmy wanted to help with the groceries, he could. Timmy smiled, happy to have found something fun to do.

Once upon a time there was a charming girl. She wanted to go on an adventure. So she left her house to explore a nearby forest.

As she started walking, she noticed a pipe in the ground. She bent down and picked it up. It was so shiny and new! She carried the pipe with her as she walked deeper into the woods.

Soon the sky grew dark, and the girl couldn't see anymore. She realized that it was time to leave. She hugged the pipe close and said goodbye to the forest.

The girl returned home feeling happy and excited. She had been on a great adventure and found a shiny pipe! She couldn't wait to show her friends her charming new treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she pretended to be a captain on a ship. She used her toy boat and sailed across the living room.

Lily's mom watched her play and said, "Wow, Lily! You look so graceful as you sail your ship."

Lily smiled and replied, "Thank you, Mommy! I'm the best captain in the world!"

Suddenly, Lily's little brother came running in and said, "Can I play too?"

Lily happily said, "Of course! You can be my first mate!"

Together, Lily and her brother sailed their ship across the imaginary seas, pretending to see dolphins and whales along the way. It was a fun adventure for both of them.

Once upon a time, there was a goat. The goat had a horn on its head. The horn was very big and pointy. All the other animals thought the goat was popular because of its big horn. 

One day, the goat wanted to organize a party. It wanted to invite all the animals in the forest. The goat went around and told everyone about the party. The animals were excited to come to the party. 

The goat decorated the forest with balloons and streamers. When the party started, everyone had a lot of fun. They danced and played games. The goat was happy that it could organize such a great party with its big horn.

Once upon a time, there was an infant named Jack. He often played with his friends, and was always the first to join in the fun. One day, Jack decided to try something different. He wanted to add something new to the regular game. 

But when Jack's friends found out, they were not happy. They thought it wasn't fair. They had been playing the same way since they were toddlers and they didn't want to change it now. 

Jack was quite sad. His friends had always let him join in before. So he tried to explain his idea to them, "I just wanted to add something extra so it would be more fun for all of us." 

His friends thought about this for a while and eventually agreed that Jack's idea could make the game even better. So they decided to give it a try.

Jack was happy again. In the end, his friends realized it was ok to try something new. That made the game fun and interesting. 

Moral of the story: it is ok to add something different to a regular routine, as long as it doesn't hurt anyone.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane was very small and loved to skip. Every morning she would wake up and skip around her house. She would skip around the kitchen, the living room, and even the garden.

One morning Jane was looking out the window. She saw a bright, clear sky and she was so excited. She wanted to go outside and skip in the sunshine.

Jane put on her red shoes and skipped outside. She skipped around the garden, over the flowers and around the trees. She even skipped so high that she could touch the sky!

Eventually Jane got tired. She stopped, sat down and began to suck her thumb. She looked up to the sky and saw a big, white cloud. The cloud was so clear and as Jane watched it, she drifted away into a peaceful sleep.

When Jane woke up she was still looking up at the clear sky. She smiled, hopped up and skipped away. She was so happy that she had a lovely day of skipping in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a train. The train liked to shake. It would shake all around the world, which was easy. All the people on the train liked how the train shook. They said, â€œIt is so much fun and very easy!â€ The train shook through forests and cities. It shook up and down hills.

One day, the train stopped shaking. The people were sad. They said, â€œWhat can we do to make the train shake again?â€ After a lot of thinking, they figured out how to make the train shake again.

They pushed it very hard and eventually, the train started shaking again. The people cheered and said, â€œThe train is shaking again! Now our train rides are easy and fun again!â€ Everyone on the train was happy the train was shaking again. They rode it together and had fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Blue. Blue lived in a cozy nest in a tall tree. One day, Blue met a friendly butterfly named Flutter. "Hello, Flutter!" said Blue. "Do you want to come to my palace in the sky?" 

Flutter was excited to see Blue's palace. "Yes, please!" she said. Blue flapped his wings and flew up, up, up. Flutter followed, flapping her wings too. They flew over the trees and the houses, until they reached the clouds. 

Suddenly, Blue saw something dangerous ahead. "Oh no!" he said. "There's a storm coming. We have to fly back down to safety." Flutter was scared, but Blue reassured her. "Don't worry, I'll protect you. Hold on tight!" 

Blue and Flutter flew back down to the tree. They landed safely in Blue's nest. "Thank you for protecting me, Blue," said Flutter. "You're welcome," said Blue. "Now let's stay here until the storm passes." And they snuggled up in the nest, waiting for the storm to end.

Once upon a time, there was a little ball. The ball was red and round. It loved to roll around the grassy field. It was a happy ball.

One day, a big storm came. The wind blew hard and the rain fell down. The ball was scared. It rolled and rolled, trying to find a safe place. Finally, it found a little hole in the wall. It rolled inside and waited for the storm to pass.

After the storm, the ball rolled out of the hole. It saw that everything was wet and messy. But the ball was happy because it was safe. It thought that the storm was not perfect, but it was okay. The ball rolled around the field again, feeling grateful for being alive.

Once upon a time, there was a sheep named Baa. Baa had very soft wool that everyone loved to touch. One day, Baa wanted to play a joke on his friends. He hid behind a tree and jumped out to surprise them. They all laughed and thought it was funny.

But Baa was not careful and he accidentally got his wool stuck on a branch. His friends tried to help him, but they couldn't get him free. Baa was scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, a kind farmer came by and saw what had happened. He carefully untangled Baa's wool and set him free.

From then on, Baa learned to be more careful when playing jokes on his friends. And everyone was happy that Baa was safe and sound. The end.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the garden. They see a big plant with red fruits. They are strawberries. Tom and Anna love strawberries. They want to pick some and eat them.

"Look, Anna, there are so many strawberries!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, they look yummy!" Anna says.

They run to the plant and try to pull the strawberries. But the plant is strong. It does not let go of the strawberries. Tom and Anna pull harder. They hear a snap.

"Oh no, we broke the plant!" Tom says.

"Sorry, plant, we did not mean to hurt you!" Anna says.

They look at the strawberries in their hands. They are big and juicy. They feel bad for the plant, but they also feel hungry.

"Maybe we can share the strawberries with the plant," Tom says.

"How?" Anna asks.

Tom has an idea. He sees a supply of water in a bucket. He also sees a straw in his juice box. He puts the straw in the water and blows. He makes bubbles.

"Look, Anna, I can make water bubbles!" Tom says.

"Wow, Tom, that is fun!" Anna says.

Tom gives the straw to Anna. She blows bubbles too. They laugh and giggle.

Then Tom says, "Maybe we can use the straw to give water to the plant. Maybe the plant will feel better."

Anna likes the idea. She puts the straw in the water and sucks. She fills the straw with water. She puts the other end of the straw near the plant. She blows the water out of the straw. She waters the plant.

"Good job, Anna!" Tom says.

He does the same thing. He waters the plant too. They take turns watering the plant with the straw. They hope the plant will grow again.

They also eat some of the strawberries. They are sweet and tasty. They save some for later. They say thank you to the plant.

"Thank you, plant, for the strawberries. We are sorry we broke you. We hope you will be strong again," Tom and Anna say.

They hug the plant. They hug each other. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a very interesting hat. It was red and blue with a big, yellow star on it. He loved to wear his hat every day.

One day, Tim saw a big tree with a kite stuck in it. He wanted to help get the kite down. Tim thought, "If I wear my interesting hat, maybe I can succeed!" So, he put on his hat and started to climb the tree.

With his hat on, Tim felt strong and brave. He climbed higher and higher until he reached the kite. He pulled it free and climbed back down. Tim succeeded in getting the kite down, all thanks to his interesting hat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She was having so much fun until she fell down and hurt her knee. 

Lily started to cry and her friends tried to help her feel better. They gave her a hug and some candy, but Lily still felt miserable. She needed her mommy to make her feel better. 

When Lily's mommy arrived, she asked what happened. Lily told her the truth about falling down and hurting her knee. Her mommy gave her a big hug and a kiss and made everything better. From that day on, Lily knew that she could always tell the truth to her mommy when she needed help.

Once upon a time, there was an empty house. In this house, there lived a family of five: mom, dad, and three children. One day, the mom and dad decided it was time to teach the children about money.

They gave each child a toy cup, and told them they could each use it to collect money. They explained that if they worked hard, they could put money in their cups to serve them in the future.

The children were so excited that they ran around the house looking for things to do. They cleaned the kitchen, helped their parents with the dishes, and swept the floor.

Each day, the children put a little money in their cups. After a few weeks, the little cups began to fill up. Soon enough, the children had enough money and could buy whatever they wanted.

The family was so proud of their hard work and dedication. The empty house was now full of love and money!

Once there was a person who was walking down the street. Suddenly, they saw a disgusting thing on the ground. It was slimy, and dripping. The person looked around and then they shrugged. They knew that no matter how much they wanted to, they couldn't pick it up.

So they kept on going, and soon they were in a park. There were lots of children playing and having a great time. But then they saw another disgusting thing! This one was a big mess and it was blocking the way. The person looked around and then they shrugged again. They didn't know what to do.

 Suddenly, one of the 3 year old children stepped forward. They looked brave and strong. With a smile on their face, they grabbed the disgusting mess and threw it in the trash. Everyone cheered and thanked the 3 year old.

The person was so happy that the 3 year old helped. They smiled, and shook their head. No matter how much they wanted to, they weren't brave enough to do what the 3 year old did.

Once upon a time, there was a dad and a daughter. Dad was in the garden and his daughter wanted to help him, so she asked him if she could use his pin. Dad said no, but the little girl was determined. She reached out to take the pin but dad quickly smacked her hand away. "No!" he said.

The little girl was fearful but she reached out to take the pin again. She picked up the pin and held it in her hand. Dad saw her and he ran towards her, but it was too late. The pin was already in her hand.

The little girl looked up at her dad, expecting to be punished. Instead, dad's face changed. He looked sad and he gently took the pin from her hand. As he did, the pin accidentally pricked the little girl's thumb and she screamed in pain.

The next morning, dad rushed her to the hospital. The doctor told him that the little girl had been infected by a virus. Dad was very upset and wished he had been more careful.

Sadly, the virus was too powerful for the little girl and she passed away several days later. Dad was devastated and buried her in the garden, close to where the pin had been.

One day, Tommy was upset. He was crying and didn't know why. He was walking around the room looking for his teddy bear. Then he saw something waving near the curtains. He walked closer and saw his teddy bear! Now he felt much better and he grabbed the bear and hugged it. He was so happy that he walked over to his mom and gave her a big hug. She smiled and wiped his tears away. Then they both walked out of the room and went to play in the garden.

Once there was a chubby bunny. He liked jumping on the carpet. He loved to count how many jumps he could do. Jump, one. Jump, two. He counted all the way to ten. Then he started again. He kept counting until he was too tired. He cuddled up on the carpet and fell fast asleep.
