His mommy and daddy rushed to him, but it was too late. Timmy had died. His mommy and daddy cried and cried. They missed him so much. They would never forget their little boy who loved parades.

Mum had a very special job for her and her daughter. She was going to weigh potatoes. The potatoes were stacked in a box on the kitchen table.

Mum taught her daughter how to use the scales. They had to place the potatoes on the metal tray and watch the dial to see how much it weighed.

Mum was very helpful and showed her daughter how to find the correct weight for the potatoes. After a few attempts, the daughter was able to read the scale and tell her mum how much the potatoes weighed. 

The mother was proud of her daughter. She said, "Great work. You are so helpful. Now we can weigh all these potatoes." 

At the end of the day, they had finished weighing the potatoes. They smiled at each other, proud of a job well done.

Once upon a time, there was a smart dog named Max. Max liked to play with blocks. He had many blocks in different colors: red, blue, and yellow.

One day, Max wanted to build a big tower with his blocks. He started to pull the blocks from his toy box. Max put one block on top of another. The tower grew taller and taller.

Max's friends, a cat and a bird, came to see his tower. They thought Max was very smart. They all played together, pulling blocks and building more towers. They had a fun day and Max was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun, but one day it was so hot that she felt tired. "I need to rest," she said to her mom.

Her mom gave her a cold glass of water and said, "You need to be careful in the heat. It can make you feel tired and sick."

Lily drank her water and felt better. She decided to play with her toys inside where it was cool. But when she went to get her favorite toy, she saw that it was spoiled. "Oh no, my toy is ruined!" she said sadly.

Her mom came to see what was wrong and saw the spoiled toy. "Don't worry, we can fix it together," she said with a smile.

Lily and her mom worked together to fix the toy and then they rested on the couch. "I'm glad we fixed my toy and now we can rest together," said Lily with a smile.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Jake. Jake was three-years-old. One day, he wanted to explore so he entered a big room. He saw a long, comfy couch. It looked so cozy that he lay down on it.

Suddenly, he felt something cold! He jumped off the couch. He looked under the couch and saw a small, white kitten.

"Hi," said the kitten, "I'm so cold. Can I come stay with you?"

Jake smiled. He said, "Yes! You can stay with me. Come up here and warm up next to me on the couch."

The kitten curled up on the couch next to Jake and they snuggled together until they were both nice and warm again. From that day on, Jake and the kitten were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Max. Max liked to play in the rain and get wet. One day, Max saw a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy had a frame for his picture, but it was broken. Max wanted to help Timmy fix his frame, so they became friends. 

But one day, a bad dog came and tried to fight Max and Timmy. Max knew he had to protect his new friend, so he bravely fought the dog. The dog ran away and Max and Timmy were safe. 

After the fight, Max and Timmy went back to Timmy's house. Max helped Timmy fix his frame and they put Timmy's picture inside. Timmy was so happy and grateful for Max's help. From that day on, Max and Timmy were the best of friends and went on many more adventures together.

There was a woman, named Joanne, who loved to teach people. Every day, she would go to the park and teach the children who went there. One day, a little boy came to the park and didn't know very much about the world around him. He was very ignorant. 

Joanne saw this and asked the little boy what he wanted to learn. He looked up at Joanne with his big, innocent eyes and said he wanted to learn about everything. 

Joanne smiled and said, "Let me teach you then." She began to show him the park and taught him about the plants and the birds. She explained to him the importance of being kind to the people and animals around him. 

By the end of the day, the little boy was not ignorant anymore. He thanked Joanne for teaching him and said he was going to be kind to everyone in the park. Joanne was proud of the little boy and smiled. 

The moral of the story is that teaching someone is a great way to make a difference. Everyone needs to be taught something in order to gain knowledge. Teaching someone not only helps them learn, but also opens up their eyes to the world around them.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous bubble. But the little bubble was not happy. It wanted to improve. 

The bubble looked around and saw lots of other bubbles. As it watched them, it noticed they seemed to be getting bigger and bigger. 

The little bubble had an idea. â€œI want to get bigger too!â€ it shouted, and set off on its mission to find a way to improve. 

The bubble searched far and wide and came across a magical pond. Inside the pond was a hidden secret - a bright, sparkly potion. 

The bubble drank the potion and felt its body start to grow. It grew, and grew, and grew until it was enormous! 

The bubble was so happy with its transformation. It had improved! Now it was ready to go back and show off its new size to all the other bubbles.

One day, a little girl named Sara went outside to play. She was having a great time when she noticed a cute little bunny hopping around. Sara smiled and decided to bring it some food. She went to the kitchen and found some meat. She carefully put the meat in her pocket and went back outside to give it to the bunny. 

The little bunny happily munched away. After it had finished, Sara smiled happily. Suddenly, the bunny got scared and hopped away. Sara had a moment of realization. She understood that giving food to animals was nice, but if she wanted to keep them around, she needed to be gentle. 

Sara learnt a great lesson that day. Being kind and gentle can bring so much joy, not only to animals, but also to people!

Once upon a time, there was a big bear that liked to eat beef. Every morning, the big bear would wake up, with a big, mysterious yawn.

One day, the big bear decided to try something new. So, the big bear went to the store and bought a big piece of beef. He took the beef back to his house.

When he opened the beef, the big bear smelled it and said, "Yuck, I don't like this beef!"

Then, he heard a voice from beside him. "I will eat the beef for you," said the tiny little mouse. "Thank you," said the big bear. 

So, the little mouse ate the beef and it was delicious! After that, the little mouse thanked the big bear and scurried away.

The big bear was happy and mysterious! He was so happy that he started to yawn with a big smile on his face. That's how the big bear and the little mouse became friends. 

The end.

Once there was a man called Bill. He was a small but brave man. One day Bill was walking down the street when he saw two boys fighting. Bill felt that it was a foolish thing to do and wanted to stop them. So he approached them and said, "Stop, why are you fighting?"

One of the boys replied, "He said I was stupid and I had to do something about it!"

Bill was surprised and asked, "Why would you fight over something so silly?" He then added, "Let's turn away from this fight and work it out with words instead."

The boys looked at each other and then stopped fighting. They thanked Bill and agreed never to fight again. Bill smiled and said, "Good. That was the wise thing to do. Fighting is foolish and only leads to more trouble." The boys nodded and went home, happy that they avoided a fight.

Once there was a fat cat. He wanted to go swimming in the lake. He asked his friends if they wanted to come but nobody wanted to go. So the fat cat went to the lake all by himself. He was so excited to feel the cool water on his fur! But when he jumped in, he quickly realized he couldn't swim. He started to miss his friends. 

The fat cat desperately tried to stay afloat, but the waves were too strong and he couldn't keep his head above the water. Eventually, the fat cat got too tired and started to sink. His friends never saw him again.

One day, a large zebra was walking along the road. He stopped and looked around, wondering where he was going. Suddenly, a little girl walked up to the zebra and questioned him.

"Where are you going?" she asked.

The zebra didn't know how to answer. He just looked at the little girl, confused.

The little girl smiled and said, "Come with me. I'll show you the way."

The zebra followed the little girl, down winding paths and past tall trees. Finally, they arrived at a large meadow. The zebra looked around, amazed. He had never seen anything so beautiful.

The little girl smiled and said, "Welcome to your new home!"

Once upon a time there was a monkey who liked to display his banana everywhere he went. Everywhere he went, people would look in amazement at the size of the banana. One day he went to a park with his banana, but he was not alone. There was a troubled little elephant there. The little elephant was curious about the banana and so he asked the monkey if he could show him his banana.

The monkey was worried. He was enjoying displaying his banana, but he was also troubled. He knew the banana was very big and the little elephant was very small. He was scared the elephant would get hurt.

Eventually, the monkey decided to do the kindest thing. He gave the banana to the little elephant to enjoy. Seeing the elephant so happy with the banana filled the monkey with joy. He had been kind and generous, and the little elephant was so delighted.

The story teaches us that kindness is important. In the face of a troubled little elephant, the monkey chose to give away his banana instead of showing off. Even though he was afraid, his generous spirit won through in the end - and it is this that counts the most.

One day, Mommy found a jolly card. She showed it to Tom the three year old. Tom was so excited to see it. The card was covered in lots of colours. On it there was a picture of a jolly clown. Tom couldn't believe his eyes.

Mommy asked, "Do you like the card?"
Tom nodded and smiled a big smile. He said, "Yes!"

Mommy said, "Let's cover the card with lots of stickers! We can make it look even better!"
Tom was so happy. He picked up all the stickers and started to cover the card. They stuck birthday stickers, heart stickers and stars all over the card.

When they finished the card look absolute jolly! Tom was so proud of what he made. He showed the card to everyone in the house and they all said it looked so special.

Tom was so proud of his jolly card. He loved showing it off to every one!

Mark was playing in the park one day and he shouted with happiness. His mom was standing nearby and smiled. She wanted to make sure he was having fun.

Suddenly, they heard someone shout out an important message. Mark and his mom went to see what it was all about.

The mayor was in the middle of the park and shouting very loudly to everyone. He said that he had an important announcement.

Mark and his mom listened carefully. The mayor said there was going to be a contest in the park. Whoever did the best in the contest would get a prize. Mark was excited!

He quickly ran up to the mayor and asked what he needed to do. His mom was so proud of him for being brave and trying to win the contest.

The mayor explained that Mark had to count the number of marks on the wall. It was very important to count them correctly.

Mark went to work and carefully counted the marks. He shouted out the correct number when he was done.

The mayor presented Mark with the prize - a stuffed bear. Mark was so excited. His mom gave him a big hug and told him how proud she was of him.

Lily was a good girl who liked to help her mom. She helped her mom serve food to the people who came to their house. She also helped her mom clean the dishes and the table. Lily was happy to serve others.

One day, Lily's mom gave her a medal. It was shiny and had a star on it. Lily's mom said, "This is for you, Lily. You are a star helper. You serve others with love and kindness. I am proud of you." Lily was very happy. She put the medal around her neck and showed it to everyone.

But not everyone was happy for Lily. Ben, who lived next door, was jealous. He wanted a medal too. He thought he was better than Lily. He said to Lily, "Your medal is ugly. You don't deserve it. You only serve others because you want to be popular. You are not a star. You are a fake." He tried to take the medal from Lily.

Lily was sad and angry. She said, "No, Ben. You are wrong. My medal is beautiful. I deserve it. I serve others because I care about them. I am not a fake. I am a star." She held on to her medal.

Ben and Lily started to fight. They pulled and pushed each other. They shouted and cried. Their moms heard them and came to see what was wrong. They saw Ben and Lily fighting over the medal. They were shocked and disappointed.

They separated Ben and Lily and took them to their houses. They said, "Ben, Lily, you should not fight. Fighting is bad. It hurts others and yourself. You should be sorry for what you did. You should say sorry to each other and be friends. You should share and respect each other. You should learn from Lily. She serves others with love and kindness. That is what makes her a star. That is what makes her medal shine." Ben and Lily felt ashamed. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They became friends. They learned to serve others with love and kindness. They both became stars.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to play outside in the yard. One day, Max's owner came outside with a treat. "Max, come here boy! I have a treat for you!" said Max's owner. Max ran over to his owner and wagged his tail. "Sit, Max," said his owner. Max sat down and his owner gave him the treat. It was so yummy!

After eating the treat, Max wanted to play hide and seek. "Let's play hide and seek, owner!" said Max. "Okay, Max. You hide and I will come find you," said his owner. Max ran to the bushes and hid behind them. His owner looked and looked but couldn't find Max. "Where are you, Max?" said his owner. Max barked and his owner found him. "Good job, Max! You are such a dependable dog," said his owner. Max wagged his tail and was happy to be found.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to find a place to take a nap. Everywhere she looked, there was nothing soft she could sleep on. Lucy saw a big rock and decided to try napping on it. 

No matter how much she tried, the rock was just too hard. Lucy started to feel an itch and picked at it. 

"Why is this rock so tough?" complained Lucy.

Just then, a small, fluffy pillow flew out of the sky and landed in front of her. She smiled and said, "This looks perfect for a nap!"

So Lucy laid down on the pillow and felt the softness against her skin. She closed her eyes and nodded off right away. 

The next morning, Lucy woke up feeling well-rested. She was so glad she found the perfect spot for her nap!

Bob was getting ready to go to work. He put on his uniform and was getting ready to leave the house. But then he paused. He remembered he had forgotten something very important. He had forgotten his lunch! He felt so stupid.

He quickly got off the uniform and dashed to the kitchen. He quickly packed some lunch and hurried back into the uniform. He paused for a moment, making sure that he had remembered everything for this time. He hadn't forgotten anything else, which made him relieved.

He was now ready for work. As he was about to open the door he paused for one final time. He gave himself a pat on the back for being so smart and remembering his lunch. He smiled and went straight to work. He was confident that today would be a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a purple dress that she loved to wear. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While they were playing, Lily saw a butterfly that was also purple. She said, "Look, a purple butterfly! I want to watch it." 

Her friend Emma said, "I want to watch it too!" They both sat down and watched the butterfly together. After a while, Lily said, "I'm tired. I want to sleep now." Emma said, "Okay, let's go home and take a nap." 

When they got home, Lily put on her purple pajamas and went to bed. She said goodnight to her mom and dad, and soon she was fast asleep. She dreamed about the purple butterfly and how much fun she had watching it with Emma. The end.

Jim was out for a jog one morning. He ran down the street and noticed something. He could hear a noise coming from the house at the end of the block. He stopped and listened. Then he heard it again. It sounded like someone crying. 

Jim ran to the house. He saw a thin woman at the door. She was crying. He asked her what was wrong.

"My son," she said. "He's gone. He was playing in the park but now I can't find him. I've been calling his name but he isn't coming home."

"Maybe he's still in the park," Jim said. "Let's go together and look for him. I'll help you."

The woman thanked him. So they went to the park. They searched but there was no sign of the little boy.

Just then, Jim heard a noise in the bushes. He looked closely and saw a thin arm reaching out. He smiled and said, "I think I found him!"

Jim and the woman gathered the little boy out of the bushes and hugged him. He was happy to be back with his mum.

They all thanked Jim for his help and the little boy gave him a big hug. And after that, Jim went back to his jog.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys. One day, she found a loop of string on the ground. She picked it up and looked at it. It was so pretty! She decided to make a necklace out of it. 

Lily went to her room and got some beads. She put the loop around her neck and started to push the beads onto it. It was hard work, but she did it! When she finished, she looked in the mirror. She felt so proud of her beautiful necklace. 

Later that day, Lily showed her necklace to her mom. Her mom said, "Wow, Lily! You are so creative and talented! You made a beautiful necklace. You are so rich in imagination." Lily smiled and felt happy. She loved her new necklace and was proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old, and her name was Mia. Mia was at home with her mom, and it was time for the mailman to come by. Mia was very scared when the mailman knocked on the door. 

Her mom opened the door, and the mailman handed her a big stack of mail. Mia's mom thanked him, and the mailman said goodbye.

Mia's mom put the mail on the kitchen table, and Mia wanted to go look at it. She slowly crept up to the table and grabbed a letter that had her name printed on it. She was so excited!

Mia's mom saw her daughter sitting at the table, and asked her if she wanted to help her deliver the mail. Mia shouted "Yes!" and grabbed the mail. She went to each mail box in the neighborhood and put the mail inside.

Mia was so proud of herself. She had done an important job, and she couldn't stop smiling. She felt brave and strong.

The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Jack and Jane who were walking down the street together. Jane said to Jack, "Let's get some juice." So the two of them both ran to the store and picked out their favourite juices.

When they got back outside, they sat down on the grass. Jane said, "Let's see who can drink their juice fastest." Jack agreed and they both started to drink their juices.

After a few minutes, Jane finished first, so she shouted, "Yay, I won!" Jack looked very happy and said, "Well done, Jane! You seem very fast today. May I have some more juice?" Jane smiled and said, "Of course!"

So they both finished their juice and went on their way. They both felt very happy and they said goodbye with a big hug.

Once upon a time there was a king who had a very special sword. The king had a joyful heart and wanted to share his cheerfulness with the people. But he was scared they wouldn't like him. So, he delayed showing them his sword. 

One day, the kind decided it was time to show everyone his sword. He was scared but he was also excited. He had made the right choice to wait. Once the people saw the sword they cheered! They said the sword was splendid and they felt happy the king wanted to share it with them. 

From that day on, the moral was clear: although it can be hard to share something special with people, it is worth it in the end! Sharing joy and happiness can lead to very cheerful results.

Once upon a time there was a crane. He loved to bow for everyone he met. He bowed for all the animals in the forest, even for the birds who flew high in the sky. He was very organized and always wanted to do things the right way.

One day he was walking through the forest and saw many animals. He bowed to all of them. When he came across a bear, the crane bowed very low. The bear loved watching the crane bow.

The crane kept walking and came across a pond. He saw a family of cranes there, so he decided to bow to them too. The family of cranes seemed surprised and flew away. But the crane was still proud of himself for being so organized.

The crane kept bowing everywhere he went and eventually it became a habit. Now, every time he meets someone he always bows to show his respect. He is very organized and proud of himself. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo liked to swim in the ocean with his friends. One day, Nemo saw a big shiny thing in the water. He wanted to see what it was, so he decided to dive down.

As Nemo got closer, he realized it was a refrigerator! Nemo thought it was cool and wanted to explore it. But as he swam closer, he accidentally bumped into the refrigerator and it fell on top of him. Nemo was hurt and couldn't swim back up to the surface.

Nemo's friends looked for him but they couldn't find him. Sadly, Nemo was stuck under the refrigerator and couldn't get out. He couldn't breathe and eventually, he passed away. His friends were very sad and missed him very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat a yummy steak for dinner. Her mommy cooked the steak and told her to wait until it was ready. 

Finally, dinner was ready and Lily sat down to eat. She took a big bite of the steak and it tasted so good! She was very happy to receive such a delicious dinner from her mommy. 

After dinner, Lily went to bed feeling full and happy. She dreamt about the yummy steak she had just received and couldn't wait to have it again. The end.

Tom and Anna liked to play with their toy train. They had a big red train that could make noise and move on the tracks. They also had many cars that they could attach to the train. Tom and Anna liked to number the cars and see how many they had.

One day, Tom wanted to play with the train by himself. He did not want to share with Anna. He said to Anna, "This is my train. You cannot play with it. Go away." Anna felt sad and angry. She said to Tom, "That is not nice. We should share the train. It is ours, not yours." But Tom did not listen. He took the train and all the cars and went to his room.

Anna was left alone in the living room. She did not have anything to play with. She felt bored and lonely. She wished Tom would come back and play with her. She thought, "Maybe I can make him happy. Maybe I can give him something he likes." She looked around and saw a big cookie on the table. She knew Tom loved cookies. She took the cookie and went to Tom's room.

She knocked on the door and said, "Tom, I have something for you. Do you want a cookie?" Tom heard Anna and opened the door. He saw the cookie and his eyes lit up. He said, "Wow, a cookie! Thank you, Anna. You are very kind." He took the cookie and smiled. He felt sorry for being mean to Anna. He said, "Anna, I am sorry for not sharing the train with you. Do you want to play with me?" Anna nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, I do. I am sorry for being mad at you. Let's play together." Tom and Anna hugged and went to play with the train. They had fun and learned to share and be nice to each other. They also learned to number the cars again and see how many they had. They were happy and the train was happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck. The duck loved to play in the water and get all wet. But one day, the duck felt very dirty and wanted to be clean. So, the duck went to the pond to bathe. The duck splashed and played in the water until it was all clean.

After the bath, the duck wanted to go on an adventure. So, the duck put on its gear, which was just a little backpack, and set off into the forest. The duck walked for a long time and met many animals along the way. Some were big and some were small, but all were friendly and kind to the little duck.

As the sun began to set, the duck realized it was lost. The duck felt scared and alone, but then remembered that it had made so many friends on its journey. So, the duck asked for help from a humble rabbit who showed the duck the way back home. From that day on, the little duck knew that it could always count on its friends to help when it was lost or scared.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was only three years old and she was learning a lot of new things. One day her mother gave her a lime. Daisy had never seen a lime before and she was so excited.

"Can I eat it?" Daisy asked.

"No," her mother said. "Limes are too fragile to eat. You can look at it and explore it, but it's too delicate to eat."

Daisy was very curious and wanted to learn more about limes. She asked a lot of questions about the lime and her mother patiently answered each one. Then Daisy asked, "So what can I do with the lime?"

"Well," her mother said, "you can squeeze it to make lemonade."

That was a new word for Daisy and she asked, "What is lemonade?"

Her mother smiled and said, "Lemonade is a drink made from the juice of a lemon or a lime. You can squeeze juice out of the lime and mix it with a little bit of water and some sugar to make a delicious drink."

Daisy was so excited to learn something new. She was very careful though; she knew that limes were fragile and she wanted to make sure she didn't squish it by mistake. She listened to her mother and used her gentle touches to squeeze the lime and make lemonade.
