Once upon a time, there was a naughty boy named Tim. Tim liked to pinch his sister's toys and eat all the cookies. One day, Tim's mother gave him a piece of coal and told him to keep it with him all day.

Tim didn't like the coal. It was black and dirty. But he listened to his mother and kept it with him. Throughout the day, Tim felt the coal in his pocket and remembered what his mother said: "If you are naughty, you will get coal instead of presents from Santa."

Tim realized that he didn't want coal for Christmas. He wanted toys and cookies. From that day on, Tim stopped being naughty. He played nicely with his sister and shared his cookies. And when Christmas came, he got lots of presents from Santa because he was a good boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She loved to eat and play. One day, she saw a huge tree in the park. She thought it was a special tree. Sue told her mom and dad about the tree. They said they would go see it later.

At home, Sue asked her mom, "Can we eat at the tree?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can have a picnic there." Sue was very happy. Her mom made a menu for the picnic. There were apples, sandwiches, and cookies on the menu.

The next day, they went to the park with the food. They saw the huge tree and put a blanket under it. Sue and her family had a fun picnic. They ate all the food from the menu. Sue knew the tree was special because it was where they had a great day together.

Once upon a time, there was a heavy cat named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play with her ball. One day, Fluffy saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was playing with a ball too. Fluffy wanted to play with Lily's ball.

Fluffy went to Lily and asked, "Can I play with your ball?" Lily said, "No, this ball belongs to me. But we can play together with my ball." Fluffy was very happy to hear that. They played with the ball all day.

At the end of the day, Fluffy was tired. She said to Lily, "Thank you for playing with me." Lily said, "You're welcome, Fluffy. I had fun playing with you too." They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a smelly dog named Max. Max loved to run and play in the park with Timmy. One day, Timmy and Max went on an adventure to a big castle. They walked through a long hallway and came to a big chamber. Inside the chamber, there was a big dragon staring at them! Timmy and Max were scared, but they remembered that dragons liked treats. So, they gave the dragon a big bone and the dragon became their friend. From that day on, Timmy and Max visited the dragon in his chamber and brought him treats. They all lived happily ever after. The end.

One day, a big dog named Spot and a small cat named Fluffy went to play outside. They ran and jumped in the green grass. They were very happy. But then, they saw a deep pit. They wanted to see what was inside.

Spot said, "I will jump in the pit and look." Fluffy was scared and shouted, "No, Spot! It is not safe!" But Spot jumped in the pit anyway. Fluffy was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Then, a useful bird named Blue flew by. Blue saw Fluffy crying and asked, "What is wrong, Fluffy?" Fluffy said, "Spot jumped in the pit and I can't get him out!" Blue said, "Don't worry, Fluffy. I will help you." Blue flew down into the pit and helped Spot out. Fluffy was so happy to see Spot again. They all played together and had a fun day.

Mummy and Daddy went to the store. They had lots of shopping to do. They bought a big box of food to keep them safe and healthy. They also bought some news.

Mummy and Daddy took the news home. They opened the news and shared it with each other. They were very happy and excited.

Mummy and Daddy took the food out of the big box and put it in the kitchen. They cooked some yummy food for dinner.

After dinner, Mummy and Daddy enjoyed a sweet treat and read the news from the store. They were very happy and had a nice evening together.

Once upon a time there was a mole. He was a very bossy mole. He wanted everything to be done his way. He would tell all the animals and bugs in the woods what to do. 

The other bugs and animals did not like this. So they decided to replace the bossy mole. They appointed a new one to take his place. 

This new mole was very friendly and polite. He said "please" and "thank you" to everyone. The other animals and bugs were very glad. 

From that day onwards the woods were much happier. Everyone felt like they could do their own things and be independent. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Tom. Tom loved to print pictures of trees with pretty prunes on them. He had a big printer in his house, where he would print lots of pictures.

One day, Tom wanted to find a real tree with prunes. He put on his hat and went for a walk. He looked high and low, but he could not find a tree with prunes. Tom felt sad.

Then, Tom saw a little girl named Sue. She had a basket of prunes. Tom asked Sue, "Where did you find the prunes?" Sue said, "I picked them from a tree in my yard." Tom was happy. Sue gave Tom some prunes, and they became good friends. They went to Sue's house and printed more pictures of trees with prunes together.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a small house with her friend, Doggy. One day, they found a hidden box under a big tree. The box had a number on it. The number was three.

Kitty and Doggy were very curious. They wanted to know what was inside the box. Kitty said, "We need to open it, but it is very hard." They both tried to open the box, but they struggled. They pushed and pulled, but the box did not open.

A wise bird saw them and said, "You need to say the magic word to open the box." Kitty and Doggy looked at each other and said the magic word together, "Please!" The box opened, but instead of something nice, a big scary monster jumped out! The monster chased Kitty and Doggy away. They were so sad that they didn't find something nice in the box. They learned that not all hidden things are good.

One day, a little dog named Spot was very impatient. He wanted to go outside and play. Spot saw a big chair and decided to seat on it. He jumped up and sat down.

"Spot, do not seat on the chair!" said Mom. "You can go outside and play now." Spot was happy and ran outside. He saw a little house that looked like a jail. Spot was curious and went inside.

Inside the jail, he found a small bird. The bird said, "Help! I am stuck in this jail. Can you open the door?" Spot tried to open the door, but it was too hard. He called his friend, a big dog named Max. Max came and helped Spot open the door.

The bird was free and thanked Spot and Max. They all played together outside and had a lot of fun. Spot was not impatient anymore and learned that helping others can be fun too.

Once upon a time, there was a magic tree. This tree had regular leaves, but the fruit it grew was very special. One day, a little girl named Amy found the tree while playing with her ball.

Amy saw the fruit and said, "Wow! This fruit looks yummy!" She picked one and started to chew it. As she chewed, she felt something strange happening. She could suddenly jump very high, just like a bunny!

Amy went back to her friends and showed them her new skill. They all wanted to try the magic fruit too. They ran to the tree, chewed the fruit, and had lots of fun jumping high together.

Once, there was a bull who was fierce. He lived in a farm with a lot of other animals.

One day, the bull was walking in the farm when he saw something that made him very angry. He saw a chicken covering an egg. This made the bull feel very fierce and mad.

The bull stomped over to the chicken and said in a loud, fierce voice: "What are you doing?"

The chicken was scared and said in a tiny voice: "I'm covering this egg."

The bull said: "I think you should stop covering the egg. If you don't stop, I'm going to hurt you!"

The chicken was very scared and quickly ran away.

The bull was so fierce and full of rage that he started to cover the whole farm. He was determined to cover everything. In the end, all the animals fled the farm in fear.

The bull had finally gotten what he wanted, but he had also destroyed the place he once called home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore. One day, she found a well in the middle of a field. It was very deep and had a delicate rope tied to a bucket. 

Lily looked down the well and said, "Hello, is anyone down there?" 

Suddenly, the well began to ring! Lily was scared and ran away. But then, she heard a voice coming from the well saying, "Don't be afraid, it's just me, a friendly frog." 

Lily came back and looked down the well again. The frog asked, "Can you please ring the bell on the other side of the field for me? I need help getting out of here." 

Lily was happy to help and ran to ring the bell. Soon, a farmer came and helped the frog out of the well. From that day on, Lily and the frog became good friends and played together often.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play outside. One day, he went to a big hill. The big hill was a volcano. He did not know it was a volcano.

Tim saw a deaf dog near the volcano. The dog could not hear anything. Tim said, "Hello, dog! Do you want to play with me?" The dog looked at Tim and wagged its tail. They played together near the volcano.

As they played, Tim stumbled on a rock. He fell down and hurt his knee. Suddenly, the volcano started to shake. It was going to erupt! Tim and the dog tried to run away, but they were too slow. The volcano erupted, and they could not escape. It was a bad ending for Tim and the dog.

Once upon a time, there was a young duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to play in the water. One sunny day, Ducky went to the pond to soak in the cool water. Ducky splashed and splashed with his friends.

Ducky's friend, Froggy, said, "Ducky, let's play a game! We can swim to the left side of the pond and back." Ducky smiled and said, "Yes, let's do it!" So, Ducky and Froggy swam to the left side of the pond and back as fast as they could.

When they were done playing, Ducky and Froggy sat on a big rock to rest. They talked and laughed about their fun day. As the sun went down, they said goodbye to their friends and went home. Ducky and Froggy were happy to have each other as friends and couldn't wait to play in the pond again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly high in the sky and see all the pretty flowers and trees. One day, Tweet saw a big lake and wanted to dive in. 

Tweet asked his friend, a little mouse named Squeak, "Do you want to come with me and dive in the lake?" 

Squeak replied, "No, I don't like water. But I can come with you and watch you dive." 

Tweet flew up high and then swooped down to the water. He dove in and swam around for a long time. When he was done, he flew back to land and said to Squeak, "That was so much fun! I want to do it again tomorrow." 

Squeak replied, "I'll come with you again tomorrow, but I'll stay on land and watch you dive." 

And so, Tweet and Squeak had a fun day together, with Tweet diving in the lake and Squeak watching from the safety of the land.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play with blocks and cars. One day, Sara found a bottle of glue in the art room. She had an idea to make a funny joke on Tom. She put some glue on one of his cars and waited for him to come back.

When Tom came back, he saw his car and picked it up. He tried to roll it on the floor, but it was stuck. He pulled hard, but it did not move. He felt something sticky on his hand. He looked at the car and saw the glue. He was very angry and sad. He shouted at Sara, "Why did you do this? This is not funny! This is mean! You ruined my car!"

Sara laughed and said, "It is funny! It is a joke! You are silly! I can do what I want!" She did not care that Tom was upset. She thought she was clever and funny.

Tom ran to the teacher and told her what Sara did. The teacher was not happy. She scolded Sara and made her apologize to Tom. She also made her clean the car and the glue. She said, "Sara, you should not tease your friends. Teasing is not nice. It can hurt their feelings and make them angry. You should be kind and respectful to your friends. How would you feel if someone did that to you?"

Sara felt ashamed and sorry. She realized that she was wrong and that she hurt Tom. She said sorry to Tom and gave him back his car. She said, "Tom, I am sorry. I was not nice. I will not tease you again. Can we still be friends?"

Tom was still a little angry, but he also felt sorry for Sara. He saw that she was anxious and sad. He said, "Sara, I forgive you. I am glad you said sorry. We can still be friends, but please do not do that again. Friends should not hurt each other. Friends should help each other and have fun together."

Sara and Tom hugged and smiled. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that teasing is not funny, but cruel. They learned that friendship is more important than jokes. They learned to be kind and respectful to each other. They played with their blocks and cars again, and had a good time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved going to the fair on Tuesdays as it was so much fun! Every Tuesday she would wake up so excited, and make sure she had all her toys ready to put in her pocket.

The little girl was playing on the swings at the fair when she suddenly heard a loud scream. She looked up and saw a big boy running away from a big balloon. She laughed out loud and the boy saw her.

"I'm sorry I scared you," she said. 

The boy felt much better after that and the two of them quickly became friends. For the rest of the day they played together until the sun started to go down. 

Every Tuesday they would meet up at the fair, and go on all the rides. They both screamed with happiness each time they went down the big slide. 

On the last Tuesday, the little girl was so sad. It was time for her to go home. With a last hug, the two friends said goodbye.

The little girl will always remember their special friendship and all their Tuesdays at the fair.

Once upon a time there was a smart wizard. He had a very special herb. He wanted to keep it safe from anyone else. So, he used a special magical spell to lock it away. Nobody else could get it.

The wizard was very intelligent. He had come up with a great plan to keep the herb safe. He knew nobody else could unlock the magic spell.

But one day, a brave explorer came along. She wanted to find the herb for herself. She knew it had magical properties.

She thought and thought. Then she realized that the only way to get the herb was to be smarter than the wizard. She had to be even more intelligent than him!

So, she worked hard and studied the spell. Finally, she figured out the secret combination and she was able to unlock it.

The explorer was very proud. She had been brave, determined and very intelligent. Now she could use the special herb she had found.

Once there was a popular furniture store. All of the furniture was in perfect condition. Everyone loved buying furniture at the store. 

One day a wicked witch came to the store. She was so angry that she wanted to destroy the furniture. She shouted, "Destroy, destroy!", as she waved her wand. 

The furniture began to shake and wobble. Everything eventually broke and pieces were all over the floor. The witch laughed in delight and flew away. 

The store owner came into the store and was so sad to see the furniture destroyed. She shouted, "Oh no! Who did this to my store!" 

Just then a small voice spoke up. A little girl of three years old had been hiding in the corner. She said, "It was a witch! A wicked witch who wanted to destroy all the furniture!" 

The store owner was amazed. She thanked the little girl for warning her. With a smile, she said, "Good job! I will make sure to keep my store safer next time."

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he found a big rock and tried to pick it up, but he struggled because it was very heavy.

After a few tries, Timmy finally managed to lift the rock and he was so proud of himself. He decided to mark the spot where he found the rock so he could come back and visit it again. He used a stick to make a mark in the dirt.

As Timmy continued to explore, he saw a butterfly fluttering around. He followed it for a while until it flew away. Timmy realized that even though he struggled with the heavy rock, he didn't give up and eventually succeeded. He felt happy and proud of himself for trying. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl called Amy. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she took a walk in the woods near her house and stumbled across a beautiful lake.

Amy was brave and so she decided to go it alone and explore the lake. She carefully walked around the edge, admiring the sparkly water and watching the fish swimming. She could even see a huge frog jumping out of the water.

Suddenly, Amy stumbled and fell into the lake and all she could do was yell for help. Fortunately, her mother was walking nearby and came to help her. She jumped in and carried the brave little girl out of the lake and back home.

Amy was so thankful for her brave mother and by the end of the day, both of them were happily dried off and ready for a warm hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very poor and didn't have many toys to play with. One day, Lily's mom called for a taxi to take them to the park. Lily was so excited to go to the park because she had never been there before.

When they got to the park, Lily saw other kids playing with their toys. She felt sad because she didn't have any toys to play with. Then, Lily saw a little boy crying because he lost his toy. Lily felt bad for the little boy and wanted to help him. She told her mom to call the taxi driver and ask if they could go back home to get one of her toys to give to the little boy.

The taxi driver was very kind and agreed to take them back home. Lily gave the little boy her favorite toy and he stopped crying. Lily felt happy that she could help someone else. She learned that even though she was poor and didn't have many toys, she could still make someone else happy. Lily didn't miss her toy because she knew it was making someone else happy.

Sara and Ben are twins, but they are very unique. Sara likes to paint and sing, and Ben likes to run and jump. They also have different colors of hair and eyes. Sara has brown hair and blue eyes, and Ben has blond hair and green eyes.

One day, they go to the park with their mom and dad. There is a lot of snow on the ground, and it is very cold. Sara and Ben want to play in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They also make snowballs and throw them at each other. They laugh and have fun.

Then, they see a sign that says "Snowman Contest". It is a game where you can make a snowman and win a prize. Sara and Ben want to join the game. They ask their mom and dad if they can. Their mom and dad say yes, and they help them make another snowman.

Sara and Ben make a very unique snowman. They use powder to make it shiny and sparkly. They also use fruits and vegetables to make its face and buttons. They use a banana for its nose, grapes for its eyes, a carrot for its mouth, and corn for its buttons. They also use a broom for its arm and a bucket for its hat.

When they are done, they show their snowman to the judge. The judge is a nice lady who wears a red coat and a hat. She looks at all the snowmen in the park. She sees some big snowmen, some small snowmen, some funny snowmen, and some scary snowmen. But she likes Sara and Ben's snowman the best. She says it is the most unique snowman she has ever seen.

She gives Sara and Ben a blue ribbon and a big hug. She says they win the game. Sara and Ben are very happy. They thank the judge and their mom and dad. They also share their prize with their friends. Their prize is a big box of cookies. They eat some cookies and give some to their snowman. They say it is the best day ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books, but she didn't have a bookcase to keep them in. One day, her parents surprised her with a big purple bookcase! Lily was so happy and excited. She quickly filled it with all her favorite books.

As she read more books, Lily gained more knowledge and imagination. She loved looking at the pictures and reading the words. Every night before bed, she would pick out a book from her bookcase and read it with her parents. They would ask her questions about the story and she would tell them what she learned.

Lily's bookcase became her favorite thing in her room. She loved how it looked and how it kept her books organized. She even showed it off to her friends when they came over to play. Lily was grateful for her bookcase and all the knowledge she gained from her books.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and make things with her hands. One day, she decided to design a special hat for her teddy bear. She used colorful paper and glue to make it just right.

Later that day, Lily went to a meeting with her friends. They were going to have a picnic in the park. When they saw Lily's bear with the unusual hat, they all wanted one too! So, Lily helped her friends design their own hats.

Everyone had a great time at the picnic, wearing their unique hats and playing games. Lily felt happy that she could share her love of creating things with her friends. From that day on, they had many more meetings where they designed and made things together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she went to her grandma's house. Grandma was famous for her delicious cookies.

Lily asked, "Grandma, can I help you make cookies?"

Grandma said, "Sure, you can hold the bowl and mix the powder."

Lily was so happy to help. She held the bowl tightly and mixed the powder. The cookies turned out to be very yummy. Grandma and Lily enjoyed eating the cookies together.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little car named Zoom. Zoom loved to drive really fast and explore new places. One day, Zoom got very tired and needed to sleep. 

Zoom drove around looking for a cozy spot to sleep. Finally, Zoom found a nice soft patch of grass and parked there. Zoom closed his eyes and fell asleep.

While Zoom was sleeping, some other cars came by and saw him. They thought Zoom was very brave for driving so fast and exploring new places. They decided to leave a note for Zoom telling him how brave he was. When Zoom woke up, he was very happy to read the note and felt even braver than before.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to explore and collect things. One day, when she was out walking she saw something special - an ancient coin!

She picked it up and put it in her pocket. When she got home, she took it to her bedroom and put it in a box.

That night, as she was going to bed, she began talking to her favourite teddy bear.
"I found an ancient coin today," she said, "And I'm going to collect more special things."

The teddy bear smiled and said, "That sounds like a great idea Lucy!"

And from that day on, Lucy went on adventures, searching for more ancient treasures that she could collect and put in her special box in her bedroom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat fruit, especially apples and bananas. One day, Timmy's mom brought home a big, gray watermelon. Timmy had never seen a gray fruit before!

"Wow, Mommy! What kind of fruit is that?" Timmy asked.

"It's a watermelon, Timmy," his mom replied.

Timmy took a bite of the watermelon and it was so juicy and delicious that he shouted with joy, "Yummy!"

His mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Timmy." From that day on, gray watermelon became Timmy's favorite fruit.

Once upon a time, a boy named Jack had a blue guitar. He loved to play it every day. One day, Jack's friend Lily came to his house. She asked, "Can I play your guitar, Jack?" Jack said, "Sure, but be careful. It's heavy. It weighs a lot." 

Lily picked up the guitar and started to play. She played a song that made Jack happy. He said, "You're really good, Lily!" Lily smiled and said, "Thanks, Jack. Your guitar is so pretty and blue. I love it!" 

Jack was happy to hear that Lily liked his guitar. He said, "You can play it anytime you want, Lily. Just be careful because it's heavy and weighs a lot." Lily nodded and said, "I will. Thank you, Jack!" 

From that day on, Jack and Lily played the guitar together. They loved the sound it made and how it looked. They were happy to have each other as friends and to share their love for music.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong lion named Leo. Leo had a lot of power in the jungle. All the animals knew him and were scared of him. Leo liked to show everyone how strong he was.

One day, a little mouse named Mimi was playing in the jungle. She did not recognize Leo when she saw him. She went up to him and said, "Hello, big lion! Can we be friends?" Leo laughed and said, "Why would I be friends with a little mouse like you?"

Mimi felt sad, but she did not give up. She asked Leo for a chance to show him that even a little mouse could be strong. Leo agreed and said, "If you can help me when I am in trouble, we can be friends." Mimi smiled and said, "Deal!"

A few days later, Leo was caught in a big net. He could not get out and was very scared. Mimi saw him and ran to help. She used her strong teeth to cut the net and set Leo free. Leo was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mimi! You are very strong and brave. I was wrong to judge you by your size. We can be friends now."

From that day on, Leo and Mimi were best friends. They learned that everyone has power, no matter how big or small they are. The moral of the story is to never judge someone by their size, as everyone has strength and can be a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play on the lawn with his friends. They would run and jump all day long.

One day, Spot's friend, Bird, told him, "Spot, I need your help! I have to deliver a letter to my friend, but my wing is hurt. Can you help me?" Spot wagged his tail and said, "Yes, Bird! I can help you deliver the letter."

They walked together until they found a big tree with sour apples. Bird said, "This is the tree! My friend lives here." Spot jumped and gave the letter to Bird's friend. They all played together on the lawn and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Ruby. She was three years old and very pale. Every day she would go to the park and play. 

One day while she was playing, a nail lay on the ground. She decided to pick it up and rub it. When she did, a wizard popped out from a puff of magical smoke! 

The wizard said, "Rub my nail three times, and I will grant you three magical wishes!" 

Ruby was so excited that she almost forgot to be careful. She thought to herself that she would wish for a puppy and lots of money. 

But before she could make her wishes, the wizard said, "Be careful what you wish forâ€¦because sometimes they can have bad outcomes!" 

Ruby hesitated, so the wizard said, "Your first wish will do good, but your second and third wishes might be bad. Be sure you want to wish for them." 

The moral of this story is that it's important to be careful when you make wishes. It's okay to think before you act, because your actions might not have the outcome you desire.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a pair of scissors. The scissors were not sharp, they were dull. Tim wanted to cut paper with the scissors, but it was hard because they were dull.

One day, Tim's mom saw him trying to cut paper with the dull scissors. She felt sad for Tim. She wanted to help him. Tim's mom had an idea! She thought she could restore the scissors and make them sharp again.

Tim's mom took the dull scissors and worked on them. She made the scissors sharp. Now, Tim could cut paper easily! Tim was very happy. He thanked his mom for helping him. From that day on, Tim and his mom cut many things together with the restored scissors. They had lots of fun and made beautiful art.

Once upon a time, there was a witch. She lived in a big, open house. The house was in the middle of the woods. The witch was nice and liked to help people.

One day, a little girl named Lily got lost in the woods. She saw the witch's house and went inside. The witch saw Lily and wanted to help her. She gave Lily some food and a warm place to sit.

The witch reminded Lily to always stay close to her home. She told Lily that the woods can be scary. Lily thanked the witch and went back home. From that day on, Lily never got lost again.

Once upon a time, there was a big parade. Lots of people and animals walked down the street. There were clowns and dancers too. A little girl named Lily watched the parade with her mommy. 

Lily liked to count the things she saw. She counted the clowns, the dancers, and the animals. She even counted the balloons! 

Mommy made sure Lily was safe while they watched the parade. They stood on the sidewalk and held hands. Lily felt happy and excited. She loved the parade and counting all the things she saw.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, she was drawing a beautiful picture of a flower when her little brother, Max, came into the room.

Max wanted to play with Lily's crayons, but Lily didn't want him to. "No, Max! These are my crayons!" she said.

Max got upset and grabbed Lily's eraser. He started to spray it with water and wipe it all over her picture. "Ha! Now your picture is ruined!" he said, being very bossy.

Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do. But then, she had an idea. "Max, do you want to help me make a new picture?" she asked.

Max nodded his head and together they made a beautiful picture of a butterfly. Lily showed Max how to use the crayons and Max was very happy to learn. From that day on, Lily and Max shared the crayons and made many more beautiful pictures together.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little bear who liked to explore the world. One day, she was walking through a dark and gloomy forest when suddenly she saw a special light. As she got closer, she could see that power was making the light glow. The power was so strong that it was like a magical surprise! 

The little bear was so excited that she jumped up to try to catch the power. But it was too slippery for her little paws and the power just kept on glowing. She tried with all her might to get hold of this special power, but nothing worked. 

Finally, the bear had an idea - she stood still and wished as hard as she could that the power would stay with her. Miraculously, the power understood and it stayed with her like a faithful friend. The bear was so happy that the power was always with her - she felt invincible! 

The little bear explored the forest with the glowing power, never having to worry about darkness or loneliness again. From then on, the clumsy little bear was never afraid!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jordan. Jordan had very long hair and his Mum wanted to give him a little haircut. So, one Saturday morning, they went to the hairdresser. 

The hairdresser supplied Jordan with a big cape to wear. Then, she brushed his hair and snipped away at it with the scissors. Jordan quite enjoyed the feeling of the brush in his hair.

After a few minutes, the haircut was finished. Jordan's Mum smiled when she saw the finished look. She said that Jordan was the most handsome boy she had ever seen. She gave Jordan a big hug and a kiss.

Once they got home, Mum put a big mirror in front of Jordan. He looked in the mirror and was very happy with his little haircut. He knew he looked smart and he knew others would think so too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park near her house. One day, she saw a big tower in the park. It was very tall and she wondered what was inside.

Suddenly, a boy named Max appeared. He asked Lily if she wanted to play with him. Lily said yes and they went to play together. They played hide and seek, tag and other fun games.

After a while, they both got hungry. Max said, "I brought some delicious cookies. Do you want to try one?" Lily replied, "Yes, please!" They sat down and enjoyed the tasty cookies.

As they were eating, Lily looked up at the tower and wondered what was inside. Max smiled and said, "Do you want to know what's in there?" Lily nodded excitedly. Max said, "It's a secret, but I'll show you tomorrow." Lily was so excited to find out what was inside the tower and couldn't wait for tomorrow to come.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse. She was very light and liked to explore the world around her. She had an idea one day that she could travel far away, so she decided to mail herself! She wrote a note and put it in a box, addressed it to herself, and went to the post office.

The mail man took the box and put it on the truck. The mouse hopped on and away they went! The little mouse was so excited to go on her new adventure.

The mouse traveled for days until finally she stopped at a new place. She opened up the box and stepped out. It was bright and there was so much to explore! She was amazed at the sights and sounds around her. 

The little mouse made friends and had lots of fun. Eventually, it was time to go back home. She mailed herself back to her old place and felt so happy. She had a great adventure and made lots of memories to last a lifetime.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. She was very anxious about touching things. Everywhere she went, things looked so nice and shiny, but she was scared to touch them. One day, Sophie came across a beautiful stone. She wanted to touch it very much, but she was too scared. So, she decided to make a wish instead. She closed her eyes and wished that she wasn't scared to touch things. Then, something magical happened. When Sophie opened her eyes, she felt like something had changed. Her anxious feeling had gone away and she was no longer scared to touch things. She slowly reached out her hand and, with a big smile, she touched the stone. Suddenly, something else unbelievable happened. The stone started to turn different colours! Sophie was amazed and laughed with joy. With her courage, Sophie had made a wish come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved lollipops and always wanted to eat them. One day, her mommy gave her a lollipop and said, "Lily, you can have this yummy lollipop, but you have to climb the stairs and go to your room to eat it."

Lily was so excited to eat her lollipop that she quickly climbed the stairs. But when she got to her room, she saw her little brother crying. He had fallen down and hurt his knee. Lily knew that she had to help her brother first, so she gave him the lollipop to make him feel better.

Her mommy saw what happened and said, "Lily, you did the right thing. It's always important to help others before we think about ourselves." Lily smiled and felt happy that she could make her brother feel better. From that day on, Lily learned that being kind and helpful to others is more important than having a yummy lollipop.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she found a door that was very tight and hard to open. She tried and tried but couldn't open it.

Lily had an idea. She decided to reverse the door and push it instead of pulling it. And guess what? The door opened! Lily was so happy that she could finally explore what was on the other side.

As she walked through the door, she saw a big, beautiful garden with lots of colorful flowers. She played there for hours with her friends, and they had so much fun.

From that day on, whenever Lily saw a door that was tight, she remembered to reverse it and push instead of pull. She knew that there might be something amazing waiting for her on the other side.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They walked slow on the sand, looking for shells. Tim found a big, pretty shell and showed it to his mom. She smiled and said, "What a nice shell, Tim!"

A little crab came out of the shell and said, "Hello! I'm Carl the Crab. Can we play?" Tim was happy to meet Carl. They played a fun game where Carl would hide in the sand and Tim would try to find him. Each time Tim found Carl, he would repeat, "I found you, Carl!"

As the sun went down, Tim knew it was time to go home. He said goodbye to Carl and thanked him for playing. Carl went back into his shell and waved goodbye with his little claw. Tim and his mom walked slow back to their car, excited to come back to the beach another day.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with robots. They have many robots of different colors and shapes. They make them do funny things with a remote.

One day, Tom has an idea. He says to Sam, "Let's mix our robots. We can make a new robot that is unique. No one else has a robot like that."

Sam thinks this is a good idea. He says, "Yes, let's do it. How do we mix them?"

Tom says, "We can use this tool. It can cut and join parts of the robots. We can take the head of this robot, the arms of that robot, the legs of another robot, and so on. Then we can join them with this tool."

They start to mix their robots. They cut and join parts of the robots. They make a new robot that is unique. It has a blue head, red arms, green legs, and a yellow body. It also has wheels, wings, and a tail.

They are very happy with their new robot. They say, "Wow, look at our robot. It is unique. It is the best robot ever. Let's make it do something with the remote."

They turn on the remote and press a button. The robot starts to move. But it does not do what they want. It does not listen to them. It goes crazy. It makes loud noises. It shoots lasers from its eyes. It breaks their other robots. It breaks their toys. It breaks their window. It breaks their wall. It runs away.

Tom and Sam are very scared and sad. They say, "Oh no, what have we done? We made a bad robot. It is unique, but it is not good. It is dangerous. It broke everything. It ran away. We are in trouble."

They cry and hug each other. They wish they did not mix their robots. They wish they played with their robots as they were. They learned a lesson. They will never mix their robots again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a man who sang every day. He sang while driving to the harbor in his car. He sang as he went up the tall hill to the harbor. Once he reached the top of the hill, he stopped his car and looked out at the harbor.

The day was bright and the water was blue. He could even see the boats in the harbor. He opened his car window and started singing his favorite song. The sound echoed over the harbor and it sounded very high.

The harbor birds joined in and flew around in the sky. They sang with the man and created a beautiful melody. The man smiled and sang louder and louder. He sang until the sun was setting behind the harbor.

The Little Prince lived in a kingdom far away. He had a purple cape that was very attractive. One day, he was feeling quite bold and decided he was going to make a demand of the King. He gathered his courage and marched right up to the throne. The King was very surprised to see a small boy in the palace, but he welcomed him in. 
The Little Prince said, "I want a purple pony!" The King said he had never heard such an outrageous demand before and he couldn't believe such a little prince could be so daring. But the Prince stood his ground and would not back down. So, the King gave in and granted him his wish. 
The Little Prince was overjoyed and thanked the King for his kindness. He ran out of the palace with a smile on his face, eager to jump on the back of his new purple pony!

Mommy and Sam were in a hurry to get to the park. Sam was excited to play in the sandbox and to swing on the swings. He was especially excited because he had a new cone in his pocket.

Mommy and Sam finally arrived at the park. Sam grabbed his cone and rushed over to the sandbox. He started to scoop the sand with his cone and then he made a big pile.

He soon started to explore the park. He found a big, unknown tree at the far end of the park. He ran up to it to take a closer look. As he looked around, he noticed a hole in the tree. Inside the hole, he saw an unknown creature. He was scared and started to run back to Mommy. 

Mommy and Sam quickly left the park. They wanted to get back home to safety. Sam kept looking back at the tree until it was out of sight. They both agreed to never go back to that park again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. He had the softest, fluffiest feathers and the cutest little beak. The bird loved to sing. Every morning, he would wake up, flutter his wings, and sing the sweetest songs.

One day, the little bird met a bigger bird. The bigger bird taught him some new songs. They sang together and flew around the sky, creating a beautiful melody. The little bird loved learning the new songs and he practiced them every day.

The little bird kept singing the new songs and he soon became the best singer in the forest. All the other birds came to listen to him and he even began teaching them the new songs. He taught them how to chirp in perfect harmony and soon, the whole forest was singing together!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to draw with his pen. He drew a picture of a car with his pen. Then, he got tired and wanted to sit down. 

Timmy's mom saw him and asked, "Are you tired, Timmy?" 

Timmy said, "Yes, Mommy. I want to seat down." 

His mom said, "Okay, let's find a seat for you." 

They found a big chair and Timmy sat down. He looked at his picture and smiled. "I like my car," he said. 

His mom smiled too and said, "You did a great job with your pen, Timmy. I'm proud of you." 

Timmy felt happy and not tired anymore. He hugged his mom and said, "Thank you, Mommy."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and explore new places. One day, Timmy's mom took him to a museum. The museum was enormous! Timmy was amazed by all the things he saw.

As Timmy and his mom walked around the museum, they saw many different things. Timmy saw a big dinosaur and a shiny spaceship. He said, "Wow, Mommy! Look at all the cool stuff in this museum! Can we store some of it in our house?"

His mom laughed and said, "No, Timmy. We can't store all these things in our house. But we can come back and visit the museum anytime we want."

Later that day, Timmy and his mom went to a toy store. Timmy saw a toy dinosaur and a toy spaceship. He said, "Mommy, can we buy these toys? They remind me of the things we saw in the museum."

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Timmy. Let's buy them and take them home. Then we can remember all the fun we had at the museum."

Once upon a time, there was a big dinosaur. He was very scary and made all the other animals anxious. They were afraid to go near him. One day, a little bird had an idea. She thought that if all the animals unite, they could make the big dinosaur go away. 

The little bird went to all the animals and told them her plan. The rabbits, squirrels, and even the mice agreed to help. They all gathered together and marched towards the big dinosaur. When the dinosaur saw all the animals coming towards him, he got anxious and started to run away.

The little bird was happy that her plan worked. All the animals were now safe and not anxious anymore. They all played together and had lots of fun. From that day on, they knew that if they unite, they can overcome any fear.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to fly away. She found a birdcage to keep her safe and jumped inside. The birdcage was closed and the little bird was stuck.

The little bird was so sad. She wanted to fly in the sky but the birdcage was keeping her trapped. Then one day she had an idea. The birdcage was set on a table and she had an idea to make it move.

The little bird flapped her wings very hard. She kept on flapping until the birdcage suddenly moved! The birdcage started to rock side to side until it was on its side and then it started to roll. The birdcage rolled and rolled until it crashed onto the floor. 

The little bird was so happy! She opened the door of the birdcage and flew away. She was free! It was a terrible thing to be stuck in the birdcage but now she was free and the bird was happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play soccer with her friends in the park. One day, Lily and her friends decided to make a goal out of sticks and stones.

As they were playing, the wind started to blow and it became very cold. Lily shivered and said, "I'm cold. Can we stop playing and go home?"

Her friend, Timmy, replied, "No, we have to keep playing until we score a goal."

So, Lily and her friends continued to play and march around the field. Finally, Lily kicked the ball and it went straight into the goal they had made. Everyone cheered and Lily felt very happy. They all went home with big smiles on their faces, feeling warm and proud of themselves.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red bike with a flat tire. He wanted to ride his bike, but he couldn't because of the flat tire. Timmy's dad said he would fix it for him.

While his dad was fixing the tire, Timmy saw a bird. The bird was singing a pretty song. Timmy wanted to sing like the bird, so he tried to whistle. He tried and tried, but he couldn't whistle.

Finally, Timmy's dad finished fixing the tire. Timmy got on his bike and rode away. The wind was harsh on his face, but he was happy because he could ride his bike again. As he rode, he tried to whistle again. Maybe one day he would be able to whistle like the bird.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her blanket very much. It was soft and cozy and made her feel happy. One day, Lily's mommy said, "Lily, it's time to go to bed." But Lily said, "Mommy, I don't want to sleep with my blanket tonight. It feels uncomfortable."

Mommy asked, "Why does it feel uncomfortable, Lily?" Lily replied, "I don't know, mommy. It just feels weird." Mommy said, "That's okay, Lily. You don't have to use your blanket if you don't want to. Maybe you can try sleeping with your stuffed animal instead." Lily thought about it and said, "Okay, mommy. I'll try that. Thank you for understanding."

Lily hugged her stuffed animal and closed her eyes. She felt happy again, knowing that she had a new way to sleep. From that day on, Lily knew that if her blanket ever made her feel uncomfortable, she could always find another way to feel cozy and happy.

Once there was a skeleton. He loved to jog every day. Every morning he would put his shoes on and jog around the lake. He was very excited to be out in the fresh air each day. 

One day, he noticed a small girl standing on the edge of the lake. She was watching him as he jogged. The skeleton felt excited and waved to her. She smiled and waved back. 

He decided to invite the happy girl to join him on his jog. She giggled and took his hand. As they jogged together, the skeleton pointed out all the interesting things he saw. 

The pair had a great time jogging together! When it was time to go home, the girl gave the skeleton a big hug and thanked him for a wonderful time. The skeleton felt really excited that he had a new friend. They still jog together every day.

Billy woke up bright and early for school one morning. He was so excited to see his friends and learn something new. He ran into the kitchen to have breakfast and saw his mom looking frustrated. 

"What's wrong, Mommy?" Billy asked.

His mom looked at him and said, â€œI have to repair my bike before you go to school.â€

Billy thought this was a bit strange, but he didn't say anything. He went to school and all his friends were talking about the amazing lunch they had brought in their lunch boxes. 

Billy was very excited, but he hadnâ€™t been able to pack a lunch because his mom was busy repairing the bike. When Billy got back home after school, he was frustrated, but he saw that his mom had fixed the bike.

When he went into the kitchen, he saw a big lunch box on the table. Inside was the most delicious lunch. Billy was so happy and started to eat it right away. His mom gave him a big hug and said, "I didn't want you to be without lunch, so I made it for you while I was repairing the bike!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, his mom said he could go play in the park, but he had to come back before it got dark. 

Timmy ran to the park and started playing on the swings. He was having so much fun that he forgot to measure the time. Suddenly, it started to get gloomy outside. Timmy knew it was time to go home. 

He went back to his mom and she was happy to see him. She allowed him to have a snack and watch his favorite cartoon. Timmy was so happy that he had a fun day and got to do what he loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very obedient. He always did what his mom and dad told him to do. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. The park was big and had lots of fun things to do.

At the park, Tim saw a big red ball. He wanted to touch it. But, his mom told him not to touch the ball because it belonged to someone else. Tim felt embarrassed because he didn't know he shouldn't touch it.

Tim was sad but he wanted to be obedient, so he didn't touch the ball. Then, a big dog came and took the ball away. Tim was sad because he didn't get to play with the ball. The dog ran away with the ball and Tim went home with his mom.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a bird with enormous wings. The bird was very nice and liked to help others. One day, the bird met a small ant who was lost.

The ant said, "Please help me find my way home." The bird, using its big wings, ordered the ant to climb on its back. The bird flew high and looked for the ant's home.

After a while, they found the ant's home. The ant was very happy and thanked the bird. The bird felt good for helping the ant. From that day on, they became very good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a cow who lived on the farm. The cow loved to use the farm and graze in the fields.

One day the farmer gave the cow a special treat. He gave her some apples. The cow was so grateful and ate the apples with delight.

The cow thanked the farmer for her treat. The farmer was happy to see the cow so grateful and gave her another treat, some carrots for lunch. The cow munched on the carrots and enjoyed them so much.

As the cow went back to the fields to graze, she was so very grateful for the farmer's kindness. She was thankful for the delicious treats he had given her.

The cow returned to the farm every day and the farmer always had something special for her. The cow and the farmer became very good friends.

The end.

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to collect pretty rocks. Every day, he would go outside and find more rocks to add to his collection. He had big rocks, small rocks, and even shiny rocks. Tim was very happy with his rocks.

One night, Tim had a bad dream. He dreamed that a big, scary nightmare took all his rocks away. Tim woke up and felt very sad. He did not want to lose his rocks. They were very special to him.

The next day, Tim told his mommy about the bad dream. She gave him a hug and said, "Don't worry, Tim. Your rocks are safe. The nightmare can't take them away." Tim felt better and went outside to collect more rocks. He knew that his rocks were safe and the nightmare was just a dream. And from that day on, Tim was never afraid of nightmares again.

Lily and Sam liked to go to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, slide down the slide, and run on the grass. Sometimes, they also liked to buy ice cream from the vendor. The vendor was a nice man who had a big cart with many flavors of ice cream.

One day, they went to the park and saw the vendor. They ran to him and asked for ice cream. But there was a problem. There was a big dog next to the cart. The dog was barking and growling. It did not let anyone get close to the cart. It wanted to eat all the ice cream.

The vendor was scared of the dog. He tried to shoo it away, but it did not listen. He tried to call for help, but no one heard him. He did not know what to do. The dog was preventing him from selling ice cream.

Lily and Sam were sad and impatient. They really wanted ice cream. They did not like the dog. They wished it would go away. They looked around and saw a stick. They had an idea. They picked up the stick and threw it far away. The dog saw the stick and ran after it. It forgot about the ice cream.

The vendor was happy and relieved. He thanked Lily and Sam for their help. He gave them each a big scoop of ice cream. They chose their favorite flavors. They licked their ice cream and smiled. They were glad they could prevent the dog from ruining their fun. They enjoyed their ice cream and their day at the park.

Teddy was a bear who loved to sleep and play. One day he decided to go explore the underground. He slowly walked inside, and it was very dark, but he saw lots of colorful lights. He followed the lights and found a cozy place to lay down. He rested and closed his eyes. 

Suddenly, Teddy heard voices coming from the darkness. He opened his eyes and noticed two shadows talking to each other.

"Look at the beautiful colors on the walls," the first said.

"Yes, they look so bright and colorful," the other one said. 

Teddy quietly watched and listened to them talk. After a moment, he realized they were fairies who lived underground! He was filled with awe and delight as he looked around.

The fairies suddenly noticed Teddy and smiled. "Hi Teddy," they said playfully.
"Would you like to come explore with us?" 

Teddy nodded and followed the two fairies as they explored the colorful underground. He had so much fun discovering the wonders of the underground with his new friends.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Emily. Emily had a heavy shirt. She loved to play with it. Every day her mum would encourage her to put on her shirt. Emily was very happy to have it on because it made her look special and beautiful.

One day Emily decided to take her shirt outside and play with it in the garden. She loved to run around in her heavy shirt. It made her feel like a princess. Her mum watched Emily from the kitchen window and always made sure to encourage her.

One day, Emily found a little bird in the garden and wanted to be his friend. The little bird was very scared at first, but Emily gently encouraged the little bird to come to her. Soon enough, the little bird was hopping all around Emily's heavy shirt.

Emily and the little bird became best friends. From that day on, Emily would always encourage the little bird whenever it was scared. Emily was very happy to have a special friend and have her heavy shirt to play in.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the forest. Suddenly, she saw a fox. The fox was very calm and just sat there watching her. 

"Hello Mr. Fox," said Lily. "What are you doing here?"

"I am just resting," said the fox. "What brings you to the forest?"

"I like to explore," said Lily. "But I am lost. Can you help me find my way home?"

"I can try," said the fox. "But first, something has happened. There is a big tree blocking our path. We need to find a way around it."

Lily and the fox worked together to find a way around the tree. Finally, they found a path that led out of the forest. Lily was very happy to be going home and thanked the fox for his help. The fox just smiled and went back to his calm rest.

Once upon a time there was a little octopus who lived under the sea. One day, he was scared of the deep blue level where he lived, so he decided to move away from it. He swam to the surface and saw a wide, available beach. He was no longer scared and happily played around the beach.

One day, he noticed two little children were playing in the water. He wanted to play with them, too. He stretched out his tentacles to reach the children, but alas! He scared them away.

The octopus was sad, realizing his tentacles scared the children away. He learned a lesson: Never do something that will scare other people away.  He returned to the sea and continued living in a deep blue level, remembering his lesson and being happy without scaring people away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to go on an adventure in the forest. It was so much fun! They saw birds, butterflies, and even a squirrel. 

Suddenly, Lily's friend, Sarah, fell into a hole. "Help! Help!" Sarah cried. Lily knew she had to rescue her friend. She ran to get help from the grown-ups. 

The grown-ups came and rescued Sarah. Lily felt incredible that she helped her friend. "You're my hero!" Sarah said to Lily. From that day on, Lily knew that helping others was the most fun thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Tim saw a big peach tree in his yard. He was very happy.

Tim wanted to pick a peach from the tree. He saw a big, round peach at the top. He tried to reach it, but he was too small. Tim called his friend, the squirrel. "Can you help me get the peach?" he asked. The squirrel was scared, but he wanted to help his friend.

The squirrel rushed up the tree and picked the peach for Tim. They shared the peach and it was very yummy. Tim was happy and thanked the squirrel. They both learned that helping each other is good. From that day on, they played together under the peach tree every day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, a big one and a small one. They were both playing in the park when the big friend said, "Let's kneel on the ground, itâ€™s fun!" The small friend was scared but the big friend said, "Don't worry, it's just a game!"

So the small friend kneeled with the big friend and they both laughed. But then, the big friend got an idea. He suggested, "Let's kneel and count to ten! Whoever stands up first is the loser."

The small friend felt scared and unhappy, but he started counting. When he got to ten he stood up, the big friend laughed and said, "Ha-ha, I win!"

The moral of the story is that you should not play games with friends which make them feel scared and unhappy. We should always be nice to our friends and never play games which have bad endings.

Johnny was walking down the street one day when he spotted something ahead. He saw a lucky pigeon, shaking and trembling on the ground. Johnny was curious and he wondered why the pigeon was so scared. He stepped a bit closer and tried to say hello to the bird, but it kept trembling.

Johnny carefully reached out his hand and the pigeon didn't fly away. He petted the pigeon cautiously and the trembling started to slow. Johnny was so lucky he got to be friends with a bird! He kept petting the pigeon until it was no longer scared.

The pigeon gradually gained more trust with Johnny and stayed with him the entire day. Johnny was so excited he had made a new friend, and it was a pigeon! They played together in the park and Johnny fed the pigeon some tasty treats. Before Johnny knew it, the day had to come to an end. 

Johnny said goodbye to his new feathery friend, but the pigeon didn't want to let him go. The pigeon shook and trembled as Johnny waved goodbye, but it managed to stay put. Johnny smiled as he walked away, happy to have been so lucky.

Once upon a time, two children went sailing on a smooth sea. "I want to see a whale!" said one of the children. Just then, they spotted a whale in the distance. The children were so delighted that they started to cheer. 

The whale also noticed them and started to swim towards them. 

The children were excited.

"Look at the whale," said one of the children, "it's so big and smooth!" 

The whale swam up to their boat and let the children pet it. 

The children were so happy! They spent the rest of the day sailing and playing with the whale.

Once upon a time, there was a big pot in the kitchen. Every day, the mommy would stir the pot. Inside the pot simmered a sweet and delicious fruit stew. 

One day, the little girl wanted to help. She asked her mommy if she could stir. Her mommy said yes, so they stirred together. 

The little girl stirred and stirred, and it was so noisy! The spoon clanked against the pot and bubbled as it stirred the stew. 

When the stew was done, it smelled so yummy! The little girl and her mommy picked out the soft, warm pieces of fruit and ate every last bite. 

The little girl liked stirring the stew and was so happy to help! And she knew next time, she would get to help again.

Once there was a bear named Ben. He was very silly sometimes. One day, he wanted to have a muffin, so he decided to lie to get one from the shop. He put on a very clear voice and said to the shopkeeper: "I want a muffin". The shopkeeper felt suspicious so he said "No, that's not true, tell me the real reason why you wanted a muffin".

Ben was frustrated and didn't know what to do. He knew lying was wrong but he still wanted a muffin. He thought hard and finally he found a solution. He said to the shopkeeper "I want a muffin to share with my friend". The shopkeeper thought it was a good idea and Ben was happy because he finally got the muffin he wanted.

Moral of the story: It's good to be honest and never lie!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie loved to fly high up in the sky and see the world from above. One day, Tweetie was flying over a big ocean when she saw a boat in trouble. The boat was going to sink, and the people on it were very scared.

Tweetie wanted to help, but she didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she remembered something her mommy had told her. "If you ever see someone in trouble, try to find land and lead them there." So, Tweetie flew around until she found a nearby island. She flew back to the boat and chirped as loud as she could to get their attention. Then, she led them to the island where they were safe.

The people on the boat were so grateful to Tweetie for saving them. They gave her lots of hugs and kisses and thanked her over and over again. From that day on, Tweetie felt very proud of herself for helping others. She knew that she would always be ready to remind herself of her mommy's wise words and help those in need.

Rosie and Jack were playing together. Rosie wanted to play hide and seek, so she closed her eyes and counted to ten. Jack ran to the window to hide. He peeked out the window.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary. Mary was very enthusiastic and was always happy. One day, Mary's mom and dad set off with her to visit a big barn. Once upon a time there was a rabbit, named Benny. Benny loved to bounce up and down in the wide field near his home. He was so restless and full of energy!

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a good dog, but he liked to chew on things he shouldn't. One day, Max chewed on his owner's favorite shoes. His owner was very angry and scolded him. Max felt sad and wanted to make things right.

Once upon a time there was a bossy little girl named Lily. She was very excited one day because it was time to decorate her room. Lily climbed up on a chair and started to hang colorful pictures on the wall with some help from her mom.

Once upon a time there was a nice girl called Jamie. One day she was feeling brave and decided to leave her house and explore the world outside. On her travels she noticed that everything had a different texture. She touched a smooth tree and it felt soft. Then she touched a dry leaf and it felt rough.

"Wow!" exclaimed Jamie.

Just then a friendly voice called out, "Good morning!" 

Jamie was a bit scared, so she looked around to see who was speaking. A little rabbit was there with its ears hopping up and down. Jamie had never seen a talking rabbit before but she smiled politely.

The rabbit spoke again. "My name is Roxy, and I'm here to show you the different textures in nature."

Jamie was excited and thanked Roxy for this new adventure. They spent the day discovering more and more textures, from prickly leaves to smooth stones. By the end of the day, Jamie felt inspired by all of the things she had seen. 

She smiled brightly as Roxy waved goodbye. Jamie thanked Roxy again for being so polite and kind, and then carried on her journey home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to build things with his dad's tools. He had a hammer that he used to hit nails into wood. The hammer was heavy, but Timmy was strong and he could hold it.

When Timmy was finished, he showed his dad the birdhouse. His dad was proud of him and said, "You did a great job, Timmy! I'm so happy I allowed you to use my tools." Timmy smiled and felt happy too.

Once upon a time, a clumsy ant was walking in the garden. Suddenly, it fell into a puddle of mud. The ant tried to get out but it couldn't.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was walking through a field one day when he found something heavy. It was a big rock, and the boy wanted to move it. He tried to pick it up but it was too heavy for him.

Once upon a time, there was a noisy bird named Bobo. Bobo lived in a big tree with his family. They loved to sing and play all day long. Bobo's tree was near a patch of pretty flowers. The flowers were red, blue, and yellow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play with her toys. One day, she decided to start a game of hide-and-seek with her friends. She was very excited to play!

"Look, we made an igloo!" Lily said. "Let's go inside and pretend we live here."

They crawled inside the igloo and sat on the floor. They felt cozy and warm. They pretended they had a fire and a pot of soup.

"What kind of soup do you want?" Sam asked.

"I want spicy soup, like the one Mommy makes," Lily said.

"Me too," Sam said. "But we don't have any spicy things here. Only snow."

Sam had an idea. He crawled out of the igloo and looked around. He saw a red pepper in the garden. It was frozen, but still bright and shiny. He picked it up and brought it back to the igloo.

"Look, I found something spicy!" he said. "Let's put it in our soup."

He broke the pepper in half and gave one piece to Lily. They both bit into it and smiled.

"Mmm, spicy!" Lily said.

But then, they felt a burning sensation in their mouths. They gasped and coughed. Their eyes watered and their noses ran. They spit out the pepper and ran out of the igloo.

"Ow, ow, ow!" they cried. "That was too spicy!"

They ran to the house and asked Mommy for some water and milk. Mommy hugged them and gave them a glass each. She asked them what happened.

"We ate a spicy pepper from the garden," Lily said.

"We wanted to make spicy soup in our igloo," Sam said.

Mommy smiled and shook her head. She said, "Next time, be careful what you put in your soup. And don't eat frozen peppers. They are not good for you."

Lily and Sam nodded and drank their water and milk. They felt better and said sorry to Mommy. They learned their lesson. They decided to make a different kind of soup next time. Maybe carrot soup, or chicken soup, or tomato soup. But not spicy soup. Never again.
