The little boy was so excited! He had never seen so many cool things in one place! There were swings, a slide, and best of all, a big sandbox.

In the sandbox, the little boy made a big pile of sand. He spread it out nice and flat and flopped down onto it. He felt the cool sand against his skin and sighed.

When he stood back up, the little boy noticed a pretty ant crawling across the sand. He decided to follow it, and off he went, on his adventure.

Wherever the ant went, the little boy followed. Then the ant suddenly scurried off and the little boy smiled. It had been a very cool adventure!

Once there was a sun that was shining very bright in the sky. One day it started to get dark and the wind began to blow. It made the trees sway and the leaves dance. Suddenly, a storm start! Big dark clouds came in and the thunder roared. Little Pete was outside and he was scared.

His mommy came to take him home. They both grabbed hands and started to run back. But it was too late - the storm had started! Rain was coming down hard and it was loud. Little Pete was still scared, but his mommy held him tight and told him it would be alright. 

They stayed inside until the storm was over and the sun came out again. Everything was different. All the trees and plants were clean from the rain and the sky was blue and shiny. Little Pete and his mommy looked at the rainbow in the sky and they smiled. Now they knew it was time to go play again!

Once upon a time, there was a lazy fox. The fox didn't like to play. But one day, it heard a beautiful sound. 

The sound was coming from a crystal. It sparkled in the sunlight and was very pretty. The fox was curious, so it crept closer. 

The fox was soon hypnotized by the sound. It started to sway back and forth, until it suddenly began to play. The fox jumped, twirled, and danced all around the crystal. 

The fox played until it was tired. Then, it lay down next to the crystal, which still sparkled in the sunlight. 

The lazy fox was very happy, and soon it fell asleep with a big smile on its face.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who went on an adventure looking for beans. The friends were called Bob and Tony. They met at the park and decided to explore the forest.

They searched and searched until they came to a big tree. It was very graceful, with long branches that touched the sky. Suddenly, they spotted a bag of beans among the leaves!

The happy friends had found what they were looking for. They picked the beans and quickly ran home to share them with their families. They made sure to give everyone a fair share of the beans and everyone enjoyed them. 

Bob and Tony were very proud of their adventure. They were grateful for the beans and for the graceful tree that helped them meet their goal. They would never forget their journey together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play with his toys and drink juice. One day, Jack's mom gave him some juice to drink, but Jack spilled it all over the floor. Jack's mom said, "You need to behave and not spill your juice." 

Jack felt sad because he knew he didn't behave well. He cleaned up the juice and apologized to his mom. Jack promised to behave and not spill his juice again. From that day on, Jack behaved like a normal little boy and enjoyed his juice without any spills.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys, but they do not like to share. Sara has a flexible doll that can bend and twist. Ben has a truck that can make loud noises and move fast. One day, Sara and Ben are playing in their room.

"Can I touch your doll?" Ben asks Sara.

"No, you cannot touch my doll. It is mine. Go away!" Sara says. She hates when Ben wants to touch her things.

"Can I touch your truck?" Sara asks Ben.

"No, you cannot touch my truck. It is mine. Go away!" Ben says. He hates when Sara wants to touch his things.

They start to fight and pull each other's hair. They scream and cry. Their mom hears them and comes to their room.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks. She is angry.

"Sara and Ben are not sharing. They are being mean. They hate each other." Mom says.

She takes away their toys and puts them in a box. She says they cannot play with them until they learn to be nice.

Sara and Ben are sad and sorry. They want their toys back. But Mom does not give them back. She says they have to go to bed early. They have no toys, no fun, and no friends. They have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable fairy named Fifi. She lived in a big tree in the forest. Fifi had a job to protect all the small animals.

One day, a little rabbit named Riri was lost. Riri was scared and cried, "Help me, please!" Fifi heard Riri and flew to her. "Don't worry, Riri. I am here to protect you," said Fifi.

Fifi took Riri's hand and led her back to her family. Riri was happy and said, "Thank you, Fifi!" From that day on, Riri knew she could always count on Fifi to protect her and her friends.

Once there was a little bird that lived in the woods. Everyday in the spring, the bird would flutter and play in the woods. One day when the bird was playing, something disturbed it. It was a dull sound. The bird looked around but could not find what was causing the noise. All around her, the birds sang and the flowers bloomed, but the dull sound kept going and going. Suddenly, a big, scary creature appeared! It was a bear. The poor bird was so frightened! But she quickly flew away and the bear roared before going back to his cave. From that day on, the little bird was extra careful in the spring, to make sure she was never disturbed again.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived many animals. They were all friends and liked to play together. One day, they decided to make their forest more organized. They wanted to make it easier to find where they belong.

The animals made a plan. The big animals, like the bear and the elephant, would live near the big trees. The small animals, like the rabbit and the squirrel, would live near the small trees. The birds would live in the trees high up in the sky.

The animals were very happy with their organized forest. They knew where they belonged and could play with their friends easily. The big forest was a happy place for all the animals to live and play together.

Once upon a time, there lived two best friends, Bill and Jane. They lived in a town close by, but never had the chance to meet up because the wide river between kept them apart. One day, they decided that they wanted to play together and quickly came up with a plan.

Huge rocks stood in the middle of the river preventing the bridge from connecting to either side. â€œWhat do we do now?â€ Jane asked, feeling a bit worried. Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy tube. He loved his tube very much. One day, Tim saw a big, dangerous hole in the ground. He wanted to play near it.

Tim's mom said, "No, Tim! That hole is dangerous. Stay away from it!" But Tim didn't listen. He took his tube and went to play near the hole. He rolled the tube near the hole and laughed.

Suddenly, the tube fell into the hole. Tim was sad. He wanted his tube back. He thought he could get it, but he was too close to the hole. Tim fell into the hole too. He vanished into the hole with his tube. Now, Tim and his tube were both gone, and everything was sad.

One day, there was a shy little girl named Lucy. She was getting ready to throw something in the mailbox. She was holding a letter that she had written.

Lucy was feeling very brave. She looked both ways and then threw the letter into the mailbox. It landed with a thump. 

When Lucy saw her letter in the mailbox, she clapped her hands and laughed. She was so happy that she had made it. 

Lucy's mom walked up behind her and said, "I'm so proud of you for being brave and throwing that letter in the mailbox!" Lucy smiled and nodded. 

She was proud of herself too! She had been very shy when she had gone to the mailbox, but she was glad she had dared to throw the letter inside.

Lily and Sam were playing with crayons. They liked to draw and color on paper. Lily had a red crayon and Sam had a blue one. They were having fun.

But then Sam wanted to use the red crayon too. He tried to take it from Lily's hand. Lily did not like that. She said, "No, Sam, this is my crayon. You have your own crayon. Go away!"

Sam did not listen. He pulled harder on the red crayon. Lily pulled back. They both started to yell. "Stop, stop, stop!" they said.

Mom heard the noise. She came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Sam fighting over the crayon. She was angry. She said, "Lily and Sam, what are you doing? You are not being nice to each other. You are not sharing. You are making a mess. Stop it right now!"

Lily and Sam stopped. They looked at Mom. They felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We were being bad. We will share. We will be good."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's better. I'm glad you are sorry. Now, why don't you draw a picture together? You can use both crayons. You can make a new color. What color do you get when you mix red and blue?"

Lily and Sam thought for a moment. Then they said, "Purple!"

Mom said, "That's right. Purple is a beautiful color. Why don't you draw a purple flower? Or a purple butterfly? Or a purple anything you like?"

Lily and Sam nodded. They took the crayons and the paper. They started to draw and color. They were happy. They said, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. We love purple."

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with paper. They cut paper, fold paper, and draw on paper. They make paper planes, paper hats, and paper animals.

One day, they decide to travel with paper. They take their paper planes and go to the park. They throw their paper planes in the air and watch them fly. They pretend they are pilots and talk to each other.

"Look, Lily, my paper plane is so fast!" Tom says.

"Wow, Tom, your paper plane is very good. But my paper plane is so cute!" Lily says.

They run after their paper planes and catch them. They laugh and have fun.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows their paper planes away. They try to chase them, but they are too far. They lose their paper planes.

"Oh no, Tom, our paper planes are gone!" Lily says.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I can't see them anymore!" Tom says.

They are sad and cry. They miss their paper planes.

But then, they see a man. He has a big bag. He has their paper planes in his bag. He smiles and walks to them.

"Hello, kids, are these your paper planes?" he says.

"Yes, sir, they are our paper planes!" Tom and Lily say.

"I found them in the sky. They are very nice paper planes. You are very clever kids. Do you want them back?" he says.

"Yes, please, sir, we want them back!" Tom and Lily say.

"OK, here you go. But be careful, the wind is strong today. Maybe you can play with them inside or somewhere else." he says.

He gives them their paper planes and leaves. Tom and Lily are happy and thank him. They hug their paper planes and go home. They decide to play with paper in their room. They make more paper planes, paper hats, and paper animals. They travel with paper in their imagination. They are friends. They like to play with paper.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. It was his birthday and he was very happy. His mom made him a thick cake with lots of frosting on top. Timmy loved it so much that he ate too much of it!

Later that day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy wanted to show his friend all of his new toys. But he couldn't find his favorite toy car. He looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy was very sad.

His mom told him to think about where he last had it. Then Timmy remembered he had let his little sister play with it earlier. He went to her room and found his toy car. He was so happy to have it back. He learned that it's important to share, and when you return something you borrowed, it makes others happy too.

Once there was a humble girl named Mary. Mary loved to play in her backyard, especially when the sun was shining and the birds were chirping. 

Today was the perfect day for playing in the backyard. Mary went outside with a big smile on her face. She found a swing and sat down in it. She held onto the ropes tight and she started to swing back and forth. It made her feel happy and free.

After a few swings, Mary noticed some little birds nearby. She wanted to play with them. She jumped off the swing and started to chase them. She ran and laughed as the birds flew away from her.

Mary had a wonderful time playing in the yard. When it was time to go in, she took one last swing before going inside. She felt so lucky to be able to play in such a beautiful place.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy called Bert. He was always up to no good, no matter how much his mom tried to tell him to be a good boy.

One day, Bert was feeling particularly naughty and decided to steal his neighbour's hat. He snuck over to their house, quietly took the hat and ran away with it.

When he got back home, he was so proud that his mom asked him "What did you get, Bert?" He proudly showed her the hat and said "Mom, look what I brought!"

His mom was very angry and said "Bert! That was not nice! You must take that hat back to where it belongs!"

So Bert sadly went back to the neighbour's house to give the hat back. When he handed it over he said: "I'm sorry I took your hat, I will not do it again!"

The neighbour laughed and said: "You must have been feeling very naughty, that's why you took the hat!"

But Bert knew he had done something wrong, and that naughtiness is never a good thing. Because of this, he never went near the neighbour's hat again!

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. She was three years old and loved to play with her toy animals. One day, her mom called to her and said, "Come, Daisy, let's make cocoa!" Daisy was so excited. She quickly rushed to the kitchen where her mom said they could make the cocoa together.

Daisy's mom put some cocoa powder in a bowl and mixed it with some milk, then put it on the stove. Soon, the cocoa was ready and Daisy and her mom shared a mug full of delicious cocoa. It was the best cocoa Daisy had ever tasted.

As Daisy and her mom sipped on the cocoa, Daisy's mom said, "You know, Daisy, cocoa is very important. It can give us energy, and make us feel happy." Daisy thought about this for a moment then smiled and said, "Yes, and it tastes really good too!"

Once upon a time, there was a lady who was very lonely. She wanted to get married and she wanted a rod to go fishing. But she was helpless and had no way of getting what she wanted.

One day, she went out for a walk and saw a man walking down the street. She asked him if he wanted to marry her and he said yes! She was so happy.

The man said he would get her a rod for fishing. She went looking for a rod but the shop was closed. She was feeling helpless and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, the man appeared out of nowhere! He had managed to find a rod and he gave it to her with a smile. She was so happy that she hugged him and they got married.

And they both lived happily ever after - fishing with their rod!

Once upon a time there was a dog named Patches. Patches was a fluffy, white pup. His goal each day was to find a dirt patch in the yard to dig.

One day, Patches saw the biggest and dirtiest patch in the yard. He couldn't resist the urge to dig. He dug and dug and dug until he couldn't dig any more.

Then, Patches heard a voice. "Mama, what's Patches doin'?" it said. Patches looked up and saw a little girl. 

The little girl said in a loud voice, "Oh look, a filthy dirt patch. Patches is diggin' it up!" 

Mama said, "Patches is just trying to reach his goal, dear. It looks like he is almost there." 

The little girl and Mama both smiled at Patches and he wagged his tail. He had reached his goal and he was so happy!

Mummy went to the shop to buy some food for dinner. She was hungry and wanted something nice.

When she arrived in the shop she saw that there was a lucky draw. Mummy said it was her lucky day and decided to take part.

"Yes, Lily. You are right. You are different, but you are the same. You are both kind and friendly. That's what matters most," mom said.

Lily and Sam learned a lesson. They learned that they can be friends with anyone, no matter what they look like or what they have. They learned to respect and appreciate each other's differences. They learned to share and care. They learned to be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and paint. One day, she decided to make a picture of a big fruit basket. She started by drawing a round apple and a juicy orange.

Suddenly, she had a creative idea! She decided to add a banana, a bunch of grapes, and a big watermelon to her picture. Lily was so happy with her beautiful fruit basket.

As she was finishing her drawing, her mom came in and said, "Wow, Lily! You are so creative! I love your fruit basket!" Lily smiled and felt proud of her work. From that day on, she started drawing more and more pictures of fruits and other things she loved.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to chew gum. He thought it was cool to blow big bubbles. One day, Timmy was chewing gum in class. He blew a big bubble and it popped all over his face. Everyone laughed at him and he felt embarrassed.

Timmy didn't want to be embarrassed again, so he decided not to chew gum in class anymore. But then, his friend Billy showed up with a new kind of gum. It was so cool that Timmy couldn't resist. He took a piece and started chewing. But when he blew a bubble, it got stuck in his hair! Now Timmy was really embarrassed.

Timmy learned his lesson and decided to only chew gum outside of school. He didn't want to be embarrassed again. And from that day on, he always made sure to check his hair before leaving the house.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her pink ball. One day, Lily went for a walk in the park. She saw a charming butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was a car that zoomed past her. Lily was scared and ran to hide behind a tree. She peeked through the branches and saw a dog running after the car. 

Lily felt sad for the dog, so she called him over. The dog was friendly and licked her face. Lily petted him and they became friends. From that day on, Lily and the dog played together in the park every day. They would chase after the pink ball and sometimes even try to catch the charming butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a gloomy tree in the middle of a dark forest. It was tall and strong, but something seemed wrong.

One day, a boy came to the tree. He tapped the bark with his little hand and said, "Hello tree!" But the tree didn't answer back. The boy looked up and saw a hole in the top of the tree with a door shut tight.

He knocked on the door and said, "Who's in there?" But all he heard was silence. Then he said, "Please come out!" In a moment, someone opened the door and the boy saw an old man.

The man said, "I have been living in this tree for many years, since I was a young boy! But it's getting too dark in here, I've got to go." Then the man grabbed a bag and stepped out into the sunlight. He thanked the boy and said goodbye.

The old man wandered off and the boy watched him go. He waved goodbye and shut the door. The tree seemed a bit gloomier now, but it was still the same old tree. And the boy smiled, knowing the old man was looking for a new home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and watch the pretty colors in the sky when the sun went down. That was called a sunset. 

One day, Lily's mom made her a yummy snack. It was a big, juicy apple. Lily took a bite and it tasted so good! She loved the way it tasted. 

Later that day, Lily and her mom went on a walk. They saw some birds flying in the sky and some flowers growing in the grass. Lily thought it was all so crazy and fun. 

As the sun started to go down, Lily and her mom sat on a bench and watched the sunset. It was so beautiful with all the colors in the sky. Lily thought it was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a kind and compassionate King who ruled over a peaceful kingdom. Everyone in the kingdom loved the King and they knew he had a big heart. 

One day, a young boy from a nearby village came to the castle. The boy had done something wrong and he was jailed for it. The King wanted to be a forgiving ruler and he wanted to help the boy. 

The King asked the boy why he had done the wrong thing. The boy sadly replied, "I wanted to make my family happy. I wanted to provide for them." 

The King was moved by the boy's plight and his compassion kicked in. He said to the boy, "You have made a mistake but I know you have a good heart. I will provide you with an opportunity to make things right. 

The King let the boy out of jail and the villagers were very happy. The King was loved by all for being so compassionate and forgiving. Everyone admired the wise and kind heart of the King. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jazz. She was only 3 years old, but she already liked to make up stories.

One day, her mum wanted to remind her to do her chores. She said, "Jazz, remember to clean your room and pick up your toys!"

Jazz was feeling uncomfortable and she did not want to obey her mum. So instead of listening to her mum, she made up a story about a magical world with a big castle and lots of magical creatures.

Suddenly, she heard some music coming from outside. It was jazz music! Jazz smiled and asked her mum if she could go outside and play.

Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, that's a good idea, Jazz. Just remember to come back soon."

Jazz was so happy that she ran outside to enjoy the music. As she danced to the jazz music, she felt so comfortable and happy.

From then on, whenever Jazz needed a reminder to do her chores, her mum would play some jazz music. Jazz knew that the music was her mum's way of reminding her that she had things to do!

Amy was a young girl who loved to set the table. Every day, she would carefully place a plate at each of the four chairs. She was so happy when she got it right and felt successful.

One day, when Amy was setting the table, her little brother wandered over. He knocked the plate off of the chair and it clattered to the floor, smashing into pieces. 

Amy was very upset and started to cry. She asked her brother, "Why did you do that?" 

Her brother shrugged and explained, "I don't know. I wanted to see what would happen."

Amy was so angry and sad. She realised her brother would never understand how much it would have meant to her to set a successful table. What a bad ending!

One day, two friends decided to measure something unusual. They hugged each other and then began to measure. They measured from head to toe and from side to side. They even measured circles and squares! Finally, they stood up and grabbed each other in a big hug.

"We did a good job!" they said. As they hugged, a funny thought came to their minds. They decided to measure their hugs! So, they stretched their arms as wide as they could and began to laugh.

When the hug was over, they looked up at the sky and smiled. Then, one of them said, "That was an unusual measure for a hug!" So, they shared one last hug and then ran off to play.

One day, Sarah was playing in the park. She saw a bright yellow duck in the pond. She wanted to catch it, so she ran fast to try and get it. But it was too fast for Sarah and it jumped away. She tried again, but the duck was still too quick. So Sarah came up with a plan. She took some of the dirty mud from the ground and smeared it on her hands. She quickly ran after the duck and when it jumped away, she grabbed it with the muddy hands. She had succeeded! Sarah was so happy and hugged the yellow duck close. From then on, Sarah kept the duck as a pet and would take it for walks around the park.

A boy named Joe was in his bedroom. He was looking for something to do, so he picked up a book from his shelf. But when he opened the book, he saw something strange. Inside was a fake doll! He stared at it in surprise. 

He wondered why it was there. He picked it up and tried to figure it out. But suddenly a voice said, "That's mine!" Joe looked up. It was his little sister! She was angry because she had given the doll to Joe's friend. His friend was supposed to put it in his room, but he forgot.

Joe stared at his sister. She was still mad and she wanted her doll back. Joe didn't want his sister to be mad, so he gave her the fake doll back. His sister was so excited and smiled. She thanked Joe and gave him a big hug. Joe smiled too. Everything was back to normal.

Once upon a time, there was a big plane. The plane had two wings and could fly high in the sky. One day, the pilot of the plane needed to shoot a movie. He needed a dependable camera to do it. 

The pilot searched for a camera that he could trust. He found one that was dependable and could shoot great videos. He put the camera in the plane and flew off into the sky.

As the plane flew, the camera shot amazing footage of the world below. The pilot was happy because he had found a dependable camera to help him with his movie. And the plane was happy too, because it got to fly high in the sky. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a fragile doll that she loved very much. One night, she had a dream that her doll came to life and they went on an adventure together.

The next day, Lily was playing with her doll when her little brother came in and accidentally kicked the doll. Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her brother said, "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to kick your doll."

Lily wiped away her tears and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. But please be careful next time." Her brother nodded and promised to be more careful. From then on, Lily made sure to keep her fragile doll safe and sound.

Once there was a delicate mine. It sparkled in the sun and shone in the night. It was magical, and people from all around wanted it!

One day when all was quiet, a small creature came and tried to steal the precious mine. But the mine was too delicate, and as the creature tried to take it, it started to scatter!

The little glittering pieces of the mine flew everywhere, and the creature couldn't scoop them up to keep. The mine was now safe and still delicate. 

The creature was sad, but soon realized that the mine was safer and happier this way. The little pieces still sparkled in the sun and shone in the night. 

The creature smiled and flew away, never to try and take the delicate mine again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. Tom was very eager to play outside, but his mommy told him to finish his lunch first. 

Tom's neighbor, Mrs. Smith, saw him eating and said, "Hello, Tom! What are you eating for lunch?" 

Tom replied, "I'm eating a sandwich with peanut butter and jelly. It's yummy!" 

Mrs. Smith smiled and said, "That sounds delicious. Don't forget to wash your hands when you're done eating." 

Tom finished his lunch and ran outside to play. He had so much fun that he forgot to come inside when his mommy called him for dinner. But his neighbor, Mrs. Smith, saw him playing and reminded him to go inside for dinner. Tom thanked her and went inside to eat with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a little bee. He lived in a hive with his bee friends. Every day, the bees would fly around and find flowers. The flowers had sweet stuff inside. The bees loved the sweet stuff.

One day, the little bee did not want to fly. He wanted to walk like a normal bug. So, he walked out of his hive. He walked on the grass and saw many bugs. He saw ants, and they were walking too. The little bee was happy to walk like them.

As he walked, he found a big flower. It had sweet stuff inside. The little bee walked back to his hive. He told his friends about his walk. The other bees wanted to walk too. So, they all walked together and had fun. The little bee was happy to share his new way to find sweet stuff with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to play and run all day. One day, Spot saw a big ball in the yard. He wanted to play with it, but he knew it was not his ball. Spot thought it would be fun, so he took the ball anyway.

Spot played with the ball all day. He did not know that he was making trouble. The ball belonged to his friend, Sam the cat. Sam was sad because he could not find his ball to complete his game. When Sam saw Spot with his ball, he felt very sorry.

Spot saw that Sam was sad and knew he made trouble. He felt sorry too. Spot gave the ball back to Sam and said sorry. They played together with the ball and had a great day. From that day on, Spot learned to share and not take things that were not his.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved motorcycles. He had a motorcycle that he rode every day. One day, Timmy's motorcycle broke. It made a loud noise and stopped moving. Timmy was sad because he loved his motorcycle. 

Timmy's dad came to help. He looked at the motorcycle and saw that the wheel was dull. He said, "Don't worry, Timmy. I can fix it." Timmy's dad took the wheel off and put a shiny new one on. Timmy was happy because his motorcycle was fixed. 

Timmy rode his motorcycle all day long. He went fast and felt the wind in his hair. He was happy that his dad could fix his motorcycle. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a best friend named Timmy. They loved to play together all the time. One day, Timmy wanted to play with his toy trucks, but Lily wanted to play with her dolls. 

Timmy said, "I don't want to play with dolls. Let's play with my trucks." 

Lily felt sad because she really wanted to play with her dolls. But then she had an idea. "Let's complete our own game. We can play with your trucks and my dolls. It will be fun!" 

Timmy thought it was a good idea and they played together happily. Lily was happy that she didn't have to give up playing with her dolls and Timmy was happy that he could play with his trucks too. They were both friends and didn't want to be bossy to each other. They knew that playing together and being happy was more important than being bossy.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant gate. It was so tall it seemed to reach up to the sky! Every day, lots of animals would come to the gate looking for food.

An old man lived nearby, and he knew the animals were hungry. So every day, he would come to the gate with some food. He would spread the food around so all the animals could eat.

The animals were so happy! They would flock around the old man and the gate, dance through the grass and chirp and squeak with delight when the food was put down.

The old man would watch with a smile and wave goodbye as the animals happily ate the food he provided. He was so kind to feed them each and every day. The animals were so thankful for the old man's generosity and kindness.

Once there was a gifted girl named Daisy. She loved spending time at the pond. Every day she would watch as the small fishes swam around.

One day she noticed a very big tree near the pond. Every time the wind blew, the leaves of the tree would whisper. Daisy stopped to listen.

She sighed and closed her eyes. Suddenly she heard singing. It was the most beautiful music she had ever heard.

Daisy opened her eyes and saw the fishes had changed colour and were now singing together. She smiled, it was the most magical thing she had ever seen!

The fishes whispered to Daisy that they were thankful to have their own secret song and they were glad she was gifted enough to have heard it. Daisy thanked them and waved goodbye. She knew she would never forget her special time at the pond.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray mouse who loved to play on his computer. He would spend all day clicking and tapping away, never taking a break. One day, the mouse felt very tired and his eyes hurt from staring at the bright screen. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud "spring" sound coming from outside. He went to investigate and found a beautiful garden full of colorful flowers and trees. The mouse realized he had been missing out on the beauty of nature because he was always on his computer. 

From that day on, the little gray mouse made a promise to himself to take breaks from his computer and enjoy the wonders of the world around him. He learned that there is more to life than just staring at a screen all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who lived in a cozy shelter made of twigs and leaves. The bird loved to sing and play all day long. One day, while the bird was flying around, it saw a beautiful shiny object in the distance. The bird felt curious and wanted to know what it was.

The bird flew closer and closer until it reached a big tree. The shiny object was hanging from one of the branches. The bird felt excited and wanted to see what it was. Suddenly, the wind blew and the shiny object revealed itself. It was a golden bell!

The bird felt happy and started to sing a beautiful melody. The sound of the bell was so attractive that all the animals in the forest came to see what was happening. The little bird felt proud and happy to have found the golden bell. From that day on, the bird sang even more beautiful songs, and all the animals in the forest loved to listen to it.

Jamie was in a room. It was very calm. Jamie looked around. He could hear a sound. He listened and then he heard it. It was music and it was very soft. Jamie liked it. He smiled. Then he heard someone talking. He listened to the voice. It was his mom talking. He couldn't understand what she was saying but it sounded nice. He was peaceful and happy. He stayed in the room, listening to the music and his mom's voice. It was a nice moment.

Mom was making something delicious in the kitchen. She was wrapping an object with paper.

"What are you making, Mom?" said Tom, who was three years old.

"I'm making a surprise, Tom," Mom said. "It's going to be delicious."

Tom was excited. He wanted to know what the surprise was. He watched as Mom finished wrapping the object. 

When she was done, she put the package on a shelf.

"Can I have it now?" asked Tom.

"Not yet," Mom said with a smile. "You can have it when the surprise is ready."

Tom was confused, but he trusted Mom. He knew the surprise would be something delicious.

John was a generous boy who liked to perform. Everyday, he would do tricks for his family and friends and make them laugh. One day John had a very special trick to show. He put out his thumb and said,"Watch this".

John's mom watched and said,"What are you going to do, honey?"

John looked up at her with a huge smile and said,"I'm going to make my thumb disappear!"

John closed his fist and waved it around, then opened it slowly. Sure enough, his thumb had vanished! John's family and friends were amazed and cheered with laughter.

John had performed the best trick yet. He was so proud of himself. From then on, he kept performing amazing tricks, and everyone continued to be amazed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she found a big box of toys in her attic. She was so excited to play with them, but the box was too heavy for her to carry. 

Lily's mom saw her struggling and asked, "What's wrong, sweetie?" Lily replied, "The box is too heavy for me to carry. Can you help me?" 

Her mom said, "Of course, let's discuss how we can make it lighter." They decided to take out some of the toys and put them in a different box, so it would be easier for Lily to carry. 

As they were moving the toys, they found a toy snake that looked harmless, but Lily was afraid of it. Her mom said, "Don't worry, it's just a toy. It won't hurt you." Lily felt better and they continued to play with their toys happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a mighty bear who believed in magic. Every night he would sit by the television and his mighty friends would come alive! 
He believed that he could make anything happen if he just wished hard enough. So he wished for all his toys to come to life, and they did! One night, a tiny toy car came out of the television and it began to drive away. 
The bear decided to follow it and so he went on a great adventure. He went to the far side of the world and he even flew on the back of a giant bird! Everywhere he went, he saw wonderful things and he made lots of new friends. 
Though his journey lasted for only one night, the bear was so happy he believed he could fly like the other animals. He had an amazing time and he never forgot the magic he felt that night.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy was driving his toy car on the sidewalk. Suddenly, a big dog appeared and chased him. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. He tried to run, but the dog was too fast.

Luckily, Timmy's mom saw what was happening and quickly ran outside. She picked up Timmy and his toy car and brought them inside. Timmy was safe and the dog went away.

Timmy's mom gave him a big hug and told him everything was okay. She gave him a mild cookie to make him feel better. Timmy was happy and played with his toy car, feeling grateful that his mom was there to save him.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl. Her name was Melinda and she was very persistent. Melinda had a special velvet cape and she liked to wear it when she needed courage.

One day, Melinda wanted to join a game that the other children were playing. She took off her cape and ran to join them, but the children said no. They did not want her to play.

Melinda felt sad but she was still persistent. She asked them again to let her join the game, but the children said no.

Then, suddenly, Melinda remembered her velvet cape. She put it on and ran back to the game. She was so brave and determined that the other kids were surprised. They let her join and Melinda had the most fun ever!

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Ben and Jo. Ben and Jo were very honest and always wanted to win the prize in their game.

One day, they found a special prize inside a block of ice. But it was too cold to pick up, so Ben and Jo had to think of a clever plan. Jo suggested they take it outside where the sun would melt the ice. 

Ben grinned. "Good idea," he said. So they took it outside and put it in the sun. 

The ice began to melt and they watched in awe as the prize inside it started to appear. In the end, they each won a prize, so they were very happy. 

Ben said, "Thanks Jo - you're so honest, and you think of the best ideas!" Jo beamed and hugged Ben. 

They never forgot how their honest friendship had helped them win their prize.

Once there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was only 3 years old, but he already loved to play pretend. 

Today, Tom had a wonderful idea. He pretended he was an explorer looking for a hidden wreck. Tom would take an imaginary boat into the ocean and search the depths with a pretend telescope.

Tom's Mum watched from the beach. She smiled when she saw how excited Tom was playing. 

Tom closed his eyes and pretended he had found something. But when he opened his eyes, he was a bit disappointed. All he saw was sand, sea and sky. 

Tom's Mum called out to him: "Are you sure you should be searching there Tom? Have you forgotten that wrecks are under the water?"

Tom looked embarrassed. "Oh, yes! I'm so ignorant!" he said. With that, he ran back and jumped into the cool water, ready to continue his pretend adventure.

A little boy was walking in a park. He saw a big balloon hidden behind some trees. He was so excited that he ran to get it. He grabbed the balloon, but it was too hard for him to hold. The balloon suddenly quit and floated up into the sky. He was so sad because he wanted the balloon. He looked up and saw it get smaller and smaller in the sky until it was gone. He was sad, but then he heard a noise. He heard a crunching sound and realized that something was hidden behind the trees. He went to investigate, and he found a lot of colorful balloons! He was so happy, and he grabbed all the balloons that he could carry and went back home. He was so excited to show his family the hidden balloons.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved playing with his dog, Max. Max was a big, brown dog with a mild temper. One day, Tim and Max were playing in the park when a loud noise disturbed them. 

Max barked loudly and Tim asked, "What's wrong, Max?" Max didn't answer, but continued to bark. Suddenly, a small bird flew out of a nearby tree and Max chased after it. 

Tim called out to Max, "Come back, Max! You're scaring the bird!" Max stopped and looked back at Tim. "Sorry," Max barked. "I didn't mean to disturb the bird." Tim smiled and patted Max's head. "It's okay, Max. Let's go home now." 

And so, Tim and Max went home, happy and tired from their day in the park.

Lily and Ben like to play pretend. They have many toys and costumes. Today, they want to pretend to be hippos. They put on big gray suits and masks. They make loud noises and splash water.

"Look at me, I am a big hippo!" Lily says. She opens her mouth wide and shows her teeth.

"Me too, I am a big hippo!" Ben says. He wiggles his ears and tail.

They run around the yard and pretend to eat grass and swim in the pond. They have a lot of fun.

But then, they see a funny thing. A real hippo is standing by the fence. He is looking at them with curiosity. He thinks they are his friends.

"Hello, hippos!" the real hippo says. He tries to join them.

Lily and Ben are very surprised. They stop playing and look at the real hippo. They are scared and excited.

"Wow, a real hippo!" Lily says.

"Where did he come from?" Ben says.

They run to their mom and dad and tell them about the real hippo. Mom and dad are also surprised. They call the zoo and ask for help.

The zoo people come and take the real hippo back to his home. They say he escaped from his cage and wandered around the neighborhood. They thank Lily and Ben for finding him.

Lily and Ben are happy. They say goodbye to the real hippo. They think he is very funny and nice.

They go back to their toys and costumes. They decide to pretend to be something else. Maybe lions or monkeys or birds. They have many ideas and they have a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play together. One day, they decided to go get a treat. They went to the store and saw a big white treat. They couldn't wait to eat it! 

The friends put the treat in their basket and headed home. They were so excited and couldn't wait to eat it.

When the friends arrived home, they quickly opened the white treat. But when they tried to eat it, it just tasted bad!

The friends looked at each other in confusion. One friend said, "Why does this treat taste so bad?"

Sadly, the friend had forgotten to check the expiration date on the treat. The treat was spoiled and they couldn't eat it.

The friends were sad and went home, not able to enjoy the treat they were so excited about.

Once there was a little girl named Emma who saw a pretty butterfly. She wanted to play with it, so she said â€œLetâ€™s jump!â€ The butterfly agreed and they jumped around together in the garden. They had a lot of fun!

Emma and the butterfly wanted to play a game. Emma said â€œLetâ€™s play match with the flowers!â€ So they looked around at all the colorful flowers. They found some yellow daisies and some blue violets. They matched all the same colors together.

Emma and the butterfly found it very interesting. They looked around and found other interesting things like bugs and little stones. The bugs were different shapes and sizes and the stones were different colors. 

Emma and the butterfly had a great time. They jumped around and played match until it was time for Emma to go home. She said goodbye to the butterfly and the butterfly said â€œBye Emma! See you soon!â€

Once upon a time, there lived a purple mill who enjoyed her days in the countryside. Each day, the mill would turn its giant wheels and bring joy to the people of the nearby village.

One day, the mill noticed two children playing near the stream. The mill was amazed how happy they looked, but then she realised that they were just playing with a stick. 

The mill felt inspired by the children's joy, so she decided to offer them something much better. She opened her mouth and a large pile of coloured ribbons and sweets filled the air. The children were so delighted and they quickly ran to collect what the mill was offering.

The children enjoyed the surprise very much and thanked the mill. They then continued playing and feeling happy for the rest of the day. 

The purple mill learned a valuable lesson from the children: the simplest pleasures can bring the greatest joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Lily found a thin stick and started to draw pictures in the snow. Suddenly, she saw a tiny bug and wanted to look at it closer. She ran inside to get her microscope. When she came back outside, she put the bug under the microscope and looked at it. The bug looked so different up close! Then, Lily felt very cold and realized that her fingers were starting to freeze. She went back inside to warm up by the fire.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Sarah. She loved to play in the spring sunshine and always smiled when the warm air kissed her face. 

One day, Sarah heard the sound of something crackling in the air. She stopped playing and looked up to see a flame in the middle of the park. It was small and pretty. She stepped closer wanting to know what was happening. 

She saw a group of people huddled around the flame. They were having a picnic and every time someone spoke, the flame danced and twinkled in the light. 

Sarah was excited so she ran to her parents and asked if she could join the picnic. They agreed and she gathered some food from the kitchen. Everyone laughed and smiled when Sarah arrived. 

With a sudden roar, the flame grew bigger, brighter and warmer and Sarah laughed ke earnestly. She had not realised that it was the sunset and the light from the flame was the start of a beautiful night.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He had a special shoe that he liked to bounce. He would bounce the shoe up and down and around. It was so impressive to watch him! He was so proud of himself and his bouncing shoe. Everytime he bounced it, he smiled and laughed.

The little boy showed his special shoe to all of his friends. They were in awe at the fantastic bouncing the little boy could do. He was so talented! Everywhere he went, he took his special shoe and bounced it.

One day, he even managed to bounce the shoe all the way over his house! His friends cheered and clapped for him. They had never seen anyone bounce a shoe so far!

The little boy was so proud of himself and his bouncing shoe. He could now do an impressive thing with it and enjoyed to show it off to all of his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Max. He wanted to go on a trip with his family, but he was very tired. So he stayed home alone.

He looked out the window to see everyone already off on their trip. He felt sad that he wasn't part of the family fun. Suddenly he heard a loud noise coming from the backyard.

He went outside to investigate. To his surprise, he saw the familyâ€™s old tree rotting away. Max was so disappointed. He decided that he needed to do something. 

He decided to take a nap to try and forget about the rotted tree. He thought maybe he could think of a way to make things right when he woke up. 

When Max woke up a few hours later, he found that the tree had completely rotted away. There was nothing Max could do. He felt so sad that he was away while this happened. He wished he had been there to prevent it from rotting. Then he sadly realized that he was too tired to help.
 
The end.

One day, a boy named Tom wanted to eat yogurt. He was very hungry. He went to the kitchen and saw a big yogurt cup. Tom was very happy. He wanted to eat it all.

Tom's sister, Lily, came into the kitchen. She saw the yogurt too. She said, "I want some yogurt too!" Tom did not want to share the yogurt. He wanted it all for himself. This made Lily sad.

Tom thought about it for a moment. He wanted to be a generous brother. So, Tom said, "Okay, we can share the yogurt." But when he tried to open the yogurt cup, it was very hard. He pulled and pulled, and then the yogurt cup broke!

Yogurt went everywhere! Tom and Lily looked at each other and started to laugh. They knew they had to clean up the mess. After cleaning, they both learned to share and be more careful with their food. And from that day, Tom and Lily always shared their snacks and became more generous with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a butterfly. The butterfly was very pretty and had many colors. 

Lily said, "Hello, butterfly! Can I play with you?" 

The butterfly said, "Yes, you can play with me. But I can't stay too long. I will melt if I stay in the sun too much." 

Lily said, "Oh no! I don't want you to melt. Let's go find some shade." 

They found a tree with lots of shade. The butterfly said, "Thank you for finding a shady spot for me. You are very kind." 

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome. I like to help insects when they need it. I have some water available if you're thirsty." 

The butterfly drank the water and then flew away. Lily was happy that she could help the butterfly. She went back to playing outside, feeling proud of herself for being kind to the little insect.

Once there was a lion who liked lollipops very much. He was different to other lions as he loved the sweet taste of lollipops.

Every day, he would go to the lollipop forest to find the biggest and tastiest lollipops. He made sure to get there before everyone else!

One day, something unusual happened. He found the biggest and yummiest lollipop ever! It was so big and sweet, he just had to roar with happiness.

He quickly grabbed the lollipop and ran away. The other animals were so surprised, they were all amazed at how the lion had found such an unusual lollipop.

The lion happily enjoyed his sweet lollipop and made sure he visited the lollipop forest again the next day.

Thomas was a young boy who loved to go outside and play. One day he was out in the park and he saw a long slide. He was so excited that he ran right over to it. He loved to slide down and it felt so fun.

After a few slides, Thomas noticed some other children playing near the slide too. One of them had a big toy car. Thomas walked over for a closer look, but the other kid did not want to share it. They started to fight and Thomas was sad.

Thomas's mom saw what was happening and quickly came over to him. She said that it was not nice to fight and took Thomas away from the slide. They went home and Thomas thought about what had happened for a long time.

In the end, Thomas learned that fighting was not the answer to his problems, and he decided to try and find other ways to solve them. He thought long and hard and finally realised that it was better to talk things out and be kind. And of course he still loves to go out and slide too.

Once there was a girl named Jennie. She loved to play with her toys and have fun. One day, Jennie went outside to play but she was feeling very fearful. She wanted to go back inside, but she was scared.

She saw a big, tall tree in the backyard and she decided to ignore her fear and go explore it. Jennie couldn't climb it, as it was too high and she was only a little girl. But she spent time looking at the leaves and twigs.

Suddenly, she heard a noise coming from a nearby bush. Jennie got very scared, but she ignored her fear and went closer. When she peeked in, she saw an animal was doing some work! He was building a house! 

Jennie was amazed and forgot about her fear. She watched the animal for a very long time and eventually went back inside to tell her family about what she had seen. 

Jennie learned that day that it is not always so bad to ignore her fear. Sometimes, when she does this, she finds something new and special and an adventure starts!

Sara was a nosy goat who liked to poke her horn into everything. She wanted to know what was inside every box, every bag, and every hole. She did not listen to her mom or dad, who told her to be careful and respectful.

One day, Sara saw a big shiny ball in the barn. It was glowing with many colors. Sara was very curious. She ran to the ball and tried to touch it with her horn. But the ball was not a ball. It was a bee hive!

As soon as Sara touched the hive, the bees came out and buzzed angrily. They stung Sara on her nose, her ears, and her tail. Sara cried out in pain and ran away. She looked for her mom and dad, who were grazing in the field.

Mom and dad saw Sara and ran to her. They licked her wounds and comforted her. They told her that the hive was not a toy, but a home for the bees. They said that Sara should not be so nosy and should respect other animals' things.

Sara learned her lesson. She apologized to the bees and to her mom and dad. She promised to be more careful and respectful. She also learned that some things that glow are not always good to touch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very hungry. She wanted a muffin to eat but there were none left. Her mom promised to make some more muffins for her. The little girl was happy and waited patiently for her mom to bake the muffins.

After a while, the muffins were ready and they smelled delicious! The little girl took a big bite and it tasted so good. She was no longer hungry and felt very happy. Her mom kept her promise and made her some yummy muffins to eat.

Once upon a time there was a young musician. She played her music in the park every day. The musician was very polite and she always smiled at everyone.

One day while she was playing, she saw a little girl who looked very sad. The musician asked her what was wrong and the little girl said that she was tired and her legs hurt.

So the musician took the little girl to a shady spot for her to rest. She lay down and almost immediately fell fast asleep. 

The musician sat with the little girl until she woke up. The little girl was feeling better, and thanked the musician for being so kind. The little girl said that she had been having a bad day, but lying in the park with the polite musician had really made her feel better. 

The musician said it was no problem and they both smiled. The little girl waved goodbye and the musician went back to playing her music.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big animal with a long neck. It is a giraffe.

"Wow, look at that!" Anna says. "It has a long, long neck. How can it eat the leaves?"

Ben says, "Maybe it can stretch its neck very high. Or maybe it can bend its neck very low. Let's go and see."

They run to the giraffe. The giraffe is friendly. It lowers its neck and lets them touch it. It feels soft and warm.

"Hello, giraffe," Anna says. "You have a nice neck. Can you tell us how you eat the leaves?"

The giraffe says, "I can eat the leaves in different ways. Sometimes I stretch my neck high and reach the top of the trees. Sometimes I bend my neck low and nibble the grass. Sometimes I eat the leaves that people give me. I like all kinds of leaves."

Anna and Ben are happy. They spend a long time with the giraffe. They give it some leaves and some water. They hug it and thank it.

"Goodbye, giraffe," they say. "We had fun with you. You are a good friend."

The giraffe says, "Goodbye, Anna and Ben. You are good friends too. Come and visit me again."

Anna and Ben wave to the giraffe. They go back to their parents. They tell them about the giraffe and its long neck. They say they want to see it again. Their parents smile and say they will.

Molly was walking through the forest. She was so excited, because she was looking for a special treat. She had heard that there might be some delicious cheese hidden in the trees.

Molly stopped to look up into the branches of the nearest tree. Then, she spotted it - a thick wedge of cheese! She couldn't believe her luck.

She reached up and tried to grab it, but it was too high. She tried again and again, but still no luck. All of her jumping and stretching wasn't doing the trick.

Molly sighed. Just then, a kind squirrel popped out of the tree and said, "Do you need help?"

Molly smiled and nodded. The squirrel kindly reached up and handed her the cheese.

Molly thanked the squirrel and said, "I knew there would be something special in this forest!"

The squirrel smiled and said, "You're welcome!"

Molly happily skipped away, munching on her thick slice of cheese.

Little Jimmy was so happy! He had won a shiny golden chain at the fair. He was so excited that he ran and showed his mama right away.

"Mama, I won a chain!" he cried.

"Jimmy, that's wonderful!" his mama said, as she hugged him tight.

Jimmy always wanted to win something, and today he did. Mama said that he had to be careful and keep the chain safe.

Just then, they heard a nasty growl coming from the doorway. It was Big Dog.

Big Dog was very ignorant; he didn't even understand the concept of winning. He tried to pounce at Jimmy, but Jimmy was so fast! He ran away holding the chain tightly.

Big Dog growled again, and ran after Jimmy.

But Jimmy was so good at running and was much faster than Big Dog. Jimmy was getting away!

Then he quickly hopped over a fence, and Big Dog could not get him. In the end, Jimmy kept his chain.

Jimmy was so proud of himself. He had won something and he kept it safe from Big Dog. What a great day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Milly who wanted to impress her mom. One day, Milly decided to make dinner all by herself. She worked very hard, and after a minute, dinner was ready! She called out to her mom to see what was for dinner. Her mom came in and was very impressed by Milly's work. She told Milly that dinner was amazing!

Milly was very happy and said, "Mommy, did I impress you?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Milly, you did! Now, let's shut the kitchen door and go eat dinner!"

Milly shut the door and they went to eat dinner together. She felt very proud of herself and was so happy that she had managed to impress her mom!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oatmeal for breakfast every day. One morning, her mom asked her to help organize the kitchen. Lily was happy to help and started to put things away in their proper places.

Suddenly, she saw a bag of oats on the counter. "Mommy, can we make oatmeal cookies?" Lily asked. "Sure, sweetie. That's a great idea," her mom replied gently.

Lily happily measured the oats and mixed them with the other ingredients. As they waited for the cookies to bake, Lily said, "I like organizing with you, Mommy. It's fun." Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you enjoy it. It's important to keep things tidy." 

When the cookies were done, Lily and her mom enjoyed them with a glass of milk. "These are delicious, Lily. You did a great job organizing and baking," her mom said. Lily beamed with pride and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I love spending time with you."

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Harry and Rory. One day, the two brothers were walking by the lake when they saw something floating on the lake - it was a raft.

Harry asked Rory, "What is that?"

Rory replied, "I think it is a raft."

Harry was excited and said, "Let's go see!"

So the two brothers went over to the raft. When they got close, they saw a big smiley face painted on the raft. They knew they were lucky!

The two brothers climbed onto the raft and began to paddle around the lake. It was so much fun! They even saw some ducks swimming around them.

After a while, the brothers decided it was time to go back home. But before they could get off the raft, Harry said, "Wait, I forgot something!"

Rory asked, "What did you forget?"

Harry said, "I found something on the raft!"

Rory looked around and could not find anything. But then Harry pulled out a big red ball from under the edge of the raft. It was a lucky find!

The two brothers waved goodbye to the raft and took the ball home. They had a lot of fun and they were so lucky to find the ball!

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to study many things. They study books, toys, animals and plants. They are very intelligent.

One day, they go to the store with Mom. Mom wants to buy some food and clothes. Lily and Tom want to buy some books and puzzles. They see a big shelf with many books and puzzles. They run to the shelf and look at them.

"Look, Tom, this book has many pictures of dinosaurs. I want to study dinosaurs. They are big and strong and have sharp teeth. Do you want to study dinosaurs too?" Lily asks.

"Yes, Lily, I want to study dinosaurs too. But I also want to study this puzzle. It has many pieces and colors. It looks fun and hard. Do you want to study this puzzle too?" Tom replies.

"OK, Tom, we can study both. Let's ask Mom if we can buy them. Maybe she will say yes. She likes when we study and learn new things. She says we are very intelligent." Lily says.

They take the book and the puzzle and go to Mom. They show her what they want to buy. Mom smiles and nods. She is proud of Lily and Tom. She says they are very intelligent and curious. She buys the book and the puzzle for them. They thank her and hug her.

They go home and study the book and the puzzle. They learn many things about dinosaurs and colors and shapes. They have fun and are happy. They are very intelligent.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jim. He was three years old and loved to swing. Every day he would go to the park and swing on the swing. He loved the feeling of the wind on his face and the way it made him go so high. 

Jim would close his eyes and imagine he was flying. As he was swinging, he heard a beautiful sound. He opened his eyes and saw a bright blue bird flying above him. The bird flew around the swing two times and then flew away. 

Jim started swinging again and he could still hear the sound of the bird. He felt so happy. The song of the blue bird was the best sound he had ever heard. He kept swinging until the sun went down. 

Jim knew he would never forget the beautiful blue bird and the sound it made as it flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a harmless little dog. His name was Spot. He loved to play and run around on the grassy hills near his house.

One day, Spot saw something really exciting - an ambulance! He didn't know what it was, but it looked like lots of fun. So, he chased after it.

Spot ended up running for such a long time that he got very tired and went to take a nap. But when he woke up, he had a surprise. A big ambulance had come to spoil his fun!

The ambulance gave him a check-up and made sure that he was still harmless and healthy. Then the ambulance drove away, taking Spot's new friend with it.

Spot was sad, but he knew that the ambulance was trying to help him. He was glad that he was harmless and healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Katrina. She loved fashion and always wore clothes with lots of color. She wanted to look like all the other kids, but her clothes were too expensive.

One day, Katrina was playing outside and saw a strange man. He had a big box and he said he could help her with her fashion problem. Katrina opened the box, and inside she found lots of colorful things.

The man told Katrina that he could twist the colorful things together and make beautiful fashion. She was very excited and they twisted the pieces together with some pretty ribbons to make some amazing clothes.

Katrina looked amazing with her new twisty clothes on. From then on, she would wear her twisty fashion whenever she went. Katrina was very happy, and everyone said she was the most fashionable girl ever!

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his best friend, a little girl named Lily. They played all day, every day. Spot liked to run and jump, and Lily liked to laugh and clap.

One day, Spot found something new in the yard. It was a box with a big bow on it. Spot knew it was a surprise for Lily. He insisted that Lily come outside to see it. Lily was so excited to find out what was in the box.

When Lily opened the box, she found a big, bouncy ball inside. Spot and Lily played with the ball all day long. They were so happy with their new toy. The surprise made Lily and Spot even more best friends than before.

Maggie was a little girl who loved to play outside. Today, she was trying to climb up a hill. With each step, she struggled, but she kept going. At the top of the hill was an enormous cone. Maggie felt a little nervous, but she took a deep breath and started climbing up the cone. 

Maggie was exhausted. Halfway up the cone she stopped to catch her breath. Suddenly she heard a voice calling her name. It was her mom. "Maggie! Come down from there! That cone is too high! You don't need to struggle so much!"

Maggie was relieved. She carefully scrambled down the cone and scrambled back down the hill. Her mom hugged her and said, "Let's go home and have an ice cream cone as a treat!"

Maggie smiled and nodded excitedly. After all her struggling, she was happy to do something easier.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She loved to look up and see the big impressive rainbow in the sky. Every day, she imagined she was an eagle, flying through the colourful sky and reaching the top of the rainbow.

One day, when her mommy and daddy weren't looking, she found a way to try and touch the rainbow. She climbed a tall tree, squeezed tight and jumped. She flew through the air as if she was an eagle, reaching out to try and grab the rainbow.

But sadly, she couldn't grab the rainbow. Instead, she felt the gentle sprinkle of the rain, falling down, and the rainbow disappeared. But when she looked up, the rainbow was still there, shining brightly like before.

The little girl smiled - she had been so close to touching the impressive rainbow. She thanked the sky for the magical rainbow and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a big cake in a cold kitchen. It was full of frosting and candies.

A little girl wanted to try it. She got down on the floor and started to crawl towards the cake. She was so excited!

When she reached the cake, she gave it a big poke. The frosting felt yummy! She licked it with her tongue and smiled. 

The little girl kept on crawling around the kitchen, looking for a spoon or fork to eat the cake. But she couldn't find anything. She was so sad!

Suddenly, she heard a voice from the doorway. It was her mom! She said "Don't worry little one, I have something for you." Her mom handed her a fork and a napkin so she could enjoy the cold cake.

The little girl was so happy! She ate the cake with the fork and enjoyed every delicious bite. 

The end.

John and Jack were best friends. One day they were playing at Jack's house. John saw a tray of snacks on the table, yummy cookies and colourful pieces of fruit.

John said "Can I have some?" but then Jack started to tease him. He said "No, you can't have any. It's all mine!"

John felt sad but then he saw some disgusting food on the tray. There was a slimy green potato and a smelly fish. John made a face and said "Ew, that's disgusting!"

Jack laughed and said "Okay, you can try the disgusting food - but only if you dare!" John was brave and he decided to take the tray and try the food. He thought it was really yucky but he was really proud that he didn't let Jack tease him. They both had a good laugh.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream more than anything in the world. One day, Timmy went to the ice cream store with his mom. He looked at all the different flavors and it was very difficult for him to choose just one.

Timmy's mom asked him, "Which flavor do you want, Timmy?"

Timmy looked up at his mom and said, "It's difficult to choose, but I want chocolate ice cream."

His mom smiled and said, "Good choice, Timmy. Chocolate is my favorite too!" They both enjoyed their delicious ice cream together and Timmy was very happy with his choice.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird liked to fly high in the sky. One day, the bird flew too high and got tired. It landed on a chest in the yard. The chest was big and brown. The bird rested on the chest and felt better. 

Soon, a cat came by. The cat wanted to catch the bird. But the bird was too fast and flew away. The cat was ignorant and didn't know the bird was too quick. The bird flew back to its nest and slept soundly.

Once upon a time, two brothers marched on a hot sunny day. The older brother was envious of his little brother's new toy, a toy truck. He wanted to play, too!

They both marched to the river. The little brother said, "Let's wash our hands in the river water since it's so hot today." The older brother thought it would be fun and, so, together, they washed their hands in the river water. 

The water felt cool and nice. They washed away the hot sun and it made them feel much better. After they were done, the brothers marched home.

The older brother was still envious of his little brother's toy truck, but he felt happy from playing in the water and being with his brother. They held hands and marched all the way home, happy and refreshed on the hot day!

It was a sunny day and two teddy bears, named Kelly and Jim, had just come home from the park. 

Kelly wanted to play with her toy cars, but Jim was interested in the bookshelf on the other side of the room. Kelly followed him to the empty bookshelf and tried to take it away from him. As soon as Jim saw this, he got angry and the two teddy bears started to fight. 

They scratched each other with their claws and knocked over books and other toys. In the end, Jim won the fight and took back the bookshelf. 

Kelly was sad but decided to make the best of the situation and helped Jim put the books back in the shelves. In the end they both hugged and made up with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a shiny red shoe on the ground. It was so pretty! She put it on her foot and it fit perfectly. 

Lily walked around with her new shoe and felt very happy. She saw some birds playing in the trees and decided to join them. They sang songs and flew around together. It was a peaceful moment. 

After playing with the birds, Lily went back home. She showed her mom the new shoe and they both smiled. Lily felt grateful for her fun day outside and her new shoe. She went to bed that night with a happy heart.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Alex. He was 3 years old and he loved playing outside in the garden.
One evening, while playing in the garden, Alex heard something in the bushes. It sounded quite strange. He stood still and listened.
Suddenly, out from the darkness hopped a small, brown bunny. Alex had never seen him from before. 
"Hi there" the little bunny said. "I was just looking for a pin in the bushes".
Alex was a little disturbed by the bunny, but he was also a little curious. 
"What do you need a pin for?" he asked the bunny.
The little bunny held up a ball of wool and said: "I want to hold the wool together, but I need a pin to do it".
Alex was now feeling less disturbed. He had seen his Mommy using pins when she sewed. So he reached down and picked up a pin from the ground.
He handed it to the bunny who smiled and thanked him. Then he hopped away back into the dark. 
Alex smiled and went back to playing in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny's friend, a squirrel named Sammy, came to him and said, "Benny, I got my license to climb trees! Let's celebrate!"

Benny was so happy for Sammy and said, "Yay! Let's have a party!" They invited all their friends and had a picnic under a big tree. They ate carrots and nuts and danced to music.

After the party, Benny and Sammy went for a walk in the forest. Benny noticed that Sammy was very persistent in climbing trees. He tried and tried until he finally made it to the top. Benny said, "Wow, Sammy! You're so good at climbing! I'm proud of you."

Sammy smiled and said, "Thanks, Benny! I worked hard to get my license and I'm happy I can climb trees now." Benny replied, "I'm happy too! Let's celebrate your success again soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a modest girl. She had the most wonderful dream of becoming a superhero. One day, she decided to go on a grand adventure.

She arrived in town, and everyone was so excited. When she saw a pistol, she knew it was time for her to start her journey. She was scared at first, but she was also brave. She grabbed the pistol and began her quest.

As she traveled, she looked for places to explore. She eventually arrived at a castle and she knew that this was the spot. She knocked on the door and a wizard answered.

"Hello. I'm here to save the world," the girl said confidently.

The wizard smiled. "That's very brave of you," he said. "But what do you plan to do with the pistol?"

"I'm going to use it to help me fight the monsters and defeat the bad guy," she said.

The wizard nodded in approval. "Very good. Go and save the world!"

The girl smiled and set off on her mission. She was modest, but with her new pistol, she was sure she could make a difference. And that is exactly what she did!

Once upon a time there was a flower who was very hungry. The flower was so small and quiet, but it was so beautiful. The petals of the flower were a deep pink color. Every day the flower looked around hoping to find food. 

One day, he noticed a butterfly with a big yellow tie. The flower watched as the butterfly flew close by. As the butterfly floated across, he accidentally dropped the tie. The flower was so excited! He quickly reached out with his stem and grabbed the tie. He used the tie to tie his stem to the ground.

The tie gave the flower all the food and water he needed to grow. The little flower bloomed and grew the prettiest petals ever seen. He glowed with happiness and thanked the butterfly. He was no longer hungry and could finally smile. From that day on, the tie was the flower's prize.

One day, Bob and his sister Sally decided to go for a ride. As they headed outside, they saw their mom discussing something with their dad. The conversation seemed serious. 

"What are they discussing?", asked Sally.

Bob looked alert as he answered, "I think they're talking about the motor in the car."

So Bob and Sally decided to have a look. When they reached the car, they saw a big motor inside! It was shiny and brightly coloured. Bob and Sally were very curious and asked their parents a lot of questions about the motor. 

Mom and dad were very happy to explain everything to the children and told them all about how the motor worked.

Bob and Sally were very pleased to learn all about the motor and thanked their parents before heading back inside to play.

Mia was so excited to decorate the house for Christmas. She had a big red Santa sack and she ran around gathering up all the decorations she wanted to use. First, she found a big red poinsettia flower and placed it on the mantel. Then, she found a big wide cane with green and red stripes. She held it up and shouted, "Mommy, look, a cane!" Mommy smiled and tied a big golden bow around the cane. Mia was delighted with the cane, and ran around showing it to everyone. 

Next, Mia and Mommy went on a hunt for more decorations. After searching through all the boxes, they found some big white snowflakes and hung them in the windows. Mia was very proud of their work â€” the house looked so cool!

At last, Mia and Mommy sat down in the warm glow of Christmas and admired all their hard work. Mia smiled at Mommy and said, "Mommy, our decorations make this house look really wide!" Mommy smiled and gave Mia a big hug.

Molly was so excited. Today was her first day of preschool! As she arrived she noticed a big picture on the wall. She wanted to take a closer look but she slipped on the way there. She felt embarrassed and a bit scared. She didn't know anybody yet, so she felt ignorant and alone. 

Suddenly she felt a gentle hand touch her shoulder. It was her teacher. She was so kind and understanding. She helped Molly get up and brought her closer to the picture. It was a painting of a big rainbow. Molly looked around and saw that everyone was enjoying the picture. She started to feel better and soon made friends with some of the other children. 

Molly realized that nobody was ignorant; they were all just getting to know each other! She was glad she decided to come to preschool and was even more excited to learn more!

Once upon a time, there was an important seed. The seed knew it was important, but it didn't know why. Every day, the seed would look around and wonder why it was so special. One day, an answer came. 

The seed heard a voice in the wind telling it that it must fit in the soil. The seed was scared, because it had never been to the soil before. But the voice was gentle and said that it would be ok. 

The seed now understood why it was important - it was meant to help the soil become more and more healthy. So the seed listened, and fit itself into the soil. 

After a few days, the seed started to grow. It grew bigger and bigger until the roots became strong and the leaves were thick and green! The soil had become healthier because the seed fit in. 

The seed was proud to be important, because it showed that it could help and make a difference. The seed knew that no matter what, it could always fit in somewhere.

Once there were two friends named Sue and Sam. They loved to spend time together and do fun things. Today they decided to go to the park. When they got there, they saw a fantastic playground with lots of things to do. 

First, they ran across the grass as fast as they could. Sue laughed and Sam smiled. Then they went on the swings. Sue went higher and higher and laughed with joy. Sam felt so comfortable and happy too. 

After that, they decided to go on the slide. They climbed up the ladder and went down the slippery slide at lightning speed. Both of them laughed and had a lot of fun. 

When it was time to go home, Sue and Sam said goodbye. They hugged and promised to come back to the park soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress that was pink and had flowers on it. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when her mom called her for lunch. Lily went to the kitchen and sat at the table. Her mom gave her a sandwich and a glass of milk. 

After lunch, Lily went outside to play. She saw a butterfly flying around and tried to catch it, but it flew away. Then, she saw a cat walking towards her. The cat had a graceful walk and a soft fur. Lily petted the cat and it purred happily. 

Later, Lily went back inside and saw her dad fixing the handle on the door. She asked him what he was doing and he said he was fixing the handle.
