Lily watched him for a bit and then went to play with her toys again. She was happy because she had a good lunch, played with a cat, and saw her dad fixing the handle.

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent kangaroo. His name was Sam. He was very friendly and he liked to jump around in the bush. One day, he went out to look for food. Suddenly, a big very mean animal appeared. It was a lion. 

The lion wanted to spoil Sam. He wanted to eat him! Sam was scared, but he thought of a clever plan. He ran away as fast as he could and he was too quick for the lion.

The lion got very angry. He couldn't believe how intelligent the kangaroo was. He then decided to spoil other kangaroos in the bush. He ran around and scared them all. 

Sam was sad. He saw the lion scaring the other kangaroos and he knew he couldn't do anything about it. He wished he had more power but he was just a kangaroo. So, Sam watched as the lion spoiled the other kangaroos. In the end he had to accept that the lion had the power and there was nothing he could do.

Once upon a time there was a very lucky waffle. He lived in a big happy town and everybody loved him. He was so happy, he wanted to marry. One day he saw a beautiful waffle who also wanted to marry. So they got married right away! 

The marriage made everyone in the town so excited. They all wanted to join in on the celebration! They put up decorations and made special waffles. Everybody was eating and having a good time.

The lucky waffle and his wife were so content. They both smiled and hugged each other. Everyone in the town was so happy they married.

The happy couple had a beautiful marriage. They were always together and were so in love. They were always encouraging each other. Everyone in the town was so happy for them, because they were so lucky!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ellie. Ellie was very curious. Everywhere she went she wanted to explore. One day she was walking in the forest and she saw something in the distance. It was a gray tent. Ellie walked over and pushed open the tent door. "Hello!" she said. She looked inside and there was someone sitting inside the tent. He was an old man.

The old man looked at Ellie with a smile. "Hello!" he said. "I'm Marco. Can I help you?" Ellie was stunned. She didn't know what to say! "I believe I'm lost," she finally answered.

Marco said, "That's okay. You can stay in my tent. I will show you the way back."

Ellie was so happy! She said, "Thank you! I believe you're very kind."

From then on, Ellie visited Marco every day and they went exploring together. They had lots of adventures. And Ellie always knew she could believe in Marco to show her the way.

John had a reliable birdcage. It was the perfect home for his little feathered friend. Every day, John would take good care of his pet by filling the birdcage with food and water. One day, John was feeling especially proud of his pet and wanted to show it off to the world. 

John asked his mom, "Mom, can we take my bird to the park?" His mom nodded in agreement and soon the two were on their way. 

At the park, John pointed at the different squawks and chirps coming from the birds in the trees. He could not believe how wonderful they looked in the sky. Suddenly, one of the birds flew into the birdcage and perched itself on the top of the reliable cage. John was so excited and quickly ran over to tell his mom, but when he returned to the birdcage, the little feathered friend was gone. 

John began to cry, and his mom could tell he was really distraught. She put her arm around John to comfort him, and then she pointed at the tree closeby. On one of the branches sat the little bird, looking back at them and chirping softly. 

John smiled and knew it was the same bird from his birdcage. He realized that he should look closer at things in the future and that his birdcage might not always be as reliable as he thought!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby gorilla. He lived in the jungle with his friends. One day, they wanted to play a game, but the gorilla disagreed with them. He wanted to eat some bananas instead. His friends were sad, but they understood. 

The gorilla went to look for some bananas. He searched and searched, but he couldn't find any. Suddenly, he saw a big tree with lots of bananas on it. He was so happy! He climbed up the tree and ate all the bananas he wanted. 

When he came back to his friends, they were happy to see him. They asked him why he disagreed with them earlier. The gorilla explained that he just wanted some bananas. His friends understood and they all played together happily. The end.

Once upon a time there was a huge book. The book was loved by a little girl named Sue. Every day she would give the book a huge hug.

One day, Sueâ€™s mommy gave her a pair of scissors. â€œYou can use these to cut,â€ her mom said.

Sue was so excited. She grabbed the scissors and ran straight to the huge book. Sue started cutting and cutting. She trimmed the pages into shapes, drew lines and designs. She was so proud of all the new shapes she made.

Suddenly, Sue heard someone calling her name. It was her mommy. â€œSue, why did you cut the book?â€ Mommy asked. She looked really mad.

Sue was scared, but she was brave to admit her mistake. â€œI wanted to make it look pretty,â€ she said. 

Mommy gave Sue a hug. â€œI know you meant well, but next time, you must ask permission before you cut anything, okay?â€ 

Sue nodded her head, and she and her mommy hugged the huge book together.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful king. He had a golden chain he wore around his neck. One day, the king was walking around his kingdom and he saw a special thimble. He knew he had to have it, so he sent his fastest messenger to get it.

The messenger galloped faster than ever before. He hopped over the hills and ran through the streets until he reached the thimble. He picked it up and put it in his pocket. Then he sent his horse back to the kingdom.

The king was so happy when the messenger returned with the thimble. He put it on the chain that hung around his neck and it looked beautiful. Now, the powerful king was the most powerful of all the kings in the kingdom!

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, mom asked them to watch the eggs in the pan while she went to get some bread. "Don't let them spoil," she said. "They will be yucky if they cook too long."

Lily and Tom nodded and stayed by the stove. They saw the eggs turn white and yellow in the hot pan. They smelled good and made a sizzling sound. Lily and Tom felt hungry and wanted to taste them.

"Can we have one?" Lily asked Tom.

"Maybe," Tom said. "But mom said not to spoil them."

Lily reached for the pan handle, but it was very hot. She burned her hand and cried out. Tom tried to help her, but he bumped the pan and spilled the eggs on the floor. They made a big mess.

Mom heard the noise and came back to the kitchen. She saw the eggs and the pan and the twins. She was very grumpy. "What did you do?" she asked. "You spoiled the eggs and the pan and the floor!"

Lily and Tom felt sorry and scared. They said they were sorry and they wanted to help. Mom sighed and hugged them. She said she was not mad, but they had to be careful and listen. She said they could have some bread and jam instead of eggs. Lily and Tom said thank you and helped mom clean the mess. They learned not to touch the hot pan and to watch the eggs. They still liked to help in the kitchen, but they waited for mom to say when.

Once there was a good squirrel. She was looking for something to do. Then she had an idea. She decided to bake something. She searched for materials and found some flour, eggs and butter. She mixed them together and put them in the oven. She waited and waited until finally it was done. She took it out and it smelled so good. She was so proud of what she had made. She enjoyed eating it and shared it with her friends. Everyone was so happy and thanked the squirrel for making them something so good.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree with high branches. A little bird lived on the tree. The little bird loved to sing and play with his friend, the squirrel.

One day, the squirrel found a cup of coffee on the ground. He asked the little bird, "What is this?" The little bird said, "I don't know. It smells good, but it might be sharp." The squirrel wanted to taste it, but the little bird stopped him. "We should not try things we don't know," said the little bird.

The squirrel listened to his friend and left the coffee alone. They went back to playing and singing. They learned that it's good to be careful and listen to friends. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a kid who loved adventures. He never stayed still. One day he decided to kick his heels and jump around. He loved kicking his heels and feeling the wind. He jumped higher and higher. He felt so alive and free. He was having the greatest adventure ever.

After a while he realized he should slow down. He had been kicking his heels for a long time. He was getting tired but he had a big smile on his face. He was so happy about his adventurous day!

He started walking back home. He got to the door and he kicked his heels one last time. He jumped up and said: "Adventure time is over". And he went to bed with a dream of having more adventures.

One day, Tommy and his Daddy were playing in the garden.
 Daddy had an enormous task to do in the garden, scattering the seeds. He spread out a pile of seeds on the ground. 

Tommy said to Daddy, "What are you doing?"

Daddy said, "I'm scattering the seeds so that flowers can grow in the garden."

Tommy asked, "Can I help?"

Daddy said, "Sure! We'll scatter the seeds together!"

Together, Daddy and Tommy scattered the seeds all over the garden. It was an enormous task, but they were having lots of fun. When they finished, Daddy smiled and said, "We did it! Now it's time for lunch."

Tommy and Daddy went into the house for lunch, proud of the enormous task they had accomplished together.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Daisy. Daisy loved playing in the park and playing with her friends. One day, Daisy was playing in the park and her friends had a kite, which looked so fun!

Daisy's friends asked her: "Do you want to fly the kite with us?"

Daisy was so excited and said, "Yes, of course!"

Together they flew the kite and it was so much fun. Daisy felt so happy, but at the same time she was a bit scared, because the wind made the kite go so high!

Suddenly, the wind stopped and the kite fell down. Everyone was scared and Daisy felt her heart beating so fast.

But luckily, the kite was alright and Daisy and her friends were so relieved.

The next morning, Daisy went back to the park and flew her own kite. She felt so brave and happy and the wind was so gentle. Daisy flew her kite until the sun went down and she was so proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent dog named Max. Max was a very smart dog who could do many tricks. One day, Max went for a walk in the park with his owner, a little girl named Sue.

While they were walking, they saw a muffin on the ground. Max looked at the muffin and started to tremble. He was very hungry and wanted to eat the muffin. Sue saw Max tremble and knew he was hungry, so she picked up the muffin and gave it to Max.

Max was very happy to eat the muffin. He wagged his tail and licked Sue's hand to say thank you. Sue and Max continued their walk in the park, feeling happy and full. They played together until it was time to go home. And from that day on, Max knew that Sue would always take care of him.

Jane was playing in the park one day with her net. She found a friendly butterfly that was fluttering around. She was so excited and tried to catch it with her net. She smiled and said to the butterfly, "Please don't be scared, I won't hurt you." 

Butterfly replied, "I'm not scared, I'm just enjoying the sun and the warm breeze today." 

Jane replied, "Please can I catch you? I would love to show you to my friends." 

Butterfly said, "Yes, please do catch me! I would like to meet your friends." 

So Jane used the net to catch the friendly butterfly. She was so happy to have caught such a pretty creature. She brought the butterfly to show her friends and they were all so excited. Everyone couldn't believe that Jane had caught such a beautiful butterfly. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to climb trees. One day, she climbed a tall tree and saw her home from the top. She was happy because her home looked so small and cute. 

Sally's mom called her for dinner. Sally started to climb down the tree, but the branch broke and she fell down. She hurt herself badly and started to cry. Her mom saw her and took her home. 

Sally's mom cleaned her wounds and put a bandage on them. Sally felt better, but she was sad because she couldn't climb trees anymore. She said to her mom, "I want to climb again!" Her mom said, "No, Sally. It's too dangerous. You need to stay home and keep yourself dry." Sally was sad, but she knew her mom was right.

Once upon a time, there was a small red planet in the sky. It was full of secrets and adventures.

One day, an explorer wanted to find out what was hidden there. So the explorer went to find a key to unlock the planet.

The explorer searched and searched and finally found the key. They were so excited! The explorer grabbed the key and ran to the planet.

When they reached it, the explorer quickly put the key in the door and unlocked it. Suddenly, a magical world was revealed!

The explorer smiled and went for an adventure in the red planet. They had so much fun! And their exploration was only the beginning.

Tommy likes to play with his rubber ball. He can bounce it, throw it, and catch it. He has fun with his ball every day.

One day, Tommy wants to try something new. He sees a big hill near his house. He thinks it would be fun to roll his ball down the hill and see how far it goes. He runs to the hill with his ball.

He puts his ball on the top of the hill and gives it a push. The ball starts to roll down the hill very fast. Tommy runs after it, but he cannot catch it. The ball goes faster and faster, and Tommy gets tired.

The ball reaches the bottom of the hill and keeps rolling. It rolls into a pond. The pond is cold and deep. Tommy stops at the edge of the pond and looks at his ball. He is sad. He cannot get his ball back.

Then he sees a duck. The duck is swimming in the pond. The duck sees the ball and swims to it. The duck picks up the ball with its beak and brings it to Tommy. Tommy is happy. He thanks the duck and takes his ball. He hugs his ball and smiles.

Tommy learned something new. He learned that rolling his ball down the hill is not a good idea. He also learned that ducks are nice and can help. He decides to play with his ball in his yard instead. He succeeds in having fun with his ball and making a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved music and wanted to play the violin. Her mommy and daddy promised to buy her one. 

One day, they went to a music store and saw a shiny, brown violin. Lily was so happy! She tried to play it, but it made a screeching sound. Her mommy and daddy said they would answer her prayers and get her lessons.

After a few weeks of practice, Lily played a beautiful song on her violin. Her mommy and daddy were so proud! They celebrated with a spicy dinner. Lily realized that practicing and patience paid off.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw and cut paper with his scissors. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a new pair of scissors. They were shiny and sharp, unlike his old, dirty ones. Timmy was very happy and hoped to make many new art projects with them.

Timmy's little sister, Lily, also liked to play with scissors. But she was too little and might hurt herself. So Timmy promised to always keep his scissors away from Lily. He hoped she would understand.

One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. They made paper airplanes and cut out pictures from magazines. But Timmy's friend accidentally dropped the scissors on the ground and they got dirty. Timmy was sad, but he knew he could clean them and make them shiny again. He hoped his friend would be more careful next time. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sally. She was very honest and she loved taking pictures with her camera. 
One day Sally and her family went on a trip to a far away place. The moment they arrived, Sally immediately unpacked her camera so she could take pictures. 
Sally was so excited about all the new things she could take pictures of. She quickly moved around the area, taking picture after picture. 
However, when Sally returned to her family's house, she realized her camera was missing. She had been so eager to take pictures that she had forgotten to unpack her camera from her suitcase. 
Sally was sad and heartbroken, but she had learned an important lesson about being honest and responsible. Even if it means something bad happens in the end.

Once upon a time there was a squirrel who lived in the woods. He was fit and strong and he loved the forest. He was often seen scurrying around the trees and frolicking in the meadow.

One day, he saw something he had never seen before - a school. He watched the children playing and enjoying themselves and wondered what was going on.

The next day, the squirrel found his way inside and saw the children learning. He was curious, so he decided to stay and learn too. The children taught him all kinds of things, like how to read and write, and he was getting smarter every day.

The squirrel soon became the best student in the entire school. He amazed all the other children with his knowledge and they were very proud.

The squirrel had become fit and clever. He had learned all kinds of new things and he had made a lot of friends. He was so happy that he decided to stay in the school and learn even more.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big tree and wanted to build a nest in it. But Tweety didn't have a saw to cut the branches.

Tweety asked a squirrel, "Do you have a saw? I need to cut some branches to build a nest." The squirrel replied, "I don't have a saw, but I can help you find one."

Tweety felt anxious because it was getting dark and she needed to build her nest before it got too late. Suddenly, the squirrel came back with a saw and helped Tweety cut the branches. Tweety was so happy and said, "Thank you, squirrel! Now I can build my nest and sleep safely tonight." And with that, Tweety flew back to the tree and built her cozy nest.

One day, a little girl named Becky decided to take a walk around the park. As she walked, she looked up at the sky, but it was a little too cloudy. She let out a big sigh.

Becky was feeling a little sick and she was worried. She had a thermometer with her so she could take her temperature. Sure enough, the thermometer showed that her temperature was mild.

Although the thermometer made her feel a little better, Becky was still worried. She needed to find something to make her better!

Suddenly, Becky saw a big bush filled with some kind of berry. She put a few of them in a bag and took them home.

Back home, Becky washed the berries and ate them. She felt much better!

The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends. They were intelligent because they both knew a lot. One friend had a very smooth texture, like a fluffy cloud. The other friend had a rough texture, like a tree trunk.

Whenever these two friends got together, they would have lots of fun. They would play games, run around, and tell each other funny stories. They would also have long conversations, talking about their adventures and the things they had seen.

The two friends were so intelligent that, over the years, they learned about an amazing secret. No one else knew about it, so they kept it a secret between them. They had so much fun exploring this secret together.

No matter what happened, these two friends always had each other. And that made them both very happy.

Mia and Leo are best friends. They like to play together every day. Sometimes they play with toys, sometimes they play with books, and sometimes they play with their bodies. They like to do yoga.

Yoga is when you make shapes with your body. You can be a cat, a snake, a tree, or anything you want. Yoga makes you feel good and strong. Mia and Leo learned yoga from their teacher, Ms. Rose.

One day, Mia and Leo decided to do yoga in the park. They found a nice spot under a big tree. They laid down their mats and started to make shapes. They were very quiet and focused.

"Look, I'm a lion," Leo whispered to Mia. He opened his mouth wide and roared softly.

"I'm a butterfly," Mia whispered back. She flapped her wings and smiled.

They did more shapes and had fun. They felt powerful and happy.

Then they heard a loud noise. It was a dog. A big, black dog. It was running towards them. It looked angry and scary.

Mia and Leo were afraid. They jumped up and ran to the tree. They hugged each other and hoped the dog would go away.

"Shh, don't make a sound," Mia whispered to Leo.

"Maybe it will leave us alone," Leo whispered to Mia.

They closed their eyes and breathed slowly. They tried to be calm and brave.

The dog came closer and closer. It sniffed their mats and their shoes. It barked and growled.

But then, something happened. Ms. Rose came to the park. She saw the dog and the children. She knew what to do.

She walked up to the dog and said, "Hey, boy, what are you doing here? You're not supposed to be here. Come on, let's go home."

She reached out her hand and touched the dog's head. The dog stopped barking and growling. It wagged its tail and licked her hand. It followed her to the gate.

Mia and Leo opened their eyes and saw Ms. Rose. They were so happy and relieved. They ran to her and hugged her.

"Thank you, Ms. Rose, you saved us," Mia said.

"You're amazing, Ms. Rose, you're so powerful," Leo said.

Ms. Rose smiled and hugged them back. She said, "You're welcome, my little yogis. You're powerful too. You did a great job staying calm and quiet. I'm proud of you."

They walked back to their mats and packed their things. They said goodbye to the park and the tree. They said thank you to Ms. Rose again.

They went home with their teacher, feeling good and strong. They learned a new lesson that day. Yoga is not only fun, but also helpful. It can help you face your fears and find your power.

Lila and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pile of snow in the park. They ran to the snow and started to make a snowman.

"Let's make him a hat and a scarf," Lila said. "And a nose and eyes and a mouth."

"OK," Ben said. "I have a hat and a scarf in my bag. And I have some buttons and a carrot."

They put the hat and the scarf on the snowman's head and neck. They used the buttons for the eyes and the mouth. They used the carrot for the nose.

"Look, he is so cute!" Lila said. "But he needs something else. Something orange."

"Like what?" Ben asked.

"Like this!" Lila said. She picked up an orange from her bag and threw it at the snowman.

"Hey, don't do that!" Ben said. "That's not nice. That's my orange. I was going to eat it."

But it was too late. The orange hit the snowman and broke into pieces. The pieces fell on the snow and made it look dirty.

"Oops," Lila said. "I'm sorry. I didn't mean to make a mess. I just wanted to make him more colorful."

"Well, you didn't," Ben said. "You made him worse. And you wasted my orange. That was not a good thing to do."

Lila felt bad. She realized she had been selfish and rude. She wanted to make it up to Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben," she said. "I was wrong. I should have asked you first. And I should have been more careful. Can you forgive me?"

Ben looked at Lila. He saw that she was sincere and sorry. He decided to be kind and forgiving.

"It's OK, Lila," he said. "I forgive you. But next time, please think before you act. And don't throw things at people or things. That can hurt them or ruin them."

Lila nodded. She learned her lesson. She hugged Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. And so is our snowman. Even if he is not orange."

They smiled and played with the snowman. They made him an icy heart and gave him a hug. They hoped he would stay for a long time. They were happy.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat lunch. But Mom said they had to wait. She was making a tasty thing in the oven.

"What is it, Mom?" Lily asked.

"It's a surprise, sweetie. You'll see soon," Mom said.

Lily and Ben looked at the oven. They smelled something good. They heard a beep.

"Is it ready, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Not yet, honey. The oven says we have to delay a little more. It needs more time to cook," Mom said.

Lily and Ben sighed. They were very hungry. They went to the living room. They played with their toys. They tried to forget about the tasty thing.

But they could not. They kept looking at the clock. They kept hearing the oven. They kept smelling the food.

Finally, Mom called them. "Lunch is ready, kids! Come and see what I made!"

Lily and Ben ran to the kitchen. They saw a big thing on the table. It was round and brown and cheesy. It had slices of tomato and ham on top.

"It's a pizza!" Lily and Ben shouted.

"Yes, it is! I made it for you. Do you like it?" Mom asked.

"We love it, Mom! Thank you!" Lily and Ben said.

They sat down and ate the pizza. It was very tasty. They forgot about the delay. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom took her to the park to play. While they were there, Lily saw a big pile of shoes. She walked over to them and picked up a shoe. It was very smelly!

Lily's mom asked her if she wanted to keep the smelly shoe, but Lily had to decide. She thought about it for a moment and then shook her head no. She put the shoe back on the pile and ran off to play.

As they were leaving the park, Lily's mom asked her if she had fun. Lily replied with a big smile, "Yes, I had fun! But I didn't want the smelly shoe." They both laughed and went home happy. The end.

Tommy was very happy. His birthday was soon. He wanted to invite his friends to his party. He asked his mom for help.

"Mom, can I invite Sam and Lily and Ben and Anna to my party?" he said.

"Of course, my dear. You can invite whoever you want. It's your special day," his mom said.

"Can I invite Aunt Lucy too?" he said.

His mom frowned. She did not like Aunt Lucy. Aunt Lucy was ignorant. She always said mean things to Tommy and his mom. She did not know how to be nice.

"Tommy, I don't think Aunt Lucy would enjoy your party. She doesn't like fun things. She likes to sit and complain. She might make you and your friends unhappy," his mom said.

"But she is my aunt. She is family. Maybe she will be happy if I invite her. Maybe she will be nice to me," Tommy said.

His mom sighed. She loved Tommy very much. She wanted him to be happy. She did not want to hurt his feelings.

"Okay, Tommy. If you really want to invite Aunt Lucy, you can. But don't be sad if she doesn't come or if she is rude. You have many other people who love you and who will celebrate with you," his mom said.

Tommy smiled. He hugged his mom. He was excited for his party. He hoped Aunt Lucy would come and be nice. He hoped she would learn how to have fun. He hoped she would not be ignorant anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her mommy's makeup. One day, Lily's mommy said, "Lily, can you hold this soft brush for me?"

Lily held the brush carefully and watched as her mommy put on her makeup. "Mommy, can I have some makeup too?" Lily asked.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Sure, I'll put some soft lipstick on you." Lily felt happy and proud as she showed off her pretty pink lips to her daddy.

From that day on, Lily loved holding the soft makeup brushes for her mommy and even got to wear a little bit of makeup herself. She felt like a grown-up and loved spending time with her mommy.

There was once a brave girl named Laura. She had a big decision to make and she was feeling very unsure. She had heard about the power of wisdom but wasn't sure if she should surrender to it. 

She took a deep breath and thought about it. She knew that some tough choices come with wisdom and she was afraid. She was afraid of failing and feeling ashamed. She asked for help and listened to the advice from the people she trusted. 

Finally, after a lot of thought, she decided to surrender to the wisdom. She closed her eyes and took a deep breath. When she opened them again she felt strong and ready for what came next. With courage and bravery, she began her journey and soon her courage was rewarded. 

Laura discovered that by surrendering to the wisdom she had learned amazing things. She felt strong and free and no longer felt ashamed. She learned that surrendering to wisdom was an act of courage and bravery. She shared her newfound wisdom with others and soon they too felt strong and free.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved to listen to the birds sing in the sky. But one day he heard something different.

It was like the sound of water pouring out of a pipe. He thought it was interesting but he couldn't figure out where it was coming from.

So he started to listen harder as he walked around his neighborhood. He looked under bushes and in the trees, but he couldn't find the sound.

Finally, he looked up in the sky and spotted it! High up in the sky was a pipe spraying water from one end. As he watched the water danced through the air.

He thought it was the most interesting thing he had ever seen. So each day he would make sure to listen for the sound of the pipe and watch the water twirl around in the sky.

Sammy the Rabbit was so flexible. He could bend his head. One day, he went to the forest to find some fun. But then he heard a big noise and he got scared. He closed his eyes and his body started to disappear. His head was still there but the rest of his body had vanished.

He ran back to his house and asked his mama what had happened. She said it was magic, and that he could hide away anytime he wanted. Sammy thought this was great. He kept practising his magic disappearing trick until he got really good at it.

He would often disappear when he was feeling shy or scared, and come back when he was ready. He loved his magic power, and enjoyed learning more about it. From then on, Sammy was never scared as he could use his magic to hide away.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and he loved to play. One day he saw a big truck outside and he went over to take a look. He asked the driver, "What are you loading into the truck?" The driver smiled and said, "I'm loading an opera." 

Jack was very curious. He asked, "What's an opera?" The driver said, "It's a type of high singing. The voice is loud and beautiful. Would you like to hear it?"

Jack said "Yes", so the driver opened the door of the truck and played a recording of the opera. The sound was so beautiful that Jack could not believe his ears! He said, "Wow! That's so high. I want to do that too!" 

The driver smiled and said, "You can learn to sing opera if you practice. Let's go get you started!" Jack was so excited and the driver took him away to learn the beautiful opera music.

Once upon a time there was a open post. One day, something special happened. A big monster appeared! It had big eyes, and three horns. The monster was very scary.

Everyone ran away from the monster, but one brave boy. He stepped forward bravely. He smiled at the monster and said hello.

The monster smiled back and gave him an open post. Inside the post was a special gift. The boy opened the post and found a magical toy. He was so happy!

The monster smiled and said goodbye. Then it suddenly disappeared! The boy kept the post and the toy safe. He was sure to remember this special day forever.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside. One sunny day, she saw something shine in the grass. She went to look and found a small box. Inside the box, there was a treasure. The treasure was a pretty necklace with a shiny stone.

Lily wanted to keep the treasure, but she knew her friend, Tom, had lost his necklace. She thought about how sad he was. Lily decided to give the necklace back to Tom. Tom was very happy and smiled. The weather was mild, so they played outside all day.

At the end of the day, Lily felt good for helping her friend. She learned that being kind and giving makes you happy too. The moral of the story is that sharing and caring for others is a true treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a pretty mirror in her room. She loved to look at herself in the mirror and make funny faces. One day, Mia's mirror fell down and broke. Mia was very sad and hurt.

Mia's dad saw how sad she was. He wanted to help her. He said, "Don't worry, Mia. I will fix your mirror." Mia's dad took the broken mirror and went to his workshop. Mia waited and hoped her dad could fix it.

After some time, Mia's dad came back with the mirror. He had fixed it! Mia was so happy. She hugged her dad and said, "Thank you for fixing my mirror." Now Mia could look at herself and make funny faces again. She was very happy, and her hurt went away.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little girl named Lily. She had a pretty skirt that she loved to wear. It was her favorite skirt. Lily wanted to show her skirt to her best friend, Tim.

One sunny day, Lily put on her pretty skirt and went to Tim's house. Tim saw Lily's skirt and said, "Wow, your skirt is so nice!" Lily felt very happy that Tim liked her skirt.

Lily and Tim played all day in the park, showing their friends the pretty skirt. Everyone thought Lily's skirt was very charming. At the end of the day, Lily and Tim went home, tired but happy. They had a great day showing off the pretty skirt.

Once there were two friends, a puppy and a kitten. They were adorable. One day, the puppy wanted to go on an adventure. He asked the kitten to come along, and so they began to follow a trail.

They walked for a long time, until they came to a beautiful lake. The puppy started to swim, but the kitten wanted to see what else was in the lake. She picked up a thermometer, attached to a buoy.

The puppy swam back and tried to explain to the kitten that the thermometer was used to measure the temperature of the lake. The kitten thought it was a funny game, so she kept the thermometer and they decided to follow the buoy, which seemed to be leading somewhere.

The buoy led them to a dock with a boat. They got in the boat and began to explore the lake. The kitten was still playing with the thermometer, laughing as she watched the numbers go up and down.

The puppy and the kitten had a wonderful time exploring the lake. They enjoyed all the sights, sounds, and smells of the lake. When it was time for them to go home, the puppy carefully placed the thermometer back on the buoy so that others could come and explore the lake too. 

The puppy and the kitten became the best of friends from their adventure, and their memories of the lake were adorable.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, their mom gave them a big purple gift to share. She said, "This is a special gift for both of you. You have to yield and take turns with it, okay?"

Sara and Ben nodded and thanked their mom. They opened the gift and saw a shiny purple bike. They both wanted to ride it first. Sara said, "I want to go first, I am older by two minutes." Ben said, "No, I want to go first, I am bigger by two inches." They started to fight and pull the bike.

Their mom heard them and came back. She said, "Stop fighting, you two. You have to yield and take turns with the bike, or I will take it away." Sara and Ben said, "Sorry, mom." They decided to flip a coin to see who would go first. Sara won the coin toss and got to ride the bike first.

She put on her helmet and rode the bike around the yard. She felt happy and proud. She did not want to yield and let Ben have a turn. She said, "This is my bike, I won the coin toss. You can wait." Ben felt sad and angry. He said, "That is not fair, you have to yield and let me have a turn. Mom said so." Sara said, "No, I don't. Go away." She rode the bike faster and faster.

She did not see the big rock in her way. She hit the rock and fell off the bike. She hurt her knee and cried. The bike was broken too. Ben ran to help her. He said, "Are you okay, Sara?" Sara said, "No, I am not. I hurt my knee and the bike is broken. Mom will be mad at us." Ben said, "I am sorry, Sara. I wish you had yielded and let me have a turn. Maybe we could have avoided the rock." Sara said, "I am sorry too, Ben. I was selfish and greedy. I should have yielded and let you have a turn. Maybe we could have enjoyed the bike together."

Their mom came and saw what happened. She said, "Oh, no. What did you do, Sara and Ben? You broke the bike and hurt yourselves. You did not yield and take turns with the gift, did you?" Sara and Ben said, "No, mom. We did not. We are sorry, mom." Their mom said, "I am sorry too, Sara and Ben. You have to learn to yield and share with each other, or you will lose what you have and hurt yourselves and others. The bike was a gift, not a prize. You have to be grateful and generous, not selfish and greedy. Do you understand?" Sara and Ben said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We will try to do better next time."

The moral of the story is: You have to yield and share with others, or you will lose what you have and hurt yourselves and others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing outside. She would run around in the grass and pick flowers. One day, she saw an elderly lady struggling to carry her groceries.
