Once upon a time, there was a playful kitten named Mittens. Mittens loved to play with yarn and chase bugs. One day, Mittens went to visit her aunt who lived by a big lake. 

Mittens saw some ducks swimming in the lake and wanted to play with them. She decided to dive into the water to say hello. Mittens' aunt was watching and was very proud of her playful niece.

After playing with the ducks, Mittens went back to her aunt's house for some milk and cookies. Mittens had a fun day with her aunt and couldn't wait to come back and play again. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant oyster. It lived in the sea with many other oysters. Each day it was filled with joy and it loved to play and explore with its friends. 
One day, the oyster decided to clean its shell. It wanted to make sure it was shiny and sparkly. So, it scraped and scrubbed with all of its might. It worked so hard that it was soon finished and its shell was the shiniest in the sea. Everyone admired its brilliant shell.
The oyster was so happy with its work. From that day on, it always kept its shell clean and sparklyâ€”just like a brilliant oyster should.

John was a little boy who liked to dress in his best clothes. He had a special shirt, pants and shoes. He loved putting them on and showing them off.

John and his mom went to the beach one day. John was so glad when he saw the beautiful view. He ran up to the shore, jumping with joy.

John's mom said, "There's a nice breeze. You should put on your special clothes, John."

"Ok, mom," John said. He went back to the beach blanket, pulled out his clothes and started to dress. When he was finished, he spun around, twirling in circles. His mom smiled.

"You look so handsome, John," she said.

John smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, mom!" He felt so happy in his special clothes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very nervous to go on a big airplane ride with her mommy and daddy. When they got on the airplane, Lily sat in her seat and held onto her mommy's hand very tight. She hoped that the airplane ride would be over soon.

As the airplane took off, Lily's tummy felt funny, but she tried to be brave. She looked out the window and saw the clouds and the sun. It was very pretty! Lily's mommy gave her a snack and some juice, which made her feel better. She hoped that the airplane ride would be fun after all.

After a little while, the airplane landed safely and Lily was so happy! She had a great time on her first airplane ride and she wasn't nervous anymore. She hoped that she could go on another airplane ride soon! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she went to the park with her mom. They sat on a bench and watched the birds. Suddenly, Lily felt something on her arm. It was a little bug! She started to panic and waved her arms around. Her mom quickly tapped the bug away. Lily felt relieved and hugged her mom. 

After a while, they decided to go home. Lily was thirsty and wanted some water. But when she took a sip, she realized her throat was dry. She asked her mom for more water, but her mom said they had to wait until they got home. Lily felt sad, but she knew her mom was right. They walked home together, holding hands. When they finally got home, Lily drank a big glass of water and felt much better.

Once upon a time there was a war. It was a very big war and very noisy too. The people in the war were very unhappy. They felt dizzy in the heat of the day.

One day, some people had a bright idea. They decided to make it rain. They opened a giant door in the sky and the rain came pouring down. Everyone was relieved by the coolness of the rain.

The rain stopped after a while and the sun came out again. Little droplets of water were everywhere and everything was wet. The people rushed to dry off with towels and clothes. Everyone was so busy getting dry they forgot all about the war. 

At night, under the sparkly stars, the people were happy. They were cool, dry, and safe. They held hands and smiled to each other. They were thankful to be so dizzy with happiness. 

The war was over and the people never had to worry about it again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, pink cat. This cat had a funny mustache. The cat loved to play with a ball. One day, the ball went far away. The cat wanted to reach the ball.

The cat tried to reach the ball, but it was too far. The cat looked around for help. A small dog saw the cat and wanted to help. The dog had a long stick. The dog used the stick to reach the ball.

The cat was happy to have the ball back. The cat and the dog played together with the ball. They became good friends. The pink cat's funny mustache made the dog laugh. They had a fun day playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden with her toys. One day, she found a bean in the dirt. It was small and brown and looked funny. 

Lily decided to plant the bean in the ground and water it every day. She hoped it would grow big and strong like the trees in the park. But the bean struggled to grow. It was too small and weak. 

Lily felt sad, but she didn't give up. She kept watering the bean and talking to it every day. And slowly, the bean started to grow taller and taller. It was still funny-looking, but Lily didn't mind. She was happy that the bean was growing and getting stronger.

Once upon a time there was a strong kite with bright colors. It loved to sing in the wind! It was so tough it never got broken.

One day a little boy wanted to fly the kite in the sky. He was so excited! He grabbed hold of the kite tightly and ran and sang as it flew.

The kite soared higher and higher and sang louder too. The little boy laughed and cheered louder and louder as the kite flew and sang higher in the sky.

As the kite flew away, the little boy and the kite sang one last song together. They both said goodbye as the kite flew away into the clouds.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. Sometimes they share, sometimes they disagree.

One day, they find a telephone in the closet. It is old and has buttons and a cord. Lily wants to play with it. She says, "I am a doctor. I need the telephone to talk to my patients."

Ben disagrees. He says, "No, I am a firefighter. I need the telephone to call for help. There is a fire in the kitchen."

They both pull the telephone. The cord breaks. The telephone falls on the floor. It makes a loud noise.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the closet. She sees the broken telephone and the wet carpet. She asks, "What happened here?"

Lily and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We disagreed about the telephone. We broke it. We spilled the water."

Mom is not happy. She says, "You should not disagree so much. You should not break things. You should not make a mess. You need to clean up and say sorry to each other."

Lily and Ben nod. They hug each other and say sorry. They help Mom clean up. They learn to play nicely. They do not disagree anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. One evening, Timmy's mom asked him to eat his vegetables. Timmy refused and said he didn't like them. His mom was sorry that Timmy didn't like his vegetables, but she said he had to eat them to be healthy. Timmy still refused and started to cry. His mom hugged him and said she loved him, but he still had to eat his vegetables. Timmy finally agreed and ate his vegetables. He felt better and his mom was happy. The end.

Once there was an old man who loved spicy food. Every morning he called out his window and shouted "I love spicy food!" 

The old man's neighbor, a 3 year old girl named Sally, heard him every day. She loved spicy food too, but she was never brave enough to tell him.

One day, Sally mustered up the courage to call to the old man out her window. She yelled "I love spicy food too!"

The old man was so surprised. He called back "Do you really?". Sally replied "Yes, I do!"

The old man was so happy to hear that Sally liked spicy food, too. He called her over, and the two of them shared a big, spicy meal together. From that day forward, the old man and Sally were friends. And every time they ate spicy food, they thought of the wonderful day they met.

Ryan and his Dad were in the car. Ryan was asking lots of questions.

â€œDaddy, where are we going?â€

â€œWeâ€™re driving to the hospital. Remember, you have to go for an x-ray.â€

â€œCan we drive fast?â€ asked Ryan.

â€œNo, not today. We have to go slow because you are feeling sleepy.â€

They drove for another 30 minutes until they reached their destination.

When they arrived, Ryan and his Dad went inside the hospital to get the x-ray. After they had finished, they got back into the car and drove home. 

On the way, Ryan was feeling much more awake, and he asked his Dad if they could drive faster.

â€œSure, we can go faster now,â€ Dad replied with a smile. 

And so Dad quickly drove home and the two of them had the best ride ever!

Once upon a time, there was a man who had no hair on his head. He was bald. He liked to walk around with his cane. One day, he saw a little boy who wanted to poke him with a stick. The man said, "Please don't poke me with that stick. It's not nice." The little boy said sorry and gave the man a flower instead. The man smiled and thanked the little boy. From then on, they became friends and walked together with the man's cane.

Tara was a three-year-old who loved to explore. She was out in the garden in her backyard when she stumbled across an ancient door. Every day she went to the door and opened it, but nothing was inside. She was not sure why, but every day she kept looking.

One day she opened the door and inside she found a room full of pain. She looked around and could see it was very old. Tara wanted to help the pain, and so she started to serve it. She served the pain with a smile and with kind words.

Tara was so happy that she was able to help the pain in the ancient room. She could feel the pain slowly getting better. She kept going back every day to make sure that everything was okay. Over time, the pain was gone and the room became filled with joy.

Tara was so happy that she had served the pain and helped make the room better. From that day on, she knew that it was important to help those in need.

Billy was a brave kid. He always wanted to explore, so one day he walked into an ancient forest. Suddenly, he heard a loud scream! He was scared and started to run away.

But then he saw a strange symbol on the ground. He was curious and decided to take a closer look. He touched the symbol and all of a sudden he heard the scream again, but it was quieter this time. He was brave and stepped closer. The symbol glowed and a big bird flew out! 

Billy was amazed. He wanted to help the bird but then a loud, deep voice sounded. "The bird is mine," it said. It was the ancient guardian of the forest!

Billy was scared and ran away. The guardian screamed harder and followed him, but they couldn't catch Billy. Eventually, the guardian gave up and Billy was safe. He was happy he saved the bird and promised to never go back to the ancient forest again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Dave and Jay. Dave and Jay always liked to play together, but Dave liked to play with things that were not dependable. One day, as they were playing, Dave allowed Jay to try one of his toys. The toy was not dependable and it broke. When Jay saw it, he cried. Dave felt bad and said sorry. But the toy was not able to be fixed, so the two friends could not play together anymore. The bad ending was that Dave and Jay never played together again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to climb the big slide and go down fast. Lily was brave and went first. Ben followed her, but he was a bit scared.

"Look, Lily, there is a dog!" Ben said, pointing to a big, black dog that was running towards them.

Lily saw the dog and felt afraid. She did not like dogs. They were loud and had sharp teeth. She grabbed Ben's hand and ran to the slide.

"Let's go up the slide and hide!" she said. "The dog can't climb the slide. He can't get us there."

They ran up the steps of the slide and sat at the top. The dog barked and jumped, but he could not reach them. Lily and Ben hugged each other and waited for the dog to go away.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Lily asked.

"I'm okay, Lily. You are very brave. You protected me from the dog," Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben. You are very charming. You made me feel better," Lily said.

They smiled and looked at the park. They saw a man coming with a leash. He called the dog and put the leash on him. He said sorry to Lily and Ben and walked away with the dog.

Lily and Ben felt safe again. They decided to go down the slide and play some more. They had fun in the park. They were good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she looked up at the sky and saw a bright comet. She asked her mommy what it was. 

"It's a comet, sweetie," said her mommy. "It's like a shooting star, but bigger."

Lily thought the comet looked yummy because it was so bright and colorful. She wanted to catch it and eat it. 

Her mommy laughed and said, "You can't eat a comet, silly! But maybe we can solve a puzzle and make a yummy treat instead. How about we make some cookies?" 

Lily loved the idea and they went to the kitchen to solve the puzzle of making cookies. They mixed the dough, cut out shapes, and baked them in the oven. When they were done, they were so yummy that Lily forgot all about the comet. She was happy to have solved the puzzle of making cookies with her mommy.

Once there was a little girl who loved to dance. One day, she went to the park to dance. She twirled and skipped around the playground. Everyone laughed and smiled as she danced.

Soon the girl found something else that made her move. It was a little razor. She used it to trace circles and lines in the sand. As she drew, she sang and hummed a song. People watched her little dance in the sand.

When the sun began to set, the girl put away the razor. She couldn't wait to come back and dance again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom made her a peanut butter and jam sandwich for lunch. Lily loved the sandwich, but she got some jam on her shirt. 

Lily's mom said, "Oh no, Lily! You got jam on your shirt. We need to change it."

Lily replied, "I understand, Mommy. I'm sorry I was naughty and got jam on my shirt." 

Lily and her mom went to her room to change her shirt. They picked out a pretty pink one and Lily felt much better. From that day on, Lily made sure to eat her sandwich carefully so she wouldn't get jam on her clothes again.

Once upon a time, there was a big teddy bear. He loved to sit on the bed and play with his friends. One day, he heard a little girl crying. "What's wrong?" he asked. "I lost my favorite toy," she replied. "Don't worry, I'll help you find it," the teddy bear said.

They looked for the toy everywhere, under the bed and behind the chair. Finally, they found it under the seat of the little girl's bike. She was so happy and hugged the teddy bear tightly. But then, the teddy bear accidentally fell off the bed and broke his arm. The little girl was sad and didn't know how to fix him. The teddy bear couldn't move anymore and had to stay in bed forever. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was very fond of playing. One day, she and her Mama were walking together in the city.

Amy said to her Mama, "I see a shop!"

Mama pointed around and said, "Yes, that's a shop. Do you want to take a closer look?"

Amy said, "Yes please!"

When they got to the shop, it was very filthy. Amy was surprised to see how dirty it was.

Mama said, "Look at all the dirt! We should not go in there. Let's go somewhere else."

Amy said, "Ok, Mama."

So Amy and her Mama went to a different shop instead. It was much cleaner and Amy was happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a pig named Pat. He lived in the biggest pan in the backyard. Pat was very enthusiastic and loved eating apples. One day, he gathered a lot of apples and decided to escape the pan. He ran away with the apples and started to explore the world outside.

Pat travelled through meadows, fields and woods. He loved the adventure but was getting tired. Pat was looking for somewhere he could rest and enjoy the apples. He finally found a big, beautiful tree. Pat quickly put the apples down and started eating.

But little did he know, there was an animal living in the tree. It was an owl, who was very angry to see Pat eating his apples. Suddenly, the owl started flying towards Pat!
Secretly, Pat prepared for the owl's arrival. He had been collecting leaves throughout his journey, and was ready to make a surprise escape. When the owl got close, Pat threw the leaves up in the air â€“ and the owl was distracted! Pat quickly ran away, safe and sound.

His adventure was back to normal, but Pat never forgot his enthusiastic escape!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to row in her boat. One day, she went out to row but she felt very sad because her boat was empty. She sat down and started to cry.

Her mother came over and asked, "Why are you crying, Lily?" 

"My boat is empty, and I have no one to row with me," Lily said.

Her mother hugged her and said, "Don't worry, I will row with you and we can comfort each other."

Lily stopped crying and smiled. She got into the boat with her mother and they rowed together. They talked and laughed, and Lily felt very happy. From that day on, Lily never felt empty again because she knew that her mother would always be there to comfort her.

Once there was a poor family who lived in a small house. One day they decided to go to the shop to buy some food. When they got there, they saw that the shop had split into two. The shop keeper was very sad, because the poor family had no money to help him fix it. So mum, dad and the children worked together and used their hands to rebuild the shop. The shop keeper was very thankful for their help! After a few hours, the shop was fixed and the happy family could buy their food. It was a good day!

Once upon a time there was a young butterfly. It flapped its wings, felt the breeze, and was so happy.

The butterfly passed by a garden full of lovely flowers. They were yellow and pink and it smiled at them.

The butterfly passed by a pond. It saw a little fish swimming and it waved hello.

The butterfly passed by a tree where a small bird was singing. It flapped its wings and sang along.

Finally, the butterfly passed by a farm. It saw the farmers spreading butter on their fields and smiled. It knew the butter would help new plants grow.

The butterfly was so happy and it flew off into the blue sky.

Yesterday, Sammy went outside, wanting to explore. He ran around the garden, and found a rabbit in the bushes. "Come here, little rabbit," he said. Sammy wanted to follow the rabbit, but Mommy said, "No, no Sammy. That's naughty. Let the rabbit go." Sammy obeyed and Mommy was very proud of him.

The next day, Mommy said, "Let's go on an adventure, Sammy!" Sammy was so excited, he quickly followed her outside. They walked around the garden until they saw the same rabbit from yesterday. Sammy wanted to follow the rabbit again, but he remembered what Mommy had said. He looked up at Mommy and asked, "Can I follow the rabbit?"

Mommy smiled and replied, "Yes, Sammy. Let's follow the rabbit together." 

So off they went, following the naughty little rabbit as it hopped around the garden. Together, they watched the rabbit explore the garden until eventually it ran away. Sammy was sad to see it go, but he knew that it was on a new adventure. He also had a new adventure of his own - one that he would remember forever.

Once upon a time, there was a friend. His name was Tom and he was always very tired. He took many naps during the day, so he never had enough time to play.

One day, Tom had an idea. He wanted to find an ugly place to take a nap. He searched and searched, but he could not find anything. He was very disappointed. Until, he looked in his closet and found an old blanket that looked very ugly. It was perfect!

Tom took his ugly blanket and went outside. He found a nice shady spot under a tree and spread his blanket out. He was so happy to find a place to take a nap.

As he lay there, Tom heard a voice in the distance. He looked up and saw an old friend of his. He was surprised to see him, but even more surprised to hear his friend call out, "Tom! I've been looking for you. I needed an ugly place to take a nap. Are you up for it?"

Tom smiled and said, "Yes, of course! You can lie down here and take a nap with me."

And so, Tom and his friend enjoyed a long, peaceful nap in their ugly blanket nest. It was a perfect setting, proving that naps can be beautiful no matter where you take them.

John was ready for an adventure. He looked around and wondered what he should do. Suddenly he saw something he had never seen before. It was long and pointed and huge! It was a thermometer. He had no idea what a thermometer was, but he was ready to find out. 

John walked over to the thermometer and saw it had markings on it. He wondered what they meant. He touched it and felt something he had never felt before. It was cool, so he wondered if it was telling him the temperature outside. 

John thought it was exciting to try something new. He looked around to see if anyone else knew what the thermometer meant, but no one was in sight. He decided to explore some more and see what else he could discover.

Lily and Tom were going on a trip with Mom and Dad. They had to pack their luggage in big bags. Lily wanted to pack her favorite doll, but Tom said no.

"That is a baby toy. You are too big for that. You need to pack different things," Tom said.

Lily was sad. She loved her doll very much. She did not want to leave her behind.

"Why do I need to pack different things?" Lily asked.

"Because we are going to a different place. It will be fun. You will see new things and make new friends. You will succeed in having a good time," Tom said.

Lily thought about it. She wanted to have fun, but she also wanted her doll. She decided to pack her doll anyway. She hid her in a small bag and put it in her big bag.

The next day, they went to the airport. They checked in their luggage and boarded the plane. Lily was excited and nervous. She held her small bag close to her.

When they arrived at their destination, they got their luggage and took a taxi to their hotel. Lily opened her big bag and took out her small bag. She smiled when she saw her doll.

"See, I told you. You did not need your doll. You have me and Mom and Dad and this nice hotel and many things to do," Tom said.

Lily hugged her doll and said, "I know, but I like having her too. She is my friend. She makes me happy. And she likes different places too. She wants to see new things and make new friends. She wants to succeed in having a good time too."

Tom looked at Lily and her doll. He felt a little sorry for being mean to her. He said, "Okay, okay. You can keep your doll. But you have to share her with me sometimes. Deal?"

Lily nodded and said, "Deal."

They smiled and hugged each other. Then they went to explore the different place with Mom and Dad. They had a lot of fun. They succeeded in having a good time. And so did the doll.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the woods near her house. One day, she saw a lumber on the ground. She wanted to step on it, but her mom told her not to because it could hurt her feet.

Lily was sad because she really wanted to step on the lumber. But then she remembered that her mom said she would be happy if she listened to her. So, Lily decided not to step on the lumber and instead, she went to play with her friends.

Later that day, Lily's mom told her how proud she was of her for making the right choice. Lily felt happy and proud too. She learned that sometimes it's better to listen to grown-ups because they know what's best for us.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to school and entered her classroom. The classroom was very dull and boring. Lily didn't like it very much. 

But then, her teacher Ms. Smith came in and started to teach the class. Ms. Smith was very funny and made learning fun. Lily started to enjoy the class and even made some new friends. 

After class, Lily went home and told her mom all about her day. She said that even though the classroom was dull, she had a lot of fun with her new friends and loved her teacher. From that day on, Lily loved going to school and learning new things.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy.

But then, Ben saw that Sara had two mittens and he had only one. He had lost his other mitten somewhere. He felt cold and sad. He said to Sara, "You have two mittens and I have one. That is not fair. Give me your mitten."

Sara did not want to give her mitten to Ben. She said, "No, Ben. These are my mittens. You have to find your mitten. Maybe it is under the snow or behind a tree. Go and look for it."

Ben did not want to look for his mitten. He wanted Sara's mitten. He said, "No, Sara. You are mean. You have to share with me. Give me your mitten or I will tell Mom."

Sara did not like Ben's words. She said, "No, Ben. You are silly. You have to look for your mmean or you will be cold. I will not give you my mitten. You are deaf. You do not listen to me."

Ben and Sara started to argue. They raised their voices and complained to each other. They did not notice that the snowman was watching them. He felt sorry for them. He wished they would stop fighting and be friends. He had an idea. He took off his hat and scarf and gave them to Ben and Sara. He said, "Here, Ben and Sara. You can have my hat and scarf. They will keep you warm. And you can share my carrot nose and rocks. They will make you smile. Please do not complain. Please be nice."

Ben and Sara were surprised. They looked at the snowman. They saw his hat and scarf and his carrot nose and rocks. They felt ashamed. They said, "Thank you, snowman. You are very kind. We are sorry for complaining. We will share your hat and scarf and your carrot nose and rocks. We will be nice."

Ben and Sara put on the hat and scarf and played with the carrot nose and rocks. They gave the snowman a hug and a smile. They were happy again. They learned a lesson. They learned to be grateful and to share. They learned to listen and to be friends.

Once upon a time there was an old lady. She loved to sing a special song, but she felt sad. She sang her song, but she didn't feel better. Nothing made her happy, until one day a very special friend showed up. It was a little 3 year old. The 3 year old had a big smile on their face and they sang the same song as the old lady. It was so lovely! The 3 year old hugged the old lady and comforted her. The old lady felt so much better. The 3 year old had brought so much happiness to her. After that, the old lady and the 3 year old sang the special song together every day and were very happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a hole. They want to go inside.

"Let's go in the tree," Anna says. "Maybe there is a secret inside."

"OK," Ben says. "But we have to be quiet. We don't want anyone to find us."

They crawl into the hole. It is dark and cozy. They see a nest with some eggs. They see a shiny stone. They see a book with pictures.

"Wow," Anna says. "This is a secret place. It is so nice."

"Yes," Ben says. "It is safe here. No one can see us or hear us. We can stay here as long as we want."

They look at the eggs, the stone, and the book. They tell each other stories. They laugh and whisper. They are happy in the tree. They have a secret.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. She loved to run around in her garden. One day, when it was hot outside, Emma noticed a poppy in her garden. The poppy was so very small and it was in danger! Emma had to save the poppy.

Emma quickly ran inside and grabbed a pail of water. Then she slowly and carefully walked back to the garden. She carefully poured the water around the poppy, so it wouldn't get too hot.

The poppy thanked Emma and said, "Thank you for saving me!" Emma smiled and said, "You're welcome, little poppy!" Emma was very happy. She knew she had done the right thing by saving the poppy.

Once upon a time, there was a persistent little girl who wanted to learn how to ride a bike. She had a shiny new bike with pedals. Every day, she would take it out and try to pedal. It was hard at first, but she kept at it. Every day she would try to pedal a little bit farther.

Finally, the day came when she managed to stay on the bike, balance and keep pedaling. She was so excited! She kept pedaling and pedaling until she had finished riding around the block. She was so proud of herself for being so persistent.

The little girl finished her ride with a big smile on her face. She had accomplished her goal! From then on, she rode her bike every day, feeling so proud of herself for being so persistent and never giving up.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry bear. He was feeling so hungry he had almost forgotten his own name. He looked around and he saw a glass on the floor. He reached out for it and took a big sip. It was the most bitter drink he had ever tasted. 

He was so angry that he roared: "Who made this glass so bitter?". Just then a little rabbit hopped by. He stopped jumping and he said: "Oh, that was me! I made the glass bitter. I don't forget easily". 

The bear was so surprised that he forgot all about his hunger. He told the rabbit he had never tasted anything as horrible as that glass of drink. The rabbit said sorry and promised to never make anything so bitter again. 

The bear and the rabbit became friends. Whenever the bear wanted a drink, the rabbit remembered to only make drinks that were sweet and tasty.

John and his dad were camping. They had been out in the wild for three days, it was getting dark.

John found a flashlight and started to unpack it. He was very excited to explore with it and his dad was happy John was having a fine time.

Suddenly, the flashlight stopped working. His dad tried to unpack it, but it had broken. John was very sad and his dad felt bad. They had no way of lighting the way and they had to return to their tent without seeing the stars. 

John felt disappointed and was not sure what to do. His dad knew they would have to wait until morning now and the camping trip was at an end.

Once upon a time, in a hot summer, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to play outside with his toys. He had a red ball that he thought was very useful. He could play with it all day long.

One day, Tim saw a big ice cream truck. He wanted to eat some ice cream, but he knew he should resist. His mom told him not to eat too much ice cream or he would get a tummy ache. So, Tim tried to be good and not eat ice cream.

Tim played with his red ball, and he forgot about the ice cream truck. He had fun in the summer sun. At the end of the day, his mom was happy he resisted the ice cream. She gave him a small treat for being good.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was very happy and liked to run. One day, she saw a big gate. She wanted to go through the gate and kept running towards it. But when she got to the gate, it was shut. She was sad.

Then she heard someone coming. It was her dad! He was very happy to see her and said, "Come on, let's go through the gate together." So, hand-in-hand, they walked over to the gate. Her dad opened the gate and it made a big sound.

The girl ran through it, and it felt so fine! She was so glad to see what was on the other side. There was a beautiful park, with lots of trees, flowers, and animals. The girl was so happy and enjoyed running around the park with her dad.

In the end, they walked back through the gate and went home. The girl had had a very fun day and that made her feel fine.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers. Sam and Bill were their names. Sam was always a wonderful brother. He was kind and always did nice things for Bill. 

One day, Sam took Bill for a walk in the park. Bill was so excited, he asked, "Where are we going, big brother?" Sam smiled and said, "Let's go explore the park, it looks so lovely today."

They walked around the park, admiring all the lovely things there. From the flowers to the butterflies. They watched the birds fly and the fountains sparkle in the sun. Sam and Bill were wondering at everything they saw. Bill asked, "This is so beautiful, right Sam?" Sam laughed and said, "It sure is, little brother."

The brothers continued exploring the park, marveling at all its beauty. At the end of the day, they both had memories of the lovely park. That day, they learned the true meaning of brotherly love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and sail her toy boat in the pond. One day, Lily's mom gave her a cup of juice to drink. Lily was so excited to drink the juice, but she accidentally spilled it all over her dress.

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We'll go inside and change your dress." But Lily was persistent. She said, "No, Mommy. I want to sail my boat first." So, Lily sailed her boat in the pond with her wet dress.

After a while, Lily's boat got stuck in some weeds. She tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge. Then, a kind old man came by and asked, "Do you need help?"

Lily said, "Yes, please." The old man helped her get the boat unstuck and said, "Remember, Lily, it's okay to ask for help when you need it. And next time, be careful with your juice." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you!" From then on, Lily always asked for help when she needed it and never spilled her juice again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved to visit her grandma's house. One day, Lily went to visit her grandma and she gave her a big hug. Her grandma had a sore shoulder, so Lily gave her a gentle pat. Then, they played games and sang songs together. Lily was so happy to visit her grandma and couldn't wait to come back again soon.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally. Sally's mum had given Sally a trusty mop to do her chores around the house. Sally loved her mop very much, she thought it was cool and hairy. One day, Sally's mum said to her; "Sally, if you use your mop to clean the kitchen I will give you a treat". Sally was very excited at this and said yes.

Sally went to the kitchen to start cleaning, but there was a problem. The kitchen was very messy, and even with her trusty mop it was hard for Sally to clean it. She tried and tried but there was still a big mess. She started to worry until she noticed something weird.

The floor was covered in fur! As Sally looked closer, she realised that it was coming from her mop! The mop was actually really hairy, and it was getting stuck in the mess she was trying to clean up.

Sally went back to find her mum, who laughed and said; "Sally, I knew this would happen with that hairy mop of yours, so I gave you an extra challenge. Now, let's go find you that treat you were promised!"

Once there was a messy jellyfish. He lived in the deep blue sea with all his friends. Every day, he and his friends played together, but something was wrong. His friends all had a lot of money, but he had none. 

One day, someone came up with an idea. They said, "Let's sell the jellyfish! We can get a lot of money." So all the jellyfish agreed to sell their jellyfish friend.

So they said goodbye and went their separate ways. The messy jellyfish went to a new place. He started selling himself to people, and soon he had lots of money. Everyone was so happy. The messy jellyfish was happy too.

Now, the messy jellyfish has enough money to buy all the things he needs. He will never be messed up and lonely again, and he'll always have enough money.

One sunny day, an enormous puppy was walking past a newspaper stand. Suddenly, he saw something he really wanted - something delicious! He couldn't help himself; he started to eat the newspaper.

But something strange happened. The puppy started to shrink! He got smaller and smaller, until he was tiny; he was the size of the newspaper he had eaten!

The puppy started to walk around the stand, exploring his new, tiny size. But soon, he got scared. He tried to run away, but his tiny legs could not carry him very far.

The puppy was stuck. He was too small now to jump over the high walls around him. He was desperate to escape, but he could not.

Suddenly, the puppy heard someone calling to him; it was an old man. The man had seen the puppy shrinking and was amazed. He said it was a magic newspaper - and it had granted the puppy's wish to be small.

The old man helped the puppy to escape. Together, they found the forgotten magic newspaper that had given the puppy such an enormous wish.

One day, a little girl named Claire turned three. She was so excited because it was her birthday.

Claire went out to visit her best friend Lexi. Lexi noticed that it was Claire's birthday and had a special surprise. She brought out a delicious cake with three candles on top.

When Lexi lit the candles, Claire was filled with joy. She blew them out and wished for a toy. Everyone cheered and clapped for her. 

Claire was so happy and hugged Lexi. "Thank you for being so thoughtful and compassionate on my birthday," she said. 

Lexi smiled and hugged her back. "You are my best friend and I want you to be happy on your special day," she said. "Happy birthday, Claire!"

Once upon a time, there was a small nail. It was lonely and wanted to be useful. It asked the other nails in the toolbox, "What can I do?"

But the other nails just looked at it and said nothing.

So the nail decided to make a plan by itself. It said, "I will give my best to do something. Even if it takes me a long time, I will keep at it!"

The nail was very persistent. It tried and tried to work, but it just couldn't do what it wanted.

Then one day, a carpenter saw the nail. The carpenter said, "Don't worry. I will give you an important job."

The nail was made part of a big project and it was happy. It learned that being patient and persistent can make things happen.

Moral of the story: Being persistent can help turn dreams into reality.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She didn't like to eat broccoli. Her mom would always tell her that it was good for her, but she didn't care. One day, Lily's mom made her broccoli for dinner. Lily didn't want to eat it, so she yelled at her mom. Her mom got mad and sent her to bed without any dinner. 

The next day, Lily's mom tried again. She made broccoli for dinner, but this time she put cheese on it. Lily tried it and she liked it! She felt successful because she had tried something new and liked it. From then on, she ate broccoli without yelling.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was three years old and loved to explore her house. One day, Sarah found a big circle in the shower. She went over and touched its hard surface, and it felt cold and uncomfortable.

Sarah went to ask her mom why it was there.

"Mommy, what is this big circle?" she asked.

"Oh that? That is a drain, honey" replied her mom. 

"Why is it there?"  asked Sarah.

"We need it so the water can drain away after we bathe" replied her mom.

Sarah smiled in understanding.

The next time she was in the bathroom, Sarah looked at the circle with a new appreciation. She could see how it was an important part of the family's bathing routine.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little girl. She wanted to find out what was in the big white freezer in her mommy's kitchen. One day, when her mommy wasn't looking, the nosy little girl tried to unlock the freezer door. She pulled on the handle, but it wouldn't open. She tugged and tugged, but the freezer stayed closed. 

The nosy little girl was getting frustrated, so she asked her mommy for help. Her mommy told her that the freezer was locked very tightly and the only way to open it was with a key. The little girl looked around, but she couldn't find a key anywhere. 

Just then, the nosy little girl had a great idea. She ran to her mommy's bedroom and opened a small box. Inside the box was a key! She took the key and ran to the kitchen. The little girl put the key in the lock and turned it. The freezer clicked and the nosy little girl opened the door. 

To the nosy little girl's surprise, inside the freezer was ice cream! She was so excited that she called her mommy to share the good news. The nosy little girl enjoyed some ice cream and learned a valuable lesson: sometimes the best things are hidden behind a locked door!

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One friend was called John and one friend was called Joan. They were very happy together because they were both unique.

John and Joan decided to have a lot of fun! They decided to share toys and play games and be silly too.

One day they went outside to play and the sun was shining brightly. The sun made their shadows. John and Joan saw their shadows and thought it was funny. They tried to make the shadows do things and play with them.

Eventually, John and Joan had to go inside. But before they went, they promised each other that they would still share and have fun. They shared laughter and hugs and said goodbye until the next day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and she was very lively and curious.

One day Lucy was playing outside when she spotted something in the sky. It was a bright purple star twinkling above her. She decided to pick it and put it in her pocket.

When Lucy got home, she opened her pocket and took out the purple star. All of a sudden the star started to sparkle and then grew, and grew, and grew. Soon it was big enough for Lucy to climb inside. 

"Am I in the universe?" Lucy asked.

The star sparkled again and replied, "Yes, you are in the universe. Would you like to explore?".

Lucy was so excited and she started to pick out the stars and planets. She twirled and spun beneath the stars and the sun and said hello to all the alien creatures she found.

Lucy had the most wonderful time. In fact she stayed so long, that by the time she got home it was dark. 

From that day on, every week Lucy would pick out the purple star from her pocket and spend the day exploring the wonderful universe.

Sara likes to go to the station with her dad. She likes to see the big trains that go fast and make loud noises. She likes to wave at the people who get on and off the trains. She likes to look at the pictures and signs that tell where the trains are going.

One day, Sara sees a new train at the station. It is very big and shiny and has many colors. It has a funny face on the front and a long tail on the back. It looks like a dragon. Sara thinks it is the most beautiful train she has ever seen.

Sara asks her dad if they can ride the dragon train. Her dad says yes, but they have to wait in a long line. Many other people want to ride the dragon train too. It is a very popular train. Sara does not mind waiting. She is very excited.

When it is their turn, Sara and her dad get on the dragon train. They find a seat near the window. Sara looks out and sees the station getting smaller and smaller. The dragon train starts to move. It goes faster and faster. It makes a loud roar. Sara feels like she is flying.

Sara smiles. She is very happy. She loves the dragon train. She hopes they can ride it again soon.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sally and Joe. They were both different, but they liked each other a lot. One day, Sally asked Joe to come to her house to play games.

When they got there, Sally showed Joe her new fan. It was so shiny and sharp, Joe was really impressed. He wanted to touch it and feel it, but Sally said he couldn't. Joe was disappointed, but he said okay.

But the next day, Joe's friend Tom came to his house to play games. Joe showed Tom his fan, and Tom was even more impressed than Joe. He asked Joe if he could touch it, too, and Joe said yes, he could! 

Sally was sad and angry that Joe let Tom touch her fan but not her. Sally was also hurt because she thought Joe was her best friend. 

So Sally and Joe had to have a talk about what friends should do. Finally, they both agreed that it's not nice to not let your friends touch something special to you. And from then on, Joe always gave Sally and all his friends a chance to touch his fan.

Once upon a time, there was a mouse called Chip. Chip was very brave and liked to explore. One day, he ventured into a weird, green wood. The wood looked scary but Chip decided to explore anyway. 

He soon got lost and started to suffer. He was so scared and couldn't find the way home. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a big, friendly owl. The owl asked Chip what he was doing so far away from home. When Chip told the owl that he was lost, the owl smiled and told him that he would help. 

The owl showed Chip the way home, pointing out all the landmarks along the way. Chip was so happy to be back home and thanked the owl for its help. The owl nodded and said, "Don't ever go into a strange, scary woods again. Even brave mice can suffer when they are lost."

The moral of this story is that even brave mice can get into trouble if they explore unknown, scary places. Always be careful and stay away from dangerous places.

Tom and Lily are playing with paper. They like to fold the paper and make different shapes. Tom folds a paper into a long and thin strip. He says, "Look, Lily, I made a snake!"

Lily likes the snake. She wants to make one too. She folds a paper like Tom. But her paper is not long and thin. It is short and wide. She says, "Oh no, my snake is fat!"

Tom laughs. He says, "That's not a snake, Lily. That's a worm!" He shows her how to fold the paper again. He says, "You have to fold it like this, and this, and this."

Lily tries to fold the paper like Tom. She folds it once, twice, three times. But she still can't make it long and thin. She says, "It's too hard, Tom. I can't do it."

Tom has an idea. He says, "Don't worry, Lily. I have something to help you." He runs to his room and comes back with a button. He says, "Look, Lily, this is a button. You can use it to make your snake longer."

He gives the button to Lily. She puts it on the end of her paper. She says, "Wow, Tom, you're right. The button makes my snake longer. Thank you, Tom!"

Tom and Lily are happy. They play with their paper snakes and button. They make them slither and hiss. They have fun.

John had a drum. He loved playing it fast. Every day after playing John would take a nap. He would sleep so soundly and for a long time. After his nap he would wake up and play his drum again, as fast as he could. He would practice hard every day, getting better and better every time. After playing he would be so tired that he could hardly keep his eyes open. He would put his drum away and then go have a nice long nap. John enjoyed sleeping and playing the drum, they were his favorite things to do.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy bear named Bobo. Bobo lived in a nice, green land. The land was called the nation. All the animals in the nation were happy and played together.

One day, a big storm came to the nation. The storm broke many trees and homes. All the animals were sad. They wanted to fix their homes and make the nation nice again.

Bobo the bear had an idea. He wanted to help restore the nation. So, Bobo and all his friends worked together. They fixed the trees and the homes. Soon, the nation was nice and green again. All the animals were happy and played together once more.

Once there was a little girl named Susie. She was three years old and very curious. One day, Susie wanted to try some sugar, so she opened a cupboard and found a big bag of sugar. She was so excited to try it that she quickly opened the bag and started eating it up. But her mom was nearby and saw her.

Susie's mom was embarrassed and came over to the cupboard. She said, "Susie, no sugar. It's not good for you". Then she quickly locked the cupboard so Susie could not get in anymore.

Susie felt very embarrassed, but she knew that she had done something wrong. She promised to never open the cupboard again. From then on, Susie remembered to never open the cupboard.

One day, Max was walking around the park. He was looking at the trees and the flowers. Suddenly he saw a picture on a bench. Max went to the bench and looked at the picture. He was very curious. He asked, "What is this picture?"

A busy bee flew by and answered, "It's a beautiful flower." Max smiled. He thanked the bee and continued walking.

Max loved looking at the pictures in the park. He answered that the purple flower was his favorite. Then he said goodbye to the bee and ran off.

Max spent the rest of the afternoon busy looking at different pictures in the park. By the time he was ready to go home, Max had seen many beautiful pictures. He was happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mommy told her they had to go to a meeting. Lily didn't want to go because she wanted to keep playing. But her mommy was persistent and said they had to go.

At the meeting, Lily got bored and started to ignore what was happening. She played with her toys quietly while her mommy talked. But then, she heard her name and looked up. Her mommy was calling her to come up and say hello.

Lily felt shy but she went up and said hello. Everyone smiled at her and she felt happy. After the meeting, they went home and Lily realized that sometimes it's good to listen and not ignore things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint pictures with her fingers and make colorful messes. One day, her mom cooked beef for dinner and Lily didn't like it because it was too chewy. She said, "Mom, this beef is rude and I don't want to eat it." 

Her mom was surprised by her choice of words and asked her why she thought the beef was rude. Lily replied, "It's too hard to eat and it doesn't taste good." Her mom explained that it's important to be polite and not use rude words. 

Later that day, Lily painted a picture of a big red heart and gave it to her mom as an apology for using the word "rude". Her mom was so proud of her and they both enjoyed a yummy dinner together. From that day on, Lily learned to be kind with her words and to express herself through her beautiful paintings.

Once upon a time, there was a man who loved to drive his car. He would go on great adventures and see many things. One day, he saw a goat on the side of the road. The goat looked at him with big eyes and the man thought it was so cute. He stopped his car and got out to say hello to the goat. The goat was friendly and let the man pet him. The man thought it was a great day because he got to meet a new friend. From then on, every time the man went for a drive, he would look for the goat and say hello. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bluebird called Toby. Toby was a very curious bird and always liked to explore new places. One day, Toby's friend, a rabbit called Sandy, asked Toby to go for a drive in the park.

Sandy said, "Toby, I'd like for you to come for a drive. It'll be fun!" Toby was so excited, he said yes right away.

Sandy and Toby hopped into the car and drove off. Sandy drove slowly as Toby enjoyed the view. Toby felt so relaxed, he shouted, "Faster, Sandy - I want to go faster!"

Sandy turned to Toby with a smile and said, "Ok Toby - I will support you and increase the speed gently, so it's still soft."

So Toby and Sandy drove around the park, going at Toby's desired speed. Toby felt so happy and content that evening, safe and secure with his friend by his side.

Once there was a little girl called Mary. She was three years old and loved to go to the park. Everyday she would go to the park with her mum.

One day she was very upset. She didn't want to go, she wanted to stay on the couch and play. She looked at her mum and said: "No mum, I don't want to go!"

Mum was surprised and felt very upset. She said: "Mary, why don't you want to go to the park? We have so much fun there!" Mary looked at her mum and said: "I don't want to go, I just want to stay on the couch."

Mum thought for a moment and then said: "Ok, we can stay on the couch today, but tomorrow we will go to the park, okay?" Mary smiled and said: "Okay, sounds good!". They both hugged and cuddled on the couch until it was time for bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little kitten. She was very cute and fluffy. One day, she went outside to play. She saw a butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Then, she saw a little girl walking by. The little girl saw the kitten and said, "Oh, you are so lucky to be so cute!" The kitten didn't understand what the little girl meant, but she was happy to be called cute. 

Suddenly, the little girl took out a box of toys. She showed the kitten a ball and said, "Let's play catch!" The kitten didn't know how to play catch, but she tried her best. She jumped and chased the ball until she finally caught it. The little girl clapped her hands and said, "You did it! We match so well!" The kitten didn't know what "match" meant, but she was happy to play with her new friend.

Once there was a little girl. She loved films. Her favourite films were magical and exciting.

One day, she asked for something very special. She asked her mummy to bring her a perfect film. Mummy said yes and went away to get it.

The little girl was very happy! She waited in her room until mummy came back.

Mummy brought the perfect film, and they watched it together. It was filled with adventure, and it was just what the little girl wanted.

When the film finished, the little girl felt so happy. She thanked mummy for bringing her the perfect film. They hugged and shared a smile.

Once upon a time there was a kind and compassionate man who lived in the nearby village. He was a cheerful soul who always tried to encourage others with his kind words.

One day he was walking through the city when he noticed a little girl, about three years old, sobbing on a nearby bench. He approached her and asked what was wrong.

The girl looked up at him, her eyes full of tears, and quietly said, "My blue balloon floated away. I wanted it for my birthday."

The man's heart melted at her story and he could see how upset the girl was. He gently put his hand on her shoulder and said, "I understand how you feel, sweetheart. Let me try to encourage you. What do you say if I help you get a new blue balloon?"

The girl's eyes lit up with a spark of hope and she smiled through teary eyes.

The compassionate stranger then took her hand and they walked to the nearby market where they bought a brand new beautiful blue balloon. He tied it to her tiny wrist and told her that it was a birthday present from him.

The girl smiled and wrapped her small arms around his neck. He hugged her back and she thanked him for his kindness before she skipped away with her new balloon, still smiling.

The man watched her until she was out of sight and he smiled, knowing that he had just done something kind. He was happy

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl. Her name was Sarah and she had the biggest smile. She loved to wander in the sunshine and one day, she asked her mom if she could go alone. Her mom said yes and gave her permission.

So Sarah skipped away, singing as she went. She wandered through the sweet smelling field, watching the butterflies flutter in the air. The grass was so soft beneath her feet and the sun was so warm on her face.

Sarah stopped at the edge of the field and saw a friendly rabbit hopping around. She hopped closer, wanting to pet the rabbit, but it was too scared and hopped away. Sarah was sad and started to cry.

Suddenly, something amazing happened! Sarah heard a voice as if from far away. It said, â€œYou can pet the rabbit if you are gentle.â€ Sarah smiled and quietly moved forward, and with a soft touch and kind words, the rabbit allowed her to pet it.

Sarah and the rabbit were friends after that day. They would meet at the edge of the field, greeting each other with friendly smiles. Sarah was so happy, and her mom was proud that she had listened and been so gentle.

Jimmy was out in the forest with his dad. Jimmy looked at the tall trees and the long lumber all around. Dad was working hard and every now and then, he would let out a big sigh.

"What are you doing, Dad?" Jimmy asked.

Dad smiled and said "I'm making something important for you, Jimmy. It's going to be a surprise." 

Jimmy smiled too and watched his dad work. He was impressed with how much Dad was doing and how hard he was working. 

After a while, Dad stopped and said "There! It's done". 
Jimmy looked and smiled, excited to see what his dad had made. Dad had made a big wooden house, just for Jimmy! 

Jimmy was so happy and he hugged his Dad and thanked him. Dad smiled and they both sighed - they were so proud of the important work they'd done together.

Once upon a time, there was a humble bug named Zip. Zip loved to go on journeys. One day, Zip decided to go on a big journey to find a new home.

On his journey, Zip met a big bird. The bird said, "Hi, Zip! Where are you going?" Zip said, "I am on a journey to find a new home." The big bird said, "I can help you. Hop on my back and we will find a new home together."

Zip and the big bird flew high in the sky. They saw many homes, but none were right for Zip. Then, they saw a big tree. Zip said, "That tree looks like a good home for me." The big bird said, "Okay, let's go down and see."

As they got closer to the tree, a mean cat saw them. The cat jumped up and caught the big bird. Zip fell off the bird's back and landed on the ground. Zip was sad and scared. He had lost his new friend and did not find a new home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to be creative. Every day, she would gather her chalk and go outside to draw on the sidewalk. She drew flowers, trees, and hearts for all the birds and bugs to see.

One night, the little girl was very tired, so she said good-night to the bugs and birds, and went inside to sleep. All night long, she dreamed about the pictures she had drawn in the sunshine.

The next morning, she woke up with a new idea! She took her chalk and drew magical pictures in the sky. The clouds were like animals and the sun was like a bright flower. Everyone in the neighborhood stopped to watch.

Finally, the little girl was satisfied with her creative work. After a day of drawing, she went inside, said goodnight to the clouds again and went to bed. As she fell asleep, she was happy knowing that her art was in the sky for everyone to see.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She liked to draw. Every day she used bright pastels to make pictures and fill her world with colourful fun.

She was very excited one day when she found some special red pastels. She couldn't wait to see what kinds of pictures she could make with them. She worked very hard, mixing and blending the colours, creating something new.

When she was finished, she was pleased with her work. Everywhere she looked were reds and pinks and oranges, swirling together to make magical pictures. She was very proud of herself, and showed her pictures to her family and friends. They all said she was a master artist, and she felt so happy.

The little girl went on to make many more pictures, but none were as bright or as beautiful as her red pastel pictures.

One day, there was a thief. He wanted to steal something very special. He knew he needed a plan. He wanted something that was very heavy, so he came up with an idea. He decided to weigh things at the market. Every day he went to the market, he would look around and weigh different items.

One day, he came upon an open box. It was very heavy, so the thief was very excited. He thought it would be the perfect item to steal. He quickly took the box and ran away.

The thief did not know that the box was filled with coins and jewels. He was only focused on the fact that it was heavy. Little did he know, that he had just stolen the most valuable item in the market!

Once upon a time, there was a big building. It had many rooms and windows. One day, the building felt uncomfortable because it was very hot outside. The people inside the building felt uncomfortable too.

But then, a kind man came to protect the building. He put big umbrellas outside so that the sun wouldn't shine on the building. The people inside the building felt happy because they were no longer uncomfortable.

From that day on, the building was protected from the hot sun. The people inside the building were very grateful to the kind man who helped them. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved robots. He had a toy robot that he played with every day. One day, Timmy went to a store with his mom and saw a big robot. It was very tall and shiny. Timmy wanted to touch it, but it was too high for him.

Timmy's mom asked the store owner if Timmy could touch the robot. The store owner said yes, and he helped Timmy touch the robot's arm. Timmy was so happy and proud that he got to touch a real robot. He smiled and told his mom that he loved robots even more now. From that day on, Timmy wanted to be a robot when he grew up.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to watch movies with her family. One day, Amy's mom told her they were going to watch a movie together after dinner. Amy was very excited and could not wait to see the movie.

During dinner, Amy's dad said he heard the movie was terrible, but they would still watch it together. Amy did not know what "terrible" meant, but she still wanted to see the movie. After they finished eating, they all sat down in the living room to watch the movie.

As the movie started, Amy noticed her mom was not happy with the movie. So, Amy decided to help make the movie better. She started to act out the funny parts and make silly faces. Her family laughed and had a great time. In the end, even though the movie was terrible, Amy helped make it a fun night for everyone.

The boy was very busy. He always had something to do. Today he had a special task. He had to match the ceiling. He found some papers with pictures on them and he matched them to the ceiling. He looked up and the ceiling had changed! It was brighter and more colourful! He was really happy and proud of his work.

The boy was so busy matching the ceiling that he didn't notice his mom come in until she said, "Wow! You're so busy!" The boy smiled and said, "I finished matching the ceiling!" His mom said, "That's great! You did a wonderful job."

The boy was so proud of his work. He felt like a grownup! He had done something he never thought he could do. He had matched the ceiling and made his room look brighter and more colourful. He was happy and couldn't wait to show his friends!

Mommy and Sammy were walking to the park. Suddenly, Sammy saw a big, yummy horse. He screamed "horse, horse!". Mommy said "Do you want to pet the horse Sammy? Please be careful, ok?". Sammy nodded and said "please horse". He was so excited he ran over to the horse. The horse made a friendly noise and Sammy patted it's neck. He said "yummy".
Mommy smiled and said "Let's go get ice cream Sammy, would you like that?". Sammy nodded as he followed mommy away from the horse. He said "yummy horse, please mommy!"

Once there was a little boy and his best friend was a fairy. Every day they would play together in the garden.

One day, when they were chasing each other, the fairy tripped and fell. She started to cry. The little boy wanted to help her so he ran to her and picked her up. He said, "Don't worry, I will make you fit again." 

The fairy shook her head and replied, "No, I don't want to be fit again. I want to stay like this."

The little boy was surprised. He asked, "Why would you want that?" 

The fairy brushed her tears away and said, "I want to resist the change. I like being a fairy and I don't want to be different." 

The little boy nodded and gave her a hug. He understood her feelings and said, "Ok, I won't change you if you don't want to change."

And from that day onward, the little boy and the fairy were never separated, and no matter what, the fairy loved being a fairy and the little boy loved the fact that his best friend was so fit.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in her garden. One day, while she was playing, she saw a butterfly. She tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Lily's mom came outside and asked her why she looked sad. Lily said she wanted to catch the butterfly, but it flew away. Her mom told her not to be frightened and that she would help her catch it. 

So, they both went to the garden and looked for the butterfly. Suddenly, the butterfly landed on Lily's mom's blouse. Lily was so happy and caught the butterfly gently in her hands. She was so excited and showed it to her mom. Her mom was proud of her for catching the butterfly. From that day on, Lily loved catching butterflies in her garden.

One day, John and his mom had very little money. Mommy said the money was tight. She was sad and asked John what they could do.
John thought carefully and then his face lit up. He suggested they could look for money in their house. 
Mommy was surprised. She said, "Where do you think we'd find money?"
John said, "Maybe in the dresser! Or behind the couch!"
Mommy smiled and said, "Let's hurry and look!"
John and Mommy searched together through the house and found some money in one of the drawers. They hugged each other and cheered with delight. They had enough money again to buy food and have fun.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to run and play with his friends. One day, they had a race. Remy wanted to win the race, so he practiced every day. He wanted to be the perfect runner.

One morning, Remy saw a big tree with a hole. He had a question in his mind. "What if I hide in the hole during the race?" he thought. "I can come out at the end and win!" Remy told his friends about the big tree with the hole. They all laughed and said, "Remy, that's not how you win a race!"

The day of the race came. Remy and his friends lined up to start. Remy remembered the big tree with the hole, but he knew his friends were right. He had to run the race, not hide. So, Remy ran as fast as he could. He ran and ran until he crossed the finish line. He didn't win, but he felt like a perfect runner because he tried his best.

One day there was a man who needed to buy a present for his dog. He decided he wanted to get something special, something shiny and sparkly. 
The man went to a store and saw a silver collar that shined in the light. He knew immediately that he had found the best present. 
But when the man took the silver collar to the counter he realised it was fake. 
The man was so sad that he couldn't find a real collar to give to his dog. He went home, feeling defeated. 
The next day he heard a knock at the door and when he answered it he saw a big box. When he opened it, he couldn't believe his eyes. It was a real silver collar, even better than the one he had seen in the store. 
He knew right away who had brought it to him- his dog! 
The man was so happy and thanked his pup. He put the silver collar on the dog and hugged her tight. From then on, whenever the man looked at the silver collar he was reminded of the special moment.

Once upon a time there was a girl who went to the beach. She looked out into the ocean and saw some jellyfish. It was a bright sunny day, the jellyfish were moving slow in the water.

The girl watched them for a while. She was amazed at their colors and how they moved so slowly. Then she had an idea. She decided to put her toes into the water and see if she could touch one of the jellyfish. She took off her shoes and slowly stepped into the water.

When she was ankle deep in the water, she saw one of the jellyfish very close to her. She looked closer and carefully tried to touch it. As soon as she did, the jellyfish filled the water with colorful sparkles!

The girl was so excited. She had never seen anything like this before. She realized that the jellyfish were magical. She smiled and slowly stepped out of the water. It was the most wonderful thing she had ever seen.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily wanted a cherry. She found a cherry tree and looked up at the cherries. They were so high up and she couldn't reach them. She stood looking at the tree and asked, "How can I get those cherries?"

Just then a friendly bird flew down. He said, "I can get you cherries. I'll make you a promise. If you wait here, I'll bring you a nice, juicy cherry."

Lily smiled and waited. She watched the bird fly away. It wasn't very long before the bird came back with a cherry. It was wet from being in the rain but it was still tasty!

Lily was so happy. She thanked the bird for keeping his promise and giving her a cherry. She ate the cherry and enjoyed it very much.

From that day on, Lily remembered that sometimes good things come from keeping your promises. And cherries are best when they are wet!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and had a toy motor that he played with all the time. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his motor. He was driving it around when he heard someone shout, "Be careful!"

It was Timmy's friend, Tommy. Tommy was worried that Timmy might crash his motor. Timmy said, "Don't worry, I'm being careful." But just as he said that, he accidentally drove his motor into a tree. 

Tommy said, "I told you to be careful!" Timmy felt bad and said sorry. Then, they both laughed and played together. From that day on, Timmy was more careful when playing with his motor, and Tommy always reminded him to be careful. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big city with lots of people and buildings. One day, a witch came and cast a spell on the city. Suddenly, everything started to shrink! The buildings became small like toys, and the people became tiny like ants. 

Everyone was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, a brave boy named Timmy came up with an idea. He knew that the witch had put a bitter potion in the city's water supply, so he decided to find a way to make it sweet again. 

Timmy searched and searched until he found a magical flower that could turn bitter things sweet. He brought it back to the city and put it in the water supply. Slowly but surely, everything started to grow back to its normal size. The people were so happy and grateful to Timmy for saving their city from the witch's spell.

Lily liked to play school with her dolls. She was the teach and the dolls were the kids. She had a big book, a chalk and a board. She showed the dolls how to write and read. She gave them stickers when they did well.

One day, she wanted to serve lunch to her dolls. She had some bread, cheese and juice. She cut the bread and cheese into small pieces. She poured the juice into cups. She put everything on a tray and carried it to the table.

"Time for lunch, kids!" she said. "Come and sit down. Be careful, the juice is wet. Don't spill it on the floor."

The dolls came and sat down. They looked at the food. They smiled and said, "Thank you, teach. You are very nice. We like your lunch. You are the best teach ever."

Lily felt happy. She liked to be the teach. She liked to serve lunch to her dolls. She thought she was very popular. She ate some bread and cheese and drank some juice. She shared with her dolls. They had a good time.

Once upon a time there was a little mouse called Sam. Sam had a long, fluffy tail which he was very proud of. One day, Sam decided to show off his tail to the other mice in the forest. 

When they saw it they all began to laugh. "Look at that silly tail!" they said. Sam was embarrassed, and he ran away so they couldn't see him.

Once Sam was out of sight, he heard a funny sound coming from one of the tree branches. It was a wise old owl watching the whole scene. 

"It's not nice to make fun of someone's tail," said the owl. "You should try to always be kind and sort out your differences in a peaceful way."

Sam thought about these words. From then on, he treated everyone with respect, no matter what their tail looked like.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear. He was distant from all the other animals in the forest and so he felt very lonely. One day he decided that he wanted to find a friend. He walked and walked until he found a small boy. 

"Hello!" said the little bear.

The little boy looked at the bear. He was scared but he answered, "Hi!"

The bear asked for help. "Will you be my friend?" he asked.

The little boy smiled and said, "Of course!"

From then on, the little bear and the little boy were friends. They played and laughed, and the little bear was no longer lonely. 

But one day, the little boy's parents forbade him from seeing the bear. They said the bear was too dangerous. The little boy was frustrated and he became angry at the bear. He yelled and threw rocks at the bear.

The little bear was sad and scared. He ran away and was never seen again. He was far away and distant again, just as he was before.

And they never became friends again.

Once there was a girl named Mandy. She was only 3 years old. One day, Mandy was walking outside in the dark. Suddenly, she saw something that made her stop. It was a big, glowing ball. It was beautiful. 

Mandy was so excited that she clapped her hands and ran towards it. As she got closer, she saw a sign next to the glowing ball. It said â€œWelcomeâ€.
