But then, in the darkness, Mandy heard a voice. It said â€œWelcome, Mandy. Have fun and it won't be bitter.â€ Mandy smiled and stepped closer again. She couldn't believe how wonderful the glowing ball was. 

From then on, Mandy visited the glowing ball every day. It was her special place, filled with warmth and welcome.

Once upon a time there was a fox who was looking for an idea. He searched and searched but could not find one. He was feeling sad, when all of a sudden a rabbit hopped by. The rabbit said, â€œWhat are you looking for?â€ The fox told the rabbit his problem. The rabbit was so compassionate that he said, â€œI have an idea! You can lend some of my ideas.â€ The fox was very happy and thanked the rabbit. Soon enough, the fox had all the ideas he wanted. He was so pleased with the rabbitâ€™s idea that he thanked him again. The rabbit smiled and they both went on their merry way.

One day, a very strong stream was flowing through the forest. The trees and the animals all enjoyed watching it go by. But the stream was getting stronger and stronger, and soon it became too powerful to stay in the same place.

So it started to move onwards, taking a journey through the forest. Everywhere it went, it picked up bits of dirt and leaves, becoming bigger and bigger.

The stream eventually reached a big lake, and when it got there, it made a big splash as it became part of the lake. Everyone who was there was happy to see that the stream was finally at its new home. They all smiled as the stream became part of the lake, and the strong stream now had a place to stay.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play and run around. One day, Buddy went with his family to the zoo. The zoo had many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds.

At the zoo, Buddy saw a little boy holding a balloon. The balloon was red and shiny. Buddy wanted to play with the balloon, so he asked the boy, "Can I play with your balloon, please?" The boy smiled and said, "Yes, you can play with it, but be careful."

Buddy was so happy to play with the balloon. But while he was playing, he accidentally let the balloon go. The balloon started to fly away. Buddy felt sad that he had released the balloon. The little boy saw Buddy's sad face and said, "It's okay, Buddy. We can get another balloon."

Buddy and the boy got a new balloon and continued to have a fun day at the zoo. They saw many animals and played together. Buddy learned to be more careful with balloons, and he made a new friend at the zoo.

Once there was a patient named Pam. Pam was very crazy. She liked to ask lots and lots of questions. One day, she asked her friends, "Let's go to the park!" They all said, "Yes, let's go!" So they went to the park, and they had so much fun.

At the park, Pam asked her friends to play tag. Everyone said, "Yes, let's play!" So they played tag for a long time. Pam asked her friends if they wanted to have a snack. Everyone said, "Yes, let's have a snack!" So they ate lots of yummy snacks. 

Next, Pam asked her friends to climb the trees. Everyone said, "Yes, let's climb the trees!" They had so much fun climbing the trees and making crazy shapes with their arms and legs. 

When it was time to go home, Pam asked her friends if they had a good time. Everyone said, "Yes, we had a great time!" So they all hugged and said goodbye. Pam was so happy and thanked her friends for being so patient with her and having such a fun time.

Once upon a time there were two birds called Jack and Jill. Every night they would collect worms to eat, and they were very happy. 

One day, Jack found a shiny coin on the ground. He wanted to collect it and put it in his nest. But Jill told him, "No, Jack! That coin is not good for you!"

Jack didn't listen to her, and he collected it anyway. But when he tried to fly with it, it was too heavy for him. He started to feel very tired and he couldn't breathe properly. His lungs started to hurt.

Then Jill flew over to Jack, and started to peck at the coin. She said, "If we share the coin, it won't be so heavy for us". So together, Jack and Jill shared the coin and flew back to their nest. 

That night, Jill told Jack, "It's good to be generous and to share what we have. If we don't share, it can be very harsh".

Jack and Jill learned a important lesson that day, and they lived very happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a clever fox. He was exploring the forest when he saw smoke in the distance. He knew it was a fire and he had to put it out. So he raced to the spot, but there wasn't enough water to put it out.

The fox looked around, and spotted a lake. He ran towards it, and started to dip his paws in the lake, then throwing the water at the fire to put it out. But no matter how hard he tried, the fire wouldn't stop.

Just then, he heard a voice. It was a farmer, standing nearby. The farmer said, "Hey Fox, what are you doing?" The fox replied, "I'm trying to stop this fire." The farmer said, "That's no good! You need to put something in the fire to make it go away!"

The fox thought for a moment, then he had a clever idea. He picked up some leaves and twigs and threw them in the fire. The leaves and twigs smothered the flames and soon, the fire was completely out. 

The fox was very happy. He had saved the forest!

Riley was feeling sad. He had lost his favourite toy and did not know where it was. He was frowning and his mommy saw him. She put some lotion on her hand and put it on Riley's forehead.

"There, there," she said.

But things weren't getting better. Riley's big brother was being bossy. He kept telling Riley to play with something else.

Riley got more and more upset, until he was crying. His mommy tried to help him again, but it was no use. Riley's toy was lost and wouldn't be found.

In the end, Riley felt very sad. He had tried his best, but things just didn't work out. He had to go to bed without his toy and it was not a happy ending.

Lily was a very intelligent girl. She liked to learn new things and read many books. She was good at math, science, and art. She wanted to be a teacher when she grew up.

One day, Lily had a big exam at school. She studied hard and knew all the answers. She was not afraid of the exam. She was excited to show what she knew.

But when she got to school, she saw that her exam paper was torn. Someone had ripped it in half. Lily was very sad and angry. She did not know who did it or why. She felt like crying.

"Who did this to my exam?" she asked her teacher. "I worked so hard for it."

"I don't know, Lily," her teacher said. "But don't worry. I have another copy for you. You can still take the exam. You are a very intelligent girl. You can do it."

Lily smiled and thanked her teacher. She took the new exam paper and started to write. She forgot about the torn paper and focused on the questions. She was confident and happy. She knew she would do well. She was a very intelligent girl.

Melanie was walking down the street and saw a vendor selling toys. She really wanted to get one, but didn't have any money. She got really sad and a tear came down her face.

But then the vendor saw and came over. He asked her to pick one of the toys. She chose a blue teddy bear. She hugged it tight and the vendor gave her a big smile.

Melanie was so happy, she couldn't stop smiling. She said thank you and skipped away, still hugging her blue teddy bear.

Lily and Ben liked to play pirates in the garden. They had a big box that was their ship, and a stick that was their sword. They also had a hook that they found in the shed. It was shiny and sharp, and they pretended it was a treasure.

One day, they decided to go on an adventure to find more treasure. They put on their hats and scarves, and took their ship, sword and hook with them. They walked around the garden, looking for clues. They saw a bird, a flower, a rock, but no treasure.

Then, they saw something shiny under a bush. They ran towards it, hoping it was gold or jewels. But when they got closer, they saw it was a frozen pond. It was very cold and slippery, and they could see fish and plants under the ice.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "Maybe there is treasure under the ice!"

"Let's find out!" Ben said. He took the hook and tried to break the ice with it. He hit the ice hard, but it did not crack. He hit it again, and again, but nothing happened.

"Be careful, Ben!" Lily said. "You might fall in!"

Ben did not listen. He wanted to find the treasure. He hit the ice harder and harder, until he made a small hole. He looked inside, and saw something shiny. He reached for it with his hook, but he lost his balance. He slipped and fell into the pond.

Lily screamed. She saw Ben go under the water. She was very scared. She did not know what to do. She wanted to help Ben, but she did not want to fall in too. She looked around, and saw a big stick. She grabbed it, and ran to the pond. She lay down on the ice, and reached for Ben with the stick.

"Ben, Ben, grab the stick!" she shouted. "I'll pull you out!"

Ben heard Lily's voice. He was very cold and wet. He saw the stick, and grabbed it. Lily pulled him out of the pond. He was shivering and coughing. He dropped the hook, and hugged Lily.

"Thank you, Lily!" he said. "You saved me!"

"I'm sorry, Ben!" Lily said. "I should have been more polite. I should have let you have the hook. It was your treasure."

Ben shook his head. He smiled at Lily. He said, "No, Lily, you are my treasure. The hook was just a hook. It was not worth it. You are my best friend."

They hugged each other, and walked back to their ship. They decided to play pirates another day, when it was warmer and safer. They learned their lesson. They learned to be careful, and to share, and to be polite. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy with blue eyes and blonde hair. He was so excited that he couldn't stop bouncing. He wanted to go to the pond and splash in the warm sunshine.

So the boy ran over to the pond and giggle as he jumped in. The water was so cool and he had so much fun. He made big splashes that reached all the way up to the sky.

Soon, the boy was getting tired, but he couldn't stop. The sun was getting impatient and starting to set. He wanted to keep playing, but his mom said it was time to go home.

So the boy got out of the pond and waved goodbye. Then he ran home, looking forward to having more fun tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very scared of the dark and had a nightmare every night. One day, she told her mom about her nightmare.

"I had a bad dream last night, Mommy," said Lily.

"What did you dream about, sweetie?" asked her mom.

"I dreamt that a big monster came out of my closet and scared me," replied Lily.

"Oh no, that sounds scary," said her mom. "But don't worry, I'll check your closet before you go to bed tonight. And if you still feel weak, you can always come sleep with me and Daddy."

"Thank you, Mommy," said Lily. "Please don't forget to check my closet."

"I won't forget," promised her mom. "Now let's go play with your toys and forget about that scary nightmare."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a tough day at school because some kids were mean to her. When she came home, she saw a ghost in her room. The ghost was making funny noises and scaring Lily.

Lily said, "Go away, ghost! You're not real!" But the ghost didn't listen and kept making noises. Lily got scared and started to cry. Her mom came in and asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

Lily said, "There's a ghost in my room and it won't go away!" Her mom smiled and said, "Don't be scared, Lily. It's just your imagination. Ignore the ghost and it will go away." Lily listened to her mom and closed her eyes. When she opened them again, the ghost was gone.

Lily liked to play with her trumpet. It was a smooth toy that made loud noises when she blew into it. She liked to pretend she was in a band with her friends. She would march around the room and make music.

One day, she took her trumpet to the park. She wanted to show it to her friends and play with them. But when she got there, she saw a big boy with a real trumpet. It was shiny and had buttons and a long tube. The boy was playing it very well. He made beautiful sounds that everyone liked.

Lily felt sad. She thought her toy trumpet was not good enough. She thought the boy's trumpet was better. She wanted to have a real trumpet too. She walked up to the boy and asked him if she could try his trumpet. The boy looked at her and said no. He said it was his trumpet and he did not share. He said her toy trumpet was silly and she should go away.

Lily felt angry. She did not like the boy. She thought he was mean and rude. She grabbed his trumpet and ran away. She thought she could keep it and play with it. She thought it belonged to her now.

But the boy was faster. He chased after her and caught her. He took his trumpet back and shouted at her. He said she was a bad girl and a thief. He said she should never touch his trumpet again. He said it belonged to him and only him.

Lily felt scared. She did not like the boy. She did not like his trumpet. She did not like the park. She wanted to go home. She ran to her mom and hugged her. She told her what happened and cried. Her mom comforted her and said it was okay. She said she was sorry the boy was mean to her. She said she was proud of her for playing with her toy trumpet. She said it was a special toy that belonged to her and only her. She said she loved her and her trumpet.

Lily felt better. She liked her mom. She liked her toy trumpet. She liked to play with it. She did not care about the boy or his trumpet. She knew her toy trumpet was good enough. She knew it was smooth and loud and fun. She knew it was hers and she was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Jack. Jack loved music a lot. He would listen to it every day and dance to the beat.

One day, Jack's mom took him to a big music concert. Jack was very excited and danced along with everyone. But suddenly, he felt sad because he couldn't see the stage very well. It was too big for his small eyes.

But then, Jack's mom remembered something. She had brought a small stool for Jack to sit on. Jack was so happy and could see the stage perfectly. He danced and sang along with the music all night long.

From that day on, Jack always remembered to bring his small stool to music concerts. He never missed a beat again!

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant dog named Max. Max loved to do exercise every day. He would run, jump, and play with his friends in the park. Max was very happy when he did exercise.

One day, Max met a new friend named Lily. Lily was a little dog who did not know how to do exercise. Max wanted to help Lily. So, Max showed Lily how to run, jump, and play. Lily tried to do exercise like Max.

Soon, Lily learned how to do exercise too. Max and Lily had lots of fun doing exercise together. They became the best of friends. And they lived happily ever after, doing exercise every day.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Sara gets a letter from her grandma. The letter is large and has a picture of a flower on it.

"Look, Tom, I have a letter!" Sara says. She shows Tom the letter. "It is from my grandma. She lives far away. She says she loves me and misses me."

"That is nice," Tom says. He smiles at Sara. "Can I see the picture?"

Sara nods and opens the letter. She takes out the picture. It is a photo of her grandma and a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy.

"Wow, what a big dog!" Tom says. He points at the photo. "What is his name?"

"His name is Spot," Sara says. She tells Tom what her grandma wrote in the letter. "She says Spot is her friend. He likes to run and play. He also likes to hug."

"Hug?" Tom asks. He looks at Sara. "How can a dog hug?"

Sara shrugs. She does not know. She thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea.

"Maybe he hugs like this," she says. She puts the letter and the photo down. She wraps her arms around Tom and squeezes him gently.

Tom feels warm and happy. He hugs Sara back. He likes to hug his friend.

"Like this?" he says.

"Yes, like this," Sara says. They giggle and hug some more.

They think Spot is a lucky dog. He has a grandma who loves him and sends him letters. They also think they are lucky. They have each other and can hug anytime.

Tom and Lily wanted to make a lantern for Halloween. They asked their mom to buy them a pumpkin. Mom said yes, but they had to find a cheap one. She gave them some money and they went to the market.

At the market, they saw many pumpkins. Some were big, some were small, some were round, some were bumpy. Tom and Lily looked for a cheap one. They found one that was small and bumpy. It was only one coin. They bought it and took it home.

They asked their dad to help them cut the pumpkin. Dad said yes, but they had to be careful. He gave them a knife and a spoon. They cut a hole on the top of the pumpkin. They scooped out the seeds and the pulp. They made two eyes, a nose and a mouth on the front of the pumpkin. They put a candle inside the pumpkin.

They waited for the night to come. When it was dark, they lit the candle. The pumpkin glowed with a warm light. It looked like a friendly face. Tom and Lily were happy. They put the lantern on the porch. They said hello to the pumpkin. The pumpkin said hello back. They smiled and hugged each other. They had made a lantern for Halloween.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy car that she loved to play with. One day, Lily's toy car broke and she didn't know how to fix it. She asked her mommy for help, but her mommy didn't know how to fix it either.

Lily decided to learn how to fix her toy car. She looked at it carefully and tried to figure out what was broken. It was a mystery to her, but she didn't give up. She kept trying and trying until she finally fixed it.

Lily was very proud of herself for learning how to fix her toy car. She played with it happily, knowing that she had solved the mystery of what was broken. From that day on, Lily knew that she could learn to do anything if she tried hard enough.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Tam. She was 3 years old and very curious. She was always asking questions and wanted to know more about the world.

One day, Tam asked her mom for a new cell phone. Her mom said no, and told her that she was too young to have a cell phone. Tam was very disappointed.

Later that day, Tam's mom talked to her and said, "I have an idea that might be better than a cell phone. We could get you a modern toy instead!" Tam was excited.

The next day, Tam's mom took her to the toy store and Tam saw a beautiful playhouse. It was modern and very colorful. Tam's mom recommended it to her and said it would help her use her imagination and learn new things.

Tam was very happy with her new toy and she loved to play with it. She learned a lot of things from it and enjoyed her new playhouse more than she would have enjoyed a new cell phone.

The moral of this story is to remember that traditional toys can be very educational and fun!

Once upon a time there was a big construction project. A boy named Jack wanted to help the workers build something.

Jack asked the workers, "What can I do?"

The workers said, "We need someone to design a huge fridge. Can you do it?"

Jack nodded. He got to work right away. He drew a picture of the fridge and showed it to the workers.

The workers said, "It's perfect! Let's get to work building the huge fridge."

So the workers and Jack built a huge fridge together. When it was finished, the fridge was grand and giant. Everyone was proud of the job they had done.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Beth. On a sunny day, Beth decided to go for a walk in the park. As she walked, she looked up and saw a beautiful ceiling twinkling in the sunshine.

Then suddenly, something strange happened. Everything froze! Everyone and everything stopped moving, apart from Beth.

Beth shouted in surprise, â€œWhatâ€™s happening?â€

From across the park, a kindly voice said, â€œYou have magical power Beth! You have frozen everything!â€

Beth looked to see who was talking and saw the smooth trunk of a big tree. She asked the tree, â€œHow do I unfreeze them?â€

The tree replied, â€œThink of the most wonderful thing and wish it to be true.â€

So Beth thought of the most wonderful thing, and wished everyone could move again. As soon as she did, everything came alive, and everybody returned to their business.

The tree said, â€œSee what you can do! Just keep looking up at that beautiful ceiling!â€

Beth thanked the tree and went on her way. She looked up at the twinkling ceiling and she knew that, with a little bit of magical thinking, she could make whatever she wished for true.

Once upon a time, there was a small, cute factory. It was owned by a friendly man named John. Every day, John would watch the factory make lots of beautiful things.

One day a magical spark appeared in the factory. It floated around, singing a sweet song. John watched this spark as it flew around, and he felt so happy.

Soon, the little spark changed and grew. It began to glow and turn in circles. Suddenly, the magical spark became a beautiful bird! The bird flew high in the sky, and then down towards John.

John felt so excited and hugged the bird. The bird sang its sweet song as they both danced around the factory. From then on, John and the bird were best friends. They played and laughed together every day, and watched the factory make lots of wonderful things.

Once upon a time, there was an elephant who was very lonely. He wanted so badly to find a friend. One day he heard some rustling in the trees and looked up. To his surprise, he saw a tiny bluebird sitting in the tree! The elephant shook his trunk and asked the bird to become his friend.

The bird happily agreed and they spent time together every day. They would talk, play games and tell stories. The elephant felt so happy and was no longer lonely.

One day, the bird heard someone in the distance calling out for help. The bird rushed over to see what was wrong and saw that the person was trying to restore a broken wagon. The bird knew he was too small to help, so he hurried back to get the elephant.

The elephant was heavy, but he was able to restore the wagon with only a few tries. The person thanked him kindly and waved goodbye. The elephant and the bird were both happy and went back home together.

From that day on, the elephant and the bird were best friends. They would play, explore and make sure to help those in need.

Once upon a time, there was a unique volcano. This special volcano looked different than all the others and some people said it was magical.

One day, a young girl named Lisa decided she wanted to explore the volcano. She thought it might be fun to see what was inside!

But before she could get too close, her mom stopped her. 

"No, Lisa," her mom said. "We can't go to the volcano. It is too dangerous. We must prevent going there."

Still curious, Lisa asked her mom why.

Her mom explained that sometimes volcanos can make fire and hot rocks come out of their tops, so it was important to stay away and prevent a bad surprise. 

So Lisa listened to her mom and stayed away from the volcano. Instead, she found other ways to have fun and learn about the unique volcano in her own way.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Abbie. She was three years old. Abbie was very curious. Everywhere she went, she wanted to learn more and try new things. But there was one thing Abbie hated â€” weight. All the other kids were playing and having fun, while Abbie had to stand still and hold the weight in her hands.

But one day, Abbie's mom told her a secret. She said that when Abbie started to do her exercises, the weight would feel lighter. Abbie started to do what her mom said and soon enough, she found that the weight was much easier to carry.

Abbie was so happy! She carried the weight around the house and even did her exercises with a smile on her face. From then on, Abbie didn't hate the weight anymore â€” she was in control of it.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He loved the outdoors and especially loved playing in the water. One day he brought a big, orange stick to the river. When he got there, he threw the stick into the water. Then, he waded in and started to splash around. 

He jumped and turned in circles, laughing and clapping his hands. He moved the stick around, making different shapes in the water. Everywhere he swam, big splashes came up. Jack was having so much fun!

At one point, he threw the orange stick far away from him. He laughed as it sped off and drifted down the river. Then, he spun around, twirling his arms and making bigger and bigger splashes. He couldn't stop and kept playing until the sun went down.

Afterwards, he was exhausted, but happy. He said goodbye to the river, ready to come back again soon and have even more fun.

There was a family who were all very excited. They were going on an adventure. They looked all around and couldn't find the way, but then one of the kids noticed a door they had not seen before. 

Everyone was surprised, they didn't know what was behind the door. But they were excited and decided to open it. So, they put their hands on the door and opened it. 

When they opened it, they were amazed! There were so many magical things behind the door and everyone gasped. 

They revealed so many things that they had never seen before. There were colorful birds flying, a big castle and even a pink dragon! Everyone was so excited! 

They stayed in this magical land for what felt like forever and had such a great time. When it was time to go, everyone was sad to leave. The family took one last look and closed the door, then went home with lots of amazing stories to tell.

Once upon a time there was a brave knight. He had a big shield to protect him when he went off on his adventures. 
One day, while he was out exploring, he found someone had stolen his shield. He was very sad and he couldn't protect himself without it.

He didn't know what to do so he asked the people in the village if they had seen his shield. One old man said he had seen it with a big yellow dragon. 

The knight was brave, so he decided he must get his shield back. He followed the path to the dragon's cave, and almost cried when he saw his beloved shield. He shouted at the dragon, and the dragon was so scared that it flew away. The knight was glad to have his shield back!

The knight was now safe and had his shield to protect him on future adventures. He was very glad to have it back and he promised to never let anyone steal it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dolls. One day, Lily wanted to measure how tall her favorite doll was. She found a ruler and measured her doll from head to toe. She was happy to find out that her doll was very tall!

Later that day, Lily went outside to play. She saw a bird flying in the sky and it was a beautiful sight. The bird had colorful feathers and Lily thought it was very pretty. She watched the bird fly around for a while before it flew away.

As the day went on, Lily decided to draw a picture of her doll. She used her favorite colors and made an original drawing. She was proud of her artwork and showed it to her family. They thought it was amazing and hung it up on the fridge for everyone to see.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to eat cherries. She thought they were very delicious. One day, her mom gave her a big bowl of cherries to eat.

Sue was so happy. She sat down and started to eat the cherries one by one. She liked how they were red and sweet. She ate and ate until there was just one cherry left.

Sue wanted to finish all the cherries in the bowl. She picked up the last cherry and ate it. It was the most delicious cherry of all. Sue was very full and happy. She thanked her mom for the yummy cherries and went to play outside.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. They also like to make jokes and tricks. One day, they find a big box in the living room. It has a bow and a tag. The tag says: "To Anna and Ben, from Santa".

Anna and Ben are very happy. They think Santa came early this year. They want to open the box and see what is inside. But they also want to wait for Christmas. They are confused. What should they do?

They decide to make a plan. They will open the box very carefully and see what is inside. Then they will wrap it again and put it back. They will act surprised on Christmas. They think this is a good joke.

They open the box and see a big teddy bear. It is soft and brown. It has a red scarf and a hat. Anna and Ben love it. They hug it and play with it. They forget about their plan. They forget about the time.

Mom and Dad come home. They see Anna and Ben with the teddy bear. They see the box and the paper. They are not happy. They are angry. They ask Anna and Ben what they did. Anna and Ben are scared. They try to lie. They say they found the teddy bear outside. They say they did not open the box.

Mom and Dad know the truth. They are not stupid. They tell Anna and Ben that they are naughty. They tell them that they broke the rule. They tell them that they have to say sorry. They tell them that they have to give back the teddy bear. They tell them that they have to wait for Christmas.

Anna and Ben are sad. They cry. They say sorry. They give back the teddy bear. They wrap it again and put it back. They learn their lesson. They do not make jokes and tricks with presents. They do not lie to Mom and Dad. They wait for Christmas. They hope Santa will forgive them.

There was a little girl who loved playing in the garden. She would happily run around, tumble, and pick up all the colorful flowers.

One day, she was playing in the garden when she saw a big, fat, orange bird with a long tail. She asked it, "Please can I have a ride on your back?"

The orange bird said, "No, silly girl! I don't want to help you get around. That's not useful for me. Instead, why don't you get some water and go take a bath? You'll have more fun that way."

The little girl smiled and ran off to get some water. She found a little pond and filled her bucket full of cool, crystal-clear water.

But when the little girl came back, the orange bird had flown away! All she had to show for her efforts was a heavy bucket of water. She didn't get to take a ride on the orange bird, and she had wasted her time getting the water.

Moral of the story: Sometimes asking for help isn't always the best choice. It's usually better to be useful and try to do things on your own.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, she saw a swing hanging from a tree. She ran over to it and started to swing back and forth. It was so much fun!

As she was swinging, her mom called out to her. "Lily, it's time to come inside and change your clothes for dinner," her mom said. Lily didn't want to stop swinging, but she knew she had to listen to her mom.

After dinner, Lily went to bed. She was so excited to wear her new thin pajamas that her mom had bought her. As she was getting ready for bed, she remembered how much fun she had swinging earlier that day. She couldn't wait to swing again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a kind bear. He lived in a big pine forest with all his animal friends. Every day, he would order food from the nearby village and everyone would enjoy it together.

One day, the bear ordered something special: a delicious pineapple! He was so excited to share it with his friends. All the animals gathered around, and the bear smiled as he passed out the pineapple to each of them.

The animals ate their delicious pineapple and thanked the bear for his kindness. From then on, the bear always ordered a pineapple whenever he wanted to give a special treat to his animal friends. 

And they all lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with glue and make pretty pictures. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big bottle of glue and some colorful paper to play with. Lily was very happy and started making a picture of a flower.

Suddenly, her little brother came running into the room and started yelling. Lily got scared and dropped the glue bottle. Glue spilled everywhere and stuck to her hands and the floor. It was very interesting to see how the glue was so sticky!

Lily's mom came in and saw the mess. She helped Lily clean up the glue and told her brother not to yell. Lily was happy again and continued making her flower picture. She learned that yelling can be scary, but glue can be fun to play with as long as she is careful.

One day, there was a girl who wanted to pour something onto her garden. She grabbed a bucket and filled it with water. She was a bit nervous because she had never done this before.

She asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Let's do it together!"

The girl and her mom walked to the garden. They slowly poured the water, making sure it covered all of the plants. When they were finished, the girl was relieved. She said, "I was so nervous!"

Her mom smiled and said, "You did a great job. Now, let's go inside and have a snack."

They went back to the house and ate a yummy snack. The girl was happy that she was brave enough to do something new. She was proud of her garden, and knew it would stay nice and healthy.

One day, Mommy and Buster were in the living room. They were playing with a gray chair. Buster was making it spin around.

Mommy said, "Buster, please don't disturb the chair!"

Buster stopped and asked, "Disturb? What's that?"

Mommy said, "It means when something moves too much and makes noise, it's disturbing."

Buster asked, "But why can't I spin the gray chair around?"

Mommy said, "Well, we don't want to disturb the other people in the house. We don't want them to be bothered by the noise."

Buster thought for a moment and said, "OK, I won't disturb the chair any more." He smiled and started playing quietly with his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to eat candy. One day, Timmy was eating a piece of candy when he felt a sharp pain in his tooth. He cried out and his mom came running to see what was wrong.

Timmy's mom looked in his mouth and saw that there was a big hole in his tooth. She knew they had to go to the dentist to fix it, but Timmy was scared. He had never been to the dentist before and the thought of someone poking around in his mouth was unknown and scary.

But Timmy's mom knew what to do. She gave him a big hug and told him that the dentist was there to help him. She explained that the dentist would use special tools to fix his tooth and make it feel better. Timmy felt a little bit better knowing that the dentist was going to help him, so they went to the dentist's office together.

When they got there, the dentist was very kind and gentle. He showed Timmy all of the tools he was going to use and explained what each one did. Timmy was still a little bit scared, but he trusted the dentist to make his tooth feel better. And sure enough, after a few minutes, the dentist was able to fix Timmy's tooth and make the pain go away. Timmy was so happy and relieved that he gave the dentist a big hug and thanked him for helping him.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab who lived by the sea. He loved to play in the sand and watch the waves. One day, he saw a big fish swimming in the distant sea. The crab wanted to be friends with the fish, but he was too scared to swim out there.

The crab asked his seagull friend for help. The seagull said he would help the crab, but only if the crab helped him first. The seagull needed the crab to find a shiny shell for his collection. The crab agreed to help.

The crab searched and searched until he found the perfect shiny shell. He brought it back to the seagull, who was happy and helped the crab complete his goal. The seagull flew the crab out to the distant sea, where the crab finally made friends with the big fish. They played together and had fun in the sea, and the crab was happy he overcame his fear.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with crayons and stickers. One day, they find a big box of new crayons and stickers in their room. They are very happy and excited.

"Look, Ben, there are so many colors and shapes!" Lily says. "Let's decorate something!"

"OK, Lily, what do you want to decorate?" Ben asks.

Lily thinks for a moment. She sees her doll on the bed. She picks it up and says, "Let's decorate my doll! She has a white dress and a white skin. She needs some color and some fun!"

Ben agrees. He takes some crayons and stickers from the box. He and Lily start to draw and stick on the doll's dress and skin. They make her look very cute and funny. They give her a red nose, a blue hat, a green skirt, and a yellow star on her cheek.

They are having so much fun that they do not hear their mom calling them for lunch. When their mom comes to their room, she sees the mess they have made. She sees the crayons and stickers on the floor, on the bed, and on the doll.

"Oh, my! What have you done to your doll, Lily?" she asks.

Lily and Ben look at their mom. They smile and say, "We decorated her, mom! Do you like her? She is very cute!"

Their mom does not know what to say. She is a little angry, but also a little amused. She says, "Well, I guess she is very cute, but you should not decorate your doll's skin with crayons and stickers. They are hard to wash off. And you should not make such a mess in your room. You have to clean it up after lunch."

Lily and Ben nod. They say, "OK, mom, we are sorry. We will clean it up. But can we keep our doll like this? We love her!"

Their mom sighs. She says, "OK, you can keep your doll like this, but only for today. Tomorrow, we will try to wash her and make her look normal again. Now, come on, let's go for lunch."

Lily and Ben hug their doll and their mom. They say, "Thank you, mom! You are the best!"

They go for lunch, happy and proud of their cute doll.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Clara. She was three years old. Clara was always happy and loved playing with her toys. 

One day, something special happened. Claraâ€™s doorbell started to ring. She ran to the front door and opened it. To her surprise, a big box of stuff was there. The box was pink and she felt so excited.

Clara opened the package. Inside, she found lots of different things. There were dolls and blocks and books too. Clara was so happy â€“ now she had even more stuff to play with! 

Clara played for hours with her new things. That night, before she went to bed, Clara thanked the kind person who had sent her the package of pink stuff. Clara smiled and climbed into bed, feeling very happy and grateful. 

The End!

Bob loves to go on adventures. He went for a walk along the beach, looking for fun and exciting things. All of a sudden, he saw a huge castle with lots of interesting things. Bob was so excited! He ran up to the castle to take a closer look.

The castle was full of organized activities and games. Bob had so much fun playing and exploring! He found all kinds of treasures, like giant shells and colorful rocks. After a few hours, it was time to go home, but Bob was sad. He wished he could stay a little bit longer.

But Bob knew he would come back one day and explore the castle again. He said goodbye and promised to return soon. Bob went home, already thinking of all the fun he would have the next time he came back!

Sara and Ben were eager to draw with their new crayons. They had many colors and a big paper to make a picture. They sat on the floor and started to draw.

Sara drew a house with a red roof and a yellow door. Ben drew a car with blue wheels and a green hood. They were happy with their drawings.

But then, Sara saw that Ben had used her orange crayon to draw the sun. She wanted the orange crayon for her flowers. She said to Ben, "Give me the orange crayon. It is mine."

Ben said, "No, I need it for the sun. It is mine."

They both pulled the orange crayon and it broke in two. They were sad and angry.

They looked at the broken crayon and saw that it had a white part inside. They wondered what it was.

Sara said, "Maybe it is an eraser. Maybe we can use it to erase our drawings and start again."

Ben said, "Let's try it. Maybe we can share the crayon and the eraser."

They rubbed the white part on their paper, but it did not erase anything. It only made a mess. They were more sad and angry.

They threw the broken crayon and the white part away. They did not want to draw anymore. They did not want to talk to each other.

Mom came and saw the paper, the crayon and the white part. She said, "What happened here? Why are you not drawing?"

Sara and Ben told Mom what happened. Mom said, "I'm sorry you broke your crayon. But the white part is not an eraser. It is the wax that holds the color. It does not erase anything. It only makes a mess."

Sara and Ben said, "Oh, we did not know that. We thought it was an eraser."

Mom said, "It's okay. You can still draw with the other crayons. And you can still share the orange crayon. You can each use one part. But you have to be careful and gentle. And you have to say sorry to each other."

Sara and Ben said, "Sorry" to each other. They hugged and smiled. They picked up the broken crayon and the white part. They threw them in the trash. They took the other crayons and the paper. They started to draw again. They shared the orange crayon. They were happy again.

One day, a large cat was walking outside. The cat was looking for something to catch. Suddenly, the cat noticed a watch. It was shiny and sparkled in the sun. The cat wanted to catch the watch so it could have something special.

The cat ran as fast as it could and managed to catch the watch. The cat was so proud of itself. It decided to take it home as a surprise for its owner.

The cat showed its owner the large watch. The owner was so happy that the cat had managed to catch it. They gave the cat lots of cuddles and praised it for being so clever.

The cat and its owner enjoyed playing with the watch together. And after that, the cat was always proud when it was out looking for things to catch.

Tommy was a very eager boy. He was always ready to do something new and exciting.

One day, Tommy went outside with some chalk. He kneeled on the sidewalk and began to draw a big picture. He was so excited about it!

When he was done, he stood proudly and showed it to his mom. His mom smiled and said, â€œWow Tommy, thatâ€™s so beautiful! What did you make?â€ Tommy beamed and replied, â€œItâ€™s a rainbow!â€

His mom hugged him and said â€œIâ€™m so proud of you, Tommy. You did a wonderful job.â€ Tommy smiled and gave his mom a hug. He was so happy he made something special!

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to run and play in the park with his owner. His owner always put a leash on him to keep him safe. One day, a weird man came to the park and talked to Max's owner. The man ordered Max's owner to give him the leash and then he ran away with Max.

Max's owner was very sad and called the police. They searched for Max and found him in the weird man's house. The man was arrested and Max was returned to his owner. But Max was not the same happy dog anymore. He was scared and didn't want to play anymore. Max's owner tried to make him happy again, but it was too late. Max had been traumatized by the weird man and never recovered.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful little dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play with his group of friends in the park. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long.

One sunny day, while they were playing, Buddy's best friend, a little girl named Lily, fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry. Buddy ran to her side and said, "Don't cry, Lily. I will help you." 

Buddy gently kissed Lily's knee, and the pain went away. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Buddy. You are so helpful!" They hugged and continued to play with their group of friends, happy and full of love.

Tim and Jen liked to play with trains. They had a big box of trains and tracks in their room. They made long and curvy tracks on the floor and put their trains on them. They pretended to be the drivers and the passengers of the trains. They had fun making noises and stories with their trains.

One day, Tim found a new train in the box. It was different from the other trains. It was shiny and red and had a black thing on top. Tim liked the new train. He wanted to play with it. He took it out of the box and put it on the track. He pushed it along the track and made a loud whistle sound.

Jen saw the new train and wanted to play with it too. She asked Tim to share the train with her. But Tim said no. He said it was his train and he found it first. He said Jen could play with the other trains. Jen was sad and angry. She tried to take the train from Tim. They fought over the train and pulled it from each other.

The train broke. The black thing on top came off and a lot of steam came out. The steam was hot and it burned Tim and Jen's hands. They dropped the train and screamed. They cried and ran to their mom. Their mom saw their hands and the broken train. She was mad and worried. She took them to the doctor. The doctor put bandages on their hands and gave them medicine. He said they had to be careful with toys and not fight over them.

Tim and Jen learned their lesson. They said sorry to each other and to their mom. They promised to share their toys and play nicely. But they could not play with trains for a long time. They missed their trains and the new train. They wished they had not fought over it. They wished they had not broken it. They wished they had not burned their hands. They were sad and sorry. The end.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toy boats in the pond. They liked to sail them and watch them float on the water. Anna had a red boat and Ben had a blue boat. They pretended they were pirates and explorers.

"Look, my boat is faster than yours!" Ben said. He made his boat zoom past Anna's boat.

"No, it's not! My boat is stronger than yours!" Anna said. She made her boat bump into Ben's boat.

They started to argue and push each other's boats. They did not see the big duck that was swimming near them. The duck was hungry and curious. It saw the toy boats and thought they were food. It opened its beak and snapped at them.

"Quack! Quack!" The duck said.

Anna and Ben heard the duck and turned around. They saw the duck trying to eat their boats. They were fearful. They did not want to lose their boats. They ran to the edge of the pond and tried to pull their boats back.

"Help! Help!" Anna and Ben shouted.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the duck and the boats. She picked up a stick and waved it at the duck.

"Shoo! Shoo! Go away, duck!" She said.

The duck was scared of the stick. It let go of the boats and swam away. Anna and Ben grabbed their boats and hugged them. They were happy and relieved.

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben said.

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She put them on her shoulders and carried them back to the picnic blanket.

"Next time, be careful and share your boats, okay?" She said.

"Okay, mom. We're sorry." Anna and Ben said.

They learned their lesson and played nicely with their boats. They had fun and enjoyed the sunny day.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy some food for dinner. Tim's mom asked him to pick out a reliable vegetable, so he chose celery. He was very proud of his choice.

As they walked home, Tim's mom asked him to balance the celery on his head. Tim thought it was a fun game. He put the celery on his head and tried to keep it from falling. "Look, Mom!" he said, "I can balance the celery on my head!"

His mom smiled and said, "Great job, Tim! You're really good at balancing the celery." They laughed and continued walking home, with Tim balancing the celery on his head the whole way. When they got home, they cooked dinner together and enjoyed their meal with the reliable celery.

Once there was a popular spirit who lived in the village. He was nice and he liked to stir things up. Everywhere he went, he made people smile. He was so popular, that everyone wanted to be his friend.

One day, the spirit decided to stir up some trouble. He ran around the village, playing pranks on the people by hiding their things and making silly noises. The people laughed and the spirit couldn't help but let out a little giggle too.

Soon, he was stirring up trouble all over the village. Everyone was having a lot of fun, but the spirit had stirred up too much trouble. He was so tired he just wanted to sleep.

The village people noticed what the spirit had done and they took care of him. They helped him find a warm place to sleep, away from all the trouble he had stirred up. From then on, everyone in the village looked out for the popular spirit. He was happy and safe, and everyone always made sure he had a lot of fun.

James opened his eyes and saw a big flag. It was red, with a yellow star in the middle. He smiled as he saw it because it was so fair. He walked closer and saw more flags all around. He excitedly opened the door and ran outside. He saw so many flags fluttering in the wind. He wanted to touch them, so he opened his arms wide and ran through them. It was so fun watching them flutter around. He was so happy that he wanted to share it with everyone. He opened his mouth and shouted, 'Come and see these flags, they are so fair!' Everyone heard him and came out to see the flags. With the flags, everyone had a fair and wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a red car, a yellow truck, and a blue train. But his favorite toy was a green pipe that he found in his backyard.

One day, Timmy's big sister came to play with him. She saw the green pipe and said, "That's a stupid toy. Why do you even care about it?" Timmy felt sad, but he didn't say anything.

Later that day, Timmy and his sister were playing outside. They were running and laughing when suddenly, Timmy's sister tripped and fell. She scraped her knee and started to cry. Timmy remembered the green pipe and ran to get it. He used it as a straw to blow bubbles and make his sister laugh. She stopped crying and hugged him. "You're the best brother ever," she said.

From that day on, Timmy's sister never called the green pipe a stupid toy again. She learned that it didn't matter what something looked like, as long as it made someone happy. Timmy was happy too, because he knew that he could always care for his sister when she needed him.

Teddy was very eager to go outside and explore. His mom opened the front door and Teddy peeked out. He saw a shiny new bike and he started to jump around in excitement. He ran over to the bike and started to peddle. Teddy peddled around the front yard and he was so proud of himself. He kept peddling and he explored all around the neighborhood, showing off his new bike. He was so excited to explore. Eventually, it was time for Teddy to go in for the night. His mom smiled at his eagerness and Teddy couldn't wait to ride his bike again the following day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a black cat named Mittens. Mittens was very soft and cuddly. One day, Timmy and Mittens were playing outside when Timmy saw a big tree. He dared Mittens to climb the tree with him. Mittens meowed nervously but followed Timmy up the tree. 

When they got to the top of the tree, Timmy accidentally fell and hurt his arm. His mom took him to the nurse who put a bandage on his arm. Mittens sat on Timmy's lap and purred to make him feel better. From that day on, Timmy never dared Mittens to do anything dangerous again.

One day, Tom went on a search. Tom wanted to find something special for today. He looked in the sky but there was nothing there. He looked in his garden and it was empty. He looked everywhere but he couldn't find anything. 

Just when Tom was about to give up, he found something in his neighbour's garden. It was a modern toy car. Tom had seen this car before, but he couldn't remember where. Tom was so excited and he quickly grabbed it. 

Tom took the car home and showed it to his parents. They were so happy that Tom had found something so modern and special. 

Tom was very proud of his find and he decided to keep the car forever as a reminder of his special search today.

Once upon a time there was an old man. He had a big stick and was walking along a path. At the end of the path there was a big, deep puddle. The old man could see his reflection in the puddle. He wanted to make it look shiny. So he rubbed his stick against the surface of the puddle. He rubbed, and rubbed, and rubbed until his stick was wet and the puddle was sparkling! When he was done, he looked at his reflection again. He smiled and was very pleased. Then, the old man continued walking along the path.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he found a rope lying on the ground. It was a cheap rope, but Timmy thought it was still very cool.

As Timmy was playing with the rope, his mother came outside and warned him to be careful. She told him that the rope could be dangerous if he didn't use it properly. Timmy listened to his mother and promised to be careful.

Later that day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Timmy showed him the rope and they decided to have a contest to see who could climb it the fastest. Billy didn't listen to Timmy's warning and climbed the rope too quickly. He fell and hurt himself.

Timmy realized that his mother was right and that he should have been more careful with the rope. He learned that it's important to listen to warnings and to be safe when playing with things that could be dangerous.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very dependable and always helped her bird friends. She would share her food and help them build their nests. All the birds admired Tweety for her kindness.

One day, Tweety saw a little bird who was lost and couldn't find his home. Tweety knew she had to help him. She showed him the way back to his family and made sure he was safe. The little bird was very thankful and all the other birds admired Tweety even more.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and helpful to others. If you are dependable like Tweety, you will make many friends and be admired by others.

Once upon a time, there was a family who were very generous. Every day they would rub each other's backs, give big hugs and share their toys. They were all very happy and they made each other smile.

One special day, they decided to go outside and rub the warm sand between their toes. The sun was shining down on them and the family laughed and said it felt so special!

They were so generous that even a little bird flew down and landed on their shoulders. The family were so happy, they just kept rubbing and rubbing the bird's feathers. 

The bird was so pleased that it flew away and came back with a surprise for the family. It dropped a nice, juicy worm at their feet and all the family laughed. 

The family were so generous that day that it made the little bird very happy. They all went inside and gave each other big hugs. That night, the family went to bed with smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside and get dirty. One day, her mommy asked her to come inside and clean up. Lily didn't want to clean, but she knew it was important.

So, she went to the bathroom and washed her hands with soap and water. Then, she used a towel to dry them off. Her mommy said she did a good job cleaning.

After that, her mommy made some tea. It was orange tea, which was Lily's favorite. She drank it all up and felt happy. She realized that cleaning up wasn't so bad after all.

Elias was playing in his bedroom. He had his toy box open and he was putting different shapes inside. He had a triangle, a square and a circle. He wanted to put the triangle somewhere special. Elias thought about it for a moment and then he had an idea. He looked around the quiet room and spotted a shelf in the corner. He decided the triangle should go there.

Elias carefully put the triangle on the top shelf. He stepped back to admire his work. He smiled. Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"That looks nice," said his mum. "You put the triangle there very nicely."

Elias beamed. He was so pleased his mum had noticed. 

"I'm so proud of you," she said.

Elias hugged her and went back to playing with his toys. He was happy he had put the triangle somewhere special.

Once there was a girl called Nell. She loved to help her mom and dad around the house.

One day, Nell saw her dad wearing a big, bright belt. Nell asked her dad why he was wearing it. He told her that it held up his trousers and kept them nice and neat. She thought it was a very clever idea.

Nell saw that her mom was having a hard time carrying all her groceries in her arms. Nell wanted to help her mom and knew just what to do. She ran to her bedroom and found an even bigger, brighter belt. Then she ran back to her mom and helped her lift up the bags with the belt.

At the end of the day, Nell was very proud of herself for helping her family. She had learnt a lesson that day - with a bit of thought, you can find clever ways to help others.

Once upon a time there was a family with two kids. One day, when they were outside, it started to rain hard. The rain came down really fast and soon the ground was all wet. The kids said to their parents, "Look, it's a flood!"

The water was coming up higher and higher and it started to come into the house. The parents were worried and said, "Come on, let's go upstairs so we can be safe." Upstairs, the family watched as the flood water kept coming in. The water was so high that it was touching the roof.

The kids were getting scared and started to cry. Their mom said, "It's okay, sweeties. Everything will be alright." But soon the water kept getting higher and the family had to go outside.

The flood was so strong that it hurt the family. They had to hold onto each other to stay safe. Finally, the flood stopped and the family was safe. The family was so happy to be safe and said, "We made it!"

One day there was a little girl named Mia. She was three years old. Mia always felt miserable because of how small she was, and she often questioned why she was so small.

One day, Mia got a great idea. She went to her mom and said, "I want to go outside and find somebody bigger and stronger than me, so I can go on adventures!"

Mia's mom smiled and said, "OK, sweetheart, but go to the left. That's the way to your grandpa's house!"

Mia was so excited. She skipped to the left down the path, eager to find her grandpa and get adventures.

When she found her grandpa's house, she ran up to him and began to question him about her big adventure.

Grandpa smiled and said, "Mia, I'm happy to help! How about we go on a walk together and explore the world around us? You can ask questions along the way and learn lots."

Mia couldn't believe it! She was no longer miserable. She was now full of energy and excitement. She ran around the room, ready for her big adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Amy who lived with her mum. Amy's mum always told her to be honest. 

One day, Amy was playing with her toy square. She wanted to throw it up in the air. Suddenly, her mum walked in. 

"Amy," said her mum, "be honest. Are you going to throw that square?" 

Amy looked scared. She nodded her head. 

"It's okay," said her mum. "As long as you are being honest, I don't mind if you throw the square."

Amy felt relieved. She smiled and threw the square up in the air. It flew higher and higher until it vanished out of sight. Amy ran around the room, clapping with joy. 

After that, Amy never forgot to be honest.

Once upon a time there was a wool sheep who lived in a big field. He was the bravest sheep in the whole field because he looked after all of the other sheep.

One day, the sheep heard a whisper. It was quiet and spooky. He didn't know what it was, so he went to check. He was scared, but he kept walking.

When he got to the edge of the field, he saw something dangerous. It was a Big Bad Wolf! The wolf was growling and he was hungry.

The sheep was scared, but he didn't know what to do. The only thing he had was a big fluffy coat of wool. So he whispered quietly to the other sheep and asked them to help.

The other sheep all gathered around and surrounded the Big Bad Wolf. Then together, they made a big big wool wall and blocked the wolf from the field.

The Big Bad Wolf gave up and went away, and the sheep were safe once again. They thanked the brave sheep for his bravery, and everything ended happily.

Once upon a time, there was an old oak tree. It was so thick and strong. One day, a brave little squirrel came by. He wanted to climb the tree. He jumped and jumped and jumped. But he couldn't reach the top.

He needed help. Suddenly, a strong wind came. It blew his ears back. He felt something sharp on his fur!

He opened his eyes and looked down. Right in front of him was an acorn. It was so shiny and sharp. The squirrel couldn't believe it. He had finally made it to the top of the oak tree!

He thanked the wind and then he picked the acorn. He chewed it and it tasted so good. Then he jumped and he jumped from the top of the old oak tree. He was so happy!

There was once a little girl called Sue. She loved exploring in the woods near her house. One day she found an old tree and thought it would be fun to climb it. She started climbing and once she was in the top she noticed a furry squirrel running through the branches. When Sue tried to touch it, the squirrel ran away. 

Sue was very sad but she suddenly noticed something in the bark of the tree - a small, round hole. She put her finger in the hole and pulled out a furry texture! She was really excited and showed it to her dad. 

Sue's dad looked at the texture and smiled. He said, "I think this texture used to belong to the squirrel. We should restore it to its rightful owner!" 

So Sue went back to the tree, ready to put the texture back. But, when she got there the tree was gone! She was so sad and started to cry. She could not see the squirrel anywhere. 

She wondered what she should do when suddenly she heard the noise of claws against the bark. She looked up and there was the squirrel jumping down the branches with its tail twitching. Sue put out her hand with the texture in it, and the squirrel took it and ran off.

Sue smiled and was happy to have been able to restore the furry texture to its rightful owner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around in the park. One day, Lily saw an aeroplane flying in the sky. She was so happy to see it and waved at the aeroplane. 

But then, Lily saw her friend crying. Her friend had lost her favourite toy. Lily felt sad for her friend and decided to help her look for the toy. They searched everywhere and finally found it under a tree. 

Lily's friend was so happy and hugged Lily. Lily felt happy too because she helped her friend. She learned that helping others can make them happy and that makes you happy too. From that day on, Lily always tried to help others and make them happy.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little bird. She was very eager to explore the world outside her nest. So one day, she spread her wings wide, and flew out of the nest.

As she flew through the warm air, she saw something far away. It was a mysterious chamber filled with wonders! She was so excited, she flew closer to take a look.

When she entered inside, the chamber started shaking and suddenly she heard a voice: "You are not allowed to enter here!" The bird was scared, and started flying away, but the voice said, "No! You must resist!" 

The bird was so scared that she turned around and fought back. She was determined to find out why the voice was blocking her way. After a long battle, the bird finally broke through, and to her surprise, she found a large cache of food in the chamber!

She was so eager to eat the food that she forgot all about the voice and the chamber. She was so happy that she collected as much food she could carry back to her nest.

From then on, the brave little bird was never afraid to explore the world outside her nest. Whenever she heard a warning, she remembered the chamber and the voice, and knew to resist and find the hidden treasures that lie beyond.

Tina wanted to organize her toys but she was feeling shy. She wasn't sure if her brother, Ben, would help her.
"Hey, Ben do want to organize my toys with me?" Tina asked.
Ben smiled at her. "Sure! Let's do it together."
Tina was so excited! She got peanuts to use as markers for the toys.
"We can put the peanuts here to show where each toy should go," she said.
Ben smiled. "That looks great. We can organize even more things like this." 
Tina and Ben worked together and got all of Tina's toys in the right place. 
Tina was so happy she gave Ben a big hug. 
"Thanks for helping me!" she said.
Ben grinned. "Any time!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jana. Jana was very thoughtful and liked to think before she acted. One day, her mom asked her if she wanted to buy a bookshelf.

Jana thought and thought and finally said, â€œYes!â€

Her mom smiled, grabbed her hand and said, â€œLetâ€™s go buy it!â€

So off they went to buy the bookshelf. When they got to the store, there were so many to choose from!

Jana finally found the perfect one! It had bright colors and lots of shelves for her favorite books. She smiled and jumped for joy, then ran to show her mom.

â€œMom, look! I found the best bookshelf!â€

Her mom smiled, hugged her and said, â€œThat was very thoughtful of you Jana!â€

And thatâ€™s how Jana found the perfect bookshelf - all with her very own thoughtful thinking.

Once upon a time there lived a small mouse. Every night, the mouse would blink its eyes in the moonlight and hop through the night. One night, the mouse stopped and sniffed the air. He could smell something heavy, like cheese. He hopped closer to investigate and found a big wedge of cheese! The mouse was thrilled.

â€œOh my!â€ the mouse said to himself. â€œThis cheese looks heavy! I don't think I can carry it alone.â€

Just then, the mouse blinked as a big brave cat came around the corner. He stopped to watch the mouse and the cheese.

The mouse scurried to the cat and said, â€œPlease help me carry this heavy cheese. I'll give you some if you help me.â€

The cat agreed and the two of them carried the cheese away, sharing it as they went. The mouse and the cat became good friends and shared the cheese every night from then on.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy who was brave and strong. He was always exploring the world around him, and one day while crawling through the grass he found something amazing! A rare bubble was perched on a blade of grass, and it shone in the sunlight.

The bubble seemed to be alive and was sparkling and twinkling like a tiny star. The boy was so excited and quickly tried to catch the bubble with his hands. But the bubble was too fast and it floated away! Then, it flew off and the boy chased the bubble. He crawled through the grass and bushes, reaching out and trying to get the bubble.

Finally, the little boy was able to catch the bubble in his hands. He carefully looked at the bubble and smiled. It was so beautiful and glittered like a diamond. Then, the boy popped the bubble and tiny droplets of soap flew up into the air.

The little boy laughed and clapped his hands. It was so much fun and he was so proud of himself for catching the rare bubble. He was happy to share the fun with everyone he knew. From that day, the little boy kept looking for rare bubbles to catch and enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved playing with her toys and making a mess in her room. Her mom would always tell her to clean up, but Lily never listened.

One day, Lily went to the park and saw a big jet flying in the sky. She thought it was so cool and wanted to fly in a jet too. But then she remembered how messy her room was and how her mom would be miserable if she didn't clean it up.

So, Lily went back home and cleaned her room all by herself. It was hard work, but she felt proud of herself when she was done. Her mom was so happy and gave her a big hug. Lily learned that cleaning up was important and made her and her mom happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad. One day, Lily went outside to play and saw a big mill in the distance. She ran over to see it up close. The mill was very tall and had big blades that spun around and around in the wind. 

Suddenly, Lily heard her mom calling her name. She ran back to the house and saw that her little brother had spilled his juice all over the floor. Her mom was very angry and said she would punish him by making him clean it up. Lily felt sad for her brother, but knew he had to learn not to make a mess. 

That night, Lily's mom made a bitter vegetable for dinner. Lily didn't like the taste, but she knew she had to eat it all or else her mom would punish her too. After dinner, Lily went to bed and dreamed about the big mill. She hoped one day she could go back and see it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on the playground every day. One day, Lily met a new friend named Max. Max was a big boy with a powerful swing. 

Lily asked Max, "Can I try your swing?" Max said, "Sure, come on!" Lily climbed up on the swing and Max pushed her. Lily felt like she was flying! 

After a while, Lily saw the sunset and said, "Wow, look at the pretty colors!" Max said, "Yeah, it's beautiful." Lily asked Max, "Do you want to slide with me?" Max said, "Sure, let's go!" 

Lily and Max went to the slide and slid down together. They laughed and had so much fun. Lily was happy to have a new friend to play with. The end.

Once there was a girl named Sarah who wanted to visit her grandma. She put on her shoes and took her backpack. She was so excited to visit her grandma.

When she arrived, her grandma hugged her tight. Sarah said, "Hi Grandma, I am here to visit you!"

Her grandma smiled and said, "Oh what a cute nose you have" She pinched Sarah's nose and said, "It's so tough!"

Sarah laughed and said, "Yes, it is tough like my superhero!" Sarah showed her grandma her superhero costume and they both laughed.

They decided to make some cookies together. Sarah helped her grandma stir the cookie dough and put eggs into the bowl.

When the cookies were done, Sarah said, "They smell so good! I had a great visit with you, Grandma!"

"Me too," said Grandma. They gave each other a big hug and Sarah went home.

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Lily. She loved to go for walks in the park. One day, she met a rude man who said mean things to her. 

The woman asked, "Why are you being rude to me?" 

The man replied, "I don't like people who go for walks in the park." 

The woman didn't let the man's words hurt her feelings. She continued to go for walks in the park every day. 

One day, the man saw the woman again and apologized for being rude. He said, "I was wrong to say mean things to you. Can we be friends?" 

The woman smiled and said, "Of course! I'm happy to go for a walk with you." And from that day on, they went for walks in the park together and became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny. Every day he would hop around and explore his neighbourhood. One day he was hopping through a park when he saw something funny on a hanger. The bunny was curious so he hopped over to take a closer look. It was a strange hat, big and yellow. He snuck up slowly to introduce himself to the hat.

The hat was surprised when he heard a voice say "Hello". He said in a deep voice "Greetings, I'm the funny hat." The bunny immediately knew he wanted to be friends. He asked the funny hat to come play with him and the hat replied, "Hmm, I wouldn't know what to do. You'll have to show me."

The bunny smiled and invited the funny hat onto the hanger. The bunny showed him all his favourite places to play and taught him how to hop like a bunny. The funny hat was thrilled and they became instant friends. They had lots of fun playing together, hopping around the neighbourhood. It looked like they might be friends forever.

Once there was a prune. He was very delicate and could talk. One day, the prune heard a voice. It said "Hello! Who is there?"

The prune was scared but brave, so he answered "I'm Prune. Who are you?"

The voice said "My name is Bird. Where are you?"

The prune replied "I'm in a tree."

Bird said "I can help you if you want!"

Prune replied "Yes please! I want to get down!"

Bird hopped over and told Prune "Jump onto my back and hang on tight!"

Prune was brave and did what Bird said. When he jumped, he felt a strange sensation. But soon enough, Prune was on the ground.

"Thank you Bird!" said Prune.

"You're welcome," replied Bird. "Be careful next time delicate Prune!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and see all the animals. One day, she saw a big, white goose walking around in her yard. The goose looked at Lily and Lily looked at the goose. Lily said, "Hello, goose! Do you want to play with me?" The goose didn't say anything, but Lily guessed that it wanted to play too.

Lily and the goose played together for a while, but then the goose got serious. It started flapping its wings and honking really loud. Lily didn't know what was wrong. She guessed that maybe the goose wanted to go somewhere else. So, Lily said goodbye to the goose and watched it fly away into the blue sky. From that day on, Lily always looked for the goose when she played outside.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. But it was a very hot day and the sun was shining bright. They felt thirsty and tired.

"Let's go find some shade," Lily said. "We can rest under a tree and drink some water."

They looked around and saw a big tree with many leaves. It looked cool and cozy. They ran towards it and sat under its branches.

"Ah, this is much better," Tom said. "The shade is nice and the water is cold."

They drank from their bottles and felt refreshed. They saw a squirrel on the tree. It was holding a nut in its paws. It looked at them and made a funny noise.

"Hello, squirrel," Lily said. "Do you want to share your nut with us?"

The squirrel shook its head and squeezed the nut harder. It did not want to share. It was greedy and selfish.

"Please, squirrel," Tom said. "We are hungry and we have nothing to eat. You have a big nut. You can give us a little bit."

The squirrel shook its head again and squeezed the nut even harder. It did not care about Tom and Lily. It only cared about itself.

Suddenly, the nut cracked and broke into pieces. The squirrel had squeezed it too hard. It lost its nut and had nothing to eat. It looked sad and sorry.

Tom and Lily felt sorry for the squirrel too. They decided to share their water with it. They poured some water into a cap and offered it to the squirrel.

"Here, squirrel," Lily said. "You can drink some water. We are sorry you lost your nut."

The squirrel looked at them and smiled. It drank some water and felt better. It realized that Tom and Lily were kind and generous. It learned that sharing is better than being greedy.

"Thank you, Tom and Lily," the squirrel said. "You are mighty friends. I am sorry I was mean to you. Can we share the shade and play together?"

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They invited the squirrel to join them. They played under the tree and had fun. They became friends and learned to share.

The end.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to eat sweet things. One day, Sue saw a big pastry on the kitchen table. It was cool and looked yummy. Sue wanted to eat the pastry, but it was not hers.

Sue thought, "I will just peek at the pastry, and maybe take a little bite." Sue took a bite, but she did not stop. She ate the whole pastry. Sue felt happy but also a little bad.

Later, Sue's mom came home with her little brother, Tim. Tim was sad and crying. Mom said, "Tim did a good job at school today, so I bought him a big, cool pastry as a treat. But now it's gone!" Sue felt very bad. She knew she should not have eaten the pastry. The moral of the story is to not take things that are not yours.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man. He had a pet rabbit and he fed it every day. The rabbit was very happy because the man always gave it something yummy.

One day, the man decided he wanted to see what was behind the big door. He opened the door and saw a big garden with lots of carrots!

He decided to gather some carrots and take them home to feed to his rabbit. The rabbit was so excited and the man was so happy he could make his pet happy. 

The man and the rabbit enjoyed the carrots together. They both had a wonderful time and were very happy. The kind man continued to feed his pet and they both lived very contentedly ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a nice little boy named Timmy. He liked to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy saw his mom washing the dishes in the kitchen. She looked tired and Timmy wanted to help her.

Timmy asked his mom if he could wash the dishes for her. She was surprised but happy that Timmy wanted to help. Timmy washed the dishes very carefully and made sure they were all clean. His mom was very proud of him and said he was a hero for helping her.

From that day on, Timmy always helped his mom with the dishes and other chores around the house. He learned that being a hero doesn't always mean fighting bad guys, sometimes it just means helping others.

Once upon a time there was a brave knight. He wore a shiny armor and carried a big shield. One day the knight went to buy a new shield. He walked into a dark cave where there was a store. 

The knight said to the storekeeper, "Hello! I would like to buy a new shield."

The storekeeper replied, "We have a very special shield. It is dark and strong."

The knight was excited. "I'll take it!" he said. 

The storekeeper gave him the shield and the knight happily paid him. He thanked the storekeeper and then took his new shield and went off to his next adventure.

Sara and Ben were playing in the backyard with their toy cars. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. Sara had a red car and Ben had a blue car. They were having fun until Sara saw something shiny in the grass.

"Look, Ben, look!" Sara said, pointing to the shiny thing. "What is that?"

Ben looked and saw a small metal box with a button on it. He was curious and wanted to touch it.

"Maybe it's a treasure!" Ben said, reaching for the box.
